outlooksByWeek.2: Jaylen Waddle did not contribute much in his Broncos' debut, catching just one of three targets for a meager two yards in the Week 1 loss to Kansas City. Steve Spagnuolo's rebuilt secondary prioritized taking Waddle out of the picture, and the former Dolphin wideout hasn't yet established enough chemistry with QB Bo Nix to overcome consistent double teams. Waddle will look to bounce back in Week 2 against a Jaguars defense that was tied for 17th last season in points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jaylen Waddle broke out in the Broncos' Week 2 win over the Jaguars, erupting for an 8-138-0 line on 10 targets as he began to get on the same page as quarterback Bo Nix. Waddle logged plenty of downfield targets but also had a red zone look, usage that promises plenty more big performances. The former Dolphin hasn't had a 1,000-yard season since 2023, but the early returns in Denver suggest he'll have little trouble returning to that level in 2026. He'll face a Rams secondary in Week 3 that's allowed just 19 receptions to WRs through two weeks, tied for seventh in the NFL, but three of those have gone for touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jaylen Waddle is struggling to adjust to his new offense with the Broncos. The former Dolphins wide receiver caught only two of his seven targets in a Week 3 win over the Rams for 10 yards, while adding a 14-yard run. Waddle leads Denver with 20 targets through three games, but he's turned them into just 11 catches for 150 yards, and he's still looking for his first TD of the season. He'll face a 49ers secondary in Week 4 that ranks ninth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jaylen Waddle scored his first touchdown with the Broncos in a Week 4 loss to the 49ers, but it was overall another disappointing performance from the former Dolphin. Waddle has recorded double-digit targets only once in four games to begin the season, leading to a modest 16-185-1 line on 26 looks from Bo Nix. That's still better numbers than Courtland Sutton, and the issue seems to be the overall struggles of the offense under first-time play caller Davis Webb. How long Sean Payton lets that situation last before reclaiming those duties is an open question for Denver. Waddle will try to hit paydirt again in Week 5 against a Chargers secondary that ranks 18th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jaylen Waddle continues to struggle in his first season with the Broncos. He's been held to 35 receiving yards or fewer in four of five games, including a 2-19-0 line on five targets in a Week 5 win over the Chargers. Having Sean Payton reclaim play-calling duties should help the offense in the long run, but Waddle will be tough to trust until he begins to display consistent chemistry with Bo Nix. Waddle will face a Seahawks secondary in Week 6 that ranks fourth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jaylen Waddle remains stuck in neutral as part of a sluggish Broncos passing game. The former Dolphin has gone four straight games without reaching 40 receiving yards, managing just a 13-88-1 line on 25 targets over that stretch while quarterback Bo Nix tries to find a rhythm. Waddle showed his upside back in Week 2 with an 8-138-0 line, but until the Denver offense begins clicking, his production will remain erratic. He could break out in Week 7 against a Cardinals secondary that's given up 10 touchdowns to wide receivers this season, 31st in the league.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jaylen Waddle left the Broncos' Week 7 win over the Cardinals in the fourth quarter with a chest injury after producing a modest 4-48-0 line on seven targets. The former Miami wideout hasn't been able to get comfortable in his new environment; he has been held under 50 receiving yards in six of his first seven games for Denver. The severity of Waddle's injury isn't clear, but the team had little incentive to get him back on the field with a big lead. Assuming he is cleared to play in Week 8, he'll have a tough time producing a ceiling game against a Kansas City secondary that ranks third in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Jaylen Waddle caught his second touchdown of the season in the Broncos' Week 8 win over Kansas City, but his overall numbers remain disappointing, The former Dolphin has just a 29-315-2 line on 51 targets through eight games, and the struggles of quarterback Bo Nix have prevented Waddle from finding a rhythm in his new offense. Waddle has been targeted 10 or more times only once in those eight games, while last season's No. 1 wide receiver for Denver, Courtland Sutton, handled double-digit targets six times in 2025. Waddle will look for more volume in Week 9 against a Panthers team that just fired its defensive coordinator, and which is tied for 15th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Waddle was traded to Denver after spending his first five seasons in Miami. The 2021 first-round pick was solid during his Dolphins tenure, finishing in the top 30 among receivers in fantasy PPG four times, though never reaching the top 10 while often playing second fiddle to Tyreek Hill. Although he has been a reliable target and has missed only seven games in five years, Waddle hasn't finished a season higher than 20th in targets or catches since 2021. In Denver, the 27-year-old Waddle will compete with Courtland Sutton for the team lead in targets in a scheme that likes to spread the ball around. Not utilized near the goal line much at 5-foot-10 and 180 pounds (he's yet to clear seven end zone targets in a season), Waddle is likely to max out as a back-end WR2 in Denver.

The NFL's leading sack-getter the past two seasons, the Broncos D/ST lost DE John Franklin-Myers during the offseason but otherwise return largely the same front for 2026. Led by Zach Allen, Nik Bonitto and four-time Pro Bowl cornerback Patrick Surtain II, the Broncos scored 15-plus fantasy points on four occasions last season and finished third in the category. Their early-season schedule presents some challenges (@KC, Week 1; LAR, Week 3; @SF, Week 4), but overall theirs is one of the most favorable, especially across a nine-week span beginning in Week 7 (@ARI, KC, @CAR, bye, LV, @PIT, MIA, @NYJ, @LV).

outlooksByWeek.2: Omarion Hampton looked like the clear lead back for the Chargers in their season-opening loss to the Cardinals, taking 12 carries for 43 yards and a touchdown, while backup Keaton Mitchell saw only four carries. Neither RB caught a pass as Justin Herbert had a very narrow target tree under new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel, connecting with just five different receivers. Hampton had been headed for a big rookie campaign before getting injured, so staying healthy will be the biggest factor in any potential 2026 breakout. He could post better numbers in Week 2 against a Raiders defense that ranked 21st last season in points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Omarion Hampton has been one of the few Chargers who seems to be benefiting from new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme. The second-year back racked up 115 scrimmage yards and a touchdown in Week 2's loss to the Raiders, and he's been the clear top option in the backfield, getting 37 touches through two weeks compared to Keaton Mitchell's 10 and Kimani Vidal's zero. Hampton lost a fumble in each game, and that split could begin to shift Mitchell's way if ball security is deemed an issue for the 2025 first-round pick. Hampton could cash in on his bell-cow role in Week 3 against a Bills defense that's allowed four touchdowns to RBs so far, two on the ground and two through the air.
outlooksByWeek.4: Omarion Hampton's workload took a step backward in a Week 3 loss to the Bills, as the Chargers' backfield teeters toward a committee. The second-year back hasn't been awful, producing 214 scrimmage yards and two rushing touchdowns in three games while averaging 3.9 yards per carry, but Keaton Mitchell is averaging 5.0 yards per carry on limited usage and may be a better fit for offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme. Kimani Vidal also had his first touches of the season in Buffalo. Hampton is the most talented player of the three on paper, but with the 0-3 Chargers struggling to generate offense, every possible solution will be on the table. He isn't likely to start turning things around in Week 4 against a Seahawks defense that ranks fifth in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Omarion Hampton scored a touchdown for the third time in four games during the Chargers' Week 4 loss to the Seahawks, but his role in the backfield continues to slip. The second-year back's nine carries and 11 touches were season lows for a spark for his unit. Hampton has still been the most productive of the trio this season with 267 scrimmage yards and three rushing TDs, but his 4.0 yards per carry trails Mitchell's, while Keaton Mitchell handled 15 touches and Kimani Vidal got seven, indicating that offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel is moving toward a full-blown committee as he searches 4.6 mark. Hampton will try to re-establish himself as the clear No. 1 on the depth chart in Week 5 against a Broncos defense that ranks 26th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Omarion Hampton continues to struggle in offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme while working behind a patchwork Chargers offensive line. Hampton does have three rushing touchdowns in five games, but his 3.7 yards per carry is a significant downturn from his 4.4 mark as a rookie, and he's averaging just 61.2 scrimmage yards per contest. He's also lost snaps and touches to Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal as the backfield devolves into a committee. Hampton will try to find a spark in Week 6 against a Kansas City defense that is tied for 13th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Omarion Hampton will look to turn his season around coming out of the Chargers' Week 7 bye. He failed to reach 50 scrimmage yards or get into the end zone in his last two games before the break, as Mike McDaniel turned his backfield into a committee. Hampton is the most talented back on the roster, but as long as Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal are garnering significant shares of the workload, all of them will have limited ceilings. Hampton will try to reassert himself as the No. 1 option in Week 8 against a Rams defense that's tied for 14th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Omarion Hampton remains stuck in a backfield committee for the Chargers while running behind an injury-weakened offensive line. Hampton led the team's RBs with 11 touches in a Week 8 loss to the Rams, while Keaton Mitchell got seven touches and Kimani Vidal handled 10, and none of the three managed more than 30 scrimmage yards. Hampton hasn't found the end zone since Week 4, and while he's nominally at the top of the depth chart, his current usage holds little appeal. He's unlikely to break out without significantly more volume in Week 9 against an underperforming Texans defense that ranks 20th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Hampton is primed for a breakout second season following an impressive but injury-shortened rookie campaign. The first-round pick was busy during nine appearances, averaging 13.8 carries and 3.9 targets. He scored five touchdowns, averaged 15.1 fantasy points per game (13th best) and ranked third among backs in forced missed tackle rate, per PFF. With Kimani Vidal and Keaton Mitchell as his primary competition, Hampton has a clear path to lead rusher duties in 2026, and his targets only figure to increase with Greg Roman out and Mike McDaniel in as the team's playcaller. Add in a much-improved offensive line with star tackles Joe Alt and Rashawn Slater back healthy, and Hampton has nothing short of elite upside. Value him as a fringe RB1 with room for more.

The No. 1 D/ST selected on average last season, the Steelers finished a disappointing 14th in fantasy points and scored fewer than five points in 8-of-17 games. They've since overhauled their coaching staff, with Mike McCarthy replacing Mike Tomlin, and Patrick Graham as defensive coordinator, the same role he held with the Raiders from 2022-25. The offseason additions of S Jaquan Brisker and CB Jamel Dean should bolster this unit, and it benefits greatly from one of the softest September and October schedules in the league. Get this D/ST early, but be prepared to seek a replacement after that point.

outlooksByWeek.2: Denzel Boston and the Browns travel to battle the Buccaneers in Week 2. The rookie pass-catcher corralled two of four targets for 59 yards and a TD during Cleveland's 34-10 season-opening loss. Boston's touchdown was a 46-yard dime from Deshaun Watson, and he finished as the team leader in receiving yards. He draws a tough matchup against Tampa Bay, which ranked fourth in receptions allowed to WRs (8).
outlooksByWeek.3: Denzel Boston and the Browns host the Panthers in a Week 3 clash between 1-1 teams. The rookie followed up his 2-59-1 receiving line in the opener with an even better outing against the Buccaneers, tallying five catches on seven targets for 95 yards and another TD. Boston led the team in yardage and targets, as he's quickly becoming Deshaun Watson's preferred target, particularly downfield. He faces a vulnerable Carolina defense that ranks 18th in fantasy points allowed (30.3) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Denzel Boston and the Browns host the Steelers and their eighth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (28.0) to WRs in Week 4. The rookie wideout caught two of four targets for 41 yards and scored on a two-point conversion during Cleveland's 21-18 victory in Week 3. Boston finished second on the team in yardage behind Harold Fannin Jr. (51) as he continues to develop chemistry with QB Deshaun Watson. He's shaping up to be a boom-or-bust fantasy option but offers plenty of upside as the Browns' deep option for an improving offense.
outlooksByWeek.5: Denzel Boston and the Browns are on the road to take on the Jets in Week 5. He caught four of seven targets for a team-high 89 yards during Cleveland's 27-24 win in Week 4. Boston tied for third in targets and continued to prove himself as a big-play option, generating 60 yards on one reception that helped set up a Browns' touchdown run. He'll face a strong Jets secondary that allows 28.5 fantasy points per game to WRs, which ranks ninth in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Denzel Boston and the Browns host the division-rival Ravens for an AFC North clash in Week 6. He caught three of seven targets for 46 yards, including a 29-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter, during Cleveland's 17-12 Week 5 loss. The rookie wideout continues to shine for the Browns, as he now has a 16-330-3 line on 29 targets through five games to begin his career. With KC Concepcion (concussion) questionable for Week 6, Boston should remain Deshaun Watson's top target versus Baltimore's 23rd-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per contest (36.2) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Denzel Boston and the Browns are on the road for an interconference clash against the Titans in Week 7. He caught just one of five targets for 15 yards during Cleveland's comeback victory in Week 6. Boston tied for last in receptions but finished second in targets, as Deshaun Watson completed only 16 of his 26 pass attempts. It's still a positive sign that the Browns want to get the ball in the rookie's hands despite the meager offensive output. Boston will aim to bounce back versus Tennessee's 24th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (35.9) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Denzel Boston and the Browns head to Pittsburgh for an AFC North clash in Week 8. He hauled in three of eight targets for 27 yards in Cleveland's 27-24 victory in Week 7. Boston finished third on the team in targets but was a distant fourth in yardage behind fellow rookie KC Concepcion (129), Harold Fannin Jr. (91) and Dylan Sampson (32). Boston will look to rebound against a Steelers defense he posted a 4-89-0 receiving line on seven targets back in Week 4.

player.seasonOutlook: Boston was selected by the Browns in the second round of April's draft. He is a big receiver with terrific ball skills and touchdown-scoring upside. He's not the fastest, but that didn't stop him from producing 62-plus receptions, 830-plus yards and nine-plus TDs during both of his seasons as a starter at Washington. He handled 45% of his team's air yards in 2025 (highest in this rookie class). Boston dropped only four of 209 career targets (1.9% drop rate is fourth best in this WR class) and has the look of a reliable possession receiver. He'll begin his career battling Jerry Jeudy, Harold Fannin Jr. and fellow rookie KC Concepcion for targets in a Cleveland offense yet to sort out its quarterback situation. Boston is a fine late-round-upside flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jadarian Price is set for his second NFL start when Seattle travels to Arizona in Week 2. Price was efficient in his professional debut last Wednesday versus New England, rushing 10 times for 52 yards while catching both of his targets for six yards. George Holani was given eight carries in the win, which helped limit Price's workload. The split between the two going forward remains to be seen, but there's certainly a chance that Price's touches will increase as the season progresses. The Cardinals' run defense looked good against the Chargers in Week 1, holding Omarion Hampton to 43 yards on 12 carries.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jadarian Price injured his shoulder in the Seahawks' Week 2 win over Arizona, and it's unclear if he'll be able to play in Week 3 against Washington. The rookie RB was injured in the fourth quarter versus the Cardinals and finished the game with 13 carries for 52 yards and one catch for eight yards. Should Price not be able to play in Week 3, Emanuel Wilson would be he lead candidate to take over as the Seahawks starting RB. The Commanders have been awful against the pass but decent against the run this season and are yielding just 3.79 YPC against running backs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jadarian Price heads into Seattle's Week 4 matchup against the Chargers with potentially a lot on the line. After fumbling early in Sunday's Week 3 win over the Commanders, the rookie ended up logging just five totes for 15 yards while adding one catch for seven yards. Meanwhile, Emanuel Wilson (nine carries) and George Holani (three carries and five catches) each out-touched Price, casting uncertainty about the Seahawks' backfield plans moving forward. Price would benefit from a productive (and fumble-free) performance against the Chargers, who rank 19th in the league in giving up 17.2 fantasy points per game through three weeks.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jadarian Price (chest) is eligible to return from IR for Seattle's Week 8 matchup against Chicago. Price hasn't played since Week 3, but he's expected to be designated to return this week. It remains to be seen if the rookie will be able to suit up against the Bears, and even if he does play, he may be part of a backfield committee that also includes Emanuel Wilson and the potentially returning Zach Charbonnet (knee). With that said, Seattle's backfield could find success against a Chicago defense that has given up 4.33 yards per carry to running backs, 25th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.9: Jadarian Price is coming off an inefficient return from IR heading into Seattle's Week 9 clash against the Cardinals. Price moved past a chest injury to lead Seattle's backfield in carries against Chicago on Monday Night Football, but he garnered just 29 yards on 10 totes and eight yards on two catches. He shared RB snaps fairly equally with Zach Charbonnet, and if the duo continues in a timeshare, both players may have a limited week-to-week fantasy ceiling. The Cardinals do present a relatively favorable matchup, as they're middling or worse in most statistical categories versus running backs.

player.seasonOutlook: Price was selected by the Seahawks with the No. 32 overall pick of April's draft. Price managed only 280 career carries while stuck behind Jeremiyah Love at Notre Dame, but he showed well, posting a 4.13 YAC (second best in this rookie class) and 3.6 forced missed tackle rate (third best). He wasn't a factor as a receiver, however, totaling 15 receptions in 41 games. Price has a path to an immediate feature role in Seattle's run-first offense, though he may eventually defer substantial work to Zach Charbonnet (ACL recovery). Value Price as a flex, though he should land on the weekly RB2 radar while Charbonnet is sidelined.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jordan Addison will look to record his first reception of the year as the Vikings travel to Chicago in Week 2. Addison ran the second-most routes for Minnesota in Week 1 against the Packers, but he was unable to convert on either of his two targets. Veteran quarterback Carson Wentz, who filled in for an injured Kyler Murray (concussion), relied more on tight ends T.J. Hockenson and Josh Oliver behind Justin Jefferson. This could make Addison's role remains small as long as Wentz remains under center. With that being said, the Bears' defense did allow the fourth-most PPR points to wide receivers (46.3) in Week 1, which could open up Minnesota's passing game.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jordan Addison will seek to ramp things up as the Vikings travel to Tampa Bay in Week 3. Addison bounced back from a zero-catch performance in Week 1 this past Sunday, logging two catches for 21 yards against the Bears. Still, his output is nowhere near sufficient for fantasy owners, especially since he's put up WR2 numbers many times throughout the last three seasons. He'll face a Bucs defense that's allowed 24.9 PPR points per game against wide receivers this season, a top-10 mark.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jordan Addison will look to build off a big game as the Vikings play the Dolphins in Week 4. Addison saw an uptick in looks after the departure of Justin Jefferson (ankle) in Week 3, finishing the win with five catches for 90 yards and a touchdown on nine targets. While Jefferson very well could return to the field in the coming week, Addison did prove to be a solid option for Kyler Murray. Addison has proven to be an asset for Minnesota alongside Jefferson when being thrown to by a competent quarterback, which could be showcased even against a Miami defense that's ranked top-five (24.2 fantasy points per game) against WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jordan Addison will aim to do more as the Vikings travel to New Orleans in Week 5. Addison logged just four catches for 52 yards in Week 4 against the Dolphins, which was a bit of a disappointment given that Justin Jefferson (ankle) was inactive. Quarterback Kyler Murray also seemed to have built a connection with T.J. Hockenson against Miami, making it less likely that Addison will produce when Jefferson inevitably returns. The Saints have ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy WRs this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jordan Addison will aim to make a return as the Vikings play the Colts in Week 7. Addison missed Week 5 against the Saints with a hamstring injury, but he luckily had a bye week of rest. The fourth-year wideout will now need to return to practice if he hopes to suit up in Minnesota's upcoming home game. He'll face an Indianapolis defense that's ranked in the middle against fantasy WRs this year.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jordan Addison will aim to do more with his targets as the Vikings play the Lions in Week 8. Addison didn't do much again in Week 7 against the Colts, reeling in two of his three targets for 30 yards. The speedy pass catcher has put together an underwhelming start to the 2026 season, totaling just 13 catches for 183 yards and one touchdown across five games. He'll look to capitalize on a faulty Detroit defense that's ranked 26th in fantasy points allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Jordan Addison will seek to build off a team-leading performance as the Vikings play the Bills in Week 9. Addison led Minnesota with 66 receiving yards on three catches in a Week 8 loss to the Lions. The speedy pass catcher has posted a modest 16-249-1 receiving line across six games this season. He'll face a Buffalo defense that's ranked 28th in fantasy points allowed to RBs so far this campaign.

player.seasonOutlook: After impressing with a 70-911-10 receiving line on 108 targets as a rookie in 2023, Addison has seen his target, reception, yardage and touchdown totals decrease each of the last two seasons. A few missed games were partially to blame for the dips, but Minnesota's quarterback woes were the main culprit in 2025, as Addison went from 10 TDs and a 65% catch rate in both 2023 and 2024 to three TDs and a 53% catch rate last season. Addison already has a pair of top-25 fantasy campaigns to his name, but it may be a stretch for him to get there in 2026 with Kyler Murray leading the Minnesota offense, not to mention Jauan Jennings' addition to the lineup. The 24-year-old is best valued as WR4/flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: Cam Little got off to an accurate start by converting both of his field-goal attempts and all four extra points in Jacksonville's Week 1 win. He made an NFL-record 68-yard field goal last season, so there are no concerns about his leg strength. Getting into scoring range will be tougher than usual for the Jaguars in Week 2 against a Broncos defense that allowed the third-fewest points in the league last season, though 70 yards could be within Little's realistic range in the thin Denver air. Little's upside is high enough to maintain fantasy starter status, even given the tricky Week 2 matchup for Jacksonville's offense.
outlooksByWeek.3: Cam Little had a rare miss in Week 2 but has been one of the NFL's best kickers since entering the league in 2024. Through 36 games with the Jaguars, he has converted 61 of 68 field-goal attempts, including an NFL-record 68-yard field goal. He's a little riskier than usual in Week 3 against a Patriots defense that's allowing just 8.0 points per game, but Little is probably too good to bench regardless of the opponent.
outlooksByWeek.4: Cam Little narrowly missed setting an NFL record in Jacksonville's Week 3 win over the Patriots, as his 70-yard field-goal attempt squeaked just wide right. Little already holds the record for the longest made field goal in a regular-season game with a 68-yarder last season, but the powerful kicker has converted just 4-of-6 field-goal attempts in 2026 while having hit all 10 of his PAT tries. Despite Little's pedestrian start, his impressive range coupled with Jacksonville's ability to move the ball effectively give Little starter-level upside each game, and a Week 4 road matchup against a Bengals team that's allowing 21.0 points per game is no exception.
outlooksByWeek.5: Cam Little made all three of his field-goal attempts in Jacksonville's Week 4 win over the Bengals. The big-legged kicker has yet to miss from inside 50 yards and has tremendous range, as Little made an NFL-record 68-yard field goal last season and narrowly missed a 70-yard attempt this season. Little remains a viable fantasy starter as usual in Week 5 against an Eagles team that's allowing 23.3 points per game but has given up only six successful field goals through four games. This game will be played at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London, where Spencer Shrader and Drew Stevens combined to make all five of their field-goal attempts in Week 4.
outlooksByWeek.6: Cam Little made both of his field-goal attempts in Jacksonville's 19-17 Week 5 win over the Eagles in London, including the game-winning 57-yarder on the game's final play. He also missed a PAT, with a bad snap contributing after the Jaguars lost long snapper Ross Matiscik to a shoulder injury in the first quarter. Snaps could again be an issue on Jacksonville's kicking attempts in Week 6, but the big-legged Little has too much upside to bench as the Jaguars play their second consecutive game in London, this time taking on a Texans team that has allowed 12 made field goals (tied for third-most in the league), and 22.0 points per game.
outlooksByWeek.8: Cam Little has started 10-for-12 on field-goal attempts with a long of 60 across Jacksonville's first six games. The big-legged kicker could be in for a busy afternoon in Week 8 at home against the Colts, who are giving up 25.7 points per game and have allowed a league-high 21 field-goal attempts, 18 of which have been successful. Little is worth snagging off waivers if he was dropped during Jacksonville's Week 7 bye, as he profiles as a top-10 kicker for Week 8 and beyond.
outlooksByWeek.9: Cam Little has attempted 23 PATs compared to just 12 field goals this season, a testament to Jacksonville's high-octane offense. His ceiling remains immense given the frequent scoring opportunities and Little's elite range, making him a viable fantasy starter for Week 9. Little will face a reeling Ravens team in Week 9 that has dropped three consecutive games while allowing at least 35 points in each of the last two. Overall, Baltimore has given up 16 made field goals in eight games while allowing 25.4 points per game.

outlooksByWeek.2: Marvin Harrison will look to get going in Arizona's Week 2 tilt against Seattle. Harrison notched just one catch on three targets in a season-opening win over the Chargers, though that reception did go for a robust 33 yards. With that said, the fact that he drew such a small amount of QB Jacoby Brissett's 37 targets provides some cause for concern, especially with newcomer Kendrick Bourne getting a healthy eight targets and No. 2 wideout Michael Wilson drawing seven. The Cardinals' wideout corps as a whole faces a tough challenge in the Seahawks, who didn't allow any Patriots pass catcher to exceed 51 yards in a Week 1 victory.
outlooksByWeek.3: Marvin Harrison will look to bounce back from his Week 2 goose egg when the Cardinals face San Francisco in Week 3. Harrison was targeted by QB Jacoby Brissett just once Sunday in a loss to the Seahawks and finished without a catch. The third-year receiver concerningly has just one catch for 33 yards through two weeks, and perhaps even more distressingly for his fantasy managers, he's drawn only four targets to Michael Wilson's 14 so far. The 49ers rank in the top 10 through two weeks by giving up only 247 receiving yards to wideouts.
outlooksByWeek.4: Marvin Harrison heads into the Cardinals' Week 4 matchup against the Giants having yet to get going this season. Harrison did record a campaign-best three catches and 40 yards this past Sunday in a loss to San Francisco, but he was far outshined by fellow wideout Michael Wilson, who posted an 11-89-1 line on a massive 17 targets. Star tight end Trey McBride also continued to shine with a 9-75-0 receiving line, so Harrison appears to be QB Jacoby Brissett's third option in the passing game at the moment. The Giants could present an opportunity for Harrison to get into the end zone, as they've given up four receiving TDs to wideouts so far this year, tied for fifth-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Marvin Harrison heads into Arizona's Week 5 matchup against Detroit struggling to build chemistry with QB Jacoby Brissett. Though Harrison recorded a 12-yard touchdown reception in Week 4 against the Giants, that was his only catch on four targets. The third-year wideout has exceeded one reception just once through four games this season and has totaled only 12 targets, remarkably far behind the 44 targets fellow wideout Michael Wilson has logged. With that said, the Lions could provide a prime opportunity for Harrison to get back on track, as Detroit has surrendered 207.3 receiving yards per game to wideouts, third-worst in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Marvin Harrison could make his Texans debut in Week 6 against the Jaguars. Harrison will likely be brought along slowly after being acquired in a trade from Arizona, so expectations should be tempered for Week 6, though the 2024 fourth overall pick is at least worth a flier in deeper leagues against a Jacksonville secondary that has allowed the most yards in the NFL to wide receivers. Harrison had just 85 receiving yards in four games for the Cardinals this season, but a reunion with former Ohio State QB C.J. Stroud could be what Harrison needs to get his career back on track. While catching passes from Stroud in 2022, Harrison posted his best college season, with 77 catches for 1,263 yards and 14 touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.7: Marvin Harrison was on the field for only 12 snaps in his Texans debut against the Jaguars in Week 6 but came away with three catches for 34 yards from former college teammate C.J. Stroud. Harrison's role figures to grow as he gets acclimated to his new surroundings and learns the playbook. The trade acquisition from Arizona had only 85 receiving yards through four games with the Cardinals this season, but Harrison was considered an elite wide receiver prospect when he was drafted fourth overall in 2024. He's certainly worth a speculative add if available, but Harrison will remain a risky flex option in Week 7 against the Giants since his usage is likely to be limited again.
outlooksByWeek.9: Marvin Harrison has drawn four targets in each of his first two games with the Texans. The 2024 fourth overall pick of the Cardinals could start to earn a larger role with his new team, especially after having a chance to further familiarize himself with the playbook during Houston's Week 8 bye. Harrison won't be a recommended fantasy option until he earns a larger role, as he played just 19% of offensive snaps in his Texans debut and 21% in his second game with the team. He'll be a risky Week 9 option against the Chargers' mediocre secondary, but Harrison's future looks brighter in Houston than it did in Arizona.

player.seasonOutlook: Harrison's pro career is off to a slow start after he was selected with the No. 4 overall pick back in 2024. The Ohio State product was serviceable as a rookie (885 yards and eight TDs), but he missed five full games and was limited in others en route to a 41-608-4 receiving line in 2025. Harrison has finished 41st and 39th, respectively, in fantasy PPG despite a massive role near the goal line (he's third in the NFL in end zone targets since he was drafted and finished both seasons in the top five). Harrison is only entering his prime at age 24 and perhaps he'll make a Year 3 leap with new coach Mike LaFleur calling the plays and with Kyler Murray no longer under center. Harrison performed better with Jacoby Brissett under center last season and has the raw talent to make him well worth post-hype consideration in the middle rounds.

outlooksByWeek.2: Rico Dowdle and the Steelers are on the road for a Week 2 matchup against the Patriots. He rushed eight times for 15 yards and caught two of five targets for another six yards during Pittsburgh's Week 1 20-13 win over Atlanta. Dowdle's backfield partner, Jaylen Warren, was much more efficient with his 15 touches, which he turned into 73 scrimmage yards. It will be difficult to trust Dowdle in a tilt versus New England's 14th-ranked defense, which has allowed 84 rushing yards to the position.
outlooksByWeek.3: Rico Dowdle and the Steelers host the Bengals and their 14th-ranked run defense in Week 3. He finished Pittsburgh's loss last week with seven carries for 22 yards and caught both targets for 22 yards. Dowdle left the game in the second quarter with a toe injury, was cleared and returned to play in the second half but then left for good after appearing to re-injure the same toe. Keep an eye on his status in practice this week, as there's a good chance he'll be limited, thus leaving his status for Sunday's contest against the Bengals in question.
outlooksByWeek.4: Rico Dowdle and the Steelers visit the division-rival Browns for a Week 4 road tilt. He sat out Pittsburgh's Week 3 victory with a toe injury he sustained in Week 2, and it looks like he's in real jeopardy of missing a second consecutive contest. Dowdle didn't practice at all last week and was not present at Monday's walkthrough session, which isn't a great sign for his availability on a short week. He'll have to practice in some capacity if he hopes to face Cleveland's sixth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (17.1) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Rico Dowdle and the Steelers host the Colts in a battle between 2-2 teams in Week 5. He missed his second consecutive game with a toe injury sustained in Week 2. Jaylen Warren accounted for 20 of 22 touches by running backs during Pittsburgh's Week 4 loss, a pattern that would surely continue if Dowdle remains sidelined against Indianapolis. Monitor his practice participation leading up to a favorable matchup versus the Colts' 23rd-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (24.2) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Rico Dowdle and the Steelers travel to face off with the Buccaneers in Week 6. After sitting out the last three games with a toe injury, it appears Dowdle is ready to make his return against the 1-4 Bucs. He was brought to Pittsburgh to form a dynamic one-two punch alongside Jaylen Warren, but the incumbent starter has excelled as the featured player out of the backfield, particularly over the last three weeks. Assuming Dowdle takes the field in Week 6, he's likely to work as the clear backup to Warren, so it's best he remains on fantasy benches versus Tampa Bay's sixth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (17.4) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Rico Dowdle and the Steelers travel to Paris for a Week 7 meeting with the Saints. He returned from a three-game absence due to a toe injury and registered seven carries for 40 yards and three catches on four targets for nine yards during Pittsburgh's overtime win in Week 6. Dowdle played just 28% of snaps on offense as he works his way back into game shape, and he was pretty effective in limited action, so his workload should rise steadily in Week 7. Jaylen Warren started and earned 16 touches to Dowdle's 10, and there's a good chance they'll both be heavily involved versus a New Orleans defense that ranks dead-last in fantasy points allowed per game (30.7) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Rico Dowdle and the Steelers look to even the season series against the Browns in Week 8. He rushed nine times for 41 yards and caught all six of his targets for 45 yards in Week 7 during Pittsburgh's 16-10 victory in Paris. Dowdle finished first in receptions and second in yardage despite being out-touched by starter Jaylen Warren, who turned his 21 touches into 137 scrimmage yards. Dowdle was inactive for the Week 4 loss against Cleveland, so he'll look to make an impact with first place in the AFC North at stake.

player.seasonOutlook: Dowdle signed with the Steelers after nearly identical campaigns with the Cowboys in 2024 (1,328 yards and five TDs on 274 touches) and Panthers in 2025 (1,373 yards and seven TDs on 275 touches). He was effective as a rusher (4.57 yards per carry) and fairly busy as a receiver (50 targets both years) en route to finishing just inside the top 25 in fantasy points per game both seasons. Now in Pittsburgh, the 28-year-old is expected to share work with Jaylen Warren. Earning lead-rusher duties could get Dowdle into the weekly flex discussion, but the ceiling will be low and he'll likely need an injury in order to find his way to consistent fantasy output. Consider him for your bench.

outlooksByWeek.2: TreVeyon Henderson could make his season debut in Week 2 when the Patriots host the Steelers. Henderson missed last week due to an ankle injury but has returned to practice ahead of the matchup. Pass-blocking concerns were rumored to be an issue during the preseason, and facing a Steelers defense that rushes the passer well may keep Henderson on the sideline more than managers would like, in addition to a potentially limited role in his first game back. Pittsburgh allowed a mere 3.8 yards per carry in Week 1 but did allow 90 receiving yards to running backs, albeit that was Bijan Robinson. Split touches in a likely low-scoring game would require Henderson's patented big-play ability for him to be fantasy relevant.
outlooksByWeek.3: TreVeyon Henderson will look to build on an impressive debut when New England faces Jacksonville in Week 3. After missing Week 1 due to an ankle injury, Henderson shouldered 16 carries in Week 2, putting up 76 yards and a touchdown. While he wasn't targeted in the passing game, Henderson showed his elite big-play ability. Rhamondre Stevenson was an afterthought after losing an early fumble, but with New England struggling to pass the ball effectively, this has the look of a run-first, split backfield. Jacksonville is allowing just 3.2 yards per carry and 110 total rushing yards through two weeks, which will keep Henderson's Week 3 expectations in check.
outlooksByWeek.4: TreVeyon Henderson remains mired in a split backfield for the Patriots ahead of their Week 4 matchup with the Bills. Henderson's snap share dropped from 60% to 35% in Week 3 as the Patriots played from behind, forcing Rhamondre Stevenson into a pass-blocking role. With only one catch through two games, Henderson isn't getting many opportunities to create his signature big play. Facing a defense that's allowing just 3.9 yards per carry while being more vulnerable to receiving backs, Henderson figures to be a boom-or-bust option.
outlooksByWeek.5: TreVeyon Henderson will seek chunk plays in the Patriots' Week 5 matchup against a vulnerable Raiders run defense. Henderson had one more rush than Rhamondre Stevenson in this shared backfield in Week 4 but converted his 14 carries into only 42 yards. Henderson has not been a factor in the passing game, catching just one ball on the season. Las Vegas is allowing 4.97 yards per carry and has been picked apart by Kenneth Walker and Omarion Hampton, so Henderson appears set up for an ideal opportunity at a few long runs even if the volume won't be high.
outlooksByWeek.6: TreVeyon Henderson is uncertain for Week 6 when the Patriots face the Jets due to an ankle injury. When healthy, he hasn't logged more than a 37% snap share in any of the last three games and has only two catches on the season. The Jets have not faced a prolific rushing offense through five games but have allowed two opposing backs to gain at least 99 yards. If active, a split role with Rhamondre Stevenson caps Henderson's appeal against a defense allowing a stingy 4.3 yards per carry.
outlooksByWeek.7: TreVeyon Henderson figures to handle a modest workload in the Patriots' Week 7 matchup against the Bears. Making a surprise appearance in Week 6 after suffering a high-ankle sprain, Henderson recorded seven carries for 31 yards while also catching his third pass of the season. Rhamondre Stevenson continues to garner a bigger workload but has plodded to a career-low 3.7 yards per carry. Until New England trusts Henderson in pass protection and ball security, however, a change in roles appears unlikely. Facing a Chicago defense on a short turnaround with Week 7's Thursday night kickoff, Henderson will need to solve a run defense that's allowed just three touchdowns to date.
outlooksByWeek.8: TreVeyon Henderson's declining role in the Patriots' rushing approach leads to low expectations in a Week 8 matchup against the Dolphins. He has logged single-digit carries in three straight games and sits with a 3.9 yards per carry average after a 5.1 mark as a rookie. He's also only caught four passes, an area where Miami has been particularly vulnerable against running backs. With New England seemingly happy to distribute the workload across multiple players, an uptick in usage for Henderson appears unlikely.
outlooksByWeek.9: TreVeyon Henderson will look to return from an illness that cost him Week 8 when the Patriots face the Packers in Week 9. Henderson has just 14 carries over his last three healthy games and has added only five catches all season. Always a big-play threat, Henderson doesn't appear to be in a spot to pop a long run against a Packers defense that's allowed only four runs of 20 or more yards through eight games.

player.seasonOutlook: Henderson enters Year 2 after a roller-coaster rookie campaign in which he delivered three huge fantasy performances (28-plus points in all three) but otherwise played second fiddle to Rhamondre Stevenson (8.3 points per game in his other 14 games). Though his role was limited, Henderson was effective, averaging 5.1 yards per carry (eighth best) and catching 83% of his targets while scoring 10 touchdowns. The 2025 second-round pick is a candidate for a similar role in 2026, but it's unlikely that Stevenson will completely disappear after he also had a strong 2025. Henderson is safest as a bench option, but there's upside for a lot more if the 23-year-old is promoted to a lead role.

Despite leading the league in turnovers generated (33), the Bears' defense finished a middling 16th in fantasy points last season. The team subsequently replaced Jaquan Brisker, Kevin Byard and Tremaine Edmunds with Devin Bush, Coby Bryant and Dillon Thieneman during the offseason, meaning this will probably again be a matchups-oriented unit. Consider the Bears for favorable early matchups against the Panthers (Week 1) and Jets (4).

outlooksByWeek.2: Josh Downs is hard to trust as anything more than a deep-league flex for the Colts' Week 2 trip to Kansas City. His four targets in the Week 1 loss to Baltimore tied for fourth on the team with Jonathan Taylor, as Daniel Jones threw more frequently to Alec Pierce, Keenan Allen and Tyler Warren. In 17 appearances since the start of last season, Downs is averaging a pedestrian 35.5 receiving yards per game in the Colts' run-heavy offense.
outlooksByWeek.3: Josh Downs is poised to work as the Colts' top wide receiver in Week 3 against the Texans, making him a solid WR3 or flex option in fantasy. Alec Pierce (heel) is expected to sit out, and the Colts lack viable alternatives, with over-the-hill veteran Keenan Allen and recent signing Darius Slayton representing the top options behind Downs in the wide receiver room. Downs caught seven of nine targets for 72 yards to lead the Colts in all three categories during the Week 2 loss to the Chiefs, which Pierce exited in the first half. Downs figures to see plenty of star Texans CB Derek Stingley, but the 25-year-old WR should get plenty of targets from Daniel Jones despite the tricky matchup.
outlooksByWeek.4: Josh Downs has exceeded 70 receiving yards in each of the Colts' last two games while racking up 20 targets over that span. With fellow Colts WR Alec Pierce (heel) on IR, Downs is a recommended Week 4 starting option since he is poised to see plenty of targets from Daniel Jones against a weak Washington secondary that has allowed the most catches (46) and touchdown receptions (six) to WRs, as well as the third-most receiving yards (573) to the position. Downs, TE Tyler Warren, and WR Keenan Allen accounted for 20 of Jones' 24 completed passes in Pierce's absence against the Texans in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.5: Josh Downs disappointed with 16 receiving yards against Washington's vulnerable secondary in Week 4 after notching at least 72 yards in each of the Colts' previous two games. Downs remains the de facto No. 1 WR for the Colts, as Alec Pierce (knee) is still on IR heading into a Week 5 road game at Pittsburgh. The Steelers are allowing 149 receiving yards per game to wideouts and traded starting CB Joey Porter to Dallas prior to Week 4. Downs is well-positioned to shake off his Week 4 dud and deliver as a solid Week 5 flex play.
outlooksByWeek.6: Josh Downs is averaging 50 receiving yards per game and has exceeded 70 twice through five games. However, the 25-year-old wideout has yet to score in his fourth NFL season after compiling 11 TDs across his first three years. He's the de facto No. 1 WR for the Colts in the continued absence of Alec Pierce (heel) heading into a Week 6 home game against the Titans. Tennessee has allowed a couple of big individual performances to wideouts, surrendering at least 117 yards and a TD to both Zay Flowers and DeVonta Smith. However, those are established No. 1 wideouts, putting them a cut above Downs, whose career average is just 46 yards per game. With the Colts likely to rely primarily on their ground game in Week 6, Downs is a decent flex play but far from an elite fantasy option.
outlooksByWeek.7: Josh Downs has been outplayed by Keenan Allen since the Colts lost Alec Pierce to a heel injury. After exceeding 70 receiving yards twice through Week 3, Downs has compiled a meager 103 receiving yards over the the past three games combined, topping out at 47 yards in a game over that span. His role as a locked-in starter at WR for the Colts makes Downs a viable Week 7 flex play against the Vikings, though he has now gone nine consecutive games without a TD dating back to last season. Minnesota is allowing 133 yards per game to WRs but has limited the position to three TDs in five games, so Downs looks unlikely to end his scoring drought.
outlooksByWeek.8: Josh Downs has opened his fourth season in Indianapolis on a seven-game touchdown drought, and he has reached the 50-yard threshold just twice this season, with the last such performance coming in Week 3. It has been Keenan Allen rather than Downs stepping up during the continued absence of Alec Pierce (heel), who remains on injured reserve. Despite his disappointing production so far, Downs leads the Colts with 46 targets and is a decent flex option for Week 8 against a Jaguars defense that's allowing a league-high 210 receiving yards per game to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Josh Downs scored his first TD of the season, accounting for the Colts' lone score in their 42-7 Week 8 loss to Jacksonville, but he fell short of 50 receiving yards for the fifth consecutive game. Downs continues to start in Indianapolis' low-octane passing game and has drawn at least four targets in every game. Ahead of a Week 9 home game against a Cowboys defense that's giving up 164.1 receiving yards and one TD per game to wide receivers, Downs' consistent involvement, coupled with Dallas' defensive struggles, makes him a viable fantasy WR3 or flex option for Week 9.

player.seasonOutlook: Downs has settled in as a serviceable slot receiver, which has helped him to finish in the 35-to-45 range among WRs in total fantasy points in each of his three NFL seasons. Downs peaked with a 72-803-5 receiving line in 2024, but took a step back in a crowded offense last season, and failed to deliver a single fantasy week better than 15th at the position. The undersized Downs isn't an option near the goal line, as he hasn't cleared five touchdowns or three end zone targets in a single season. The 25-year-old has a path to a slightly larger role in 2026 with Michael Pittman Jr. gone, leaving Alec Pierce, Tyler Warren and Keenan Allen as his primary target competition. Downs is a sleeper for flex production in PPR formats.

outlooksByWeek.2: Mark Andrews and the Ravens host the Saints and their defense, which ranks 13th in fantasy points allowed per game (11.3) to TEs, in Week 2. Andrews caught four of his six targets for 49 yards during Baltimore's 41-23 win in the season opener. He tied with Zay Flowers (hamstring) for the team lead in targets and finished second behind him in receptions. With Flowers and a host of other receivers dealing with injuries, Andrews could be in line for additional looks as a safety net for Lamar Jackson.
outlooksByWeek.3: Mark Andrews and the Ravens look to rebound from an upset defeat when they visit the Cowboys in Week 3. He caught six of seven targets for 49 yards during Baltimore's 24-17 Week 2 loss, making it two straight outings with exactly 49 receiving yards for the 31-year-old. Andrews draws a favorable matchup versus a Dallas defense that surrendered eight receptions for 78 yards and two TDs to Isaiah Likely in the season opener. The Cowboys rank 26th in fantasy points allowed (16.9) and are one of two teams with a catch rate of 100% to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Mark Andrews and the Ravens welcome the 0-3 Titans to town for a Week 4 showdown. After missing some time with a hand injury during Baltimore's 34-31 Week 3 win, Andrews returned and ultimately finished with three catches for 24 yards on five targets. He's still in search of his first TD of 2026, but he's been consistently involved on offense, totaling 18 targets across three contests. Andrews could find it difficult to break through in the scoring department against the Titans' third-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (7.4) to TEs, as they're one of nine teams yet to surrender a receiving touchdown to the position.
outlooksByWeek.5: Mark Andrews and the Ravens are on the road for the first time since the season opener to face the Falcons in Week 5. He corralled five of six targets for 27 yards and his first touchdown of the season in Baltimore's Week 4 win. Andrews has yet to top 50 yards receiving through four outings to date, and that trend could continue if Lamar Jackson (ankle) is unable to play on Sunday Night Football. The veteran tight end will aim to find paydirt for the second straight week against Atlanta's 21st-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (15.9) per game to the position.
outlooksByWeek.6: Mark Andrews and the Ravens are in Cleveland for an AFC North divisional clash in Week 6. He caught four of six targets for 28 yards and lost a fumble during Baltimore's overtime victory in Week 5. Andrews is averaging a solid six targets through five outings in 2026, but he's yet to top 50 receiving yards, only has one touchdown, and tallies 35.4 yards per contest. He'll look to break out versus a Browns defense that's tied for 19th in fantasy points allowed per game (15.0) to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Mark Andrews and the Ravens are back home to square off against the Bengals in Week 7. He caught one of three targets for four yards during Baltimore's 13-10 loss in Week 6. Andrews turned in his worst performance of the season on a day the Ravens tallied a meager 252 total yards of offense. Fellow tight end Josh Cuevas, a rookie fifth-round pick in 2026, recorded a 4-44-1 line on five targets, finishing second on the team in yardage while tying for second in receptions and targets. Andrews will look to rebound versus Cincinnati's 25th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (16.2) to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Mark Andrews and the Ravens travel to face the Bills in Week 8. He caught three of four targets for 23 yards during Baltimore's 35-13 defeat in Week 7. Andrews was unable to take advantage of game flow, as Tyler Huntley attempted 34 passes and threw for a career-high 298 yards. Andrews has failed to top 30 receiving yards in five straight outings, making him a tough start in fantasy despite the potential return of Lamar Jackson (ankle).
outlooksByWeek.9: Mark Andrews and the Ravens host the Jaguars for an AFC showdown in Week 9. He caught three of four targets for 14 yards during Baltimore's 36-10 Week 8 defeat. Andrews finished second on the team in receptions and third in targets, but the entire Ravens offense struggled with Lamar Jackson (thumb/IR) and Tyler Huntley (toe) both forced out with injuries. Andrews has compiled an underwhelming 29-218-1 receiving line on 41 targets through seven games this season. Fantasy managers should look elsewhere, with the 31-year-old squaring off against Jacksonville's eighth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (11.0) to TEs.

player.seasonOutlook: One of fantasy's biggest mysteries, Andrews' usage has dipped substantially over the past two seasons. After finishing in the top five in fantasy PPG five seasons in a row from 2019 to 2023, Andrews slipped to eighth in 2024 (it would've been much worse if not for 11 touchdowns on 68 targets) and fell even further to 24th last season. Andrews appeared in all 17 of Baltimore's games but ranked 18th among tight ends in targets and outside the top 20 in catches and yards. The combination of a new coaching staff, a healthy Lamar Jackson and the departure of Isaiah Likely could lead to a rebound season for Andrews, but we now have two straight seasons of underperformance. The 31-year-old remains a force near the goal line (top 10 in end zone targets seven years in a row), but he's now more of a fringe TE1 than a fantasy star.

outlooksByWeek.2: Khalil Shakir will look to remain Josh Allen's security blanket in Week 2 when the Bills host the Lions. Shakir managed four grabs on six targets to open the season, finishing with 50 yards. He operated underneath while newly acquired DJ Moore stretched the field. The Lions' vulnerable secondary gave up 410 yards passing in Week 1, but Shakir will likely be limited by shorter routes, creating a safe but uninspiring fantasy option.
outlooksByWeek.3: Khalil Shakir remains a steady, stable cog in Buffalo's passing game entering a Week 3 matchup with the Chargers. Shakir logged six targets in each of the Bills' first two games but hasn't topped 50 yards or scored. Shakir didn't take on an elevated role in Week 2 following DJ Moore's (shoulder) early exit, but he faces a secondary that allowed 75 yards to Kendrick Bourne and 119 yards to Tre Tucker, and both operate in a similar slot role to Shakir.
outlooksByWeek.4: Khalil Shakir seeks more opportunities in Week 4 when the Bills face the Patriots. Despite a season-high 71% snap share in Week 3, Shakir had his lowest output of 2026, catching just a six-yard pass on three targets in a game where Josh Allen struggled. Shakir could benefit from additional looks in Week 4 if DJ Moore is matched up consistently with CB Christian Gonzalez. Operating primarily out of the slot tempers high yardage totals.
outlooksByWeek.5: Khalil Shakir maintains a steady role out of the slot for Buffalo as they prepare to face the Rams in Week 5. Shakir is coming off a season-high 82 yards in Week 4, his third game with at least six targets. His workload is independent of DJ Moore's shoulder status. Shakir will either garner more targets if Moore is out, or benefit from the attention Moore usually draws. However, the Rams defense hasn't allowed an opposing receiver to top 50 yards, suggesting Shakir is a risky floor and limited ceiling option.
outlooksByWeek.6: Khalil Shakir continues to play a minimal role in the Bills' passing game as they enter a Week 6 matchup with the Raiders. Shakir had just three targets in Week 5, the second time he's experienced that limited volume in three weeks despite the continued absence of DJ Moore (shoulder). Shakir is averaging a career-best 14.2 yards per catch and with Las Vegas proving vulnerable over the middle (nine catches, 122 yards, two touchdowns last week to DeMario Douglas and Efton Chism), Shakir could exploit a favorable matchup despite a lack of heavy volume.
outlooksByWeek.8: Khalil Shakir will reprise his slot role in Week 8 when the Bills host the Ravens. Shakir hasn't directly benefited from DJ Moore's (shoulder) absence, with a largely unchanged role prior to Buffalo's Week 7 bye, logging six or more targets in four of six contests. While he's topped four catches just once, he's averaging 13.2 yards per catch, his highest mark since 2023. Baltimore's secondary has been more vulnerable to larger, outside X receivers, with Drake London, Tee Higgins, and Carnell Tate all topping 100 yards against them. Shakir will need to continue to take advantage of his opportunities to be a viable fantasy option.
outlooksByWeek.9: Khalil Shakir continues to provide stability in Buffalo's passing game ahead of a Week 9 matchup with the Vikings. Shakir has recorded at least six targets in five of seven outings, going for 50 or more yards four times. It's a modest floor with only one touchdown catch, and it's even lower facing a Minnesota defense that's allowing the third-fewest fantasy points to opposing receivers, including just four touchdowns in seven games.

player.seasonOutlook: Shakir has settled in as a reliable, short-range target for Josh Allen, though the role hasn't led to much fantasy success. The 2022 fifth-round pick has cleared a 20% target share and 70 catches in consecutive seasons, ranking top five among receivers in catch rate and RAC both years. A nonfactor near the goal line, however, Shakir totaled eight TDs and five end zone targets during the span. Shakir finished the two seasons just outside of the top 35 fantasy receivers and will now have to compete with DJ Moore for the team lead in targets. Shakir was already barely worth flex consideration, so the potential for a slight decrease in target volume suggests the 26-year-old is no more than a low-ceiling bench option.

outlooksByWeek.2: Devaughn Vele is expected to remain an important part of the Saints' offense in the Week 2 matchup against the Ravens. Vele saw nine targets in the Week 1 overtime loss, tying his career high and trailing only Chris Olave in the Saints' receiving corps. Vele should continue to benefit from the absence of Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) and is expected to see consistent volume until Tyson returns. It'll be a tough Week 2 matchup for Vele, however, as the Ravens' defense has given up just 4.8 yards per pass attempt this season, which is tied for the second-best mark in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.3: Devaughn Vele is expected to remain the Saints' No. 2 wideout in the Week 3 matchup against the Raiders, whose defense has given up just 15 receptions to WRs through two contests. Vele has clearly positioned himself as one of New Orleans' top receiving options early in the season, catching 12 of 16 targets for 133 yards and one touchdown thus far. He's expected to continue benefitting from the Saints' high volume of pass attempts, as Tyler Shough has already thrown the ball 90 times in two games, the second-most in the NFL. Despite this, Vele is in for a difficult Week 3 matchup against a Las Vegas defense that has yet to allow a receiving touchdown this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Devaughn Vele is likely to remain the Saints' second option at wideout in the Week 4 matchup against the Falcons. While Jordan Tyson (hamstring) has been sidelined, Vele has been very fantasy-relevant, catching 15 of 22 targets for 172 yards and a touchdown (12.7 PPR points per game). Vele has almost no competition outside of Chris Olave in the Saints' WR room, which bodes well for his fantasy outlook going forward. Additionally, New Orleans' offense is averaging 44 pass attempts per game, which suggests Vele will continue having scoring opportunities. He's in for a favorable Week 4 matchup, as Atlanta's defense has allowed 604 receiving yards to wideouts this season, the most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Devaughn Vele is expected to remain very involved in the Saints' offensive game plan in the Week 5 matchup against the Vikings. Vele has been targeted 30 times (second-most on the team) through New Orleans' first four contests this season, logging 226 receiving yards and a pair of touchdowns. With Tyler Shough averaging a whopping 45 pass attempts per game this season, Vele will likely remain a solid fantasy option as the year progresses, at least until the return of Jordyn Tyson (hamstring, IR). However, Vele is in for a difficult Week 5 matchup against a Minnesota defense that's allowed just 7.7 yards per target to opposing WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Devaughn Vele is expected to remain one of the Saints' top receiving options in the Week 6 matchup against the Giants. Vele was quiet in the Week 5 loss to the Vikings, catching four of six targets for just 26 yards. He still ranks second on the Saints in targets (36) and receiving yards (252) through five contests, which is a positive sign for his outlook moving forward. Vele could thrive in Week 6 against a Giants defense that's already allowed five touchdowns to opposing WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Devaughn Vele is expected to remain New Orleans' No. 2 wideout in the Week 7 matchup against the Steelers. Vele has been relatively quiet over the last two weeks, catching seven of 12 targets for 68 yards. Despite this, he's played over 90% of the Saints' offensive snaps in the last two contests, suggesting more fantasy production is coming soon, especially if New Orleans continues throwing the ball at such a high clip (39.2 pass attempts per game -- fourth-most in the NFL). Vele could struggle against a strong Steelers defense in Week 7 though, as they've allowed just 6.1 yards per pass attempt this season.
outlooksByWeek.9: Devaughn Vele is expected to remain the Saints' No. 2 wideout in the Week 9 matchup against the Browns. Vele has recorded over 50 receiving yards in four of seven appearances this season, ranking second on the team in yards (348), targets (46) and receptions (33). He's expected to continue benefitting from head coach Kellen Moore's high-volume passing attack, as Tyler Shough currently leads the NFL with 39.0 pass attempts per game. Vele could struggle in Week 9, however, as Cleveland's secondary has allowed just 10.1 yards per completion this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Vele is expected to open the season as New Orleans' No. 2 receiver behind Chris Olave until Jordyn Tyson returns from injury near midseason. Vele's first season with the Saints was marred with injuries. The 2024 seventh-round pick, who posted a 41-475-3 receiving line with Denver as a rookie, barely played throughout most of 2025 prior to taking on an every-down role during Weeks 10-15. In those five games (one of which he left hurt), he averaged 5.6 targets per game, but reached 12.0 fantasy points once (an 8-93-1 effort in Week 13 against Miami). The 28-year-old has yet to show he can be relied on for consistent targets and fantasy production, but he'll play an every-down role early on, which makes him a sleeper for flex value in deep leagues. He'll be worth a roster spot until Tyson returns.

outlooksByWeek.2: Omar Cooper is uncertain to play for the Jets in Week 2 against the Packers due to an ankle sprain. In his NFL debut, he caught his only target for 30 yards. The Jets ran a heavy ground game to open the year, and while they will likely need to throw more in Week 2 to keep up, Cooper's role, even if healthy, is uncertain. The passing game should continue to flow heavily through Garrett Wilson, leaving Cooper's fantasy value volatile.
outlooksByWeek.7: Omar Cooper brings momentum into the Jets' Week 7 matchup with the Dolphins. Returning from a four-week absence due to an ankle issue, Cooper flashed with 103 yards and a touchdown on seven targets. The Jets remain a low-volume passing attack, and Miami has allowed the second-fewest fantasy points to opposing wide receivers, but Cooper provides a big-play option, averaging 19.0 yards per catch in limited action. He could offer a high-upside bye-week fill-in.
outlooksByWeek.8: Omar Cooper's two-week surge is set to extend into Week 8 when the Jets have an inviting matchup with the Raiders. Cooper has topped 100 yards and scored in consecutive outings since returning from an ankle injury, while snagging 11 of his 12 targets. The volume remains modest in a run-first offense, but Las Vegas is allowing 8.9 yards per target to opposing wide receivers with seven similar players registering at least 53 receiving yards.
outlooksByWeek.9: Omar Cooper will look for consistent chances when the Jets face the Chiefs in Week 9. After consecutive 100-yard outings, Cooper failed to collect a target despite a 79% snap share in Week 8, with Adonai Mitchell and Garrett Wilson dominating opportunities. Despite a banged-up secondary in Week 8, Kansas City is allowing the second-fewest fantasy points to opposing wideouts, which includes just two touchdown catches. The Jets' offense could be forced to throw more frequently from behind, but the passing game isn't strong enough to support multiple receivers on a regular basis.

player.seasonOutlook: Cooper was selected by the Jets in the first round of April's draft. The Indiana product is fresh off a breakout 2025 season in which he posted a 69-937-13 receiving line after totaling 46 catches during his first three seasons with the Hoosiers. Primarily a perimeter target in limited action from 2022 to 2024, Cooper aligned in the slot on 80% of his routes last season. He is a short-area target (9.0 aDOT last season), but still posted strong efficiency numbers, including a 2.61 YPRR. He'll begin his career behind Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell in New York's Geno Smith-led offense and is unlikely to produce consistent flex value as a rookie.

outlooksByWeek.2: DeMario Douglas will seek more production in Week 2 when the Patriots face the Steelers. He logged a reasonable seven targets to open the season but turned that into just 20 yards on five grabs. Douglas has a rapport with QB Drake Maye as a safety valve, and while snaps seem safe with A.J. Brown (ankle) sidelined for the foreseeable future, Douglas topped 40 yards just four times last season.
outlooksByWeek.3: DeMario Douglas' role in New England's struggling passing offense is questionable ahead of a Week 3 game at Jacksonville. In Week 2, Douglas logged just two targets in his first full game without A.J. Brown after a seven-target opener, and he's averaging just 4.8 yards per reception to start the season. Jacksonville is allowing a hefty 10.3 yards per target to opposing wideouts, but Douglas' inability to stretch the field would require uncharacteristic heavy volume to provide a modest fantasy return.
outlooksByWeek.4: DeMario Douglas hasn't been consistently targeted in the Patriots struggling passing attack ahead of a Week 4 matchup with the Bills. Douglas has just one catch in each of his last two games, and while last week's popped for 38 yards, he's averaging just 9.4 yards on his seven snags to date. Buffalo's defense has been friendly to opposing wideouts, allowing 9.3 ypt with six receivers going for 40+ yards, but with limited volume, Douglas doesn't seem destined to exploit that.
outlooksByWeek.5: DeMario Douglas hasn't emerged in the Patriots' receiving corps ahead of a Week 5 matchup against the Raiders. Despite A.J. Brown's continued absence, Douglas has just four total catches over the last three weeks, tallying 62 yards. An uptick in volume appears unlikely against an exploitable secondary that allows 8.2 yards per target, leaving Douglas as a dart throw as opposed to a reliable lineup option.
outlooksByWeek.6: DeMario Douglas faces an uphill battle to match Week 5's success when the Patriots face the Jets in Week 6. Douglas shined with two touchdowns and a season-high 65 yards against the Raiders, but he's still hauled in no more than two balls in three of five outings while being held to 38 yards or fewer in his first four games. New England is spreading the ball around in its surging passing attack, so Douglas seems unlikely to retain heavy volume. The Jets have allowed four opposing receivers to register 63 yards or more in the last two weeks, giving Douglas a shot at some upside.
outlooksByWeek.7: DeMario Douglas is emerging as a viable option for the Patriots ahead of a Week 7 matchup with the Bears. Over the past two weeks, Douglas has garnered 13 targets, turning them into 11 catches and three touchdowns. Though A.J. Brown is back from an ankle injury, New England could be without Romeo Doubs due to a shoulder ailment, suggesting Douglas' place in the receiving pecking order may be unchanged, giving him a chance to post solid numbers against a secondary that's allowed nine opposing receivers to gain at least 55 yards.
outlooksByWeek.8: DeMario Douglas will seek a rebound in Week 8 when New England travels to Miami. He was on a two-game heater entering Week 7, but finished with just three catches for 23 yards and has been held to 38 yards or fewer in five of seven outings. Miami is allowing an attractive 8.8 yards per target, the eighth-highest total league-wide, but because of vulnerabilities to tight ends and running backs in the passing game, opposing wideouts have the second-fewest yards, suggesting it may be better to look elsewhere for meaningful production.
outlooksByWeek.9: DeMario Douglas' volume has been sporadic despite the Patriots' receiving corps rarely being at full strength entering a Week 9 matchup with the Packers. Douglas has four touchdowns over his last four games, but he has four or fewer targets in half of New England's eight games, failing to top 23 yards at the same rate. Green Bay is allowing just 7.0 yards per target to wideouts, suggesting Douglas would need to maintain his scoring prowess to be a viable Week 9 option.

outlooksByWeek.2: Makai Lemon was listed as the No. 3 wideout for the Eagles heading into their Week 1 clash with Washington. Unfortunately, Lemon lost five yards on three catches in his NFL debut.  On the bright side, he was targeted four times and was one of only three Eagles receivers to record a catch. Better outputs lie ahead, perhaps as early as Week 2 versus Tennessee.  The Titans surrendered 215 yards passing to Geno Smith of the Jets in their opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Makai Lemon had just one catch in Philadelphia's win over Tennessee. Lemon is battling with Darius Cooper for the No. 3 wideout spot, as Dontayvion Wicks has all but claimed No. 2 for his own. Lemon had just one target last game, while Cooper had three and Wicks managed six. In Week 3, Philadelphia will face a Bears defense allowing 240 passing yards per tilt thus far this season, which is 25th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Makai Lemon is coming off his best game as a member of the Eagles.  Unfortunately, the output was rather pedestrian, as Lemon managed three catches and 29 yards on four targets in the ugly 27-7 loss to the Bears. Lemon has yet to find the end zone as a rookie. In Week 4, he will face a rather stingy Rams pass defense allowing just 171.3 yards per game through the air, which is fourth in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Makai Lemon saw a career-high six targets last game for the Eagles. With DeVonta Smith shelved due to a hamstring ailment, Lemon finished with the second-most targets on the team behind Darius Cooper.  However, the Philadelphia passing game struggled mightily overall, with no wideout gaining more than 33 yards through the air. While Smith should remain sidelined for Week 5, it remains to be seen how the targets will be divided between Lemon, Cooper and Dontayvion Wicks. Nevertheless, an intriguing matchup lurks in Week 5 against the Jags. Jacksonville has surrendered 280.3 passing yards per game this season, which is second-to-last in the league. In an odd twist, though, the Jags have yielded just three passing scores, which is tied for first in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Makai Lemon set career highs across the board last game for the Eagles. Lemon was targeted seven times en route to five catches for 43 yards in the 19-17 loss to the Jags. Lemon has 13 targets in his last two outings. The continued absence of DeVonta Smith with a hamstring injury has boosted the opportunities for Lemon, a trend that could continue in Week 6 versus Carolina. In addition, the Panthers are allowing 230.8 passing yards per tilt, which is 22nd in the league.
outlooksByWeek.7: Makai Lemon caught three passes for 19 yards last game for the Eagles. Lemon was third on the team in targets with six, though the return of DeVonta Smith to the lineup may have limited his production overall. Tanner McKee should start at quarterback for the foreseeable future, which could cap Lemon's upside as well.  In Week 7, the Eagles will face a Dallas defense that has struggled to defend the pass in 2026. The Cowboys are allowing 232.7 passing yards per game, which is 23rd in the NFL. In addition, Dallas has surrendered 11 passing touchdowns, which is tied for 24th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.8: Makai Lemon set career highs across the board last game for the Eagles. With both DeVonta Smith as well as Dontayvion Wicks sidelined due to injury, Lemon snagged seven passes for 67 yards and his first NFL touchdown. He was targeted eight times in the contest. If Smith and/or Wicks are unable to suit up in Week 8 versus the Commanders, Lemon could have a delicious matchup, even with backup quarterback Tanner McKee under center. Washington is allowing 254 passing yards per game, which is 28th in the NFL. In addition, the Commanders have surrendered 15 passing scores, which is tied for 28th in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Lemon was selected by the Eagles with the 20th overall pick of April's draft. Lemon is on the small side (5-foot-11, 192 pounds), but he posted a 3.04 YPRR (best in this rookie class) during his collegiate career, dropping only three of 190 career targets (his 1.6% drop rate also paced this class). Lemon, who aligned in the slot on 74% of his collegiate routes, posted a dominant 79-1,156-11 receiving line in 2025, while also contributing as a rusher (two TDs) and returner. With A.J. Brown now in New England, Lemon will battle Dontayvion Wicks for No. 2 work opposite DeVonta Smith. Lemon's skill set provides him with upside, but with plenty of mouths to feed in Philly's low-volume pass offense, he's best valued as a flex option in 2026.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kyler Murray's status is up in the air as the Vikings travel to Chicago in Week 2. Murray went down early in Week 1 against the Packers after taking a hard hit to the head. Before his exit, Murray completed three of five passes for 18 yards and one interception, tacking on two rushes for nine yards on the ground. The veteran is now under evaluation for a concussion, which could very likely keep him sidelined for an extended period. Backup quarterback Carson Wentz delivered the win for Minnesota, and he's set to assume QB duties once again. The Bears gave up 361 passing yards, three touchdowns and one interception to Bryce Young in Week 1, so big output could definitely be in the cards for whoever lines up under center for the Vikings.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kyler Murray will return to the field as the Vikings travel to Tampa Bay in Week 3. Murray has cleared concussion protocol after suffering a nasty hit early in Week 1. The veteran quarterback will finally get the chance to prove himself, especially given that he completed just three of five passes for 18 yards and one interception before his opening-game departure. He'll face a Bucs defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 20.4 fantasy points per game to QBs across its first two games.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kyler Murray will aim to build on a serviceable performance as the Vikings play the Dolphins in Week 4. Murray returned to the field in Week 3 versus the Buccaneers, completing 15 of 29 passes for 168 yards with a 1:1 TD:INT ratio, along with rushing the ball twice for 17 yards. The veteran quarterback also lost star wideout Justin Jefferson in the first half, so his final output and delivery of a win were more impressive. Miami has been much more favorable against quarterbacks than Tampa so far this season, allowing the seventh-most fantasy points per game (23.7) to the position.
outlooksByWeek.5: Kyler Murray will look to do more as the Vikings travel to New Orleans in Week 5. In his second full start of the year, Murray completed 27 of 37 passes for 247 yards, but he was unable to find the end zone. The veteran quarterback also now holds a 1:2 TD:INT through his three appearances this season, so he'll need to do more for Minnesota to lock him down as a long-term option. The Saints have ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy quarterbacks this season.
