outlooksByWeek.7: Kyler Murray will look to keep the Vikings rolling in Week 7 against the Colts. Murray recorded his best game of the season against the Saints heading into Minnesota's bye, completing 80 percent of passes for 229 yards and a touchdown, with 10 rushes for 51 yards. The veteran quarterback could be a dangerous threat moving forward, especially if he can get it going on the ground once again. He'll face an Indy defense that's ranked 21st in fantasy points allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Kyler Murray will look to do more as the Vikings play the Lions in Week 8. Murray completed 14 of 24 passes for 150 yards and a touchdown, with five carries for 39 yards in a Week 7 win over the Colts. The veteran has yet to lose a game this year, but his output has been quite low compared to that of usual winning quarterbacks. He'll luckily face a Detroit defense that's allowed the most fantasy points per game to QBs so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.9: Kyler Murray will look to get healed ahead of Minnesota's Week 9 matchup against Buffalo. Murray completed 17 of 29 passes for 210 yards with two touchdowns and one interception, along with four rushes for 35 yards in a Week 8 loss to Detroit. The veteran was also dealing with hamstring tightness throughout the game, but a full week of practice should mitigate the injury. Barring any major setbacks, Murray will face a Bills defense that's ranked a favorable 28th in fantasy points allowed to quarterbacks.

player.seasonOutlook: Murray signed with the Vikings after spending his first seven seasons with the Cardinals. The change comes after a disappointing and injury-shortened 2025 season in which he failed to clear 18.3 fantasy points in any of his five appearances. Murray has settled in as an accurate but conservative passer and continues to add value with his legs (78-572-5 in 17 games in 2024). Prior to the 2025 dud, Murray had finished each of his first six NFL seasons as a top-12 fantasy QB (points per game). Now that he beat out J.J. McCarthy for Minnesota's starting job, he'll have the luxury of working with Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison and T.J. Hockenson. Add that to his rushing ability, and the 29-year-old certainly could find his way into the weekly QB1 mix. Consider Murray in the middle to late rounds.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jake Bates will aim to stay perfect as the Lions travel to Buffalo in Week 2. Bates nailed his only field-goal attempt and all four extra points against the Saints in Week 1. The third-year player led all NFL kickers in PATs last season in Detroit's high-powered offense, so he'll hopefully stay on the field plenty in the coming weeks. Given that the Bills' defense should provide more problems for the Lions, Bates could also get more field-goal shots in what could be a tough away matchup.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jake Bates will seek to stay perfect as the Lions play the Jets in Week 3. Bates has now drilled both of his two field-goal attempts and all eight of his PATs this season. The third-year kicker hasn't been on the field for many field goals this season, and Detroit playing from behind doesn't help his case. Luckily, the team's current high volume of touchdowns has kept Bates relevant. He'll face a New York squad that's allowed 6.0 points per game to kickers across two games, a top-10 mark.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jake Bates will look to stay perfect as the Lions play the Panthers in Week 4. Bates nailed his sole extra-point attempt and all four of his XPAs in Week 3 against the Jets. The third-year boot has now converted all three of his field-goal kicks and each of his 12 extra-point tries. While the field-goal volume isn't quite there, Detroit's ability to score keeps Bates on the field and scoring. Carolina has allowed a middle-of-the-pack 7.0 points per game to kickers this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jake Bates will aim to stay perfect as the Lions play the Cardinals in Week 5. Bates logged his best game of the season in Week 4 against the Panthers, nailing all four of his field-goal attempts and converting two XPAs. The second-year kicker has now gone a perfect 21-for-21 on boots (seven field goals, 14 extra points) this season. He'll face an Arizona defense that's ranked top 10 against fantasy kickers.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jake Bates will look to stay hot as the Lions play the Packers in Week 7. Bates has yet to miss a kick this season, nailing eight field-goal attempts and converting all 20 of his XPAs across five games. While the field-goal usage hasn't quite been there, the touchdown-scoring ability of Detroit's offense has kept Bates on the field. He'll face a Green Bay squad that's allowed the fewest fantasy points per game (4.2) to kickers this season.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jake Bates will aim to stay perfect as the Lions play the Vikings in Week 8. Bates nailed both of his two extra-point tries and two field-goal attempts including a game winner in Week 7 against the Packers. The third-year kicker has yet to miss a kick this season, making 10 field goals and 22 XPAs. He'll face a Minnesota team that's ranked fourth in fantasy points per game allowed to kickers (5.3).
outlooksByWeek.9: Jake Bates will look to stay solid as the Lions play the Dolphins in Week 9. Bates missed his first kick of the season in a Week 8 win over Minnesota, but he still converted two of three field goals and nailed his sole XPA. The second-year kicker has now gone 12-for-13 on field goal attempts and made all 23 of his extra-point tries across seven outings. The Dolphins have ranked in the middle against fantasy kickers this campaign.

outlooksByWeek.2: Chris Godwin is expected to remain one of the Buccaneers' top receiving options in the Week 2 matchup against the Browns. The 30-year-old was Tampa Bay's second-most productive wideout in the Week 1 loss, hauling in all four of his targets for 40 yards. Godwin likely won't have many big plays after sustaining multiple serious lower-body injuries throughout his career, but he should remain a reliable PPR option and an important part of the Buccaneers' offense moving forward. Additionally, he's in for a great Week 2 matchup, as the Browns defense allowed 13.6 yards per target to WRs in Week 1, the second-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chris Godwin will look to bounce back from a slow start in the Buccaneers' Week 3 matchup against the Vikings. Godwin leads Tampa Bay's receiving corps in offensive snaps played (101) and has caught all seven of his targets through two weeks. However, this hasn't translated to much production, as he's accumulated just 86 receiving yards. Expect Godwin to remain one of the Buccaneers' most reliable targets in a difficult matchup against a Vikings defense that's given up just 27 receptions to wideouts through two games.
outlooksByWeek.4: Chris Godwin is expected to remain one of the Buccaneers' most reliable targets in the Week 4 matchup against the Packers. Godwin had a quiet Week 3 performance (3-25-0), though he had an 85-yard touchdown reception called back for holding. The veteran wideout has struggled along with the rest of Tampa Bay's offense, and those struggles could be amplified with Baker Mayfield (thumb) sidelined for the Week 4 contest. However, Godwin is in for a favorable matchup against a Packers defense that's allowed 6.7 yards per pass attempt this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Chris Godwin is expected to remain one of the Buccaneers' top weapons in the Week 5 matchup against the Cowboys. Godwin was targeted a season-high seven times in the Week 4 loss to the Packers, catching six of them for just 31 yards. The veteran wideout may actually benefit from Jalon Daniels acting as Tampa Bay's starting quarterback while Baker Mayfield (thumb) is sidelined, as Godwin could act as the rookie's safety blanket. Additionally, Godwin is in for a good Week 5 matchup against a Dallas defense that's allowed five receiving touchdowns to WRs through four contests this year.
outlooksByWeek.6: Chris Godwin is expected to remain Tampa Bay's top safety blanket in the Week 6 matchup against the Steelers. Godwin has caught 19 of 22 targets this season, totaling 179 yards. Despite ranking second on the Buccaneers in receptions and third in targets, he's gotten just one red-zone target all season and could struggle finding fantasy relevance without a touchdown. Regardless, Godwin is in for a tough Week 6 matchup against a Steelers defense that's given up 220.8 passing yards per game this year.
outlooksByWeek.7: Chris Godwin is expected to remain one of the Buccaneers' top receiving options in the Week 7 matchup against the Panthers. Godwin was targeted a season-high eight times during the Week 6 loss to the Steelers, recording four receptions for 37 yards. The veteran wideout ranks second on Tampa Bay in targets (30), receptions (23) and yards (216) through the first six games and could benefit from the potential return of Baker Mayfield (thumb) in Week 7. However, Godwin is in for a tough matchup against a Panthers secondary that's allowed just 5.9 yards per pass attempt this season.
outlooksByWeek.8: Chris Godwin is expected to remain one of Tampa Bay's top wideouts in the Week 8 matchup against the Falcons. Godwin was the Buccaneers' second-leading receiver in the Week 7 win over the Panthers, catching four of five targets for 27 yards. After Emeka Egbuka (concussion/foot) was sidelined last week, Godwin now leads Tampa Bay in receiving yards (243) through seven games. Godwin could remain successful in Week 8 against a Falcons defense that's allowed 8.0 yards per target to opposing wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.9: Chris Godwin will look to bounce back from a lackluster Week 8 performance when the Buccaneers face the Bears in Week 9. He struggled along with the rest of Tampa Bay's receiving corps in last week's rainy win over the Falcons, as Baker Mayfield completed no passes. If Emeka Egbuka (foot) misses his third consecutive game in Week 9, Godwin would operate as Tampa Bay's top wideout. Even so, the Buccaneers have attempted just 14 passes over the last two weeks, so Godwin's fantasy production is capped by the team's limited passing volume. Nonetheless, Godwin could find success against a Chicago secondary that's given up 9.5 yards per target to opposing wideouts through seven games this year.

player.seasonOutlook: Godwin is on the comeback trail after injuries have limited him to 16 games during the past two seasons. In 2025, he appeared in nine games and reached 11 fantasy points only twice. It seems like a long time ago, Godwin was second among receivers in fantasy points in 2024 when he suffered a severe ankle injury. He wasn't nearly as effective when he was on the field last season, but he's now more than a full year recovered from the injury and has less target competition with Mike Evans no longer on the roster. Entering his age-30 season, Godwin's days as a fantasy WR1 may be over, but with Emeka Egbuka as his only competition to lead the team in targets, he certainly has a path to flex numbers.

outlooksByWeek.2: Chris Boswell and the Steelers are on the road to face the Patriots in Week 2. He finished Pittsburgh's 20-13 Week 1 win versus the Falcons 2-for-3 on field-goal attempts and 2-for-2 on PATs. Boswell's first miss of the season was from 56 yards out, but he was able to connect from 43 and 28 yards. The Steelers have several talented players on offense, but until they prove they can consistently put up 24-28 points a week, Boswell may not generate enough scoring opportunities to warrant a roster spot.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chris Boswell and the Steelers host the Bengals in Week 3. The 12th-year kicker went 1-for-2 on field-goal attempts during Pittsburgh's 20-3 loss to New England. Both of Boswell's attempts came from 50-plus yards out, and he's now 1-for-3 from that distance and 3-for-5 overall through two outings in 2026. He'll look to get back on track this Sunday versus a Cincinnati defense allowing 16.5 points per game, tied for eighth.
outlooksByWeek.4: Chris Boswell and the Steelers visit the division-rival Browns in Week 4. He made all three of his field-goal attempts and went 3-for-3 on PATs during Pittsburgh's 30-27 win in Week 3. It was Boswell's first perfect outing through three games, and his 33-yard kick just before the two-minute warning gave the Steelers the lead for good. He'll look to stay hot against Cleveland's 18th-ranked scoring defense, which is allowing 23.7 points per game thus far in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.5: Chris Boswell and the Steelers return home to take on the Colts in Week 5. He finished Pittsburgh's 27-24 loss in Week 4 converting one of two field-goal attempts while connecting on his lone extra-point try. Boswell's miss came from 48 yards out, and he's now 1-for-4 on kicks equal to or longer than that across four games in 2026. He'll aim to bounce back versus an Indianapolis defense giving up 26.0 points per contest, which ranks 21st in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Chris Boswell and the Steelers are on the road to battle the Buccaneers in Week 6. He connected on both of his field-goal attempts and went 4-for-4 on extra-point tries during Pittsburgh's 34-22 victory in Week 5. Over his last three outings, Boswell is 6-for-7 on field goals while making all eight of his PATs. He's on the fantasy radar with the recent strong performances by the Steelers offense, as they've averaged 29.3 points during this three-game stretch. Boswell will try to make an impact against a Tampa Bay defense allowing 22.4 points per game in 2026, but just 15.0 PPG over their previous two.
outlooksByWeek.7: Chris Boswell and the Steelers are in Paris for a Week 7 clash against the Saints. He converted four of five field-goal attempts, including a season-long 58-yarder, and both of his PATs during Pittsburgh's 26-19 overtime win in Week 6. Boswell missed his first kick from 48 yards out, but he made up for it by making four in a row, with three of those makes coming in the fourth quarter to help send the game to OT. He'll get another chance to make an impact versus a New Orleans defense that allows 29.7 points per game, which is tied for the most in the NFL in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.8: Chris Boswell and the Steelers play host to the division rival Browns in Week 8. He went 3-for-3 on field goals and converted his lone PAT during Pittsburgh's 16-10 victory over the Saints in Paris. Boswell is looking to avenge his underwhelming performance against Cleveland in Week 4, as the 35-year-old missed one of two FGAs in the 27-24 defeat. Since then, Boswell is 9-for-10 on FGs and 7-for-7 on extra points. He'll try to keep rolling versus a Browns defense allowing 20.9 points per game, the 12th-fewest in the league.

outlooksByWeek.2: Alec Pierce led the Colts with 61 receiving yards in the season opener despite battling a heel injury heading into the game. In addition, he left during the first half to get X-rays on his hand and wrist after hitting a defender's helmet. His practice participation is likely to be affected by those injuries, but Pierce is seemingly on track to suit up in Week 2 against the Chiefs and can be viewed as a solid WR3 or flex option. He brings big-play ability to an otherwise underwhelming Colts passing game, averaging at least 21.3 yards per catch in each of the past two seasons and leading the team with 1,003 receiving yards in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Alec Pierce aggravated a left heel injury in Week 2, stemming from his offseason left ankle surgery. The Colts' leading receiver from last season probably faces a multi-week absence and won't play against the Texans in Week 3. Josh Downs and Keenan Allen are set to lead Indianapolis' underwhelming WR room versus Houston.

player.seasonOutlook: Pierce has spent the majority of his first four NFL seasons as a situational deep threat, but that didn't stop him from becoming one of the league's highest-paid wide receivers during the offseason. The 2022 second-round pick is fresh off a career year and he's now paced all receivers in YPR, YPT and aDOT each of the last two seasons. However, he's yet to finish a season better than 48th at WR in target share (18%), 42nd in targets (84), 45th in catches (47), 18th in yards (1,003), 18th in TDs (seven) or 25th in fantasy PPG. Of course, with Michael Pittman Jr. no longer in the mix, Pierce is a good bet for a more well-rounded role as Daniel Jones' top target. There's some risk here, but the 26-year-old's hefty contract suggests we should take him seriously as a fantasy WR3.

outlooksByWeek.2: Romeo Doubs will seek a larger role in the Patriots' passing game in Week 2 against the Steelers. Doubs failed to record a catch on three targets in his team debut, playing only 56% of the snaps despite New England losing A.J. Brown to a high-ankle sprain. With Brown set to miss significant time, Doubs should garner more opportunities, but it looks as though he's still developing chemistry with Drake Maye. Questions remain regarding the Steelers' secondary, which is likely to remain without Joey Porter Jr. They weren't tested last week, but counting on a breakthrough from Doubs is risky.
outlooksByWeek.3: Romeo Doubs will look to build on Week 2's uptick in workload in the Patriots offense when they face the Jaguars in Week 3. After not catching a pass in his Week 1 debut, Doubs snagged three of four targets for a team-high 96 yards in Week 2. New England's passing game is sputtering, and despite A.J. Brown missing the last game and a half, Doubs has not logged heavy volume. Jacksonville's secondary was just beaten for 138 yards by Jaylen Waddle, but otherwise, has held up with only one touchdown to opposing wideouts. Until his opportunities increase, Doubs presents a risky profile.
outlooksByWeek.4: Romeo Doubs' workload remains minimal for the Patriots ahead of their Week 4 matchup with the Bills. Despite A.J. Brown's absence (ankle), Doubs has just 11 targets through three weeks. He's averaging a robust 24.2 yards per reception, and the Bills are allowing a big 9.3 yards per target to opposing wideouts. With Drake Maye struggling, gambling on a few Week 4 chunk plays is risky.
outlooksByWeek.5: Romeo Doubs has an ascending role in the Patriots' passing game ahead of a Week 5 matchup with the Raiders. He collected a season-high nine targets in Week 4, and while it resulted in just six catches and 58 yards, he found the end zone twice. Las Vegas will rush the passer, which has troubled Drake Maye. The secondary is allowing 8.2 yards per target to wideouts, so Doubs can capitalize on whatever volume he receives.
outlooksByWeek.6: Romeo Doubs' opportunities have been limited through five games, with the Patriots hosting the Jets in Week 6. After recording nine targets in Week 4, Doubs hauled in just one of three looks in Week 5, giving him three or four targets in four of the first five games with his new team. Though the Jets have been statistically stout against the pass, allowing just 195.4 yards per game, they've allowed five opposing wide receivers to post at least 58 yards in as many games. With Drake Maye spreading targets around, Doubs' ceiling is low, making him a fringe flex option.
outlooksByWeek.7: Romeo Doubs was placed on the injured list after injuring his shoulder while making a diving touchdown catch in Week 6. The Patriots expect him to return following their Week 11 bye. While Doubs is out, DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism, and Kyle Williams should log more targets.

player.seasonOutlook: Doubs signed with the Patriots during free agency after spending his first four NFL seasons with the Packers. He was a serviceable player during his Green Bay tenure, but he never finished a season in the top 30 among receivers in targets, catches, yards or fantasy points. Consistently mediocre, Doubs has averaged either 10.2 or 10.3 fantasy PPG each of the last three seasons. In New England, Doubs is likely to settle in as Drake Maye's No. 2 target behind A.J. Brown, though his target ceiling figures to be capped with the likes of DeMario Douglas, Mack Hollins and Kyle Williams also in the mix at receiver. Doubs, 26, is a fine addition to your bench, but his upside is limited.

outlooksByWeek.2: Keenan Allen can still get open on short passes, but the 34-year-old WR's lack of big-play potential limits his fantasy relevance to deeper formats heading into the Colts' Week 2 road game against the Chiefs. Allen caught all six of his targets in his Colts debut, leading the team in receptions, but he totaled just 32 receiving yards. Expect him to post plenty of similar stat lines this season after averaging a career-low 9.6 yards per catch with the Chargers last year.
outlooksByWeek.3: Keenan Allen should get plenty of playing time in Week 3 against the Texans with the Colts' banged-up WR room, but the 34-year-old wideout may not have enough gas in the tank to make much of the opportunity. Allen has exceeded 44 yards just once and failed to score a TD in his last 12 games. Despite that lack of recent production, he's a viable deep-league dart throw, as Indianapolis will be without Alec Pierce (heel) and possibly Ashton Dulin (ankle), leaving Allen as the top option for snaps at WR alongside Josh Downs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Keenan Allen turned back the clock in the Colts' Week 3 win over the Texans, catching six of nine targets for 63 yards and his first TD since Week 7 of the previous season. The 34-year-old WR is poised to maintain an expanded role in Week 4 against Washington's weak secondary as the Colts continue to play without starting WR Alec Pierce (heel), who is on IR. A repeat effort may be too much to ask from Allen, who averaged just 32 yards per game during his 12-game touchdown drought, but he's a viable flex option considering the Commanders have allowed league-high totals in catches and touchdowns to WRs, with 46 and six, respectively.
outlooksByWeek.5: Keenan Allen missed the Colts' Week 4 win over the Commanders due to a groin injury. If the 34-year-old WR is cleared to return in Week 5, he could play a prominent role opposite Josh Downs in a Colts WR room that remains without Alec Pierce (heel), who is on IR. Concerns about Allen's injury and performance limit his viability to deeper formats, even against a Steelers secondary that's giving up 149 receiving yards per game to wide receivers. Allen snapped a 12-game touchdown drought in the Colts' Week 3 win over Houston.
outlooksByWeek.6: Keenan Allen has caught 11 of 18 targets for 108 yards and a TD in his last two outings for the Colts, sandwiched around a Week 4 absence due to a groin injury. The 34-year-old wideout has stepped up in the absence of WR Alec Pierce (heel), who remains on injured reserve ahead of a Week 6 home game against the Titans. Allen lacks Pierce's ability to stretch the field, but a steady diet of short targets should put Allen back into the flex mix in Week 6 against a Titans defense that ranks among the 10 most generous units in terms of catches and yards allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Keenan Allen has turned back the clock over his past three appearances for the Colts, securing 19 of 29 targets for 190 yards and a TD over that span while drawing at least nine targets in every game. The 34-year-old wideout should continue to fill a high-volume role in a Colts WR room that lacks appealing alternatives in the continued absence of Alec Pierce (heel). Allen is a high-floor fantasy WR3 in Week 7 against the Vikings, who are allowing 10 catches for 133 yards per game to WRs. Minnesota's aggressive blitz packages will likely force the Colts into plenty of the quick and short throws on which Allen thrives.
outlooksByWeek.8: Keenan Allen is averaging over seven targets per game and has operated as the Colts' co-No. 1 WR alongside Josh Downs since Alec Pierce went down with a heel injury. Pierce remains on injured reserve ahead of a Week 8 trip to Jacksonville. Allen will be a high-floor flex candidate against a Jaguars defense that's giving up a league-high 210 yards per game to wide receivers. He's averaging 55 receiving yards per game over the past four and has scored one TD this season.
outlooksByWeek.9: Keenan Allen has recorded at least six receptions in four of seven appearances for the Colts this season and is likely to maintain a prominent role in Week 9 against a Dallas defense that's giving up 11.9 catches, as well as 164.1 receiving yards and 1.0 TD per game to WRs. Allen leads the Colts with 34 catches despite missing a game, and his 325 receiving yards are just five shy of Josh Downs' team-leading total. However, the 34-year-old Allen has scored just one TD in his last 17 regular-season games, dating back to last season with the Chargers. He remains a rock-solid, high-floor flex play for Week 9.

player.seasonOutlook: The Giants' linebacker corps is their D/ST strength, and it's possible this could be a sneaky-good source of sacks. Nevertheless, it's almost impossible to make a case to draft them, being that they face the Cowboys and Rams to open 2026. Should the Giants impress in those games, however, they could be a prime pickup for a soft Weeks 3-6 portion of their schedule (TEN, ARI, @WSH, NO).

outlooksByWeek.2: Jake Ferguson was surprisingly quiet in Week 1 for the Cowboys versus the Giants. Ferguson finished with just two catches for six yards in the 28-20 loss. Meanwhile, fellow tight ends Brevyn Spann-Ford and Luke Schoonmaker both gained more yards through the air. However, the Dallas passing attack struggled as a whole, leaving no pass-catcher with more than 45 yards receiving in the contest. In Week 2, the Cowboys will look to rebound versus the Commanders. Washington only allowed 182 passing yards in its season opener, though did give up three passing scores to Philadelphia quarterback Jalen Hurts.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jake Ferguson scored twice last game for the Cowboys. Ferguson caught four passes for 43 yards and the two scores in the 37-20 win over Washington. In Week 3, Dallas hosts the Baltimore Ravens. Baltimore is allowing just 191 passing yards per contest, which is 12th in the NFL. In addition, the Ravens have given up just two passing touchdowns through two tilts.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jake Ferguson found the end zone again for the Cowboys last game. Ferguson caught three passes for 23 yards and the touchdown in the 34-31 loss to the Ravens. Ferguson has three touchdowns over his last two contests, all coming within the red zone. However, Ferguson has yet to gain even 45 yards in a single outing, making him a touchdown-dependent option in Week 4 versus the Texans. Houston has yielded five touchdowns through three tilts, which is tied for 16th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jake Ferguson had a two-game scoring streak snapped for the Cowboys. Ferguson managed three catches for just 11 yards in the 34-30 win over the Texans. Ferguson has just 12 catches for 83 yards through the first four games of the season, though has scored three times over that span. In Week 5, Dallas will face a Tampa Bay defense that has been fairly stingy against the pass in terms of yardage. The Bucs are allowing just 204.3 passing yards per tilt, which is ninth in the NFL. However, Tampa Bay has also given up seven throwing scores, which is tied for 23rd in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jake Ferguson saw a season-high six targets last game for the Cowboys. CeeDee Lamb was dealing with a quadriceps issue, which likely contributed to the additional looks for other players, including Ferguson. However, Ferguson managed three catches for just 19 yards in the loss, and Lamb's injury does not appear serious, which would knock Ferguson back down the pecking order in Week 6 versus the Packers. Green Bay's defense is also allowing just 181 passing yards per contest, which is fifth in the league. Likewise, the Packers have surrendered only six passing touchdowns on the season, which is tied for 10th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jake Ferguson continues to struggle to find his place in the Dallas offense. Ferguson managed just two catches for 13 yards in the dismal 23-13 loss to the Packers. Ferguson has been held out of the end zone in three-straight games, and has failed to gain even 20 yards receiving in any of those contests. He will look to right the ship in Week 7 versus Philadelphia. The Eagles are allowing 244.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 26th in the NFL. However, Philadelphia has given up just eight passing scores in 2026, which is tied for 14th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jake Ferguson was held without a catch last game for Dallas. Ferguson's decline has been steep this season. He has failed to find the end zone in four-straight games, and has not even gained 20 yards in any contest over that span. He will look to get back on track in Week 8 with an extremely favorable matchup against the Arizona Cardinals. Arizona has been prone to surrendering the touchdown pass. In fact, Arizona has given up 17 passing scores, which is dead last in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.9: Jake Ferguson left the last game for Dallas due to an ankle injury. His status remains up in the air for Week 9 versus Indianapolis. Ferguson has failed to register a single catch in each of the last two contests. Brevyn Spann-Ford could see additional looks if Ferguson is sidelined. Spann-Ford snagged five passes for 31 yards following Ferguson's departure. In Week 9, Dallas will face a Colts defense allowing just 211.8 passing yards per tilt, which is 12th in the NFL. However, Indianapolis has given up 14 passing scores, which is tied for 23rd in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Ferguson has emerged as a reliable target for Dak Prescott in the high-scoring Dallas offense, which has led to solid fantasy production. Ferguson, who has handled a 17% target share each of the past three seasons, is fresh off a career year in which he ranked third among tight ends in receptions, touchdowns and end zone targets (10). His nine top-12 fantasy weeks tied for second, though it's worth noting that his production dropped off substantially with a healthy CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens on the field during the second half of the season (under 12.0 fantasy points in each of his final eight healthy games, 7.3 PPG during the span). The 27-year-old's role as a short-range target (4.7 aDOT last season) limits his yardage upside, but he sees just enough work, including near the goal line, to allow fringe-TE1 production. Don't call him "Joke Farterson" ("Fantasy Football Now" viewers get it); Ferguson is vying for his third top-10 fantasy campaign in his past four seasons.

outlooksByWeek.2: Cameron Dicker didn't get many chances to hit the scoreboard in the Chargers' season-opening loss to the Cardinals, converting both his extra points but failing to see a field-goal attempt. The team's offense didn't quite look in sync yet under new coordinator Mike McDaniel, and top wideout Ladd McConkey was knocked out of the game early with a rib injury, so scoring drives could be tough to come by for the club in the short term. Dicker will look to bounce back in Week 2 against a Raiders team that finished 25th in points per game allowed in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Cameron Dicker has had a rough start to the season as the Chargers adjust to a new offensive scheme under Mike McDaniel. The fifth-year kicker has converted all four of his PATs through two games, but his only field-goal attempt so far came from 58 yards out, and he clanked it off the upright. Better days should be ahead for Dicker and the offense, but his streak of seasons with 40-plus FG attempts could be about to come to an abrupt end. Dicker could be a little busier in Week 3 against a Bills team that's allowed 31.0 points a game in the early going, tied for the third-worst total in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Cameron Dicker has had a shaky start to the season as the Chargers struggle to put points on the board. The fifth-year kicker has seen just five extra points in three games, converting all five, and he's connected on just three of five FG attempts, with all three makes coming in a Week 3 loss to the Bills. That volatility isn't fantasy-friendly, and until the team's skill players begin to get the hang of new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme, Dicker's volume is likely to remain limited. He probably won't be able to afford to squander any chances in Week 4 against a Seahawks team allowing just 16.7 points per game, tied for third in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Cameron Dicker's volume increased for a second straight week in the Chargers' Week 4 loss to the Seahawks, converting all three of his field-goal attempts and both of his PATs. While the team's offense continues to struggle, Justin Herbert is at least putting together longer drives, and during those two contests Dicker has gone 6-for-7 on FG tries with all of his attempts coming from inside 50 yards. He likely won't be able to squander many chances in Week 5 against a Broncos team allowing 23.5 points per game, 17th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Cameron Dicker's opportunities continue to be inconsistent due to the struggles of the Chargers' offense. The kicker hasn't attempted more than two PATs in any of the team's first five games, going a perfect 9-for-9, and he's seen one or fewer field goal attempts in three of those five contests. With the offensive line in shambles and Justin Herbert running out of healthy targets, Dicker's volume doesn't seem likely to pick up anytime soon. He'll face a Kansas City squad in Week 6 that's allowing 19.3 points per game, seventh in the league.
outlooksByWeek.8: Cameron Dicker failed to get an extra-point attempt in Week 6 for the first time this season, accounting for all the Chargers' points with two field goals in a 22-6 loss to Kansas City. Coming out of a bye, the offense will hopefully be a bit healthier and energized, providing Dicker with more opportunities, but he has kicked multiple field goals in three of the last four contests. In Week 8, he'll take aim at a Rams team that's allowing 22.7 points per game, 16th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.9: Cameron Dicker hasn't missed a kick in four straight games, converting all three of his field goal attempts in a Week 8 loss to the Rams but failing to even see a PAT for a second straight contest. The Chargers' offensive struggles limit Dicker's opportunities despite his accuracy, and the advantage of playing his home games indoors. Dicker will look for a little more volume in Week 9 against an underperforming Texans team that's giving up 24.3 points per game, 18th in the league.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jacory Croskey-Merritt found the end zone in Week 1 for Washington.  Bill served as the primary ballcarrier, toting the pigskin 16 times for 63 yards and the score. Meanwhile, fellow running back Rachaad White had seven carries for only 22 years. In Week 2, Croskey-Merritt will have a favorable matchup versus the Cowboys. Dallas allowed 165 yards rushing and one score on the ground to the Giants in the season opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jacory Croskey-Merritt took 12 carries for 43 yards in Washington's loss to Dallas last game. Meanwhile, fellow running back Rachaad White took seven carries for 43 yards, while also catching six passes for 40 yards as a receiver with Washington playing from behind. Croskey-Merritt looks like the preferred back between the tackles, with White acting as the pass-catching or third-down option. The timeshare will likely continue against a devastating Seattle defense in Week 3. The Seahawks are allowing just 8.5 points per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league. In addition, Seattle has yet to allow a rushing touchdown to the opposition, and the Commanders will be without their starting quarterback, Jayden Daniels due to injury.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jacory Croskey-Merritt was perhaps predictably stymied by the Seattle Seahawks last game. However, the touches were a silver lining, as Croskey-Merritt garnered 20 opportunities in the 33-31 win over the defending champions. Bill rushed 19 times for 36 yards, while also catching a seven-yard pass out of the backfield. However, fellow running back Rachaad White  averaged more than double Croskey-Meritt's yards per carry, while also finding the end zone through the air. However, there could be plenty of room to roam in Week 4 versus the Colts. Indianapolis has been dreadful against the run in 2026, allowing 141.3 yards per contest on he ground, which is 29th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jacory Croskey-Merritt was stymied last game in a dismal loss for the Commanders. Bill had nine carries for a season-low 15 yards in the 30-13 defeat to the Colts. Even with Rachaad White sidelined due to injury, Croskey-Merritt could find little room to roam. Bill is struggling overall this season, averaging just 2.8 yards per tote. In Week 5, Washington will face a Giants run defense that has vastly improved from a season ago. New York is allowing 109 rushing yards per tilt, which is tied for 15th in the league. In addition, the G-Men have surrendered only two rushing touchdowns through four contests.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jacory Croskey-Merritt rushed for a season-high 82 yards last game for the Commanders. Bill also found the end zone for the second time this season. Croskey-Merritt has seen double-digit touches in every contest thus far in 2026. In Week 6, Washington will face the San Francisco 49ers. The Niners are allowing 97.6 rushing yards per tilt, which is 10th in the NFL. San Francisco has also given up just three rushing touchdowns through five outings, which is tied for sixth in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: One of the most hyped-up players entering the 2025 fantasy season, Croskey-Merritt didn't quite live up to lofty expectations, but he was certainly very busy for a seventh-round rookie. "Bill" played 39% of Washington's offensive snaps but, while he finished 23rd among backs in rushing yards, he wasn't much of a factor in the passing game (3% target share). Croskey-Merritt will now compete with newcomer Rachaad White in what appears to be setting up as a committee in Washington. The 25-year-old has shown to be an effective rusher (4.60 yards per carry, 2.19 YAC), but he'll need a big boost in receiving work to find his way into the RB2/flex discussion. He's worth only a late-round flier.

Tyson was selected by the Saints with the No. 8 overall pick of April's draft. He is a versatile receiver with decent size who led this rookie class with a 35% target share during the nine weeks he was active in 2025. Injuries cost him time during all four collegiate seasons, but he still managed a 158-2,282-22 receiving line in 33 games, posting a strong 2.73 YPRR along the way (third best in this class). Tyson suffered a hamstring injury in August and will miss a month or two of the regular season prior to taking over as the Saints' No. 2 receiver behind Chris Olave. Once healthy, Tyson has a path to a substantial role in an ascending offense led by second-year QB Tyler Shough and could find himself on the WR3 radar. Of course, with the injury, he's only worth a late flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Cairo Santos will aim to stay perfect as the Bears play the Vikings in Week 2. Santos was on the field a lot in Week 1 against the Panthers, but most of his 11 points came from his eight PATs. The veteran kicker could continue to benefit from a high-scoring offense, and he'll look to continue against a Minnesota squad that allowed three field goals and an extra point to Trey Smack this past Sunday.
outlooksByWeek.3: Cairo Santos will aim to do more as the Bears play the Eagles in Week 3. Santos made his first field-goal attempt against the Vikings in Week 2, but his second chance for a tie was blocked in the fourth quarter. The veteran kicker's potential for the rest of the season remains up in the air following the injury to Caleb Williams, but an inexperienced Tyson Bagent could get the field-goal team on the field more often rather than finding the end zone. Philly has allowed 6.0 fantasy points per game to kickers this year, a top-10 mark in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Cairo Santos will aim to stay solid as the Bears play the Jets in Week 4. Santos nailed both of his field-goal attempts and went three-for-three on PATs in Week 3 against the Eagles. The veteran kicker has now made all but one of his field-goal tries and all 10 XPAs in the first three games of the season. He'll face a Jets squad that's allowed a top-ten 6.3 fantasy points per game to kickers.
outlooksByWeek.5: Cairo Santos will look to deliver on high volume again as the Bears play the Packers in Week 5. Bagent converted a season-high three field goals against the Jets in Week 3, and he also nailed both of his XPAs. The veteran kicker has now gone 7-for-8 on field-goal attempts while making all 13 of his extra-point tries across four weeks this season. He'll face a Green Bay defense that's ranked top five against fantasy kickers so far.
outlooksByWeek.6: Cairo Santos will look to get more involved as the Bears play the Falcons in Week 6. Santos missed his only field-goal attempt and converted an XPA in a Week 6 blowout loss to the Packers. The veteran kicker has now converted seven of nine field-goal kicks and all 14 of his extra-point tries across five games this season. He'll face an Atlanta squad that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy kickers this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.7: Cairo Santos will aim to get back on track as the Bears play the Patriots in Week 7. Santos nailed all four of his XPAs in a Week 6 win over the Falcons, but he went one-for-two on field-goal attempts. The veteran kicker has now missed a kick in back-to-back games. He'll face a New England defense that's ranked top 10 against fantasy kickers.
outlooksByWeek.8: Cairo Santos will look to stay busy as the Bears play the Seahawks in Week 8. Santos went 3-for-4 on field-goal attempts, including a career-high 58-yarder, and nailed all three of his XPAs in a Week 7 win over the Patriots. The veteran has now missed a field-goal try in each of the last three weeks,  but he's gone an otherwise serviceable 11-for-15 on field goals, and 21-for-21 on extra-point kicks this season. He'll face a Seattle squad that's ranked sixth in fantasy points allowed to kickers.
outlooksByWeek.9: Cairo Santos will look to build on a solid showing as the Bears play the Buccaneers in Week 9. Santos made all of his kicks in Chicago's Week 8 win over the Seahawks, nailing two field goal attempts and four XPAs. The veteran kicker had also missed a field goal in three straight games before this matchup, so he's hopefully now back on track. Tampa Bay has ranked 13th in fantasy points allowed to kickers so far this campaign.

player.seasonOutlook: Raheem Morris comes aboard as the 49ers' defensive coordinator this season, and between questions about his scheme's fit to the team's personnel and the injuries that have struck this roster in recent years, it's tough to get fully behind a rebound from this D/ST. An opening-week road matchup with the Rams should make this a no-go draft day pick, but the 49ers could have their matchup moments later in the year.

Injuries have bred disappointing fantasy totals from the Lions' D/ST the past two seasons, as the team finished 12th and 17th despite what was a solid roster on paper. Fantasy managers should hope for better luck on that front, but at least the schedule will grant the Lions as good a chance to rebound as anything. They open with a home game against the Saints, have a trio of must-start matchups from Weeks 3-5 (NYJ, @CAR, @ARI) and one of the best second-half schedules.

outlooksByWeek.2: Eddy Pineiro heads into a Week 2 matchup versus Miami on the heels of making two field goals in San Francisco's season-opening victory against the Rams. Pineiro's makes came from 20 and 56 yards out, though he also missed a 52-yarder. The veteran kicker made a career-high six FGs from 50-plus yards out last year, so San Francisco is clearly comfortable relying on his leg from that distance. The 49ers could put up plenty of points in Week 2, as the Dolphins just gave up 27 points to Las Vegas in a Week 1 loss.
outlooksByWeek.3: Eddy Pineiro remains a solid fantasy kicker option heading into the 49ers' Week 3 matchup against Arizona. Pineiro didn't attempt a field goal Sunday against the Dolphins, but he converted all five of his extra-point tries. San Francisco has averaged 31.0 points per game through two weeks, so Pineiro figures to see frequent opportunities to kick, though that won't always result in field-goal chances. Arizona's opponents have attempted just one FG through two weeks, but the Cardinals gave up a hefty 31 points to Seattle in a Week 2 loss.
outlooksByWeek.4: Eddy Pineiro will look to get his consistency back on track for San Francisco in Week 4 versus the Broncos. Pineiro missed a pair of extra-point tries Sunday in a win over Arizona, but he also nailed a 57-yard field goal. The veteran kicker hadn't previously struggled with PATs, making all eight over his first two games of the campaign, so his erratic boot may have just been an aberration. Denver has yielded eight field-goal attempts and seven extra-point tries through three weeks.
outlooksByWeek.5: Eddy Pineiro's leg could be key for the 49ers in Week 5 versus Seattle in a battle of tough defenses. Pineiro has been mostly asked to kick extra points this season, making 14 of 16 PAT tries while attempting just six field goals (and making four of them). He missed a 54-yard try against Denver this past Sunday, though it was blocked by the Broncos. There may not be many opportunities for Pineiro against the Seahawks, who are giving up the fifth-fewest points (18.3) in the league this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Eddy Pineiro enters a Week 6 tilt against Washington coming off hitting a game-winning field goal for San Francisco this past Sunday. The veteran kicker missed a 52-yard attempt in that contest, but he atoned for that with a 44-yard make that ended up being the deciding score. Pineiro is now 5-for-8 on FG attempts this season, with all three of his misses coming from 50-plus yards. He could see plenty of chances against the Commanders, who are allowing the third-most points (29.8) in the league.
outlooksByWeek.7: Eddy Pineiro and the 49ers are back on the road for a meeting with the 2-4 Falcons in Week 7. He converted his only field-goal attempt but went 2-for-3 on extra-point tries during San Francisco's 23-17 victory in Week 6. Pineiro has been underwhelming despite playing for a 49ers team that scores 29.5 points per game, which is the third-most in the league. He's now 6-for-9 (66.7%) on field goals and 19-for-22 (86.4%) on PATs, and he hasn't attempted more than two FGs since the season opener. Pineiro should remain on fantasy waiver wires with more reliable options available at the position.
outlooksByWeek.9: Eddy Pineiro will hope the 49ers' Week 8 bye has helped him get back on track against the Raiders in Week 9. Piniero missed an extra-point attempt in each of his previous two contests before the bye, and he's made just six of nine field goal tries this season. All three of his misses have come from 50-plus yards, but it's still a notable downturn after the veteran kicker went 6-for-7 on attempts from that distance last season. He could be mostly busy with PATs against a Las Vegas defense that has had 27 PAT tries versus only 14 FG attempts against it so far this season.

outlooksByWeek.2: Adonai Mitchell will look to stretch the field for the Jets in Week 2 against the Packers. Mitchell hauled in all three of his targets to open the year, finishing with 60 yards. Green Bay allowed a mere 7.7 yards per target in Week 1, but that was largely due to facing Carson Wentz for the bulk of the game. Their secondary remains vulnerable and will likely commit multiple bodies to Garrett Wilson, setting up Mitchell for a few plays downfield in single coverage. Mitchell seems likely to continue his low-volume, high-upside role in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.3: Adonai Mitchell hopes for a continued elevated workload in Week 3 when the Jets face the Lions. After just three targets in a run-heavy Week 1, Mitchell logged an eye-opening 12 targets in Week 2, with the Jets throwing 41 times. Detroit's defense has been a fantasy bonanza for opposing offenses, allowing the sixth-most fantasy points to wideouts. Assuming the Lions score plenty themselves, the Jets should throw heavily, giving Mitchell ample opportunities for a big play or two.
outlooksByWeek.4: Adonai Mitchell is questionable for the Jets in Week 4 against the Bears after missing Week 3 due to a finger injury. Mitchell has been a valuable secondary option opposite Garrett Wilson in his first two games, garnering 15 targets and averaging 13.7 yards per catch. With minimal options behind him and running back Breece Hall (thigh) likely to miss Week 4, Mitchell could have a stable workload against a defense that's allowing 8.5 yards per target to opposing receivers.
outlooksByWeek.5: Adonai Mitchell needs to overcome a finger injury that has cost him the last two weeks if he's to help the Jets against the Browns in Week 5. Prior to injury, Mitchell was giving the Jets a field-stretching option, averaging 13.7 yards per catch on nine grabs. Targets will continue to be heavily funneled toward Garrett Wilson, but Mitchell will be in a favorable spot if cleared to play, as Cleveland has allowed six touchdowns to opposing receivers through four games. Sterling Shepard and Isaiah Williams would continue to register additional snaps should Mitchell miss his third straight game.
outlooksByWeek.6: Adonai Mitchell will need to overcome a finger issue that's cost him the last three weeks if he's to help the Jets against the Patriots in Week 6. He had emerged as a field stretcher for the Jets, but it's an offense that prefers to run and heavily target Garrett Wilson. New England has allowed five touchdown catches by opposing receivers in as many games, and Mitchell would likely require that end-zone success to be considered a starting option. Isaiah Williams and Tim Patrick will continue to get additional snaps if Mitchell remains sidelined.
outlooksByWeek.7: Adonai Mitchell will need to overcome a finger injury that cost him four games if he's to help the Jets against the Dolphins in Week 7. Mitchell looked firm in his role opposite Garrett Wilson prior to injury, but it's fair to question his immediate role should he be active in Week 7. Facing a Dolphins' secondary that's surprisingly allowing the second-fewest fantasy points to opposing wide receivers despite a desirable 8.2 yards per target doesn't profile as a re-emergent spot, especially with Omar Cooper healthy and surging.
outlooksByWeek.8: Adonai Mitchell has a minimal role in the Jets' limited passing attack entering a Week 8 clash with the Raiders. Returning from a four-week absence in Week 7, Mitchell failed to record a catch on his three targets. Omar Cooper's emergence paired with Garrett Wilson's steady presence won't leave a plethora of opportunities for the remaining Jets' receivers in a run-first offense, giving Mitchell too few chances to exploit a defense that's allowing a generous 8.9 yards per target through seven games.
outlooksByWeek.9: Adonai Mitchell faces an uphill battle if he hopes to repeat a career outing when the Jets face the Chiefs in Week 9. After being shut out since Week 2, Mitchell popped for seven catches, 142 yards, and a touchdown in Week 8, shifting the spotlight from surging rookie Omar Cooper. Mitchell has always shown big-play potential but sees inconsistent opportunities. This sets him up as a high-potential, low-ceiling option against a Chiefs secondary that's allowing just 6.9 yards per target and the second-fewest fantasy points to opposing wideouts.

player.seasonOutlook: Mitchell is entering his first full campaign with the Jets, having been acquired in the Sauce Gardner trade during the 2025 season. After playing sparingly during his first 25 NFL games (all with the Colts), the 2024 second-round pick handled a hefty 24.4% target share in eight games with New York last season. The usage led to two fantasy outings with 17-plus points, but he was otherwise a nonfactor (4.0 PPG). Efficiency remains an issue, as Mitchell's 44% catch rate ranks last, and his 6.0 yards per target is fourth worst among 77 receivers with 100-plus targets since he entered the league. The vertical threat will compete with rookie Omar Cooper Jr. for No. 2 duties opposite a now-healthy Garrett Wilson in the Jets' Geno Smith-led offense. Mitchell, 23, is not worth much more than late-round consideration.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kaelon Black is coming off an impressive NFL debut as San Francisco heads into a Week 2 matchup versus the Dolphins. Black surprisingly got more carries than Christian McCaffrey in a season-opening win over the Rams, logging 14 carries for 65 yards to McCaffrey's 10 carries for 68 yards. While there's no chance of Black usurping a healthy McCaffrey in the pecking order anytime soon, the Week 1 usage suggests Black could take on a significant role in San Francisco's offense if the team looks to lighten McCaffrey's workload. Both backs could be in for a good day against Miami, who allowed Las Vegas running backs Ashton Jeanty and Mike Washington to combine for 143 rushing yards, 45 receiving yards and two touchdowns in a Week 1 loss to Las Vegas.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kaelon Black enters a Week 3 tilt against Arizona having established himself as San Francisco's clear No. 2 back. While Black has caught only one pass (on one target) through two contests, he's carried the ball 21 times -- one more than starter Christian McCaffrey (20 carries) and well ahead of No. 3 RB Jordan James (four totes). Of course, McCaffrey is the unquestioned leader of the 49ers' backfield, but Black has at least carved out a significant role and put himself on the fantasy radar in his first NFL campaign. The Cardinals just gave up 144 total rushing yards to Seattle's Jadarian Price and Emanuel Wilson in a loss Sunday, so they could be vulnerable against San Francisco's ground game.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kaelon Black has seen his involvement on offense dwindle in recent games as the 49ers prepare to face the Broncos in Week 4. After the rookie garnered a hefty 14 carries in Week 1, he's logged just 11 totes over the subsequent two weeks, including just four this past Sunday in a win over Arizona. Black was at least fairly efficient by gaining 17 yards on those carries, but with only one reception to date this season, he's not getting enough touches to make an impact in fantasy. Perhaps that will change against the Broncos, who are giving up 5.26 yards per carry to running backs, the second-worst mark in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Kaelon Black should continue to back up 49ers star RB Christian McCaffrey in Week 5 against Seattle. Black surprisingly logged 14 carries in Week 1 against the Rams, but since then he's topped out at seven totes as McCaffrey has dominated touches out of the backfield. Black also has just one catch this season, so he hasn't been able to establish much fantasy value except as an insurance policy in case of a McCaffrey injury. It may be hard for Black to find success on what will likely be limited opportunities against Seattle, as the Seahawks are allowing a paltry 3.35 yards per carry to RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Kaelon Black will likely again get a handful of carries again for the 49ers in Week 6 against Washington. Black has logged between four and seven carries each of his past four games after getting 14 totes in Week 1 against the Rams. The rookie hasn't been particularly efficient with his opportunities, managing just 2.4 yards per carry over the past two weeks and 3.7 overall this season. Things may not get easier against the Commanders, who have yielded the sixth-fewest rushing yards per game to RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Kaelon Black and the 49ers visit the Falcons for a Week 7 showdown. He had eight carries for 34 yards and caught his lone target for three yards in San Francisco's 23-17 victory in Week 6. Christian McCaffrey tallied 25 touches to the rookie's nine, leaving no doubt about who the leader is in the 49ers' backfield. Black will look to make more of an impact with his limited touches versus Atlanta's 21st-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (23.3) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Kaelon Black may have an opportunity for more work in Week 9 versus the Raiders with San Francisco's top RB, Christian McCaffrey, managing a hamstring strain. McCaffrey picked up the injury in Week 7 against Atlanta, and Black ended up logging a healthy 12 carries, which he turned into 63 yards and a touchdown. McCaffrey was able to finish out that game, and the team's Week 8 bye along with optimism that the strain is mild gives him a good chance of suiting up this Sunday, but Black could be productive even if McCaffrey plays. Las Vegas has posted some of the worst numbers in the NFL against running backs, giving up 22.3 fantasy points per game to the position, fifth-most in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Black was selected by the 49ers in the third round of April's draft. It was a bit of a surprise selection after Black failed to clear 190 touches in four collegiate seasons prior to not landing an invite to the scouting combine. He did clear 1,000 rushing yards at Indiana in 2025, but remained a nonfactor as a receiver, totaling exactly four receptions in each of his two seasons with the Hoosiers. Black will open his career handling No. 2 duties behind Christian McCaffrey. He'll be worth an add if the 30-year-old McCaffrey misses time, but a lack of third-down ability may severely limit his fantasy output. Stash Black in dynasty formats.

outlooksByWeek.2: Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers visit the Patriots for a Week 2 road clash. He completed 24 of 40 pass attempts for 221 yards with one TD and no INTs while rushing three times for minus-3 yards during Pittsburgh's 20-13 Week 1 victory over the Falcons. The Steelers attempted 41 passes compared to just 21 rushing attempts, as Rodgers connected with seven different receivers on the day. They'll face a tougher test on the road against New England's eighth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (15.3) to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers host the division-rival Bengals in Week 3. He threw for 187 yards (23-for-39) with no touchdowns and one INT and lost one of his two fumbles during Pittsburgh's Week 2 loss to the Patriots. Cincinnati has been somewhat stingy against opposing QBs, allowing 20.2 fantasy points through two outings (15th) despite giving up 353 passing yards versus Houston in Week 2. The Bengals are the only defense without an interception to this point, but they're also the only team that has yet to surrender a passing TD.
outlooksByWeek.4: Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers visit the division-rival Browns in Week 4. He's coming off easily his best outing of the young campaign, throwing for 292 yards (19-for-34) with three TDs and one INT while rushing three times for 10 yards during Pittsburgh's 30-27 win in Week 3. Rodgers spread the ball around to nine different receivers, finding Roman Wilson, DK Metcalf, and Ben Skowronek for his three scores. He'll face Cleveland's 16th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (20.9) per game to QBs as the Steelers look to improve to 3-1 in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.5: Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers host the Colts for a Week 5 showdown. He threw for 299 yards (22-for-40) with three TDs and two INTs during Pittsburgh's 27-24 loss in Week 4. That's two straight outings with three passing TDs and nearly 300 yards through the air, but the 42-year-old was sacked five times in addition to his two turnovers. Rodgers will look to clean up the mistakes against a Colts defense allowing 24.3 fantasy points per game to QBs (27th) and 261.3 passing yards (29th).
outlooksByWeek.6: Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers are in Tampa Bay for an interconference clash in Week 6. He threw for 235 yards (22-for-31) with three TDs and no INTs while rushing once for six yards during Pittsburgh's 34-22 victory in Week 5. That's three straight weeks that the 42-year-old has tossed three scores, and he now has a 10:4 TD:INT through five games this season. Rodgers looks to stay hot versus a stingy Buccaneers defense that ranks 11th in fantasy points allowed to QBs (18.4 per game).
outlooksByWeek.7: Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers are in Paris for a Week 7 matchup against the Saints. He threw for 253 yards (33-for-49) with two TDs and one INT while rushing once for minus-one yard during Pittsburgh's 26-19 comeback win in overtime. Rodgers led four straight scoring drives to send the game to OT after the Steelers trailed 16-3 to start the fourth quarter. He now owns an 11:4 TD:INT over his last four outings, and he'll face a New Orleans defense that ranks 18th in fantasy points allowed per game (21.4) to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers welcome the division-rival Browns to town in Week 8. He completed 19 of 30 pass attempts for 212 yards with one TD and no INTs while rushing three times for six yards during Pittsburgh's 16-10 win in Week 7. The performance snapped Rodgers' four-game multi-touchdown streak, although he was able to avoid making any turnovers. He'll aim to get back on track versus a Cleveland defense he threw for 299 yards and three TDs against during a Week 4 loss.

player.seasonOutlook: Rodgers re-signed with the Steelers and will return for his second season with the team. The 42-year-old is reuniting with his longtime head coach from Green Bay, Mike McCarthy. The duo will look to improve on a 2025 campaign in which Rodgers finished just outside the top 12 in passing yards and touchdowns while ranking 23rd among 28 qualified QBs in QBR. Even if Rodgers' efficiency improves, he remains a nonfactor as a rusher (he last cleared 107 yards in 2020) and hasn't been fantasy relevant since 2021 (25th, 18th and 25th in points per game in his past three full seasons). Even with a more pass-friendly playcaller and with Michael Pittman Jr. and Germie Bernard added to the wide receiver room, Rodgers is no more than a low-ceiling QB2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jonathon Brooks is expected to operate as Carolina's No. 2 running back in the Week 2 matchup against the Falcons. Brooks received just four carries in the Week 1 loss, which is fewer than Chuba Hubbard (10) and AJ Dillon (five). However, all of Dillon's work came when the Panthers were down substantially in the fourth quarter. Brooks showed flashes of brilliance when on the field, most notably on a 48-yard catch and run. He could continue to take work from Hubbard as the season continues. However, he's in for a tough Week 2 matchup, with Atlanta allowing just 2.8 yards per rush attempt in Week 1, the best mark in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jonathon Brooks (groin) is expected to operate as the Panthers' No. 2 running back if active for the Week 3 matchup against the Browns. Brooks is considered week-to-week after tweaking the same groin he first injured during training camp in the Week 2 win over the Falcons. Prior to his injury, the Texas product was clearly operating as Carolina's second RB, tallying just nine carries for 30 yards and two catches for 43 yards over the team's first two contests. Brooks will likely to find fantasy relevance if active in Week 3, with Cleveland's defense allowing just 16.9 PPR fantasy points per game to the position thus far.

player.seasonOutlook: Brooks is hoping to get his career on track in 2026 after appearing in only one game since being drafted in the second round of the 2024 draft. Brooks spent most of his rookie season recovering from a torn ACL suffered while at the University of Texas. He returned in Week 12 and handled 12 touches in three games prior to retearing the same ACL and missing the entire 2025 season. Only 23 years old and skilled as a rusher and receiver, Brooks figures to eventually get his shot at a lead-back role in the pros. He's expected to battle for touches with Chuba Hubbard this season, so it's possible he quickly earns his way into a fantasy-relevant role. Consider him in the middle rounds.

Though the 2025 Eagles took a step backwards from the defensive stalwart that won Super Bowl LIX, their D/ST scored only 12 fewer total fantasy points and finished eighth at the position in scoring. Coordinator Vic Fangio typically extracts the most from his defenses, but the departures of S Reed Blankenship, LB Nakobe Dean, DE Brandon Graham and LB Jaelen Phillips heighten the challenge -- though the additions of LB Jonathan Greenard and CB Riq Woolen at least soften the blow. At least the team starts off with some soft matchups (WSH, Week 1; @TEN, Week 2), but be prepared to swap quickly if they're underperforming.

outlooksByWeek.2: MarShawn Lloyd will aim to be more effective as the Packers play the Jets in Week 2. While Lloyd was the leading rusher for Green Bay in Week 1, he still only totaled 37 yards on 13 rushing attempts. Fellow ball carrier Chris Brooks also recorded seven carries for 29 yards, so the margin between the two doesn't appear to be too large. Lloyd will look to do more with his opportunities against a New York front that should be less menacing than Minnesota's.
outlooksByWeek.3: MarShawn Lloyd will aim to be more efficient as the Packers play the Falcons in Week 3. Lloyd scored his first career touchdown off a six-yard catch in Week 2, but he also rushed six times for just 20 yards. The inexperienced running back has now averaged just 3.0 YPC off 19 carries this season, which is far from what Green Bay is looking for out of its RB1. Lloyd will also face an Atlanta defense that's allowed a top-10 127 rushing yards to running backs, which could make his job even harder.
outlooksByWeek.4: MarShawn Lloyd will aim to turn things around as the Packers travel to Tampa Bay in Week 4. Lloyd continued his disappointing season against the Falcons in Week 3, rushing four times for 11 yards and catching two of three passes for seven yards. While the inexperienced running back was hindered by a pass-heavy game script, he's still averaged just three yards per carry across 23 attempts and seen his offensive snap share decrease in each of his first three games. He'll also face a Bucs defense that's allowed the second-fewest rushing yards (165) to RBs this year, making him a very risky play.
outlooksByWeek.5: MarShawn Lloyd remains in the mix of Green Bay's backfield ahead of Week 5 against Chicago. Lloyd remained extremely inefficient on the ground in Week 4, rushing the ball seven times for 13 yards, but he did salvage his performance with five catches for 36 yards. The second-year running back looks to be in direct competition with Kaleb Johnson for carries as of late, but the Packers have utilized Lloyd in different ways even when Johnson has been more effective. Chicago has ranked 26th in yards per carry allowed (4.73) to RBs this season, which could give Lloyd the opening he needs to do more as a rusher.
outlooksByWeek.6: MarShawn Lloyd figures to be Green Bay's primary option in the running game again versus the Cowboys in Week 6. Lloyd put together his best fantasy performance of the year versus the Bears in Week 5, recording 10 carries for 31 yards and two touchdowns along with one catch for six yards. The second-year ball carrier has totaled 112 rushing yards and two touchdowns off 40 carries and caught 10 of 13 targets for 55 yards and a score across the first five games of the campaign. He'll face a Dallas defense that's ranked 25th in fantasy points allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.7: MarShawn Lloyd could be in line for a smaller role as the Packers play the Lions in Week 7. Lloyd was extremely inefficient on the ground in Week 6 against the Cowboys, rushing eight times for 10 yards and logging three fewer carries than position mate Pierre Strong. Lloyd is also now set to share the backfield with a reinstated Josh Jacobs, which could further limit his opportunities. Detroit has ranked eighth in fantasy points allowed to running backs this season.
outlooksByWeek.8: MarShawn Lloyd figures to be a complementary option once again as the Packers play the Panthers in Week 8. Lloyd's role wasn't completely chalked with the return of Josh Jacobs in Week 7, as he still logged six carries for 20 yards and caught two passes for 15 yards. Jacobs also averaged just 3.27 yards per carry on the ground, which could keep Lloyd relevant as a secondary rushing option if this persists. Carolina has ranked 31st in fantasy points allowed to RBs so far this season, so Lloyd will aim to take advantage of what could be limited touches.
outlooksByWeek.9: MarShawn Lloyd will look to make the most of his touches as the Packers play the Patriots in Week 9. Lloyd logged his lowest touch total of the year in a Week 8 win over Carolina, rushing the ball three times for seven yards and catching one pass for nine yards. While starting running back Josh Jacobs' status remains uncertain in the coming weeks, Lloyd's production even when Jacobs was inactive makes him a risky option. New England has ranked sixth in fantasy points allowed to running backs this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Due to a variety of injuries, Lloyd has appeared in one game since being selected in the third round of the 2024 draft. Now healthy, he appears to have a hold on No. 2 RB duties in Green Bay, which is notable with Josh Jacobs facing a potential suspension. Lloyd is likely to open the season on the RB2/flex radar and should be on your radar in the middle rounds, though note that he'll fade back to no more than an insurance stash once Jacobs returns.

outlooksByWeek.2: Justin Herbert struggled in the Chargers' season-opening loss to the Cardinals, completing 17 of 27 passes for 209 yards and one touchdown with one interception, while adding 29 rushing yards on five carries. Injuries along the offensive line were once again an issue for the club; the interior of the line, with rookie Jake Slaughter at center, wasn't able to hold up, and new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel didn't seem to have many answers. Ladd McConkey also suffered a rib injury in the game, which could make things even more difficult for Herbert if the top wideout misses any time. Herbert will look to rebound in Week 2 against a Raiders defense that ranked 15th in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Justin Herbert has had a rough start to the season with Mike McDaniel as his new offensive coordinator. Through two games, he's completed less than 60% of his passes with a 2:3 TD:INT ratio and barely over 200 passing yards per game. Ladd McConkey was his only reliable target in the Chargers' opener, but the third-year wideout was limited by a rib injury in Week 2's loss to the Raiders, and no one else stepped up. As in years past, Herbert's protection has also been decimated by injuries. An offensive line that was already missing starting center Tyler Biadasz was down to a third-string left guard against Las Vegas in Week 2, and the team also lost its two best blocking tight ends, Charlie Kolar and David Njoku, over the course of that contest. Herbert could be in for another long day in Week 3 against a Bills defense that has seven sacks through two games, tied for fourth in the league, but which has been vulnerable through the air when the opposing QB has found some time.
outlooksByWeek.4: Justin Herbert continues to struggle in new Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme. The veteran quarterback has yet to throw multiple touchdowns in a game this season, while his 59.1% completion rate would be a career-worst mark. Herbert is also dealing with his usual protection issues and has been sacked eight times in three contests, a pace that would see him get brought down more than 40 times for a third straight year. His top target, Ladd McConkey, should be healthier as he puts a rib injury further behind him, but as yet none of his other pass catchers have made any kind of impact. Herbert's rough year could get worse in Week 4 against a Seahawks defense that's tied for third in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Justin Herbert continues to struggle in offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme. The 28-year-old quarterback posted season lows with 189 passing yards and 6.1 yards per attempt in the Chargers' Week 4 loss to the Seahawks. Through four games, he has a career-low 59.7% completion rate and a weak 4:6 TD:INT. An ineffective running game, along with injuries to the offensive line and his wide receiver corps, have contributed to the team's 0-4 start, but Herbert has been the focal point of the offense's woes. He'll try to turn things around in Week 5 against a Broncos defense that could be missing its top two cornerbacks, including Patrick Surtain, and which ranks 21st in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Justin Herbert and the Chargers remain winless after a Week 5 loss to the Broncos, as their season spirals down the drain. Injuries have once again gutted the offensive line, with left tackle Rashawn Slater joining center Tyler Biadasz on IR, but offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel also doesn't seem to have any answers. Herbert has posted a career-low 59.4% completion rate and 6.6 yards per attempt through five games with a woeful 5:7 TD:INT, and now his top four wide receivers, along with tight end David Njoku, are all injured. Herbert doesn't seem likely to turn things around in Week 6 against a Kansas City defense that ranks seventh in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Justin Herbert is hoping the Chargers' Week 7 bye will help the offense get sorted out. Through six games under offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel and working behind a patchwork offensive line, the 28-year-old quarterback is on pace for career worst in every major category, including a 59.4% completion rate, 6.3 yards per attempt and a weak 5:8 TD:INT. He's even failed to score a rushing TD, after running for multiple scores in five of his first six NFL seasons. Herbert will try to right the ship in Week 8 against a Rams defense that ranks 16th in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Justin Herbert is coming off another shaky performance, as he failed to throw a touchdown and got picked off twice in the Chargers' Week 8 loss to the Rams. The 28-year-old quarterback has a miserable 5:10 TD:INT through seven games this season, and the offense under Mike McDaniel appears to be broken beyond repair, as the winless team has scored more than 17 points only once all year. Herbert remains a very risky play heading into a Week 9 meeting with a Texans defense that has also underperformed, sitting 23rd in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Herbert enters his seventh NFL season following a solid 2025 campaign in which he ranked just inside the top 10 quarterbacks in pass attempts, yards and touchdowns. Herbert added serious value with his legs, ranking fifth at the position in carries and second in rushing yards (career highs in both). He finished 10th among quarterbacks in fantasy points, but that's a bit misleading, as his inconsistent production led to five top-five weeks but no other finishes better than 13th. Herbert has finished between 11th and 15th in fantasy points per game in each of the past four seasons, though it's fair to expect a leap forward in 2026 with star tackles Joe Alt and Rashawn Slater healthy and a new playcaller in Mike McDaniel. Herbert is safest as a QB2, but there's upside for more.

A middling, matchups-driven D/ST last season, the Buccaneers saw much change among their linebacker corps during the offseason. Lavonte David retired, and the team drafted Rueben Bain Jr. 15th overall and signed Alex Anzalone and Christian Rozeboom. Take a wait-and-see approach to how the new personnel jells, especially since the Buccaneers get a tough opening matchup in a road game against the Bengals.

outlooksByWeek.7: J.J. McCarthy led a furious comeback attempt by the Giants last game. Though McCarthy's efforts fell short, he threw for an astonishing 243 yards in the fourth quarter alone in relief of starter Jameis Winston. While the G-Men ultimately lost to the Saints by a score of 34-27, McCarthy's near-heroics have likely created a quarterback controversy heading into Week 7 versus the Texans. Whomever lines up under center may have a favorable matchup, as Houston is allowing 246 passing yards per tilt, which is 27th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.9: J.J. McCarthy comes off the bye as the starting quarterback of the first-place Giants as they head into a divisional matchup in Week 9 versus bumbling Philadelphia. The Eagles have lost six-straight contests. Philadelphia's defense is allowing 235.4 passing yards per tilt, which is 24th in the NFL. Meanwhile, McCarthy has thrown for at least 243 yards in each of the last two games for the G-Men.

player.seasonOutlook: McCarthy's career is off to a slow start after the 2024 first-round pick missed his entire rookie season because of an injury then struggled through 2025. McCarthy appeared in 10 games and totaled 11 passing TDs and 12 interceptions while completing an ugly 58% of his passes. McCarthy added some value with his legs (including four TDs), but his production was extremely inconsistent (18-plus fantasy points in four games, but 6.7 per game in his other six outings). The 23-year-old still has plenty of time to develop, but that will come as a backup to Kyler Murray this season. McCarthy is worth considering only in dynasty leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jalen Hurts tossed three touchdowns in Week 1 for the Eagles. Hurts was not terribly efficient, though did hit on several big plays en route to the 24-22 win. Hurts also rushed for 46 yards in a brand new offense under the direction of offensive coordinator Sean Mannion. In Week 2, Philadelphia will face a dismal Titans squad that allowed 367 yards from scrimmage to the Jets in their season opener. Tennessee was torched on the ground in particular, allowing 152 rushing yards and two touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jalen Hurts tossed two touchdowns and two interceptions in a last-second win over Tennessee last game. Hurts threw for 264 yards in the rollercoaster battle and was able to overcome the two picks to find Darius Cooper for the winning score. Hurts has five touchdowns in two games for the Eagles. In Week 3, Philadelphia will face a Bears defense allowing 240 passing yards per tilt thus far this season, which is 25th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jalen Hurts had a performance to forget last game for the Eagles. Hurts threw for just 153 yards and an interception in a dismal loss to the Bears in Week 3. Hurts did score once on the ground, though gained just 25 yards as a rusher. Hurts will look to get back on track in Week 4 versus a Rams defense that has been fairly stingy against the pass in 2026. The Rams are allowing just 171.3 passing yards per tilt, which is fourth in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jalen Hurts tossed two touchdowns last game for the Eagles. Unfortunately, he threw for just 93 yards in the 24-20 loss to the Rams. Hurts was missing DeVonta Smith and Dallas Goedert in the passing game, while Saquon Barkley left early due to an injury of his own, so Hurts cannot shoulder all the blame for this meager performance. Still, he has thrown for less than 250 yards combined in the last two contests. An intriguing matchup lurks in Week 5 versus the Jags, though.
