Jacksonville has surrendered 280.3 passing yards per game this season, which is second-to-last in the league. In an odd twist, though, the Jags have yielded just three passing scores, which is tied for first in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jalen Hurts struggled again last game for the Eagles. Hurts completed just 21-of-40 passes for 220 yards and a touchdown in the ugly 19-17 loss to the Jaguars. Hurts has yet to throw for 300 yards in a game this season. He also had by far his worst rushing output of the 2026 campaign with only two yards on the ground, perhaps due to a nagging calf issue. In Week 6, Philadelphia will face a curious Carolina Panthers pass defense. Carolina is allowing 230.8 passing yards per tilt, which is 22nd in the NFL. However, the Panthers have yielded just five passing touchdowns, which is tied for fourth in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Hurts enters his seventh NFL season and sixth as the starter in Philadelphia. The 28-year-old tossed a career-high 25 touchdowns last season, but his rushing production was way down (105-421-8 after delivering at least 139 carries, 605 yards and 10 TDs in each of the prior four seasons). Hurts' fantasy production dipped, as his 18.7 points per game was his lowest as a starter and ranked eighth at the position after three straight top-five campaigns. Hurts' supporting cast remains strong (even without A.J. Brown), and new playcaller Sean Mannion very well could add some juice back to the offense. Hurts' fantasy stock is down a bit from years past, but his dual-threat ability locks him in as a midrange QB1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Mike Washington's volume was limited in his NFL debut, but he was productive, gaining 41 rushing yards on seven carries in the Raiders' season-opening win over the Dolphins. The quality of his opposition needs to be taken into account, but it was still a strong showing from the 2026 fourth-round pick. Lead back Ashton Jeanty had a huge game, proving he was fully recovered from a preseason ankle injury, but if he has trouble staying on the field, Washington appears very capable of stepping into a larger role. He'll face a tough matchup in Week 2 against a Chargers defense that ranked second in points per game allowed to RBs in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Mike Washington hasn't seen much action to begin his NFL career, getting 10 carries through the Raiders' first two games and turning them into 48 yards. He also failed to bring in his only target. Ashton Jeanty is locked into the top spot in the backfield and has 54 touches, third in the league behind only Jahmyr Gibbs and Kenneth Walker, and unless he gets hurt, Washington's workload figures to be limited. The rookie will look to take advantage of the chances he does get in Week 3 against a Saints defense that ranks in the bottom four in rushing yards and rushing TDs allowed to RBs so far in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.4: Mike Washington showed off his big-play potential in the Raiders' Week 3 win over the Saints, turning one of his five carries into a 36-yard touchdown. The rookie fourth-round pick hasn't logged big volume behind Ashton Jeanty, but that could begin to change if the starting RB continues to average just 3.3 yards per carry, compared to Washington's 6.8 mark. Until his workload ticks up, Washington will be little more than a dart throw or bench stash for fantasy rosters. He'll face a Kansas City defense in Week 4 that ranks 13th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Mike Washington failed to produce another big play in the Raiders' Week 4 loss to Kansas City, managing only 18 rushing yards on nine carries while catching one of two targets for minus-1 yard. Ashton Jeanty continues to struggle on the ground, but Washington hasn't yet shown enough consistency to be any kind of threat to his workload on early downs. The rookie is averaging 5.0 yards on his first 24 NFL carries, though, well clear of Jeanty's 3.4 mark, so volume could begin to tilt his way a little more if that trend continues. Washington will try to break free in Week 5 against a Patriots defense that ranked 15th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Mike Washington logged a season-low two touches in the Raiders' Week 5 loss to the Patriots, turning one carry and one reception into just 10 scrimmage yards. Ashton Jeanty continues to get a bell-cow workload despite his struggles on the ground, and Washington's 5.0 yards per carry on the season might encourage coach Klint Kubiak to give him more work on early downs. The rookie has flashed his big-play potential, but until he gets more consistent volume, his main value will be as injury insurance behind Jeanty. Washington may not need many touches to contribute in Week 6 against a Bills defense that ranks 28th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Mike Washington is coming off an intriguing showing in the Raiders' Week 6 loss to the Bills, as he turned nine carries into a team-high 43 yards. The rookie remains behind Ashton Jeanty on the running back depth chart, but Washington has been the more effective option on the ground, averaging 4.9 yards per carry on his limited volume while Jeanty has struggled to a 3.2 mark. Washington has posted double-digit touches in two of the last three games as his usage creeps up, but he's unlikely to make a splash in Week 7 against a Rams defense that ranks 11th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Mike Washington remains stuck as the backup to Ashton Jeanty in the Raiders' backfield, despite being more effective on the ground. Through seven games, Jeanty has a woeful 3.1 yards per carry on 106 totes, while Washington has produced 4.9 yards per carry on 40 rushes. Jeanty is the superior pass catcher, however, and coach Klint Kubiak has shown no signs of shifting the two closer to a timeshare. Washington will try to capitalize on his opportunities in Week 8 against a Jets defense that ranks 18th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Mike Washington may be in the process of taking over the early-down role in the Raiders' backfield. The rookie saw a career-high 25 carries in a Week 8 win over the Jets, turning them into 83 yards, while Ashton Jeanty mainly saw usage as a pass catcher and got only two carries. Washington's been far more effective on the ground, averaging 4.3 yards per carry to Jeanty's 3.1 mark, so the move from coach Klint Kubiak seems long overdue. The workload split could tip back toward Jeanty depending on the matchup, and a Week 9 tilt against the 49ers likely favors him over Washington. San Francisco's defense ranks 21st in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs, but 32nd in the league in receptions allowed to the position.

player.seasonOutlook: Washington was selected by the Raiders in the fourth round of April's draft. He's a big back with terrific speed who lit up the combine with a 4.33 40-yard dash at 6-foot-1, 223 pounds (127 speed score), while also checking in with the longest arms in this rookie RB class. His collegiate efficiency wasn't very good during stops in Buffalo and New Mexico State, but it was better in 2025 -- his lone season at Arkansas -- as he averaged 6.41 yards per carry and 3.62 yards after contact, both of which rank seventh or better in this RB class. He might not be much of an option in the passing game, as his career 4.2 yards per target is the worst in this RB class, but his traits make him an intriguing prospect. Washington will open his career as a clear No. 2 option behind Ashton Jeanty, which makes him an intriguing end-of-bench insurance stash.

outlooksByWeek.2: De'Von Achane should again be featured for the Dolphins against the 49ers in Week 2. Achane recorded only 11 carries to open the year, with Miami falling behind early-something that is likely to be a weekly occurrence-but he logged five targets. In Week 1, San Francisco allowed 114 rushing yards and a touchdown plus four receptions to backs, and with Achane rarely leaving the field (88% snap share), the makings are there for a safe outing with scoring upside.
outlooksByWeek.3: De'Von Achane's volume remains elite as the Dolphins get set to host the Chiefs in Week 3. Achane has amassed 31 carries and 11 targets through two weeks, and while his 3.5 yards per carry is modest, there aren't many other options with such a safe workload. Kansas City is allowing 4.0 yards per carry, and they'll surely stack the box against Achane, as everyone else is doing. However, the Chiefs have allowed four catches to an opposing back in consecutive weeks. Achane's volume generates a floor, with scoring providing upside.
outlooksByWeek.4: De'Von Achane will miss the remainder of the season after tearing his ACL. Ollie Gordon and Jaylen Wright will handle the bulk of the Dolphins' carries.

player.seasonOutlook: Achane has quickly staked his claim as one of the best running backs in the league. The 2023 third-round pick has scored either 11 or 12 touchdowns in each of his three seasons and put up a career-high 1,838 scrimmage yards in 2025. Achane's elite receiving production is nothing new (he has finished in the top five among backs in targets and receiving yards in each of the past two years), but he made another leap forward as a rusher last season, finishing fifth at the position in rushing yards. His 5.62 yards per carry is best among qualified backs since he entered the league. The 24-year-old is eyeing his third straight top-five fantasy campaign, and while that might be tricky in an overhauled Miami offense led by quarterback Malik Willis, Achane has minimal competition for touches and should easily be the offensive centerpiece. He's a solid RB1 option.

outlooksByWeek.2: Caleb Douglas will look to build on his Week 1 emergence when the Dolphins face the 49ers in Week 2. Douglas logged an impressive five catches for 94 yards in his NFL debut, garnering seven targets. Miami will likely continue to pass while playing from behind on a weekly basis, and it appears Douglas and QB Malik Willis have a solid connection. San Francisco's defense was stingy against the pass to open the year, allowing just 6.4 yards per target, but volume can reign supreme and Douglas appears to have that potential, making him an intriguing Week 2 option.
outlooksByWeek.3: Caleb Douglas' status for the Dolphins' Week 3 matchup with the Chiefs is uncertain due to an ankle injury. Douglas played a hefty 85% of the team's offensive snaps before suffering the injury late in Week 2 but recorded just 19 yards after a 94-yard career debut. Should he play, Douglas is a speculative upside play for fantasy teams in need of Week 3 help.
outlooksByWeek.4: Caleb Douglas will need to overcome an ankle injury keeping him out of Week 3 to help the Dolphins in Week 4 against the Vikings. After an impressive Week 1, Douglas recorded only three targets in Week 2 despite an 86% snap share. Malik Willis' play under center remains shaky, leading to inconsistency among Miami's receivers. Willis will be scrambling facing a blitz-heavy Vikings defense, but they are allowing generous 8.2 yards per target to opposing wideouts if Douglas is able to push downfield.
outlooksByWeek.5: Caleb Douglas will need to overcome an ankle injury to help the Dolphins against the Bengals in Week 5. He missed the last two weeks, and his role in this low-volume passing offense is questionable; he drew seven targets in Week 1 and only three in Week 2. The Bengals defense is much improved and ranks 14th in points allowed to opposing wideouts, with no receiver topping 63 yards against them. While Douglas can stretch the field, availability and usage remain question marks.
outlooksByWeek.7: Caleb Douglas hopes to emerge from the Dolphins' bye week healthy and help their struggling passing game in Week 7 against the Jets. Douglas hasn't played since Week 2 due to an ankle injury and was used at varying rates when healthy: seven targets in his debut followed by just three the following week. While his 94 yards in Week 1 show potential, uncertain availability and opportunity likely keep him off the radar for lineup consideration against a slightly above-average Jets' secondary that's surrendering 7.3 yards per target.
outlooksByWeek.8: Caleb Douglas appears to be emerging as a big-play option in the Dolphins' low-volume passing game ahead of a Week 8 matchup with the Patriots. Returning from a three-game absence in Week 7, Douglas brought in two of three targets for 70 yards and two touchdowns. He's only caught two balls in two of his three healthy appearances, but is averaging 20.3 yards per catch, and his large frame makes him a potential red zone candidate. If New England jumps out to an early lead, it could help Douglas' snap share, setting him up as a low-floor, high-ceiling option against a defense allowing a generous 8.8 yards per target.

player.seasonOutlook: Douglas was selected by the Dolphins in the third round of April's draft. Douglas is a tall, perimeter receiver with big hands and long arms who, after not seeing much work during two seasons at Florida, exploded for 60-877-6 and 54-846-7 receiving lines at Texas Tech over the last two seasons. His overall efficiency was underwhelming, including six drops and a shaky 1.81 YPRR in 2025. He impressed with a 4.39 40-yard dash at 206 pounds (111 speed score) at the combine. Douglas has a path to a large offensive role as a rookie (Malik Washington, Jalen Tolbert and fellow rookie Chris Bell are his primary competition), but life may be tough in a rebuilding Miami offense led by unproven Malik Willis. He's only worth a late flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Travis Hunter is unlikely to get enough touches on offense to be worth considering in fantasy against Denver's stout defense in Week 2. He had one target and one carry in Jacksonville's season opener, which he turned into 11 scrimmage yards across four snaps on offense while playing primarily on defense. Hunter played both wide receiver and cornerback at Colorado before being drafted second overall by the Jaguars in 2025. With WRs Parker Washington, Brian Thomas, and Jakobi Meyers ahead of him, the versatile Hunter is currently more useful to the Jaguars on defense, much to the chagrin of his fantasy managers.
outlooksByWeek.3: Travis Hunter didn't have a target or carry in Week 2 and has played only a handful of snaps on offense for the Jaguars this season. He's off the fantasy radar heading into a Week 3 home game against the Patriots, outside of IDP formats that reward Hunter's contributions as a cornerback. Parker Washington, Brian Thomas, and Jakobi Meyers should continue to lead Jacksonville's wide receiver room.
outlooksByWeek.4: Travis Hunter hasn't touched the ball on offense in either of Jacksonville's last two games heading into a Week 4 trip to Cincinnati. The 2025 second overall pick has been playing almost exclusively on defense, so Hunter's off the fantasy radar in formats that don't count individual defensive statistics. He's trending up as a cornerback after intercepting Drake Maye in Jacksonville's Week 3 win over the Patriots.
outlooksByWeek.5: Travis Hunter hasn't touched the ball on offense for the Jaguars since Week 1. He played every defensive snap in Week 4 and is focusing primarily on playing cornerback rather than wide receiver. Hunter is a fantasy non-factor except in formats that reward his defensive contributions. Jacksonville will face the Eagles in Week 5 in London, where Hunter showcased his upside on offense last season with eight catches for 101 yards and a TD against the Rams. Don't expect a repeat performance anytime soon, if ever.
outlooksByWeek.6: Travis Hunter got his first offensive touch since Week 1 during the Jaguars' Week 5 win over the Eagles, but he's being used as a full-time defensive player while barely seeing the field on offense. Barring a rash of injuries at wide receiver, the Jaguars will likely remain content using Hunter primarily at cornerback. He has enough talent to warrant a bench stash if you have space on the roster, but he isn't an appealing fantasy option in Week 6 against the Texans unless your league counts defensive contributions.
outlooksByWeek.8: Travis Hunter had his best offensive performance of the season in Week 6 against the Texans prior to Jacksonville's Week 7 bye, catching all four of his targets for 59 yards and a touchdown. He remains a full-time defensive player, but Hunter's offensive opportunities have increased in recent weeks. The former two-way college football star tied his season high with six snaps on offense in Week 5 against the Eagles before setting a new high with nine snaps against Houston in Week 6. Hunter is a risky fantasy option due to his limited opportunities, but he has the talent to make the most of his chances and is at least a viable dart throw in deeper formats in Week 8 against a Colts defense that's giving up 25.7 points per game.
outlooksByWeek.9: Travis Hunter has touched the ball on offense at least once in each of Jacksonville's last three games. The full-time cornerback is slowly increasing his role on offense heading into a Week 9 game against the Ravens, but he still isn't playing enough to warrant consideration in fantasy formats that don't reward his defensive contributions. Hunter has put forth just one fantasy starter-worthy performance this season on offense, catching all four of his targets for 59 yards and a TD in Week 6 against the Texans.

player.seasonOutlook: Full-time focus on defense should unlock rewarding production from a unique talent. Not only can Hunter mirror receivers, he frequently turns his head to track the ball, leading to big plays in coverage.

outlooksByWeek.2: Brian Robinson is expected to operate as the Falcons' No. 2 running back in the Week 2 matchup against the Panthers. Despite playing behind Bijan Robinson, Brian Robinson could have material fantasy value this week, as Carolina's defense allowed 291 rushing yards and six touchdowns in Week 1. Additionally, Robinson received nine carries in the Week 1 loss to the Steelers, which is solid volume for a complementary role. He could find value with the Panthers giving up 52.8 PPR fantasy points to the running back position last week.
outlooksByWeek.3: Brian Robinson (ankle) will operate as the Falcons' No. 2 running back if active for the Week 3 matchup against the Packers. Robinson logged 13 touches in Atlanta's Week 2 loss to the Panthers, but eight of those came in the fourth quarter -- suggesting he's still firmly the second option at RB. The Alabama product has been efficient, however, averaging 4.1 yards per carry through two weeks. He's also in for a favorable matchup, with the Packers defense allowing 22.9 PPR fantasy per game to RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Brian Robinson is expected to continue operating as the Falcons' No. 2 running back in the Week 4 matchup against the Saints. Robinson had his best performance of the season in the Week 3 win over the Packers, rushing 10 times for 50 yards and a touchdown. Despite playing behind Bijan Robinson, Brian Robinson has managed to be extremely efficient when given opportunities, averaging 4.6 yards per touch. He's also in for a favorable Week 4 matchup against a New Orleans defense that's given up 4.8 yards per carry this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Brian Robinson is expected to remain involved in Atlanta's offensive game plan in the Week 5 matchup against the Ravens. Robinson had his best game of the season in the Week 4 win over the Saints, accumulating 67 yards on 15 touches while scoring three touchdowns. The Alabama product has now logged double-digit carries in three straight games, suggesting that he's established himself as a valuable portion of this Falcons offense. Expect Robinson to remain Atlanta's No. 2 running back behind Bijan Robinson in a tougher Week 5 matchup against a Baltimore defense that's given up just 3.8 yards per carry to RBs this year.
outlooksByWeek.6: Brian Robinson is expected to remain the Falcons' No. 2 running back in the Week 6 matchup against the Bears. Robinson was ineffective in the Week 5 overtime loss, accumulating just 16 yards on seven carries (2.3 yards per carry). Through five contests this season, Robinson has averaged 42 rushing yards per game, with most of his value coming from touchdowns (four on the season). He could struggle in Week 6 against a Bears defense that's given up just 409 rushing yards to RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Brian Robinson is expected to remain the Falcons' No. 2 running back in the Week 7 matchup against the 49ers. Robinson was held to just three touches during the Week 6 loss to the Bears, mostly because of the Falcons large deficit early in the game. On the season, Robinson has rushed 53 times for 211 yards and four touchdowns while catching five of six targets for an additional 30 yards. He could struggle finding the end zone in Week 7, however, as San Francisco's defense has given up just three total touchdowns to RBs through five games.
outlooksByWeek.8: Brian Robinson (hamstring) will operate as Atlanta's No. 2 running back if active for the Week 8 matchup against the Buccaneers. Robinson was sidelined for the Falcons' Week 7 win over the 49ers but has been a major part of the team's offense throughout the year. Despite playing behind Bijan Robinson, Brian Robinson has tallied 211 rushing yards, 30 receiving yards and four touchdowns in six contests. Even if he returns for the Week 8 divisional matchup, Robinson could struggle against a tough Buccaneers defense that's given up just 3.6 yards per carry this season.
outlooksByWeek.9: Brian Robinson (hamstring) is expected to operate as the Falcons' No. 2 running back if active for the Week 9 matchup against the Bengals. Robinson has been sidelined for two consecutive games due to a hamstring issue. However, he's been an effective runner when healthy, averaging 4.0 yards per carry and rushing for four touchdowns in six appearances this season. Despite this, he'll likely need to find the end zone to be fantasy relevant against a Bengals defense that's given up just 19.7 fantasy points per game to opposing running backs this year.

player.seasonOutlook: After a one-year stint as Christian McCaffrey's backup in San Francisco, Robinson signed with Atlanta where he'll now operate as a change-of-pace back behind Bijan Robinson. The 2022 third-round pick soaked up 200-plus touches in each of his first three NFL seasons (all with Washington) prior to dipping to 100 touches in 2025. Robinson is a big back who can handle early-down and short-yardage work, but he's not much of a factor as a receiver (92 career targets). He's yet to post a top-20 fantasy campaign and he won't come close to that in 2026 unless Bijan Robinson suffers a major injury. The 27-year-old back is no more than a solid insurance stash.

outlooksByWeek.2: Mike Gesicki and the Bengals are on the road in Week 2 to take on Houston. The Texans have the 27th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (19.7) to TEs, and they are last in receiving yards allowed to the position after Dalton Kincaid and Dawson Knox combined for 137 yards last week. Gesicki led the Bengals in catches (5), targets (7), and receiving yards (78) in Week 1, to go along with one TD. He could be primed for another big performance in what may very well be another high-scoring affair.
outlooksByWeek.3: Mike Gesicki and the Bengals are in Pittsburgh for an AFC North showdown in Week 3. After leading Cincinnati in receptions, yards, and targets in the season opener, Gesicki failed to record a single target versus the Texans in Week 2. Some of that could be chalked up to game flow with the Bengals ahead for most of the game, but it's nonetheless worrisome. The Steelers rank second in fantasy points allowed per game (5.5) and are first in receptions allowed to TEs through two weeks.
outlooksByWeek.4: Mike Gesicki and the Bengals welcome the 2-1 Jaguars to town in Week 4. He caught all three of his targets for 37 yards and a touchdown during Cincinnati's 30-27 loss in Week 3. Gesicki finished third in receiving yards while catching his second TD of the young season, just one week after failing to earn a target. Jacksonville's defense ranks fifth in fantasy points allowed (7.8) and second in receptions (8) to TEs, so he could be in for another quiet day.
outlooksByWeek.5: Mike Gesicki and the Bengals travel to take on the winless Dolphins in Week 5. He grabbed three of five targets for 40 yards and a touchdown during Cincinnati's Week 4 loss. Gesicki now has two straight outings with a TD and recorded his third overall, and he could be in line for an uptick in opportunities in a favorable matchup versus a Miami defense that allows 18.6 fantasy points to TEs, which is tied for 28th. Ja'Marr Chase (concussion), Tee Higgins (adductor), and Colbie Young (knee) are all questionable, potentially leaving Gesicki as one of Joe Burrow's primary receivers against a Dolphins unit that just gave up 13 receptions and 119 yards to T.J. Hockenson
outlooksByWeek.7: Mike Gesicki and the Bengals are in Baltimore for an AFC North clash in Week 7. He caught one of two targets for a four-yard touchdown during Cincinnati's 31-24 win in Week 5. Fellow tight end Erick All Jr. notched a 3-25-0 line on three targets, finishing second on the team in yardage. Gesicki is hard to trust with Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) and Tee Higgins (adductor) healthy, especially versus a Baltimore defense tied for seventh in fantasy points allowed per game (10.5) to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Mike Gesicki and the Bengals host the 1-6 Titans in Week 8. He caught his only target for a six-yard touchdown during Cincinnati's 35-13 victory over Baltimore. Gesicki extended his TD streak to four consecutive games, as he's now compiled a 13-165-5 receiving line on 18 targets in 2026. He'll try to make it five in a row versus Tennessee's eighth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per contest (11.1) to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Mike Gesicki and the Bengals are in Spain for a Week 9 interconference tilt against the Falcons. He caught four of six targets for 76 yards and a touchdown during Cincinnati's 43-36 overtime win in Week 8. The 76 receiving yards were Gesicki's most in a game since he went for 78 in the season opener, and the 31-year-old was able to extend his streak of outings with a TD catch to five. He now owns a 17-241-6 line on 24 targets through seven contests and will try to make it six straight with a score versus an Atlanta defense allowing 14.4 fantasy points per game (T-20th) to TEs.

player.seasonOutlook: There was an era when Gesicki was a viable starting option in fantasy, but that time has come and gone. Since posting back-to-back top-eight fantasy campaigns in 2020 and 2021, Gesicki has finished 23rd, 37th, 13th and 41st the past four seasons. The latter came during a 2025 campaign in which he was limited to 41 targets in 13 games. Gesicki is no more than a situational seam stretcher and not much of an option near the goal line (he has exactly two TDs and five end zone targets each of the past three seasons). The 30-year-old will be a risky streaming option even if Ja'Marr Chase or Tee Higgins misses time.

outlooksByWeek.2: Ryan Flournoy managed two catches for 22 yards on four targets in the Week 1 loss for Dallas to the Giants. Flournoy finished fourth on the team in targets for the game. The Dallas passing attack struggled as a whole, leaving no receiver with more than 45 yards receiving in the contest. In Week 2, the Cowboys will look to rebound versus the Commanders. Washington only allowed 182 passing yards in its season opener, though did give up three passing scores to Philadelphia quarterback Jalen Hurts.
outlooksByWeek.3: Ryan Flournoy managed six targets last game for Dallas. Flournoy parlayed those looks into five catches for 23 yards. Flournoy was third in targets behind CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. In Week 3, Dallas hosts the Baltimore Ravens. Baltimore is allowing just 191 passing yards per contest, which is 12th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Ryan Flournoy tied for the second on the Cowboys in targets last game. Flournoy saw eight balls thrown his way, though managed just two catches in the 34-31 loss to the Ravens. Flournoy also gained just 22 yards for the game; in fact, he has yet to gain more than 25 yards in any contest in 2026. In Week 4, Dallas faces a Houston defense that has been surprisingly subpar against the pass.  The Texans are allowing 238.7 passing yards per clash, which is 25th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Ryan Flournoy has been targeted at least four times in every game this season for the Cowboys. However, he has yet to cross 40 yards receiving in any contest. Versus the Texans, he had four catches but only for a season-high 37 yards. With a lot of mouths to feed like CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens and even tight end Jake Ferguson, Flournoy's output may continue to be depressed. In Week 5, Dallas will face a Tampa Bay defense that has been fairly stingy against the pass in terms of yardage. The Bucs are allowing just 204.3 passing yards per tilt, which is ninth in the NFL. However, Tampa Bay has also given up seven throwing scores, which is tied for 23rd in the league. Flournoy is still looking for his first score of the season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Ryan Flournoy set a season high in receiving yardage last game for the Cowboys. Flournoy brought in three passes for 90 yards in the 24-16 loss to the Bucs. CeeDee Lamb was dealing with a quadriceps issue, which also likely contributed to Flournoy's success. However, Lamb's injury does not appear serious, which would knock Flournoy back down the pecking order in Week 6 versus the Packers. Green Bay's defense is also allowing just 181 passing yards per contest, which is fifth in the league. Likewise, the Packers have surrendered only six passing touchdowns on the season, which is tied for 10th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Ryan Flournoy found the end zone last game for Dallas. Flournoy reeled in seven passes for 40 yards and the score in the 23-13 loss to the Packers. Flournoy has at least four targets in every game this season, though has gone over 40 yards receiving just once. He remains firmly behind CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens heading into a Week 7 clash with Philly. The Eagles are allowing 244.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 26th in the NFL. However, Philadelphia has given up just eight passing scores in 2026, which is tied for 14th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.8: Ryan Flournoy was second on the Cowboys in receiving yards last game. Flournoy reeled in four passes for 70 yards in the 38-21 win over the Eagles. Flournoy has at least three catches in four-straight contests. In Week 8, the Cowboys will face an Arizona Cardinals defense that has been prone to surrendering the touchdown pass. In fact, Arizona has given up 17 passing scores, which is dead last in the NFL. The Cardinals are also giving up 228 passing yards per tilt, which is 20th in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Flournoy is an intriguing deep sleeper as the favorite for No. 3 wide receiver duties behind CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens in Dallas. Flournoy flashed in 2025, putting up 14.2 fantasy PPG during the only five games in which his route participation was at least 60%. Flournoy did disappear quite a bit behind the heavily targeted Lamb and Pickens (three or fewer targets in seven of his final 10 games), so he's a long shot for standalone fantasy value even if he locks down the No. 3 gig. The 26-year-old should be added to rosters only if Lamb or Pickens are sidelined.

Run defense was the Bills' undoing last season, as they allowed a league-worst 24 rushing scores and snapped a seven-year streak of placing among the position's top 10 in fantasy points scored. Jim Leonhard was brought in as defensive coordinator, switching from a 4-3 to 3-4 scheme, though the team's personnel remains light up front. Regard the Bills a D/ST streaming candidate, and one better to leave undrafted due to their rough early schedule (@HOU, DET, LAC, NE, @LAR).

outlooksByWeek.2: Quentin Johnston wasn't able to get much going in the Chargers' season-opening loss to the Cardinals, catching just two of his six targets for 17 yards. The entire passing game under new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel wasn't yet in rhythm aside from Ladd McConkey, and he was knocked out of the game in the third quarter with a rib injury. The injury doesn't appear to be serious, but if McConkey isn't able to play in Week 2, Johnston could be the biggest beneficiary when it comes to additional volume from Justin Herbert. Johnston will face a Raiders secondary in Week 2 that was tied for 21st in PPR points per game allowed to WRs last season.
outlooksByWeek.3: Quentin Johnston has struggled through the Chargers' first two games, catching just three of 11 targets for 24 yards. The fourth-year wideout had emerged as a deep option over the prior two seasons, but new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme is built on quick passes and yards after the catch, giving little time for Johnston's typical downfield routes to develop. Tre' Harris and rookie speedster Brenan Thompson both seem better suited to that style of passing game, and Johnston runs a real risk of becoming an afterthought as the season progresses. He does at least get a potentially favorable matchup in Week 3 against a Bills secondary that's given up the fourth-most receiving yards to WRs so far this year.
outlooksByWeek.4: Quentin Johnston could be in danger of losing his spot as the Chargers' No. 2 wide receiver. The 2023 first-round pick leads the team with 17 targets through three games, but that volume has resulted in just a 6-64-0 line, and Johnston has been unable to take advantage of Ladd McConkey's limitations due to a rib injury. Second-year WR Tre' Harris did in Week 3, suggesting he could be about to move past Johnston in the pecking order. Johnston will have a hard time building any momentum in Week 4 against a Seahawks secondary that ranks fourth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Quentin Johnston saw only two targets in the Chargers' Week 4 loss to the Seahawks, but he was able to turn one of them into a 44-yard gain for his only catch. The season-low volume was especially disappointing given that Ladd McConkey left the game early with a foot injury. The passing game as a whole is struggling, and Johnston could end up getting passed on the depth chart by Tre' Harris if he doesn't begin to make a more consistent impact. Johnston will try to earn more look from Justin Herbert in Week 5 against a Broncos secondary that ranks eighth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs, but which could be missing its top two cornerbacks including Patrick Surtain.
outlooksByWeek.6: Quentin Johnston was unable to play through a chest injury in the Chargers' Week 5 loss to the Broncos, missing his first game of the season. The fourth-year wideout has just a 7-108-0 line on 19 targets in four contests, and the team's offensive struggles under coordinator Mike McDaniel have dragged down essentially every skill player on the roster. If Johnston returns in Week 6, it will be for a brutal matchup against a Kansas City secondary that ranks first in the NFL in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Quentin Johnston has struggled this season along with the rest of the Chargers' offense, catching only one pass in three of his five games and failing to reach 60 receiving yards or score a TD in any of them. He has had receptions of 40-plus yards in each of his last two contests, however, reaffirming that he does have some big-play upside. Johnston faces a tough test in Week 8 against a Rams secondary that ranks fifth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Quentin Johnston remains mostly an afterthought in the Chargers' struggling passing game. The fourth-year wide receiver caught a season-high four passes in a Week 8 loss to the Rams, but turned them into just 37 receiving yards. Johnston hasn't seen more than six targets in any of his six appearances this year, piecing together a 12-202-0 line on 26 targets. He might be able to make an impact on limited volume in Week 9 against an underperforming Texans secondary that ranks a stunning 30th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Four weeks into the 2025 season, it appeared Johnston was on the verge of a breakout campaign. The 2023 first-round pick found the end zone four times and scored 14-plus fantasy points in each game during the span. The return to earth was abrupt, as Johnston went on to average 9.2 PPG in his final 10 games. The 25-year-old has posted consistent receiving lines in each of the last two seasons (55-724-8 and 51-735-8), but neither resulted in a top-30 fantasy campaign. The Chargers offense should be better in 2026 with a healthy line and Mike McDaniel calling plays, but Johnston is unlikely to see a big boost in usage with the likes of Ladd McConkey and sophomores Tre Harris and Omarion Hampton also in the fold. Johnston is no more than a boom/bust flex in deeper leagues.

outlooksByWeek.5: Tank Dell (knee) is expected to have his practice window opened ahead of the Texans' Week 5 road game against the Titans. The 2023 third-round pick hasn't played since sustaining a significant knee injury in Week 16 of the 2024 season. Dell is currently on injured reserve and will likely take some time to ramp up. He's unlikely to return in Week 5 against Tennessee, but forward-looking fantasy managers should take notice of Dell's impending return, as he averaged 55 receiving yards and scored 10 TDs in 25 games prior to his injury.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tank Dell (knee) had his 21-day return window opened ahead of Houston's Week 5 win over the Titans and has rejoined his teammates at practice but remains on injured reserve ahead of the team's Week 6 trip to London to face the Jaguars. Considering the Texans just traded for WR Marvin Harrison, Dell seems unlikely to be a major contributor in Week 6, even if he is activated from IR. Dell isn't viable in Week 6 but could be worth stashing if you have an open bench or IR slot, as Houston's 2023 third-round pick averaged 55 receiving yards and scored 10 TDs in 25 games prior to sustaining a major knee injury late in the 2024 season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tank Dell (knee) had his 21-day window to return from IR opened ahead of Houston's Week 5 win over the Titans, and he has a realistic chance of being activated ahead of the Week 7 home game against the Giants after sitting out against the Titans in Week 5 and the Jaguars in Week 6. Even if Dell suits up in Week 7, he's likely to be brought along slowly in a Texans WR room that also has Nico Collins, Marvin Harrison, Jaylin Noel, Xavier Hutchinson, and Kayshon Boutte vying for playing time. Dell is a viable bench stash, but he isn't a recommended starting option against the Giants.
outlooksByWeek.9: Tank Dell made his season debut in Week 7, ahead of Houston's Week 8 bye. The 2023 third-round pick showcased his trademark big-play ability with a 43-yard catch on his only target. This was Dell's first game action since Week 16 of the 2024 campaign due to a knee injury. The Texans also have Nico Collins, Marvin Harrison, Xavier Hutchinson, and Kayshon Boutte vying for snaps at wide receiver, which makes Dell a risky Week 9 fantasy option against the Chargers. The Chargers rank in the middle of the pack at defending WRs. Dell is worth stashing on the bench, as he delivered starter-level fantasy production prior to his extended absence, but he'll need to increase his involvement to regain fantasy relevance.

player.seasonOutlook: Dell is on the comeback trail after suffering a devastating knee injury late in 2024 that cost him the entire 2025 season. It was a tough break for the 2023 third-round pick, who finished 18th among receivers in fantasy PPG as a rookie. While he wasn't quite as productive the next season, he was on pace for career highs in catches and yardage. The undersized Dell is certainly a question mark off the major injury, but, with Jayden Higgins out for the 2026 season, he has a path back to a role behind Nico Collins at some point this year. The 26-year-old will begin on injured reserve, but he'll be a fine end-of-bench stash once activated.

outlooksByWeek.2: Baker Mayfield will look to rebound from a tough Week 1 performance in Tampa Bay's Week 2 matchup against the Browns. Mayfield threw for 216 yards while adding a rushing touchdown last week, but he fumbled three times and struggled to finish drives. He should be in for a very favorable Week 2 matchup against a Browns defense that allowed 28.3 fantasy points to quarterbacks and four passing touchdowns in Week 1. If Mayfield isn't able to respond with a solid fantasy performance in a clear revenge game, there could be doubts about his reliability moving forward.
outlooksByWeek.3: Baker Mayfield is set for a difficult Week 3 matchup when the Buccaneers take on the Vikings, whose defense has allowed 20.6 fantasy points per game to quarterbacks this season. Mayfield has really struggled during Tampa Bay's first two contests, accounting for just two touchdowns while turning the ball over four times. He's thrown for just 184.5 passing yards per game while completing 71 percent of his passes. Additionally, he's in for a tough Week 3 matchup, with Minnesota's defense giving up just 12.5 points per game this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Baker Mayfield (thumb) will operate as the Buccaneers' signal caller if active for the Week 7 matchup against the Panthers. Mayfield has been sidelined for Tampa Bay's last three contests, but head coach Todd Bowles told reporters he's "supposed to practice" Wednesday, suggesting he could return Sunday. Before the injury, Mayfield struggled in his first three games, throwing for 615 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions while also losing three fumbles. However, he could bounce back against a Panthers defense that's allowed 22.0 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season.
outlooksByWeek.8: Baker Mayfield is expected to lead the Buccaneers' offense into the Week 8 matchup against the Falcons. Mayfield had a very light workload in his return from injury in the Week 7 win over the Panthers, completing seven of 11 pass attempts for 64 yards and a touchdown. In his first three games this season, Mayfield threw for an average of 205 yards, 0.7 touchdowns and 0.7 interceptions per contest. He'll look to catch fire against a Falcons defense that's given up 21.2 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season.
outlooksByWeek.9: Baker Mayfield is expected to lead the Buccaneers' passing game into the Week 9 matchup against the Bears. He was the first quarterback since 1974 to win a game without completing a single pass, doing so in a rainy Week 8 divisional matchup against the Falcons. Since returning from injury in Week 7, Mayfield has attempted just 14 total passes, partially due to last week's rainy conditions. However, offensive coordinator Zac Robinson has heavily leaned on the ground game over the last four weeks, which is a poor sign for Mayfield's fantasy outlook. Mayfield is still in for a favorable Week 9 matchup against a Bears defense that has allowed 22.3 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks through seven contests.

player.seasonOutlook: Mayfield is back for Year 4 as Tampa Bay's starting quarterback. He has put together three consecutive top-12 fantasy campaigns, though his 2025 season (12th in total points, but 19th in points per game) was a big step back from 2024 (fourth overall and per game). Mayfield tossed 26 touchdowns (way down from 41 in 2024) and severely lacked upside, managing only four top-10 fantasy weeks. Granted, the 31-year-old was not fully healthy throughout the season and did still finish in the top 10 at the position in key categories, including passing yards, passing TDs and rushing yards. With a solid supporting cast and Zac Robinson as playcaller, Mayfield has some rebound potential and does just enough with his legs to make him an appealing QB2 target.

outlooksByWeek.2: Keon Coleman doesn't appear to have a meaningful role in the Bills' offense entering Week 2 against the Lions. Despite playing 52% of the team's offensive snaps, Coleman drew only one target, which resulted in a one-yard catch. Always a candidate for an end-zone jump ball, Coleman is no better than fourth in the target pecking order, suggesting he's unlikely to contribute despite an inviting matchup against a secondary that allowed 410 passing yards in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Keon Coleman will look to build on a mild breakout when the Bills face the Chargers in Week 3. He hauled in six passes last week, his highest total since Week 1 of 2025, as the Bills lost DJ Moore (shoulder) early in Week 2. The Chargers have been more vulnerable to slot options than bigger outside receivers, and Moore's availability remains in flux. With the Bills offense clicking at all levels, Coleman can still garner enough volume to be a deep-league flex consideration.
outlooksByWeek.4: Keon Coleman's role in the Bills offense remains limited ahead of a Week 4 matchup with the Patriots. Dealing with a Week 3 ankle injury, Coleman caught a 37-yard pass on two targets, a significant decrease in volume with DJ Moore healthy. Moore dominates targets and Buffalo is a run-first offense. Facing a defense that's allowing a mere 6.6 yards per target, there may not be enough opportunities for Coleman to contribute.
outlooksByWeek.5: Keon Coleman's role in the Bills offense remains unsettled ahead of a Week 5 matchup with the Rams. DJ Moore exited Week 4 after aggravating a shoulder injury that forced a similar result in Week 2, and Coleman again shined. In the two games with Moore leaving early, Coleman has 12 catches on 13 targets for 179 yards and a touchdown. With Moore playing four quarters, Coleman has two catches for 38 yards. Facing a defense that hasn't allowed an opposing receiver to top 50 yards leaves Coleman as a fantasy risk regardless of Moore's status.
outlooksByWeek.6: Keon Coleman brings inconsistent volume in the Bills' passing game into a Week 6 matchup with the Raiders. Coleman saw just two targets in Week 5 despite the absence of DJ Moore, marking the third time in five outings he's drawn that limited amount of volume. Buffalo remains a run-first offense and while Coleman has shown red zone and downfield ability, the lack of consistent volume leads to volatility against a Las Vegas secondary that's allowing the 11th-most fantasy points to opposing wideouts, though has been more vulnerable over the middle of late than to boundary receivers.
outlooksByWeek.8: Keon Coleman will try to extend his scoring streak to four games when Buffalo hosts the Ravens in Week 8. Despite his nose for the end zone, Coleman hasn't collected steady volume, three times being limited to just one catch, though more consistent opportunities have come with DJ Moore (shoulder) sidelined. Coming out of a bye, Moore likely is the healthiest he's been in some time, which may result in fewer snaps for Coleman. Should he remain involved, Baltimore has allowed three 100-yard games to outside receivers over the last four weeks, setting Coleman up for a potential productive outing.
outlooksByWeek.9: Keon Coleman will benefit if DJ Moore is sidelined ahead of the Bills' Week 9 matchup with the Vikings. Coleman was held to just one catch in Week 8, the fourth time that's occurred in seven games, with three of those coinciding with Moore on the field. Moore is again dealing with a knee issue that's believed to be minor, but even if he's unable to play in Week 9, Coleman's potential against a defense that's allowed only four touchdown passes in seven games likely isn't appealing.

player.seasonOutlook: So far, so bust for Coleman, who has struggled to make an impact after being selected 33rd overall in the 2024 draft. After flashing in a situational deep-threat role as a rookie (15.0 aDOT), Coleman saw more high percentage looks in 2025 (11.2 aDOT). That led to a much better catch rate (from 51% to 66%), but a big dip in yardage (19.2 YPR to 10.9). Coleman has yet to emerge as a reliable, full-time starter and was even a healthy scratch at times last season. Perhaps the 23-year-old will make a Year 3 leap with Joe Brady now running the show, but he'll have his hands full overtaking DJ Moore and Khalil Shakir atop the depth chart. Coleman is only worth a late flier in deeper leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: Malik Willis looks to rebound from a shaky debut when the Dolphins again travel west to face the 49ers in Week 2. Willis was held without a touchdown pass in his first start for his new team, and while the rushing volume was lower than expected, he scampered for a touchdown. It's a challenging road spot against a defense that allowed just 168 yards passing and no scores in their opener, but game flow should remain positive for Willis to flirt with fantasy-worthy production. Miami will likely play from behind, necessitating throws, and dropbacks will continue to lead to rushing yards when pressured.
outlooksByWeek.3: Malik Willis figures to labor again in Week 3 when the Dolphins host the Chiefs. He has yet to top 220 yards or complete more than 15 passes through two games, and his rushing attempts haven't been as plentiful as anticipated. Any potential late production while playing from behind has also failed to manifest, and that game script figures to repeat in Week 3 against Kansas City, a defense that's allowed only 341 passing yards, two touchdown passes, and 12 rushing yards this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Malik Willis will be under heavy pressure when the Dolphins face the Vikings in Week 4. Willis has just one touchdown pass through three weeks and has surprisingly topped 40 yards with his legs just once. Minnesota is the heaviest blitzing team in the league, so Willis will likely need his mobility often in Week 4. Without De'Von Achane (knee) and no emerging receivers, scrambling appears his only path to production against a defense that's allowing 7.0 yards per attempt while also allowing three touchdowns with four interceptions.
outlooksByWeek.5: Malik Willis will seek a breakthrough outing in Week 5 when the Dolphins face the Bengals. He has accounted for just two total touchdowns through four games and completed a mere nine passes for 85 yards in Week 4, both season-lows. An improved Cincinnati defense has allowed only four touchdown passes, but all of them have come over the last two weeks. With Miami's defense likely to give up points, Willis will at least have the opportunity to produce at a higher level than he's shown thus far.
outlooksByWeek.7: Malik Willis hopes to emerge from the Dolphins' bye week with answers to get their offense in gear during a Week 7 matchup with the Jets. He has been held under 200 yards passing in three of his five games and has only two touchdown passes but has shown signs of his dual-threat capability, averaging 47.0 rushing yards over his last three contests. The Jets have allowed the eighth-fewest fantasy points to quarterbacks thus far, surrendering only nine touchdown passes and 92 rushing yards in six games, boding poorly for Willis's chances to shine.
outlooksByWeek.8: Malik Willis needs his legs to create a fantasy-relevant outing in Week 8 when the Dolphins face the Patriots. He has rushed for a touchdown in consecutive games and has at least eight carries in three of four contests, while also coming off his first multi-touchdown passing effort of the season. New England has only allowed nine touchdown passes and 70 total rushing yards to quarterbacks, suggesting Willis faces an uphill battle for counting stats. However, game flow could force additional passing volume assuming Miami falls behind early, creating a path to fantasy production.
outlooksByWeek.9: Malik Willis will look to extend his multi-touchdown pass streak to three games in an inviting Week 9 matchup for the Dolphins against the Lions. Willis isn't taking many downfield chances, limiting him to a season-high of 220 passing yards, but he has four touchdowns over the last two weeks after just two in his first five games prior to Miami's Week 6 bye. Detroit has been the league's worst defense against quarterbacks, surrendering 18 touchdown passes through seven games, and while Willis hasn't run as often as expected, he'll carry some intrigue as a potential Week 9 streaming option in deeper formats.

player.seasonOutlook: Willis signed with Miami during the offseason and is set to start after two successful seasons backing up Jordan Love in Green Bay. Willis, a 2022 third-round pick, has very little experience (155 career pass attempts), but he was outstanding in limited work the past two seasons, completing 70 of 89 passes for 972 yards, six TDs and zero INTs (12.1 yards per attempt, 86% completion rate), while also adding major value with his legs (42-261-3) during the span. Willis played at least 80% of the snaps in three games with Green Bay and averaged 23.3 fantasy points in those outings. Willis' inexperience makes him risky and the Miami supporting cast is perhaps the worst in the NFL, but his dual-threat ability makes him a very fascinating late-round flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Evan McPherson will look to stay perfect when the Bengals visit the Texans in Week 2. He nailed all four of his field-goal attempts, including kicks of 55 and 58 yards, and made all three PATs during Cincinnati's 33-27 win in the season opener. McPherson should remain a top fantasy kicker as a member of one of the NFL's elite offenses. Houston gave up 36 points and 409 total yards in their Week 1 loss to the Bills.
outlooksByWeek.3: Evan McPherson and the Bengals visit the Steelers for an AFC North divisional matchup in Week 3. He remained perfect on the season after connecting on both of his field-goal attempts and both PATs during Cincinnati's Week 2 win over Houston. McPherson drilled both of his field goals from 50-plus yards out, and he's now 6-for-6 on the season, with four of his makes coming beyond 50 yards. He'll continue to earn plenty of scoring opportunities on an elite offense, even despite Pittsburgh's strong defense.
outlooksByWeek.4: Evan McPherson and the Bengals host the 2-1 Jaguars in Week 4. He stayed perfect on the year after drilling both field-goal attempts and all three PATs during Cincinnati's 30-27 loss in Week 3. McPherson is now 8-for-8 on FGAs and extra-point tries, including five kicks from at least 50 yards out. He'll aim to stay hot against one of the league's best defenses, as Jacksonville allows just 12.0 points per game, which ranks first. Still, McPherson should continue seeing plenty of scoring opportunities for a Bengals squad averaging 26.7 PPG (12th).
outlooksByWeek.5: Evan McPherson and the Bengals visit the Dolphins for a Week 5 road tilt. He made his only field-goal attempt from 29 yards out and connected on both of his PATs during Cincinnati's 22-17 loss in Week 4. McPherson remained perfect on his kicks through four outings, but he'll hope to get more involved against a Miami defense that ranks 21st in the league, allowing 25.3 points per game.
outlooksByWeek.7: Evan McPherson and the Bengals travel to face the Ravens for an AFC North clash in Week 7. He made his lone field-goal attempt and all four of his PATs during Cincinnati's 31-24 win in Week 5. McPherson was forced to do his damage with extra points, as the victory marked his second straight outing with only one FGA. He'll look to make more of an impact against a Baltimore defense allowing 22.0 points per game, which ranks 15th.
outlooksByWeek.8: Evan McPherson and the Bengals return home for a Week 8 showdown against the 1-6 Titans. He did not attempt a field goal but converted all five of his extra-point tries during Cincinnati's 35-13 win in Week 7. McPherson is perfect through six contests this season, going 10-for-10 on FGs and 19-for-19 on PATs. However, with the Bengals offense routinely finding the endzone, his opportunities to make a big fantasy difference have suffered.
outlooksByWeek.9: Evan McPherson and the Bengals travel to take on the Falcons for a Week 9 interconference tilt in Spain. He made all five of his PATs for the second consecutive game during Cincinnati's 43-36 overtime victory in Week 8. It was also the second time in as many weeks that McPherson did not attempt a field goal, as Joe Burrow and the Bengals offense racked up six total TDs in the win. McPherson has yet to miss a single kick in 2026, going 10-for-10 on FGs and 24-for-24 on PATs, but his fantasy ceiling is seemingly capped with Cincinnati frequently finding the endzone.

player.seasonOutlook: Hill is currently a free agent after being released by Miami. One of the top fantasy players of the past decade, Hill's best days may be behind him as he enters his age-32 campaign. The former fifth-round pick was fantasy's top-scoring receiver from 2017-23, but struggled to an 18th-place finish in 2024 (31st PPG) and then suffered a season-ending knee injury in Week 4 of last season. If he's able to play in 2026, Hill may still be able to hit for the occasional explosive play, but considering his age and the major injury, his ceiling is likely that of a boom/bust flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kenyon Sadiq could have an emerging role for the Jets in Week 2 against the Packers. Sadiq notched four touches in his NFL debut, including a three-yard rushing score, out-gaining starter Mason Taylor handsomely in a run-heavy game for the Jets. They'll likely need to throw more to keep up with Green Bay's offense in Week 2, and the Packers allowed a touchdown to a tight end last week. The floor is volatile, but Sadiq offers high ceiling potential for those in need at tight end.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kenyon Sadiq could be poised for a major breakout for the Jets in Week 3 if Mason Taylor (thumb) is unable to play against the Lions. Sadiq has played just 42% and 38% of the offensive snaps through two games, easing into the rotation after recovering from hernia surgery prior to the year. The Jets' offense isn't prolific, but the matchup with a porous Lions' defense could change that. Detroit has allowed two touchdown catches to opposing tight ends in each of the first two weeks and 187 total yards, the second-highest total across the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kenyon Sadiq could struggle to build on a breakout performance in Week 4 when the Jets face the Bears. After recording just six targets in his first two games, Sadiq shined in Week 3, catching seven of eight targets for 105 yards and a touchdown, despite playing just 56% of the offensive snaps in Mason Taylor's absence. The Bears have not allowed an opposing tight end to top 30 yards this season, with teams finding more success targeting their corners, so a repeat performance may be challenging.
outlooksByWeek.5: Kenyon Sadiq faces an unsettled role in the Jets' limited passing game ahead of a Week 5 matchup with the Browns. After a Week 3 breakthrough performance, Sadiq failed to record a catch on four targets in Week 4 and now has 21 or fewer yards in three of his first four games. The Browns haven't allowed an opposing tight end to top 51 yards while surrendering just 6.7 yards per target, not boding well for Sadiq in Week 5. A potential Mason Taylor return would further dampen Sadiq's potential.
outlooksByWeek.6: Kenyon Sadiq will need to clear the league's concussion protocol to help the Jets against the Patriots in Week 6. After a breakout Week 3 performance, Sadiq has just two catches for three yards (seven targets) over the last two games. New England struggled against Brock Bowers in Week 5 but had previously not allowed more than 32 yards or a touchdown to opposing tight ends. With Geno Smith not throwing a plethora of passes, Sadiq has minimal fantasy allure. Mason Taylor would elevate if Sadiq sits.
outlooksByWeek.7: Kenyon Sadiq's role in the Jets' passing game has ground to a halt ahead of a Week 7 matchup with the Dolphins. After spiking in Week 3 with seven catches for 105 yards and a touchdown, Sadiq has only three catches for 15 yards over the last three weeks while sharing looks with Mason Taylor. Miami is allowing the fourth-most fantasy points to opposing tight ends, and Sadiq remains long on potential, suggesting a dart throw as a bye-week replacement is possible, but the floor is minimal.
outlooksByWeek.8: Kenyon Sadiq's role in the Jets' passing game is steadily declining ahead of their Week 8 matchup with the Raiders. After flashing in Week 3 with 105 yards on seven catches, Sadiq has totaled just four catches for 21 yards over the last four games, while Mason Taylor's stats continue to increase. While the Raiders have allowed the fourth-most fantasy points to opposing tight ends, it's almost all touchdown-related, surrendering eight in seven games but a low 6.5 yards per target average. With minimal volume, Sadiq's chances of reaching the end zone appear minimal.

player.seasonOutlook: Sadiq was selected by the Jets with the No. 16 pick of April's draft. After playing a limited role his first two collegiate seasons, he broke out with a 51-560-8 receiving line in 2025. He handled a respectable 17% of Oregon's targets and aligned in the slot 62% of the time. Sadiq is a bit on the small side, but he totaled 106 targets in three collegiate seasons. He needs to cut down on drops (six on 70 targets in 2025), but he's one of the youngest players in this rookie class and crushed it at the combine, posting a ridiculous 4.39 40-yard dash at 241 pounds (130 speed score) and a 43.5-inch vertical, 133-inch broad jump and 26 bench reps. Sadiq's career might start slow, especially with Mason Taylor also on the Jets' TE depth chart, but the rookie has the upside to eventually emerge as a fantasy TE1. Consider him with a mid-to-late pick.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jayden Reed will look to make more of his opportunities as the Packers take on the Jets in Week 2. Reed struggled even with seven targets in a loss to the Vikings, logging just three catches for 20 yards. The fourth-year playmaker could start to slip into a WR3 role if he continues to play similarly, but luckily there appears to be plenty of targets to go around in the short term. Reed will face a New York defense that ranked middle-of-the-pack against wide receivers this past Sunday.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jayden Reed's status is up in the air as the Packers play the Falcons in Week 3. Reed was carted off the field after injuring his back on the first drive of Week 2, which in itself makes it unlikely that he'll be rushed back for a TNF matchup. The fourth-year playmaker's absence would give Matthew Golden even more looks, with Skyy Moore and Bo Melton slotting in as supplementary options for Jordan Love. If Reed somehow does play, he'll face an Atlanta defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 30.3 PPR points per game to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jayden Reed is unlikely to play in Week 4 as the Packers take on the Falcons. Reed sustained a neck injury against the Jets in Week 2, and he hasn't seen the field since. The fourth-year wide receiver also has no current return timeline. His absence should continue to pave the way for Skyy Moore and Bo Melton to get more opportunities in Green Bay's passing game.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jayden Reed will not play in Week 5 as the Packers play the Bears. Reed sustained a neck injury against the Jets in Week 2, and he'll now require season-ending surgery. His absence should continue to pave the way for Skyy Moore and Bo Melton to get more opportunities in Green Bay's passing game.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jayden Reed will remain out as the Packers play the Cowboys in Week 6. Reed sustained a neck injury against the Jets in Week 2, and he'll now require season-ending surgery. His absence should continue to pave the way for Skyy Moore and Bo Melton to get more opportunities in Green Bay's passing game.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jayden Reed will remain inactive as the Packers play the Lions in Week 7. Reed sustained a neck injury against the Jets in Week 2, and he'll now require season-ending surgery. His absence should continue to pave the way for Savion Williams and Bo Melton to get more opportunities in Green Bay's passing game.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jayden Reed will be inactive again as the Packers play the Panthers in Week 8. Reed sustained a neck injury against the Jets in Week 2, which requires season-ending surgery. His absence should continue to pave the way for Savion Williams and Bo Melton to get more opportunities in Green Bay's passing game.
outlooksByWeek.9: Jayden Reed will remain out as the Packers play the Patriots in Week 9. Reed sustained a neck injury against the Jets in Week 2, which requires season-ending surgery. His absence should continue to pave the way for Savion Williams, Bo Melton and  J. Michael Sturdivant to get more opportunities in Green Bay's passing game.

player.seasonOutlook: Reed began his NFL career with a pair of top-30 fantasy campaigns, but the Green Bay slot receiver was limited to only seven appearances last season due to injury. Even when active, Reed wasn't as effective as in years past, averaging 6.9 fantasy PPG and finding the end zone once (Week 1). This comes after the 2023 second-round pick produced 75 touches, 900-plus yards and seven-plus touchdowns in each of his first two seasons. The 26-year-old signed a contract extension in April and will battle the likes of Christian Watson, Matthew Golden and Savion Williams for targets this season. While he'll likely hit for the occasional solid game, his limited usage (career-high 18% target share) will put a cap on his fantasy upside. He's barely in the flex conversation in PPR leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: Antonio Williams led the Commanders in receiving in Week 1 despite playing just 26 offensive snaps. Williams ended up with four catches for 64 yards and a touchdown in his NFL premiere. He had as many targets as Terry McLaurin. Williams should see the field with increasing frequency if he continues to perform this well. He has a favorable matchup in Week 2 versus a Dallas defense that was the worst in the NFL last season, and surrendered three passing scores in the season-opening loss to the Giants.
outlooksByWeek.3: Antonio Williams snagged all three of his targets for 24 yards in the 37-20 loss to the Cowboys last game. Williams has seven catches for 98 yards and a touchdown through hsi first two NFL contests. Unfortunately, starting quarterback Jayden Daniels only played a half due to injury, so veteran backup Marcus Mariota will likely start in Week 3 versus a devastating Seattle defense. The Seahawks are allowing just 8.5 points per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league. Seattle is also allowing the fewest passing yards per contest at 124.5 per tilt. None of this appears to be a recipe for success for Williams and the rest of the Washington offense.
outlooksByWeek.4: Antonio Williams finished third in targets for the Commanders last game. Williams caught just two balls on four looks, though, en route to only 15 yards receiving. Williams caught all of his passes from backup Marcus Mariota, who will likely also line up under center in Week 4 versus the Colts. Indianapolis has been rather poor against the pass in 2026, allowing 276 yards per tilt through the air, which is 30th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Antonio Williams had eight targets last game for Washington, which was second on the squad behind Stefon Diggs. Unfortunately, Williams could muster just three catches for 21 yards in the lackluster loss to the Colts. Starting quarterback Jayden Daniels could return to the fold in Week 5 versus the Giants, which would certainly be a boost for Williams, regardless of whether Terry McLaurin also suits up. McLaurin was sidelined with a hamstring issue. New York has been fairly stingy against the pass in 2026, though, allowing just 205.3 passing yards per tilt, which is 10th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Antonio Williams managed three catches last game for Washington. Even without the services of fellow wideout Stefon Diggs, Williams accumulated fewer than 35 yards receiving for the third-straight contest. In Week 6, the Commanders face the undefeated San Francisco 49ers. The Niners are allowing just 199.6 passing yards per tilt, which is eighth in the league. In addition, San Fran has given up just five passing touchdowns, which is tied for fourth in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.8: Antonio Williams should see an uptick in targets for the remainder of the season, as No. 1 wideout Terry McLaurin will miss the rest of the 2026 campaign for the Commanders due to a knee injury. Williams has double-digit catches in every game thus far during his rookie year, and should slot in just behind Stefon Diggs in terms of opportunities in the passing game moving forward. Following the bye, Washington will face division rival Philadelphia in Week 8. The reeling Eagles have been suspect in defending the pass this season.  Philadelphia is giving up 244.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 27th in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Williams was selected by the Commanders in the third round of April's draft. He is an undersized slot receiver (75% slot in his collegiate career) who soaked up 208 catches (fourth most in this rookie class) during his four seasons (43 games) at Clemson. He was primarily a short-range option (8.0 aDOT), but he caught a healthy 75% of his targets and added value as a rusher (career 25-187-2 rushing), punt returner and even as a passer (143 yards and two TDs on four attempts). Williams is in an all-out battle with the likes of Dyami Brown, Luke McCaffrey, Jaylin Lane and Treylon Burks for the No. 3 WR gig behind Terry McLaurin and Stefon Diggs. He's worth no more than a late pick in deep leagues.

Micah Parsons' health has a bearing on the performance of this defense; it was 13th in fantasy points across the 13 games before his ACL tear, but had a negative score in four games without him. Tuck that away before diving head first into the team's soft September schedule (@MIN, @NYJ, ATL the first three weeks), though those are matchups that make this defense well worth streaming consideration.

outlooksByWeek.2: Dontayvion Wicks made his presence felt in his Eagles debut in Week 1. Wicks reeled in two passes for 73 yards and a touchdown in the 24-22 win over Washington. Only Dallas Goedert had more receiving yards than Wicks for the game. Wicks also notched four targets in his premiere for the Birds. In Week 2, Wicks will face a dismal Titans defense. Tennessee allowed 30 passing scores a season ago, which was tied for 23rd in the NFL
outlooksByWeek.3: Dontayvion Wicks continues to cement himself as the No. 2 wideout in the Eagles offense. Wicks caught five passes for 74 yards in the 24-20 win over the Titans. Wicks was second on the team in targets for the game. In Week 3, Philadelphia will face a Bears defense allowing 240 passing yards per tilt thus far this season, which is 25th in the NFL. The Eagles could also rely even more on the passing game if Saquon Barkley is sidelined due to injury, and with Dallas Goedert also banged up, Wicks could be one of the chief beneficiaries.
outlooksByWeek.4: Dontayvion Wicks had his first subpar game of the season for the Eagles. Wicks had five targets but caught just two passes for 32 yards in the ugly 27-7 loss to the Bears. Wicks had a crucial drop en route to being held under 73 yards receiving for the first time in 2026. In Week 4, he will face a rather stingy Rams pass defense allowing just 171.3 yards per game through the air, which is fourth in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Dontayvion Wicks was expected to operate as the No. 1 wideout for the Eagles last game due to the injury to DeVonta Smith. Unfortunately, Philadelphia's offense was stymied, and Wicks managed three catches for just 18 yards in the 24-20 loss to the Rams. Smith appears unlikely to play in Week 5 versus the Jags, so Wicks should continue to play a prominent role in the offense. However, it was Darius Cooper who scored twice last game, and rookie Makai Lemon outpaced Wicks in both targets as well as receiving yards. An intriguing matchup lurks in Week 5 against the Jags. Jacksonville has surrendered 280.3 passing yards per game this season, which is second-to-last in the league. In an odd twist, though, the Jags have yielded just three passing scores, which is tied for first in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Dontayvion Wicks led all Eagles wideouts in targets last game. Wicks was targeted eight times en route to five catches for 63 yards in the 19-17 loss to the Jags. The continued absence of DeVonta Smith with a hamstring injury has boosted the opportunities for Wicks, a trend that could continue in Week 6 versus Carolina. In addition, the Panthers are allowing 230.8 passing yards per tilt, which is 22nd in the league.
outlooksByWeek.7: Dontayvion Wicks caught two passes for 24 yards last game for the Eagles. Lemon had just four targets overall, as the return of DeVonta Smith to the lineup may have limited his production overall. Tanner McKee should start at quarterback for the foreseeable future, which could cap the upside for Wicks as well. However, in Week 7, the Eagles will face a Dallas defense that has struggled to defend the pass in 2026. The Cowboys are allowing 232.7 passing yards per game, which is 23rd in the NFL. In addition, Dallas has surrendered 11 passing touchdowns, which is tied for 24th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.8: Dontayvion Wicks missed Philadelphia's last game due to an ankle injury. It was the first missed game of the season for Wicks, though he could also be sidelined in Week 8 versus the Commanders. If he is able to suit up, Wicks could have a delectable matchup, even with backup quarterback Tanner McKee under center. Washington is allowing 254 passing yards per game, which is 28th in the NFL. In addition, the Commanders have surrendered 15 passing scores, which is tied for 28th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.9: Dontayvion Wicks missed yet another game for the Eagles due to a balky ankle. In fact, Wicks has missed the last two contests because of the ailment.  If he is somehow able to suit up in Week 9, he would be facing a much-improved Giants pass defense. New York is allowing just 184.9 passing yards per clash, which is third in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Wicks was traded to the Eagles after spending his first three NFL seasons in Green Bay. The 2023 fifth-round pick was limited to situational work during his Packers tenure, never finishing a season among the top 50 receivers in snaps, routes, targets, catches or yards. Wicks flashed at times (exactly one game of 24-plus points in each season), but otherwise scored 5.3 PPG. Even after the Eagles traded A.J. Brown, Wicks' path to targets may not be any easier in Philly. DeVonta Smith, Dallas Goedert and Saquon Barkley are all assured substantial roles, with first-round rookie Makai Lemon and Hollywood Brown also very much in the mix. Wicks, 25, will need to win the team's No. 2 receiver gig in order to have any shot at weekly flex consideration. He's barely worth late-round consideration in deep leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: Dylan Sampson and the Browns are in Tampa Bay to face the Buccaneers in Week 2. Unfortunately for the second-year pro, he's expected to miss "significant time" with a left knee injury sustained in Cleveland's 34-10 season-opening loss, according to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler. The severity of his injury is still being evaluated, but there's a high chance of him being placed on IR once more information comes out.
outlooksByWeek.6: Dylan Sampson and the Browns host the division-rival Ravens in Week 6. The second-year running back, who has been on injured reserve with a knee injury since September 15, could potentially return to practice ahead of their matchup with Baltimore. Head coach Todd Monken said Monday that there's a "possibility" Cleveland opens the 21-day practice window for Sampson this week. If he's able to get back on the field, it couldn't come at a better time for the Browns, as they're currently dealing with injuries to Quinshon Judkins (ankle) and Raheim Sanders (hip) sustained in Week 5's loss. It would be wise to monitor the practice reps for the entire backfield as they prepare for Week 6.
outlooksByWeek.8: Dylan Sampson and the Browns travel to face the division-rival Steelers in Week 8. He rushed six times for 45 yards and caught all three targets for another 32 yards during Cleveland's Week 7 win. Sampson made his first appearance since Week 1 due to a knee injury that forced him to be placed on IR. Quinshon Judkins (ankle) also returned from a one-game absence and out-touched Sampson 18-9, but it was still encouraging for Sampson to take advantage of his opportunities. He'll look to build upon this showing versus a Steelers defense allowing 20.5 fantasy points per game (T-11th) to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Sampson is back for Year 2 in Cleveland after an underwhelming rookie campaign in which he struggled on a small sample of work as a rusher (his 2.69 yards per carry was dead last among 65 qualified backs), but was a contributor in the passing game (23rd among RBs with 33 receptions). Sampson was a young rookie (he doesn't turn 22 until September), so there's still some room for growth, and he's positioned for a larger role behind Quinshon Judkins with Jerome Ford no longer on the roster. Expect Sampson to see some change-of-pace carries and a moderate pass-catching role in 2026. He'll land on the flex radar only if Judkins misses time.

The first team to make it through a season without recording an interception since the category began being tracked in 1933, the Jets finished last in defensive fantasy scoring last season. Hey, they can only go up from here, right? Perhaps, but offseason additions of LB Demario Davis, S Minkah Fitzpatrick and LB David Bailey (the No. 2 overall pick in the draft) hardly vault this unit into the position's upper echelon. They do get a great matchup against the Titans in Week 1, though, so there's that?

outlooksByWeek.2: Michael Penix (knee) is expected to operate as Atlanta's starting quarterback if available for the Week 2 matchup against the Panthers, whose defense allowed 59 points to the Bears in Week 1. Penix has appeared in just 14 games during his two NFL seasons, throwing for 2,757 yards, 12 touchdowns and six interceptions. While healthy last season, Penix lead the Falcons to a 3-6 record while the offense averaged 20.6 points per game. He should be in for a very favorable matchup, with Carolina's defense giving up 40 fantasy points to Caleb Williams last week.
outlooksByWeek.3: Michael Penix is slated to make his 2026 debut during the Falcons' Week 3 matchup against the Packers. Atlanta has struggled offensively with Cooper Rush and Jack Strand as the team's quarterbacks over the last two weeks, scoring just 16 total points while Rush and Strand accounted for seven turnovers. However, Penix led the Falcons' offense to 20.6 points per game while throwing for 220.2 yards per game when healthy in 2025, suggesting improvement could be coming. Penix will be in for a tough matchup though, as Green Bay's defense has given up just 19.2 fantasy points per game to opposing QBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Michael Penix is expected to lead Atlanta's offense into the Week 4 matchup against the Saints.
