The 2024 first-round pick was impressive in his 2026 debut, throwing for 256 yards, one touchdown and one interception in a win against the Packers. Despite playing in the same division as New Orleans, Penix has never played a game against the Saints before. Following his Week 3 performance, the expectation is for Penix to elevate Atlanta's offense by getting the ball into the hands of Bijan Robinson and Drake London. Penix is in for a relatively favorable matchup as well, with the Saints' defense allowing 20.8 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Michael Penix will look to stay hot in the Falcons' Week 5 matchup against the Ravens. Penix has been great through two starts in 2026, throwing for 479 yards, two touchdowns and an interception. He's helped rejuvenate Atlanta's offense, as the team has scored a whopping 40 points per game since his return. Despite this, Penix is in for a tougher Week 5 matchup against a Ravens defense that's allowed just 18.8 fantasy points per game to quarterbacks this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Michael Penix (ribs) will lead the Falcons' passing attack if active during the Week 6 matchup against the Bears. Penix was productive for the third consecutive game before exiting with a rib injury in the overtime loss to the Ravens, throwing for 240 yards and a touchdown. Through three weeks, Penix is averaging 239.7 passing yards and a touchdown per game. He's in for a favorable matchup if ready for Week 6, as the Bears' defense just allowed Jordan Love to throw for 367 yards and two touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.7: Michael Penix will continue leading the Falcons' offense during the Week 7 matchup against the 49ers. Penix was productive despite a loss in Week 6, throwing for 225 yards and three touchdowns while also completing two two-point conversions. Since returning from injury, Penix has led the Falcons' offense to 31.5 points per game, the second-most in the NFL during that span. However, he could struggle against a tough 49ers defense that's given up just 16.4 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks through five contests.
outlooksByWeek.8: Michael Penix will continue leading the Falcons' offense into the Week 8 matchup against the Buccaneers. Penix has rejuvenated Atlanta's offense since his return from injury, throwing for an average of 231.4 yards and 1.8 touchdowns per game. He has thrown for three touchdowns in consecutive games while turning the ball over just once, leading the Falcons to 30 points per game during that span. Despite this, Penix is in for a tough Week 8 matchup against a Buccaneers defense that's allowed just 18.5 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season.
outlooksByWeek.9: Michael Penix will look to rebound from a poor Week 8 performance in the Falcons' Week 9 matchup against the Bengals. Penix really struggled in last week's loss to the Buccaneers, completing just eight of 24 passes for 125 yards and four interceptions while playing in heavy rain. He could very well bounce back in Week 9, however, as Cincinnati's defense has allowed 22.1 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season. Additionally, the Bengals' defense just allowed Cam Ward to throw for 304  yards and two touchdowns in a Week 8 win, which bodes well for Penix's outlook this coming week.

player.seasonOutlook: Penix is no longer guaranteed a starting job entering his third season. The 2024 first-round pick has appeared in 14 games and has 14 total touchdowns, a 21% off-target rate and a 60% completion percentage to show for it. Penix has done well to avoid turnovers (six career INTs), but he's a nonfactor with his legs (career 28-81-2 rushing) and failed to post a single fantasy outing better than 10th last season. Penix tore an ACL in Week 11, which further complicates his path to beating out newcomer Tua Tagovailoa for the team's Week 1 starting gig. The 26-year-old might eventually emerge into a fine NFL starter, but even if he does, his lack of rushing will limit his fantasy output. He's well off the fantasy radar.

The Cowboys underwent a major roster overhaul and finished on a massive cold spell defensively late last season, making it difficult to get behind them as a fantasy option at the onset of 2026. Only the Jets scored fewer fantasy points for the year. The Cowboys did restock their roster during the offseason, adding Caleb Downs, Jalen Thompson and Rashan Gary (among others), and they do have a Giants matchup to open their schedule. It's still better to wait and see how this unit jells before diving in, however, even from a streaming standpoint.

outlooksByWeek.6: Dameon Pierce was the last running back standing for the Eagles last game. Will Shipley started the game and found the end zone early for the Eagles, but did not return to the contest due to a foot injury. His status for Week 6 versus Carolina is up in the air. Pierce could start against the Panthers, as Saquon Barkley is nursing a hamstring ailment and Tank Bigsby is on Injured Reserve. Whoever lines up in the backfield could have a tasty matchup versus a suspect Panthers run defense. Carolina is allowing 156.5 rushing yards per tilt, which is second-to-last in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Dameon Pierce rushed for 35 yards and a touchdown in Saquon Barkley's place last game for the Eagles.  Pierce also caught four balls out of the backfield. If Barkley cannot suit up in Week 7 due to his balky hamstring, Pierce would be facing a Dallas defense that has allowed the most rushing yards in the NFL to date. Per game, the Cowboys are allowing a brutal 149.8 yards on the ground.
outlooksByWeek.8: Dameon Pierce still managed to maintain a solid role despite the return of Saquon Barkley from injury for the Eagles.  Barkley rushed seven times for 62 yards and a touchdown but tweaked his hamstring while also suffering a compensatory back injury. This allowed Pierce to take 14 carries for 47 yards and a touchdown of his own.  However, Pierce could be seen leaving the field late in the fourth quarter with a potential injury as well. If neither Barkley nor Pierce can play in Week 8 versus Washington, Elijah Mitchell would be the only healthy option at running back. The Commanders are allowing 100.5 rushing yards per tilt, which is 14th in the league.

outlooksByWeek.2: Devin Singletary acted as the No. 2 back for the Giants in their season-opening win in Week 1 over Dallas. He received the second-most carries out of the backfield behind starter Cam Skattebo, while also catching four passes for 22 yards and a touchdown in the 28-20 triumph. Fellow rusher Tyrone Tracy lost a fumble in this game as well, which could further solidify Singletary's role, though veteran Najee Harris also looms. In Week 2, the Giants will be facing a Rams defense that was surprisingly suspect against the run in their first game of the season. The Rams allowed 174 yards on the ground, which currently ranks them 30th in the league. However, Aaron Donald will return to the fold out of retirement versus the G-Men to give the defensive line a boost.
outlooksByWeek.3: Devin Singletary managed just three carries for nine yards last game for the Giants. He remains firmly behind Cam Skattebo on the depth chart. Starting quarterback Jaxson Dart could be lost for the season due to a knee injury, so teams will likely gameplan to stop the run. That could mean tough sledding for the running game for the G-Men overall. However, in Week 3, the Giants will face a mediocre Titans run defense that has given up 120.5 rushing yards per tilt, which is 21st in the NFL. In addition, the Titans have already surrendered three rushing scores in the first two games of the season.
outlooksByWeek.9: Singletary scored the winning touchdown last game for the Giants, and could have a larger role in the backfield moving forward. Tyrone Tracy was placed on Injured Reserve following the most recent contest, leaving only Singletary and Cam Skattebo as the healthy options out of the backfield. Though talks of a trade for Jonathan Taylor have intensified, nothing appears imminent heading into a tasty Week 9 clash with Philadelphia. The Eagles have been torched on the ground in 2026, allowing 131.9 rushing yards per tilt, which is 28th in the league. Likewise, the Eagles have given up 10 rushing scores, which is tied for 24th in the NFL.

outlooksByWeek.2: Isiah Pacheco will miss Week 2 as the Lions travel to Buffalo. Pacheco was placed on IR to start the season due to a back injury, and he recently underwent surgery. This puts the former Kansas City RB's return in jeopardy. He's currently expected to be back sometime in December, so Sione Vaki will handle whatever RB2 duties are available behind Jahmyr Gibbs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Isiah Pacheco will remain sidelined in Week 3 as the Lions take on the Jets. Pacheco was placed on IR to start the season due to a back injury, and he recently underwent surgery. This puts the former Kansas City RB's return in jeopardy as the season progresses. He's currently expected to be back sometime in December, so Sione Vaki will handle any RB2 duties behind Jahmyr Gibbs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Isiah Pacheco will remain out in Week 4 as Detroit faces Carolina. Pacheco was placed on IR to start the season due to a back injury, and he underwent surgery in mid-September. This puts the former Kansas City RB's return in jeopardy as the season progresses. He's currently expected to be back sometime in December, so Sione Vaki will handle any RB2 duties behind Jahmyr Gibbs in the meantime.
outlooksByWeek.5: Isiah Pacheco will remain out in Week 5 when Detroit travels to Arizona. Pacheco was placed on IR to start the season due to a back injury, and he underwent surgery in mid-September. This puts the former Kansas City RB's return this season in jeopardy. He's currently expected to be back sometime in December, so Sione Vaki will continue to handle RB2 duties behind Jahmyr Gibbs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Isiah Pacheco will remain sidelined in Week 7 as Detroit plays the Packers. Pacheco was placed on IR to start the season due to a back injury, and he underwent surgery in mid-September. This puts the former Kansas City RB's return this season in jeopardy. He's currently expected to be back sometime in December, so Sione Vaki will continue to handle RB2 duties behind Jahmyr Gibbs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Isiah Pacheco will stay sidelined in Week 8 as the Lions take on Minnesota. Pacheco was placed on IR to start the season due to a back injury, and he underwent surgery in mid-September. This puts the former Kansas City RB's return this season in jeopardy. He's currently expected to be back sometime in December, so Sione Vaki will continue to handle RB2 duties behind Jahmyr Gibbs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Isiah Pacheco will remain sidelined in Week 9 as the Lions travel to Miami. Pacheco was placed on IR to start the season due to a back injury, and he underwent surgery in mid-September. This puts the former Kansas City RB's return this season in jeopardy. He's expected to be back sometime in December, so Sione Vaki will continue to handle RB2 duties behind Jahmyr Gibbs.

player.seasonOutlook: Pacheco signed with Detroit in the offseason after a four-year stint with the Chiefs. The 2022 seventh-round NFL draft pick opened his pro career with a bang, totaling 2,139 yards and 14 touchdowns on 432 touches during his first two seasons (31 games). Injuries and a big drop in efficiency have limited him to 952 yards and three TDs on 232 touches over the past two seasons (20 games) and ultimately led to his exit from Kansas City. The 27-year-old will now get a shot to replace David Montgomery as Detroit's change-of-pace back to Jahmyr Gibbs. Pacheco might hit for the occasional touchdown, but he won't have standalone fantasy value unless Gibbs misses time. Consider Pacheco a late-round insurance flier.

outlooksByWeek.8: Elijah Mitchell could end up seeing significant carries in Week 8 for the Eagles due to injury.  Both Saquon Barkley and Dameon Pierce appeared to leave the last game early due to various ailments, leaving Mitchell as potentially the only healthy back for the upcoming matchup with Washington.  Will Shipley and Tank Bigsby are already on Injured Reserve. If Mitchell maintains a role, he will face a Commanders defense allowing 100.5 rushing yards per tilt, which is 14th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.9: Elijah Mitchell led the Eagles in rushing last game. Jaydon Blue was initially thought to be the primary backup to Saquon Barkley, but it was Mitchell who led the Eagles with 34 yards on the ground. In fact, Blue did not even register a carry in the 27-10 loss to the Commanders. Barkley has been assured he will not be traded, leaving Blue as an afterthought, and perhaps even behind Mitchell on the depth chart. Meanwhile, a potentially juicy matchup is on the horizon in Week 9 versus the Giants for whomever is the bell cow. New York is allowing 128.1 rushing yards per tilt, which is 26th in the NFL.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jacoby Brissett will look to help Arizona pull off another upset against Seattle in Week 2. Brissett was great in a season-opening win over the Chargers, throwing for 277 yards with a touchdown and no interceptions. His passing score went to tight end Trey McBride, who should continue to be his top weapon as one of the league's top players at the position. The Seahawks present a tough challenge, however, as they are expected to have one of the league's top defenses and picked Drake Maye off three times in a Week 1 win.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jacoby Brissett will look to bounce back from a poor performance when Arizona faces the 49ers in Week 3. Brissett recorded just 95 passing yards with one touchdown and one interception Sunday in a loss to Seattle, with that yardage being less than half of his previous low mark across any of his 16 starts for the Cardinals. Still, McBride was able to maintain his rapport with star tight end Trey McBride, as the pair connected for 41 yards and a touchdown through the air. Brissett's path to a rebound isn't an easy one, as San Francisco has given up just 11.8 fantasy points per game to QBs -- the second-fewest in the league -- through two weeks.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jacoby Brissett is coming off his best game of season heading into Arizona's Week 4 clash with the Giants. Brissett threw for a season-high 280 yards and two touchdowns in a Week 3 loss to San Francisco while adding a TD as a rusher. His three total scores were more than the two (both through the air) he compiled over the first two weeks of the campaign. The Giants have been middle-of-the-pack statistically against the pass so far but will be without star edge rusher Brian Burns, who is out for the campaign due to a torn ACL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jacoby Brissett will aim to clean up his mistakes when Arizona hosts Detroit in Week 5. Brissett threw three interceptions against the Giants in Week 4 after getting picked off just once through his first three games of the season. The veteran quarterback has still been pretty productive with 818 passing yards, six touchdowns and 43 rushing yards (with one touchdown) overall this season. He next draws a juicy matchup against the Lions, who have given up the most fantasy points per game (32.7) to quarterbacks on the campaign.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jacoby Brissett is coming off his first three-TD performance of the campaign heading into Arizona's Week 6 clash against the Rams. Two of Brissett's scores in this past Sunday's blowout loss to Detroit came after the outcome was already decided, but they count the same in the world of fantasy football. The veteran quarterbacks also threw for a season-high 292 yards and rushed for a season-best 19 yards, though he did throw his fifth interception of the campaign. Brissett could find the sledding tougher against the Rams, who have given up just 5.65 yards per attempt this season, second-best in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jacoby Brissett will look to build on Arizona's Week 6 victory over the Rams when the Cardinals host the Broncos in Week 7. The veteran quarterback has completed 156 of 234 passes for 1,328 yards, nine touchdowns and six interceptions through six games, averaging 221.3 passing yards per contest. However, his 5.7 yards per attempt are the best example of the struggles Arizona's offense endures to generate explosive passing plays, and Denver represents another challenging opponent. The Broncos have allowed just 14.9 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season, the 12th-best mark in the NFL, limiting Brissett's appeal despite his established passing volume. He's best viewed as a lower-end QB2 in superflex formats.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jacoby Brissett will look to guide Arizona to more scoring in Week 8 versus Dallas. Though Brissett has thrown for a combined 490 yards over his past two games, he's tossed just one touchdown during that span. The veteran QB has taken to the air a league-high 282 times this season, so his fantasy managers have at least been able to count on consistent volume. Brissett could put up big numbers versus a Cowboys defense that ranks in the the bottom 10 of the league in fantasy points per game allowed to quarterbacks.

player.seasonOutlook: Brissett is back for his second season in Arizona and is currently positioned as the team's probable Week 1 starter. One of the biggest fantasy surprises of 2025, Brissett reeled off nine consecutive top-12 fantasy outings spanning Weeks 6 to 15. He averaged 18.9 fantasy points across 12 starts, which was a big surprise considering his prior career high was 12.9, and that was way back in 2017. Brissett played solid ball, but he's not a major contributor with his legs (260 yards is his career high for a season). He certainly benefited from the league's pass-heaviest offense, a luxury he's unlikely to have with Mike LaFleur now calling plays. Expect the 33-year-old to regress to fringe QB2 production, and keep in mind that it's possible Arizona will turn to rookie Carson Beck at some point this season.

outlooksByWeek.3: Terrance Ferguson is coming off a big game as the Rams prepare to face Denver in Week 3. Ferguson notched six catches on nine targets for 54 yards and a touchdown on Monday Night Football, trailing only star wideout Davante Adams in receptions, targets and receiving yards. That followed Ferguson's quiet Week 1 performance, when he didn't catch his only target. Repeating Monday's big effort could be tough for Ferguson in Week 3, as he'll face a Broncos defense that limited Jacksonville's tight ends to a modest 24 receiving yards Sunday.

player.seasonOutlook: Ferguson is a potential breakout candidate in his second NFL season. As expected, the 2025 second-rounder played a situational role behind the likes of Tyler Higbee, Colby Parkinson and Davis Allen as a rookie. He didn't get much run, but when he did, he was used as a vertical threat to the extreme. His 17.5 aDOT is highest by any tight end (minimum 10 targets) in at least a decade. The Rams are returning the same tight end room plus second-round pick Max Klare, so while consistent production could prove elusive, Ferguson very well could emerge as the No. 3 pass catcher behind Puka Nacua and 33-year-old Davante Adams in the Rams' elite offense. The 23-year-old, who also saw five end zone targets as a rookie, is worth a late-round lottery ticket.

outlooksByWeek.2: Chig Okonkwo had a rough debut Week 1 for the Commanders. On only three targets, the former Titan caught a mere two passes for 16 yards in the 24-22 loss to the Eagles. He subsequently injured his hamstring and did not return. Meanwhile, both Stefon Diggs and rookie Antonio Williams found the end zone in their respective debuts for Washington. John Bates and Ben Sinnott would step in at tight end if Chig misses Week 2 versus Dallas. If he suits up, Okonkwo would have a favorable matchup against a Cowboys defense that allowed two touchdowns to Giants tight end Isaiah Likely in the season opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chig Okonkwo did not play in Week 2 for the Commanders. Washington's active tight ends did not fare well, catching a combined two passes for 20 yards in the 37-20 loss to Dallas. Starting quarterback Jayden Daniels only played a half due to injury, and veteran backup Marcus Mariota will likely start in Week 3 versus a devastating Seattle defense. The Seahawks are allowing just 8.5 points per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league. Seattle is also allowing the fewest passing yards per contest at 124.5 per tilt. None of this appears to be a recipe for success for Okonkwo, even if he is able to suit up.
outlooksByWeek.4: Chig Okonkwo is set to practice with the Commanders as the squad heads to London for Week 4. John Bates has handled the tight end slot amid limited fanfare without Okonkwo, as Bates caught a nine-yard pass last game in Okonkwo's absence. If Okonkwo can suit up in Week 4, he may have an intriguing matchup versus the Colts, even with backup quarterback Marcus Mariota under center. Indianapolis is allowing 276 passing yards per tilt, which is 30th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Chig Okonkwo returned to the lineup for the Commanders following a two-game absence due to a hamstring ailment. Okonkwo was targeted four times, but managed two catches for a mere five yards in the dismal 30-13 loss to the Colts. Starting quarterback Jayden Daniels could return to the fold in Week 5 versus the Giants, though, which would certainly be a boost for the passing game. However, New York has been fairly stingy against the pass in 2026, allowing just 205.3 passing yards per tilt, which is 10th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Chig Okonkwo made his presence felt for Washington in his return to the lineup. Following a two-game absence due to a hamstring ailment, Okonkwo led the team with six targets en route to four catches for 60 yards in the 27-27 tie with the Giants. In Week 6, the Commanders face the undefeated San Francisco 49ers. The Niners are allowing just 199.6 passing yards per tilt, which is eighth in the league. In addition, San Fran has given up just five passing touchdowns, which is tied for fourth in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.8: Chig Okonkwo has posted back-to-back 60-plus yard outings for Washington, and could see an uptick in targets for the remainder of the season.  No. 1 wideout Terry McLaurin will miss the rest of the 2026 campaign for the Commanders due to a knee injury. Okonkwo has amassed 13 targets in the last two games alone. In Week 8, Washington will face division rival Philadelphia. The reeling Eagles have been suspect in defending the pass this season. Philadelphia is giving up 244.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 27th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.9: Chig Okonkwo made a dazzling one-handed catch last game for Washington. The highlight-reel grab is a candidate for one of the top receptions of the NFL season to date. Okonkwo finished with two catches for 32 yards in the 27-10 win over the Eagles. He was targeted four times. In Week 9, Okonkwo will face a stellar Rams pass defense. Los Angeles is allowing just 191.9 passing yards per game, which is fourth in the NFL. In addition, the Rams have yielded just 10 passing scores this season, which is tied for eighth in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Okonkwo signed with the Commanders after spending his first four seasons in Tennessee. The 2022 fourth-round pick is one of only four tight ends who have appeared in all 68 games since he entered the league, and he's also one of only six tight ends who have registered 50-plus receptions each of the past three seasons. On the other hand, Okonkwo has yet to clear a 16% target share in a single season, and he has been a nonfactor near the goal line (eight TDs and 11 end zone targets in his career). As a result, he has finished exactly 21st in fantasy points each of the past three seasons. Perhaps he'll make a leap as one of Jayden Daniels' top targets, but the 27-year-old is no more than a back-end TE2 lottery ticket.

Aiyuk remains on the 49ers' roster, but is not expected to rejoin the team. The veteran receiver was out all of last season while recovering from a torn ACL and MCL suffered in October 2024. In his two full seasons prior to the injury, Aiyuk delivered back-to-back top-15 fantasy seasons, including a 2023 campaign in which he produced a career-high 1,342 yards (seventh among wide receivers) and ranked in the top five at the position in yards per reception, yards per target and yards per route run. Even prior to the 2024 injury, however, Aiyuk was underperforming, scoring zero TDs and reaching double-digit fantasy points only once in seven games. Aiyuk is still in his prime at 28 years old, but his role and effectiveness are currently unclear. He's off the fantasy radar.

outlooksByWeek.5: Treylon Burks snagged a 47-yard touchdown last game for the Commanders. Burks has scored in consecutive games for the Commanders. However, Terry McLaurin is likely to return from a hamstring injury in Week 5 versus the Giants, which could negatively affect Burks. New York has also been fairly stingy against the pass in 2026, allowing just 205.3 passing yards per tilt, which is 10th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Treylon Burks was second on the team in targets last game. Burks had a season-high five looks in the 27-27 tie with the Giants. Unfortunately, he corralled just two of those balls for 26 yards, and had a two-game scoring streak snapped. In Week 6, the Commanders face the undefeated San Francisco 49ers. The Niners are allowing just 199.6 passing yards per tilt, which is eighth in the league. In addition, San Fran has given up just five passing touchdowns, which is tied for fourth in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.8: Treylon Burks could see an uptick in targets for the remainder of the season, as No. 1 wideout Terry McLaurin will miss the rest of the 2026 campaign for the Commanders due to a knee injury. Burks posted season highs in targets, receptions and receiving yardage in Washington's last game before the bye.  In Week 8, Washington will face division rival Philadelphia. The reeling Eagles have been suspect in defending the pass this season.  Philadelphia is giving up 244.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 27th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.9: Treylon Burks led the Commanders in receiving last game. Burks caught three passes for 81 yards in the 27-10 win over the Eagles. Burks has at least five targets in three-straight tilts. However, in Week 9, Burks will face a superb Rams pass defense. Los Angeles is allowing just 191.9 passing yards per game, which is fourth in the NFL. In addition, the Rams have yielded just 10 passing scores this season, which is tied for eighth in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: While the Saints showed improvement under first-year defensive coordinator Brandon Staley over the course of 2025 -- their 66 fantasy points following their Week 11 bye was fifth-best in the league -- the team has a rough go of it at the onset of 2026. Road matchups with the Lions (Week 1) and Ravens (2) are tough as nails, and even the addition of LB Kaden Ellis isn't going to ease those matchup worries. Consider this a streaming defense at best.

outlooksByWeek.2: Deshaun Watson and the Browns visit the Buccaneers for an interconference clash in Week 2. In his first regular-season game since Oct. 20, 2024, Watson completed 16 of 22 pass attempts for 205 yards with one TD and one INT while rushing six times for 38 yards. Although his debut was uninspiring, head coach Todd Monken said he will stick with the 31-year-old as the starting quarterback after seeing enough positive glimpses on film. Watson will face another difficult matchup against Tampa Bay's 14th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (18.7) to QBs and therefore should remain on waiver wires.
outlooksByWeek.3: Deshaun Watson and the Browns host the Panthers for their home opener in Week 3. He completed 24 of 30 pass attempts for 238 yards with two TDs and no INTs, while rushing seven times for 22 yards during Cleveland's surprising Week 2 win over the Buccaneers. Watson led the comeback victory with scoring strikes of 55 and 17 yards, and chemistry appears to be brewing between him and the Browns' young playmakers. He'll face a Carolina defense that held the Falcons to 129 yards passing and forced three INTs and two fumbles in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.4: Deshaun Watson and the Browns host the division-rival Steelers on Thursday night in Week 4. He completed 16 of 30 pass attempts for 144 yards with two TDs and no INTs while adding 11 rushes for 45 yards during Cleveland's 21-18 victory in Week 3. Watson did a lot of damage with his legs, a growing trend as he's racked up 105 yards on 24 carries across three outings. The Browns' offense continues to surprise, but they'll have their hands full versus a Pittsburgh defense that ranks seventh in fantasy points allowed (16.9) to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Deshaun Watson and the Browns take their surprising 3-1 record into a road battle against the Jets in Week 5. In Week 4's 27-24 victory, he threw for 268 yards (24-for-33) with one TD and one INT, while rushing seven times for 22 yards. Watson lost one of his two fumbles, but he was able to do enough to lead his team to a third straight win. He hit seven different receivers en route to his highest passing yardage total since 2023. Watson aims to keep improving in a tough matchup versus the Jets, who have the second-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (16.0) to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Deshaun Watson and the Browns host the division-rival Ravens in Week 6. He completed 15 of 33 passes for 155 yards with one TD and no INTs while rushing six times for 40 yards during Cleveland's 17-12 loss in Week 5. Watson was sacked eight times for 53 yards and fumbled three times, although he recovered two of them. After leading the Browns to a three-game win streak behind strong performances, Watson struggled with pressure and the rainy conditions in the Week 5 defeat. He'll aim to bounce back versus Baltimore's 12th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (18.7) to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Deshaun Watson and the Browns travel to square off against the Titans in Week 7. He completed 16 of 26 pass attempts for 164 yards and rushed eight times for 29 yards during Cleveland's 13-10 win in Week 6. Watson is not much of a fantasy-friendly quarterback, but he has the Browns at 4-2 and tied for first in the AFC North. Next up is a stingy Tennessee defense that ranks 10th in fantasy points allowed per game (18.6) to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Deshaun Watson and the Browns travel to Pittsburgh for a divisional clash in Week 8. He completed 25 of 36 pass attempts for 308 yards with no touchdowns and one interception, while rushing three times for 19 yards and a TD during Cleveland's Week 7 victory. Watson mounted a game-winning drive in the fourth quarter for the fifth time this season, leading the Browns to a 5-2 record and a tie with the Steelers atop the AFC North. He'll face Pittsburgh's fourth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (17.1) to QBs for the second time in 2026. Watson threw for 268 yards with one TD and one INT to go along with 22 rush yards in a Week 4 win over the Steelers.
outlooksByWeek.9: Deshaun Watson and the Browns visit New Orleans for an interconference clash in Week 9. He completed 27 of 39 pass attempts for 324 yards with no touchdowns or interceptions and rushed three times for two yards during Cleveland's 27-6 loss in Week 8. Watson lost a fumble and was sacked eight times in another tough showing for the Browns' offense. He'll try to turn things around against a Saints defense allowing 20.5 fantasy points per game (T-14th) to opposing QBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Watson will return to the field this season after a disastrous four years in Cleveland. A top-six fantasy QB (points per game) during each of his first four NFL seasons, Watson has appeared in a total of 19 games since joining the Browns, averaging a poor 13.1 fantasy points during the span. A torn Achilles suffered in Week 7 of 2024 (followed by tearing it again less than three months later) cost Watson all of 2025. Now 30 years old, with a young, unproven supporting cast and having not been a factor since 2020, Watson will open the season as Cleveland's starter, but he's a long shot to return to fantasy relevance. He should be considered only in superflex formats.

outlooksByWeek.2: Samaje Perine and the Bengals travel to face the Texans for a Week 2 tilt. He was highly efficient with his touches in the season-opening win, tallying five carries for 20 yards while catching all three targets for 30 yards. Perine was the only other running back to record a carry, so his status as the No. 2 RB is not in question. Houston's defense is tied for third in fantasy points allowed per game (10.5) to RBs, but it surrendered 409 total yards of offense in their Week 1 loss to the Bills.
outlooksByWeek.3: Samaje Perine and the Bengals travel to take on the division-rival Steelers in Week 3. After dealing with an illness that forced him to miss two days of practice, he was active in Week 2 and recorded two carries for six yards and caught his lone target for 16 yards during Cincinnati's win over the Texans. With backfield mate Chase Brown handling 23 total touches, Perine's limited involvement on offense makes him a solid fantasy insurance policy, but nothing more. Pittsburgh's defense ranks 28th in rushing yards (233) and 29th in receiving yards allowed (97) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Samaje Perine and the Bengals play host to the Jaguars in Week 4. He rushed three times for nine yards and caught one of three targets for five yards during Cincinnati's 30-27 Week 3 loss. Lead back Chase Brown handled 13 carries, so Perine is firmly established as the No. 2 option and primary passing-down option out of the backfield. Jacksonville's defense ranks seventh in fantasy points allowed (17.2) to RBs, and it has surrendered just one rushing TD to the position through three contests.
outlooksByWeek.5: Samaje Perine and the Bengals are on the road to take on the Dolphins in Week 5. He tallied three carries for seven yards and failed to bring in his only target during Cincinnati's Week 4 defeat. Perine's offensive snaps and involvement continue to fluctuate as the clear back behind Chase Brown, even despite his team playing from behind more recently. Miami's defense ranks last in fantasy points (29.7) allowed to RBs, but Perine should remain on fantasy benches.
outlooksByWeek.7: Samaje Perine and the Bengals travel to take on the 4-2 Ravens in Week 7. He rushed 14 times for 68 yards and caught both of his targets for 10 yards and a TD during Cincinnati's Week 5 victory. Perine out-carried starter Chase Brown (13) and was much more efficient, as Brown managed just 39 yards on the ground. If Brown continues to struggle, Perine could have a larger role than initially anticipated at the beginning of the campaign. However, it might be wise to wait until we know more about the backfield hierarchy following the matchup against Baltimore's seventh-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (18.6) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Samaje Perine and the Bengals host the 1-6 Titans in Week 8. He had four carries for 16 yards and a one-yard touchdown but was not targeted during Cincinnati's Week 7 victory. The Bengals' backfield has been tricky with Chase Brown struggling as of late, and it looks like it could be headed toward more of a timeshare than initially thought at the start of the year. Perine will try to continue building momentum against the Titans' 19th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (22.3) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Samaje Perine and the Bengals travel to Spain for a Week 9 clash against the Falcons. He rushed four times for 10 yards and caught his only target for nine yards during Cincinnati's overtime victory in Week 8. Perine played 33% of the offensive snaps but was unable to produce much on a day the Bengals put up a season-high 43 points. He'll aim to get more involved against an Atlanta defense that ranks 30th, giving up 28.1 fantasy points per game to opposing RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Perine is expected to resume his role as Chase Brown's primary backup in Cincinnati. The veteran back played 31% of the Bengals' snaps last season, totaling 84 carries and 21 targets. He cleared 400 total yards for the fifth consecutive season, though he has yet to reach 200 touches in a single season in his career, nor has he produced a top-30 fantasy campaign. The 30-year-old has reached double-digit fantasy points three times over the last two seasons and would require a Brown injury in order to flirt with flex appeal. He can be left on waivers.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tyler Higbee remains in a crowded Rams tight-end corps heading into a Week 2 matchup versus the Giants. Though Higbee led Los Angeles TEs with two catches in a Week 1 loss to San Francisco, he logged only 12 offensive snaps -- fourth-most among the group. The Rams frequently use three-TE sets, so Higbee figures to be involved in some capacity each week, but he could have a hard time carving out consistent production if he remains at the bottom of the pecking order in terms of playing time. The Giants held a trio of Cowboys tight ends to five catches for 32 yards in a Week 1 win.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tyler Higbee may be in line for an upgraded role for the Rams in Week 4 versus Philadelphia. After falling below a 30% offensive snap share each of the first two weeks and producing just two catches for 12 yards, Higbee exploded for an 8-62-1 receiving line on 11 targets and a 71% percent offensive snap share in Week 3 against Denver. That was partly due to fellow tight ends Terrance Ferguson (ankle) and Colby Parkinson (shoulder) getting hurt, and at least Ferguson (and possibly Parkinson) is expected to be sidelined for Week 4. However, the Eagles have been stingy versus tight ends so far, yielding only 89 receiving yards and no touchdowns to the position through three weeks.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tyler Higbee may have worked his way back up to the Rams' No. 1 tight-end role with a Week 5 matchup against Buffalo on tap. After logging just two catches over the first two weeks of the season, Higbee has tallied a 13-129-1 line over the past two weeks. He's led Los Angeles tight ends in offensive snaps in each of those contests, with injuries to Colby Parkinson (shoulder) and Terrance Ferguson (ankle - IR) contributing to the uptick in playing time. Buffalo has given up just one touchdown to tight ends so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tyler Higbee has become a key target for Rams QB Matthew Stafford ahead of a Week 6 battle against Arizona. Higbee recorded a season-high 83 receiving yards on five catches while drawing six targets Monday versus Buffalo. After beginning the campaign with just two catches for 12 yards over his first two contests, Higbee has posted no less than five receptions and 62 yards each of the past three weeks. He could find more success against the Cardinals, who have surrendered a league-worst 9.81 yards per target to tight ends on the season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tyler Higbee has emerged as the Rams' most productive receiving tight end, catching 24 passes for 246 yards and a touchdown through six games. Even though he delivered a subpar showing in Week 6 against the Cardinals, finishing with four catches for 22 yards, he's clearly ahead of Colby Parkinson in the pecking order in the passing game. With Davante Adams (hamstring) sidelined for the time being, Higbee should be one of the players in line for an uptick in targets and touches. The Week 7 matchup against the Raiders is favorable on paper, as Las Vegas has allowed the sixth-most fantasy points per game to TEs in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.8: Tyler Higbee continues to work in an unpredictable Rams tight-end timeshare ahead of a Week 8 matchup against the Chargers. While Matthew Stafford targeted tight ends 14 times in Sunday's win over Las Vegas, Higbee got just three of those looks and put up a meager 2-14-0 line. Meanwhile, fellow TEs Colby Parkinson (5-48-0) and Davis Allen (4-20-2) had bigger performances. Wideout Davante Adams (hamstring) is expected to miss several weeks, so Stafford will likely continue to look to his tight ends often, but it's anyone's guess which of the trio will be the top performer on a week-to-week basis. The Chargers have been relatively stingy against tight ends, giving up 6.8 fantasy points per game, tied for 10th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.9: Tyler Higbee will look to snap a recent downturn in production when the Rams take on the Commanders in Week 9. After logging at least five catches and at least 62 yards in three straight games Weeks 3-5, Higbee has topped out at four receptions and 22 yards over his past three contests. The problem hasn't been opportunity -- in fact, Higbee's offensive snap share has actually increased during the more recent three-game span. He could rediscover success against a Washington defense that has given up the second-most fantasy points per game (14.4) to tight ends this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Higbee re-signed with the Rams and will battle for work with the likes of Colby Parkinson, Davis Allen, Terrance Ferguson and rookie Max Klare. The 2016 fourth-round pick has a pair of top-10 fantasy campaigns in his career, but the last one came in 2022 and he's finished 24th or worse in three consecutive seasons. Injuries have been part of the issue (21 missed games over the last two seasons), but so has a lesser role and minimal goal-line work (seven touchdowns and four end zone targets over the last three years). Now 33 years old, Higbee is likely third in line for targets at his position on his own team and, thus, nowhere close to fantasy relevance.

outlooksByWeek.2: Trey Smack will look to stay solid as the Packers take on the Jets in Week 2. Smack converted all three of his field-goal attempts against the Vikings in Week 1, but he did go 1-for-2 on XPAs. Still, the perfect field-goal percentage outshines his one miss. Smack will face a Jets defense that allowed a bottom-five fantasy points (4.0) total to Titans kicker Joey Slye this past Sunday.
outlooksByWeek.3: Trey Smack will aim to stay perfect as the Packers play the Falcons in Week 3. Smack went perfect in Week 2 against the Jets, nailing two PATs and two field-goal tries, including a game-winner. The rookie kicker has now gone a perfect five-for-five on field goals and made all but one of his four extra-point attempts. He'll take on an Atlanta team that's allowed 9.0 fantasy points per game to kickers on the year, a bottom-10 mark.
outlooksByWeek.4: Trey Smack will have a favorable matchup as the Packers travel to Tampa Bay in Week 4. Smack went 2-for-2 on extra-point tries in Week 3 against the Falcons, but he also had his sole field-goal attempt blocked. The rookie kicker will seek to get back on track versus a Bucs squad that's allowed the most fantasy points per game (12.3) to kickers this year.
outlooksByWeek.5: Trey Smack will look to be consistent for the Packers once again in Week 5 against the Bears. Smack nailed a 58-yard field goal and both of his extra-point tries against the Buccaneers in Week 4. The rookie kicker has now gone 6-for-7 on field-goal kicks this season, with three of them from 50-plus yards. He'll face a Chicago defense that's ranked top five against fantasy kickers this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.6: Trey Smack will aim to get back on track as the Packers take on the Cowboys in Week 6. Smack's accuracy was not on point against the Bears in Week 5, as he went just 1-for-3 on field-goal attempts and 2-for-3 on XPAs. While the rookie kicker's struggles didn't matter in an eventual blowout win, he'll need to get better when high-importance kicks come up more later in the year. Smack will face a Dallas defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack (8.0 points allowed per game) versus fantasy kickers this year.
outlooksByWeek.7: Trey Smack will look to build off a solid performance as the Packers play the Lions in Week 7. After a disappointing performance even in a blowout victory against the Bears, Smack nailed all three of his field-goal tries and went two-for-two on XPAs in a Week 6 win over Dallas. The rookie kicker has now converted 10 of 13 field-goal kicks and gone 11-for-13 on extra-point attempts this season. He'll face a Detroit defense that's ranked fourth in fantasy points per game allowed to kickers.
outlooksByWeek.8: Trey Smack will need to get back on track as the Packers play the Panthers in Week 8. Smack had another rough outing in Week 7 against the Vikings, making two PATs but going just 1-for-3 on field-goal attempts. The rookie has now missed five field goals and two extra-point tries this season, and his job will definitely be in jeopardy if he continues to be inaccurate. He'll face a Carolina squad that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy kickers this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Ejiro Evero coaxed a No. 15 positional finish in terms of fantasy points from this defense last season, and the defensive front has been fortified since with the additions of Devin Lloyd and Jaelen Phillips. There should be streaming potential with this D/ST, which could be worth the pickup for matchups in Weeks 3 (@CLE), 10 (@NO), 14 (NO) and 16 (@PIT).

outlooksByWeek.3: Darius Cooper caught the game-winning touchdown for the Eagles in Week 2. Cooper managed just two catches for 26 yards, though one of them gave the Eagles the lead for good with precious seconds left on the clock. Cooper also tied for third on the team in targets for the game. In Week 3, Philadelphia will face a Bears defense allowing 240 passing yards per tilt thus far this season, which is 25th in the NFL. The Eagles could also rely even more on the passing game if Saquon Barkley is sidelined due to injury.
outlooksByWeek.5: Darius Cooper scored twice last game for the Eagles. Cooper finished the contests with seven targets, parlaying those looks into three catches for 33 yards and the pair of scores. If Devonta Smith, Dallas Goedert and/or Saquon Barkley are sidelined in Week 5 versus the Jags, Cooper could see an uptick in usage again.  Jacksonville has surrendered 280.3 passing yards per game this season, which is second-to-last in the league. In an odd twist, though, the Jags have yielded just three passing scores, which is tied for first in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Darius Cooper continues to flash his big-play ability for the Eagles. Cooper snagged his fourth touchdown of the season last game versus the Jaguars en route to leading the Eagles in receiving yards. Four of Cooper's seven receptions have gone for touchdowns in 2026. The continued absence of DeVonta Smith with a hamstring injury has also likely boosted the opportunities for Cooper, who has 10 targets in his last two contests alone. This trend could continue in Week 6 versus Carolina. The Panthers are allowing 230.8 passing yards per tilt, which is 22nd in the league.
outlooksByWeek.7: Darius Cooper caught just one pass for nine yards last game for the Eagles. Cooper had just two targets overall, as the return of DeVonta Smith to the lineup may have limited his production overall. Tanner McKee should start at quarterback for the foreseeable future, which could cap Cooper's upside as well. However, in Week 7, the Eagles will face a Dallas defense that has struggled to defend the pass in 2026. The Cowboys are allowing 232.7 passing yards per game, which is 23rd in the NFL. In addition, Dallas has surrendered 11 passing touchdowns, which is tied for 24th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.8: Darius Cooper disappointed for Philadelphia last game despite the Eagles dealing with a multitude of injuries at the wide receiver position. Both DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks were sidelined due to injury, but Cooper still only managed just one catch for 17 yards. He was targeted eight times in the contest, though rookie Makai Lemon saw eight targets by contrast. If Smith and/or Wicks are unable to suit up in Week 8 versus the Commanders, the matchup still favors Cooper, even with backup quarterback Tanner McKee under center. Washington is allowing 254 passing yards per game, which is 28th in the NFL. In addition, the Commanders have surrendered 15 passing scores, which is tied for 28th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.9: Darius Cooper finished second on the Eagles in targets last game behind Makai Lemon. With starting wideouts DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks both sidelined due to injury, Cooper saw an increase in looks. Unfortunately, Cooper could only manage two catches for 19 yards in the dismal 27-10 loss to the Commanders. Cooper has just 11 catches on the season. In Week 9, the Eagles will face a much-improved Giants pass defense. New York is allowing just 189.4 passing yards per tilt, which is third in the NFL.

outlooksByWeek.2: Rashod Bateman and the Ravens host the Saints in Week 2. Despite leading Baltimore's receivers with 53 offensive snaps, he logged just one target and did not record a reception. With Zay Flowers' (hamstring) status up in the air and rookie Ja'Kobi Lane out with a fractured wrist suffered in the opener, Bateman's opportunities to contribute could increase. Regardless of who's active, he'll aim to bounce back against New Orleans' 21st-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (37.2) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Rashod Bateman and the Ravens are on the road for a Week 3 matchup against the Cowboys. In the absence of top wideout Zay Flowers (hamstring), Bateman caught seven of nine targets for 88 yards and a touchdown during Baltimore's Week 2 loss. He'll likely slide back to a supporting role if Flowers is able to suit up this Sunday. However, if he's unable to do so, Bateman will have the chance to replicate his solid outing versus a Dallas defense that ranks 18th in fantasy points per game (31.2) allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Rashod Bateman and the Ravens return home to host the 0-3 Titans in Week 4. He caught two of three targets for 37 yards during Baltimore's 34-31 win in Week 3, finishing second on the team in yardage. However, with Zay Flowers (hamstring) returning from a one-game absence, Bateman saw his involvement dip heavily after posting a 7-88-1 line in Week 2's loss. Flowers paced the Ravens in receptions, targets, and yardage, and as long as he remains healthy, managers can expect Bateman to see similar results against Tennessee's 18th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (32.9) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Rashod Bateman and the Ravens square off against the 2-2 Falcons on the road in Week 5. He caught both of his targets for 46 yards during Baltimore's 24-18 victory in Week 4. Bateman tied with five other Ravens in targets while finishing second on the team in yardage, but Zay Flowers (8-118-1) and Mark Andrews (5-27-1) did most of the damage on offense. He'll try to make more of a contribution versus an Atlanta defense that's tied for 27th in fantasy points allowed (38.4) per game to WRs, although that could be challenging given Lamar Jackson's (ankle) uncertain status for Week 5.
outlooksByWeek.6: Rashod Bateman and the Ravens are in Cleveland for an AFC North divisional clash in Week 6. He caught five of six targets for 62 yards during Baltimore's 30-23 overtime win in Week 5. Bateman led the team in receiving yards and was second in receptions while tying for second in targets. Tyler Huntley, who started for Lamar Jackson (ankle), attempted 32 passes and relied heavily on the wideout, as all five of Bateman's catches resulted in first downs for the Ravens. He'll aim to make a similar difference against a Browns defense allowing 36.4 fantasy points per game to WRs, which ranks 24th.
outlooksByWeek.7: Rashod Bateman (shoulder) and the Ravens host the division-rival Bengals in Week 7. He failed to catch his only target before exiting in the second quarter of Baltimore's 13-10 loss in Week 6. Bateman sat out the entire second half while dealing with the nagging shoulder issue, allowing rookie Jakobi Lane to rack up a 4-40-0 receiving line on five targets. Even if Bateman is able to suit up against Cincinnati in Week 7, he should remain on fantasy benches due to his inconsistent involvement in the offense, regardless of the Ravens' quarterback situation.
outlooksByWeek.8: Rashod Bateman and the Ravens are on the road for a Week 8 clash against the Bills. He hauled in two of four targets for 33 yards during Baltimore's 35-13 loss in Week 7. Tyler Huntley attempted 34 passes and connected with eight different receivers on the day, but Zay Flowers (8-137-1) was the only one with more than three receptions and five targets. Lamar Jackson (ankle) could return from a three-game absence in Week 8, so Bateman may have an opportunity to take advantage of a Bills defense allowing the most fantasy points per game (42.3) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Rashod Bateman and the Ravens return home to face the Jaguars in Week 9. He caught one of three targets for 22 yards during Baltimore's 36-10 loss in Week 8. Bateman led the team in yardage after both Lamar Jackson (thumb/IR) and Tyler Huntley (toe) were forced out of the contest with injuries, which should tell you all you need to know about the current state of the Ravens' offense. Bateman should be left on fantasy benches/waiver wires despite facing the Jaguars' 29th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (37.2) to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Bateman is entering his sixth season in Baltimore following an injury-plagued 2025 campaign in which he was limited to a career-low 224 receiving yards in 13 games. After scoring nine touchdowns on only 45 receptions in 2024, Bateman had "regression" written all over him entering last season, but it was worse than expected. The 2021 first-round pick saw his target share fall from 15.4% to a career-low 11.4% and his only double-digit fantasy effort came in Week 3. The 26-year-old remains second on Baltimore's depth chart behind Zay Flowers, but even in a new scheme and with a healthy Lamar Jackson under center, he's unlikely to produce his first top-35 fantasy campaign. Bateman isn't the most appealing late-round draft pick.

Chris O'Leary takes the helm as Chargers defensive coordinator, a year after this unit finished 11th in fantasy points (119). With stars like Khalil Mack, Derwin James Jr. and Tuli Tuipulotu on the roster, the Chargers should again put forth solid defensive numbers, health willing. But the biggest advantage here is the team's first-two-weeks' schedule: The Chargers host the Cardinals and Raiders, two of the most favorable D/ST matchups. Just beware that things get far tougher from there (@BUF, @SEA, DEN, @KC the next four weeks).

outlooksByWeek.2: Cooper Kupp and the Seahawks travel to Arizona to take on the Cardinals in Week 2. Kupp caught two of three targets for 35 yards in a season-opening win against New England, though he would have had a bigger performance if not for a 24-yard touchdown grab that was nullified by a penalty. Of note, Drew Lock is expected to start behind center for Seattle, as Sam Darnold is dealing with a glute injury and is unlikely to suit up. The Cardinals aren't expected to field a top secondary this year, but they did a good job of holding Justin Herbert and the Chargers' offense in check in a Week 1 win.
outlooksByWeek.3: Cooper Kupp has so far had a quiet campaign heading into Seattle's Week 3 matchup versus Washington. Kupp has logged just two receptions in each of the Seahawks' first two games, registering 55 yards across the four total catches. He ranks third on the team with five targets, trailing Jaxon Smith-Njigba (22) and Rashid Sheheed (nine). As those numbers suggest, Smith-Njigba is dominating looks again this season, so Kupp and Shaheed may be left to compete for scraps throughout the campaign. With that said, there may be lots of receptions to go around against the Commanders, who have given up 27 catches to wideouts through two weeks -- tied for third-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Cooper Kupp is coming off his biggest performance of the season as the Seahawks prepare to host the Chargers in Week 4. Kupp logged season-best marks with four catches, five targets and 46 receiving yards against Washington in Week 3, and he got into the end zone for the first time with a seven-yard TD reception. Also of note is that Kupp logged a 67% offensive snap share after being on the field for just 43% of Seattle's offensive snaps the previous week. Kupp will look to build upon the promising effort against the Chargers, who have yielded a 67.3% catch rate to wideouts so far this season, seventh-worst in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Cooper Kupp will look to rebound from a quiet performance when Seattle faces San Francisco in Week 5. Against the Chargers this past Sunday, Kupp caught just one of two targets for 13 yards. It was his lowest offensive output of the season, though he's been pretty quiet overall with two or fewer receptions in three of four contests so far. The 49ers are yielding just 123.5 receiving yards per game to wideouts, seventh-fewest in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Cooper Kupp has had a quiet campaign so far with Seattle's Week 6 matchup in Denver on tap. Kupp has produced a modest 11 catches for 129 yards and a touchdown through five weeks, and he's posted just three catches for 28 yards in his past two games. He's regularly logging a healthy offensive snap share, but there hasn't been much room for any of Seattle's complementary wideouts to shine behind star Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who is averaging 10.0 targets per game. Kupp may need a big play or two to break out, but the Broncos are yielding just 7.65 yards per WR target, 12th-best in the league.
outlooksByWeek.7: Cooper Kupp and the Seahawks host the 5-0 Chiefs on Sunday Night Football in Week 7. He caught five of 10 targets for 50 yards during Seattle's 17-14 overtime loss in Week 6. Kupp finished behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba (16) for second on the team in targets, as his 10 looks from QB Sam Darnold were a season high for the 33-year-old. He'll try to relieve some of the pressure Smith-Njigba will face versus a Kansas City defense that allows 21.2 fantasy points per game to WRs, which ranks first.
outlooksByWeek.8: Cooper Kupp may be operating without fellow wideout Rashid Shaheed during Seattle's Week 8 matchup versus Chicago. Shaheed suffered a knee injury Sunday against Kansas City and is a question mark to play versus the Bears. If he does miss Week 8, Kupp could be set for more responsibilities, though he'd still be far behind superstar Jaxon Smith-Njigba in the pecking order. The Bears rank in the middle of the pack with 20.1 fantasy points per game allowed to wide receivers.
outlooksByWeek.9: Cooper Kupp heads into Seattle's Week 9 matchup versus the Cardinals looking for a more impactful role in his team's offense. Kupp caught a touchdown in Week 8 against the Bears, but the seven-yard score was his only reception of the game. With three of fewer targets in six of his eight contests on the campaign, Kupp simply isn't getting much of an opportunity to be productive when he isn't getting into the end zone. The Cardinals do present a good matchup, as they've yielded 11 receiving TDs to wideouts this season, tied for the most in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Kupp heads into his age-33 season positioned for situational targets in Seattle's run-first offense. The longtime Rams slot man appeared in 16 games for Seattle in 2025 -- his first season with the team -- and was limited to a career-low 16% target share. Kupp was a nonfactor in fantasy, clearing 12.0 fantasy points only once (16.0 in Week 2). The veteran remains a reliable short-range target, but his ceiling is very low with Jaxon Smith-Njigba soaking up a huge share of the targets and the likes of Rashid Shaheed and Tory Horton also in the mix. Kupp is an unexciting late-round pick.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jerry Jeudy and the Browns visit the Buccaneers in Week 2. They'll face the fourth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (19.1) to WRs. Jeudy brought in two of four targets for 26 yards in Cleveland's season-opening blowout loss, but he didn't see any looks in the second half. He tied rookie Denzel Boston for second in targets and third in receptions, while fellow rookie KC Concepcion led the way with four catches and five targets. As long as the Browns' QB play remains shaky, there's no reason to consider Jeudy in any fantasy formats.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jerry Jeudy and the Browns host the Panthers in Week 3, whose defense allowed just 145 yards through the air in Week 2. He failed to corral his lone target during Cleveland's upset win over the Buccaneers in Week 2, giving him a 2-26-0 receiving line on five targets through two games. Meanwhile, rookies Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion combined for 123 yards and one TD while catching 11 of 13 targets, and they look to be the leaders in the WR room. It will be difficult to start any of them until the Browns' offense consistently proves it can sustain any fantasy-relevant players.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jerry Jeudy and the Browns play host to their division rival Steelers in Week 4. He did not record a target in Cleveland's 21-18 Week 3 victory after failing to catch his only target in Week 2's win. Jeudy now owns a 2-26-0 receiving line on five targets through three games, and it's clear he's fallen down the offensive pecking order behind rookies Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion and TE Harold Fannin Jr. He should remain on waiver wires against Pittsburgh's eighth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (28.0) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jerry Jeudy and the Browns travel to take on the Jets in Week 5. He hauled in all three of his targets for 36 yards during Cleveland's 27-24 win in Week 4, setting new season highs in receptions and yardage. Jeudy had a solid bounce-back effort after failing to record a target in Week 3, but he remains behind Denzel Boston, KC Concepcion, and Harold Fannin Jr. in the offensive pecking order. Jeudy belongs on fantasy benches against a Jets defense that ranks ninth in fantasy points allowed (28.5) per game to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jerry Jeudy and the Browns host the Ravens for a divisional clash in Week 6. He caught three of seven targets for 19 yards during Cleveland's Week 5 defeat. Jeudy became more involved after KC Concepcion (concussion) exited in the first quarter, and there's a chance the rookie will be unable to clear the NFL's five-step protocol before their matchup with Baltimore. If that is indeed the case, Jeudy will slide into the No. 2 receiver role behind Denzel Boston against a Ravens defense allowing 36.2 fantasy points per game to WRs, which ranks 23rd.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jerry Jeudy and the Browns travel to take on the Titans in Week 7. He caught all four of his targets for 69 yards during Cleveland's 13-10 win in Week 6. After compiling a 6-55-0 line on 11 targets over his last four outings, Jeudy led the team in yardage and tied for first in receptions, surpassing the 40-yard mark for the first time all season. However, despite a favorable matchup versus Tennessee's 24th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (35.9) to WRs, he should remain on fantasy waiver wires as a member of an inconsistent offense.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jerry Jeudy and the Browns take on the Steelers for a Week 8 road tilt. He caught all four of his targets for 21 yards during Cleveland's 27-24 comeback victory in Week 7. The outing marked two straight with at least four receptions for Jeudy, although he's still clearly behind rookies KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston, and tight end Harold Fannin Jr. in the passing game. Jeudy remains off the fantasy radar in this AFC North showdown.
outlooksByWeek.9: Jerry Jeudy and the Browns visit the Saints for an interconference clash in Week 9. He was unable to catch his lone target during Cleveland's 27-6 loss in Week 8, marking his third outing of the season without a catch. Jeudy had four receptions in each of his last two contests prior to getting blanked, and he now boasts a 16-171-0 line on 24 targets over eight games. He'll try to rebound versus a New Orleans defense that ranks 15th in terms of fantasy points allowed per game (30.2) to opposing WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Jeudy's up-and-down career continues, as he has now finished outside the top 50 receivers in fantasy PPG four times in six seasons and inside the top 25 twice in the last four years. Jeudy has handled a target share in the 19-23% range all six seasons, but he hasn't found the end zone very often (17 TDs in 91 games) and has struggled with drops (32). Horrific efficiency (48% catch rate, 5.7 YPT) was a big issue last season and led to a career-low 7.1 fantasy PPG. Life might not be much better in 2026 with Cleveland's quarterback situation still unsolved and a lot more target competition (rookies KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston join Harold Fannin Jr.). On the other hand, Jeudy, 27, is still in his prime and it has only been one season since he ranked sixth in the league with 1,229 receiving yards. He has some bounce-back potential, but Jeudy is safest as a bench player.

outlooksByWeek.2: Ja'Kobi Lane and the Ravens host the Saints for an interconference matchup in Week 2. The rookie third-round pick is doubtful to suit up with a fractured wrist sustained in the opener. Head coach Jesse Minter advised that Lane is seeking second and third medical opinions before establishing a timeline for his return. His health is something to monitor, but for now, his absence could make way for Devontez Walker (groin) and Elijah Sarratt (coach's decision).
outlooksByWeek.7: Ja'Kobi Lane and the Ravens return home to face off against the division-rival Bengals in Week 7. He impressed in his first game back from a four-week stint on injured reserve with a wrist injury suffered in Week 1, catching four of five targets for 40 yards during Baltimore's Week 6 defeat. Lane tied for second on the team in receptions and targets while finishing third in yardage, setting career highs across the board. With Rashod Bateman (shoulder) exiting the loss in the first half, Lane could see a boost in opportunities if the former is unable to suit up in Week 7. However, he'll be facing Cincinnati's ninth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (29.3) to WRs, so it's best to proceed with caution.
outlooksByWeek.8: Ja'Kobi Lane and the Ravens are in Buffalo for a Week 8 showdown. The rookie corralled three of five targets for 25 yards during Baltimore's 35-13 Week 7 defeat. Lane tied for second on the team in receptions and finished second behind Zay Flowers' 11 looks from Tyler Huntley. Lamar Jackson (ankle) has a decent chance to return against Buffalo's 32nd-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (42.3) to WRs, but Lane is still an unproven fantasy commodity on an offense that prefers to run the ball.

player.seasonOutlook: Lane was selected by the Ravens in the third round of April's draft. Lane is a tall, perimeter receiver with the biggest hands in this rookie class. He produced solid 43-525-12 and 49-745-4 receiving lines during his final two seasons at USC. Lane was rarely used in the intermediate area and struggled to produce after the catch (career 3.7 RAC is second worst in this class), but he has the frame and skill set to allow him plenty of pro potential. He'll battle the likes of Devontez Walker and fellow rookie Elijah Surratt for work behind Zay Flowers and Rashod Bateman in Baltimore's low-volume pass offense. Lane's primary value is as dynasty stash.

outlooksByWeek.2: Ryan Fitzgerald is in for a favorable Week 2 matchup when the Panthers face the Falcons, who gave up 8.0 kicking points in a Week 1 loss. Fitzgerald made five of his six kicks last week, drilling his only field-goal attempt while going four-for-five on point-after tries. He's expected to continue seeing plenty of scoring opportunities in Week 2, as he averaged 11.0 kicking points per game in two games against Atlanta in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Ryan Fitzgerald is expected to have plenty of scoring opportunities in the Panthers' Week 3 matchup against the Browns. Fitzgerald has started the season strong, converting on all three of his field-goal tries and eight of nine point-after attempts. Additionally, he could continue to benefit from the Panthers' offensive success, as the team currently ranks second in points per game (35.5). Fitzgerald is in for a great Week 3 matchup as well, with Cleveland allowing 11.5 kicking points per game through two contests this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Ryan Fitzgerald will look to continue building on an impressive performance in the Panthers' Week 4 matchup against the Lions. Fitzgerald was perfect in Carolina's Week 3 loss, converting on all four of his field-goal tries. On the season, he's made all seven field-goal attempts and eight of nine point-after tries. Fitzgerald expected to continue seeing plenty of scoring opportunities in Week 4, as Detroit's defense has allowed 31.7 points per game this season, despite giving up just 5.0 kicking points per game.
outlooksByWeek.6: Ryan Fitzgerald will look to bounce back from a poor performance in Carolina's Week 6 matchup against the Eagles. Despite an upset win over the Lions in Week 4, Fitzgerald made just two of four point-after attempts. On the season, the second-year pro has made all nine field goals but has struggled on extra points, converting on just 10 of 13 tries. He's in for a tougher Week 6 matchup as well, with Philadelphia's defense allowing just 6.8 kicking pints per game this year.
outlooksByWeek.7: Ryan Fitzgerald will likely have plenty of scoring opportunities in Carolina's Week 7 matchup against the Buccaneers. Fitzgerald has struggled over the last two contests, making just three of six point-after attempts. On the season, Fitzgerald is a perfect 11-for-11 on field-goal tries but just 11 of 15 on extra-point attempts. He's in for a very favorable Week 7 matchup against a Buccaneers defense that's given up 10.0 kicking points per game this season.
outlooksByWeek.8: Ryan Fitzgerald will likely have limited scoring opportunities in the Panthers' Week 8 matchup against the Packers. Fitzgerald made just one of two point-after tries in the Week 7 loss to the Buccaneers and has now missed five this season. Despite going 11 for 11 on field-goal attempts, Fitzgerald has converted on a league-low 70.6% of his extra points. He likely won't have many scoring chances against Green Bay either, as the Packers defense has allowed just 4.7 kicking points per game this season, the fewest in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.9: Ryan Fitzgerald likely won't have many scoring opportunities in the Panthers' Week 9 matchup against the Broncos. Fitzgerald was perfect in the Week 8 loss to the Packers, making all three of his kicks (two field goals and one extra point). On the season, Fitzgerald has converted on all 13 of his field goal tries but just 13 of his 18 point-after attempts. He could have few scoring chances against the Broncos as well, with Denver's defense allowing just 7.6 kicking points per game this year.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kalif Raymond could continue to be a consistent option as the Bears play the Vikings in Week 2. Raymond benefited from a high-scoring Week 1 win, reeling in eight of nine targets for 84 yards. The veteran wide receiver was also on the field for 60 percent of offensive snaps, so it appears at least a WR3 role is cemented moving forward. He'll face a Minnesota defense that ceded the second-most PPR points (55.2) to his position this past Sunday.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kalif Raymond will look to stay involved as the Bears play the Eagles in Week 3. Raymond was a consistent option once again in Week 2 against the Vikings, catching all five of his targets for 40 yards. The veteran wide receiver has now recorded 13 catches for 124 yards on 14 targets through two games. With quarterback Tyson Bagent also slated to get the start under center, Raymond could be a safe target against a middle-of-the-pack Philly defense against WRs (29.4 PPR points per game).
outlooksByWeek.4: Kalif Raymond will look to continue his tear as the Bears play the Jets in Week 4. Raymond remained a top option in Chicago's passing game in Week 3 against the Eagles, pulling in six of seven targets for 90 yards and a touchdown. The Lion transfer has now garnered five or more targets in each game this season, and eclipsed 80 yards in two of three. He'll face a Jets secondary that's been tougher on WRs this season, allowing a top-five 337 receiving yards to the position so far.
outlooksByWeek.5: Kalif Raymond will seek to reestablish himself as a consistent option in Chicago's passing game against the Packers in Week 5. After totaling 19 catches for 214 yards and one touchdown across the Bears' first three games of the season, Raymond recorded just two catches for six yards versus the Jets in Week 4 with Tyson Bagent under center. The veteran pass catcher will have Bagent throwing to him once again this Sunday, but he will also face a Green Bay defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against wide receivers so far this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.6: Kalif Raymond will look to bounce back as the Bears play the Falcons in Week 6. After an impressive start to the season, Raymond has now caught five passes for just 12 yards in the past two weeks. Chicago has had struggles at the quarterback position in this stretch, but the veteran still appears behind Rome Odunze and Luther Burden in the WR pecking order. Raymond will face an Atlanta defense that's ranked 27th in fantasy points allowed to his position this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Kalif Raymond remains a secondary option in Chicago's passing game in Week 7 against the Patriots. Raymond was unable to capitalize on Caleb Williams' return in Week 6, recording just two catches for 18 yards. After an impressive start to the season, Raymond is now situated behind Rome Odunze, Luther Burden and Colston Loveland in the target hierarchy. He'll take on a New England defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack versus fantasy WRs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Kalif Raymond figures to be a depth option once again as the Bears play the Seahawks in Week 8. Raymond logged his first catch-less game of the season in Week 7, which only supports the fact that his role has diminished at this point in the year. The veteran pass catcher remains a safe option in the passing game, but he's way behind Rome Odunze and Luther Burden in the wide receiver hierarchy. Seattle has ranked first in fantasy points allowed to WRs so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.9: Kalif Raymond remains a secondary option in Chicago's offense heading into Week 9 against Tampa Bay. Raymond finished a Week 8 win over the Seahawks with two catches for 14 yards, and he tacked on one rush for 39 yards. The veteran has taken a major backseat to Rome Odunze and Luther Burden in the WR hierarchy at this point in the season, but he's still a reliable option when needed for quarterback Caleb Williams. Raymond will face a Bucs defense that's ranked eighth in fantasy points allowed to WRs.

outlooksByWeek.7: Bam Knight got an extended opportunity in the absence of Jeremiyah Love (ankle) in Week 6 against the Rams and made the most of the situation, notching 15 carries for 80 yards and outplaying Tyler Allgeier, who mustered just 38 rushing yards on 18 rushing attempts. It remains to be seen whether Love will be an option in the backfield in Week 7, as much of that will depend on whether Love is cleared to play, but he's a player worth keeping close tabs on in the event Love isn't 100 percent ready. The matchup is favorable on paper, as the Broncos have given up the sixth-most fantasy points per game to opposing tailbacks this season.
outlooksByWeek.9: Bam Knight's status for Arizona's Week 9 battle in Seattle is in question due to a concussion he suffered this past Sunday. The head injury happened when Knight took a shoulder from a Dallas defender to his helmet, and he subsequently entered concussion protocol. He'll need to clear the NFL's concussion protocol before being eligible for game action again, but if he is able to play in Week 9, he could see a decent share of action given that No. 1 RB Jeremiyah Love is dealing with an ankle injury. The Arizona run game could struggle against a Seattle defense that is giving up just 3.28 yards per carry to running backs, though Chicago's D'Andre Swift did just burn the Seahawks for three rushing scores on Monday Night Football.

outlooksByWeek.3: Darren Waller could remain a valuable part of the Panthers' offense in the Week 3 matchup against the Browns. Through two games, Waller appears to be the Panthers' top receiving option at tight end, leading the TE room in yards (66), receptions (five) and touchdowns (two). However, having only received five targets through two weeks, Waller is likely a touchdown-or-bust streaming option going forward. He's in for a tough Week 3 matchup against a Browns defense that's given up just 10.5 PPR fantasy points per game to the position this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Darren Waller continues to emerge as a major part of the Panthers' passing attack ahead of the Week 4 matchup against the Lions. Waller had his most productive outing of the 2026 campaign in the Week 3 loss to the Browns, catching five of eight targets for 51 yards. He's taken over as Carolina's top receiving option at TE and could continue receiving more opportunities if Jalen Coker (hamstring) or Xavier Legette (knee) remain sidelined for Week 4. Regardless, Waller is in for a phenomenal Week 4 matchup against a Detroit defense that's allowed a whopping six receiving touchdowns to tight ends in three games this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Darren Waller is expected to remain Carolina's top receiving tight end during the Week 6 matchup against the Eagles. Despite signing with the Panthers in early August, Waller ranks first amongst the team's tight end corps in targets (19), receptions (13), yards (148) and touchdowns (two) through four games. Waller could receive fewer opportunities in Week 6, however, with Jalen Coker (quadriceps) expected to return from injury. Regardless, Waller is in for a difficult matchup against an Eagles defense that's allowed just 9.9 fantasy points per game to opposing TEs this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Darren Waller is expected to remain the Panthers' primary pass-catching tight end in the Week 7 matchup against the Buccaneers. Despite going with a catch in Carolina's Week 6 win over the Eagles, Waller still leads the TE corps in targets (18) and yards (148) through five contests. However, Waller will likely see less opportunities to score with Jalen Coker back from injury. Regardless, Waller is in for a favorable Week 7 matchup against a Tampa Bay defense that's already allowed four receiving touchdowns to TEs this year.
outlooksByWeek.8: Darren Waller is expected to remain Carolina's top receiving option at tight end in the Week 8 matchup against the Packers. Despite the Panthers' poor offensive performance in the Week 7 loss to the Buccaneers, Waller was productive, catching one of two targets for 50 yards and a touchdown. On the season, Waller has paced Carolina's tight-end corps in touchdowns (three), targets (22) and yards (198). However, he could struggle against a strong Packers defense in Week 8 that's allowed just 9.0 fantasy points per game to opposing TEs this season, the second-fewest in the NFL.
