outlooksByWeek.9: Darren Waller will look to bounce back from another poor performance in Carolina's Week 9 matchup against the Broncos. Waller has underwhelmed over the last two weeks, catching just two of four targets for 61 yards and a touchdown. Despite this, he still ranks first amongst Panthers tight ends in targets (24), yards (209) and touchdown (three), though he still likely isn't reliable enough to be a weekly starter. Waller could have success against Denver in Week 9, however, as its defense has allowed 16.9 fantasy points per game to tight ends this season, the sixth-most in the NFL.

outlooksByWeek.6: Roschon Johnson could be in line for another solid workday in Week 6 as the Bears play the Falcons. Johnson got solid opportunities in Chicago's Week 5 blowout loss to Green Bay, with Kyle Monangai out with a toe injury, rushing the ball five times for six yards and reeling in five of seven targets for 34 yards. Johnson's receiving upside could keep him relevant again if Monangai remains sidelined. He'll face an Atlanta defense that's ranked 21st in receiving yards allowed to RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Roschon Johnson could be in line for another solid workday again in Week 7 as the Bears play the Patriots. Johnson capitalized on his usage once again with Kyle Monangai (toe) sidelined in Week 6, rushing 13 times for 51 yards and a touchdown and catching two passes for 34 yards. He's now totaled 125 yards and a touchdown on 27 touches in the last two games with Monangai out. If this stays the case, Johnson will be playable against a New England defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy RBs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Roschon Johnson could return to a depth option as the Bears travel to Seattle in Week 8. Johnson benefited from the absence of Kyle Monangai (toe/thumb) in Weeks 5 and 6, but he logged just two carries for 13 yards in Week 7 against the Patriots. With Monangai tracking for a possible return in the upcoming away matchup, Johnson's role is unlikely to hold much value. If Monangai does sit out again, Johnson's worth keeping an eye on even versus a Seahawks defense that's ranked top 10 in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs (15.4).
outlooksByWeek.9: Roschon Johnson could return to being a depth option as the Bears play Tampa Bay in Week 9. Johnson has benefited from the absence of Kyle Monangai (toe/thumb) during the last four weeks, as he's averaging 9.5 touches per game in this stretch. Unfortunately, Monangai could return in the upcoming home front, which would shrink Johnson's role. Even if Monangai sits out again, Johnson would be a tough play against a Bucs defense that's allowed the fewest fantasy points per game to RBs.

outlooksByWeek.2: Justice Hill and the Ravens are at home to battle the Saints in Week 2. Hill rushed six times for 18 yards and had one catch for 10 yards in Baltimore's 41-23 win. He's established himself as the clear No. 2 RB, as his 31 offensive snaps trailed slightly behind Derrick Henry's 37. Hill should continue to see opportunities as a change-of-pace back against a New Orleans defense that ranks 28th in fantasy points allowed per game (38.4) to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Justice Hill and the Ravens travel to face a Cowboys defense in Week 3 that ranks 25th in fantasy points per game (25.9) allowed to running backs. He tallied two carries for six yards and caught both of his targets for eight yards during Baltimore's 24-17 Week 2 loss to the Saints. As long as Derrick Henry, who accounted for 16 of 18 carries out of the backfield, is healthy, Hill's action will be limited as the No. 2 RB. However, in a contest that is expected to be high-scoring, Hill could contribute as a receiver, but he's still a risky fantasy play outside of deeper leagues.
outlooksByWeek.4: Justice Hill and the Ravens are back home to host the 0-3 Titans in Week 4. He was explosive with his five carries during Baltimore's thrilling Week 3 victory, racking up 33 yards and a 6.6 average. However, Derrick Henry handled 26 of the 31 total carries for running backs, and he remains in firm control of the Ravens' backfield. Tennessee's defense ranks 17th in fantasy points allowed (20.7) to RBs, and despite the possibility of Baltimore playing from ahead, Hill's involvement will continue to be limited.
outlooksByWeek.5: Justice Hill and the Ravens visit the Falcons for a Week 5 showdown. He rushed once for three yards and caught two of three targets for 22 yards during Baltimore's 24-18 victory in Week 4. Derrick Henry out-carried Hill 23-1, even with Lamar Jackson missing the entire second half with an ankle injury. It appears that regardless of who's under center, the Ravens' backfield belongs to Henry. Hill should remain on fantasy benches against an Atlanta defense allowing just 17.9 points per game to RBs, which ranks ninth.
outlooksByWeek.6: Justice Hill and the Ravens visit the division-rival Browns in Week 6. He rushed four times for 73 yards and caught two of four targets for five yards during Baltimore's Week 5 overtime win. Derrick Henry out-carried him 24-4, although Hill led the way with a game-long 47-yard run. However, as long as Henry is the lead back and the Ravens don't fall into a massive deficit, Hill's involvement in the offense will remain limited.
outlooksByWeek.7: Justice Hill and the Ravens host the Bengals for an AFC North clash in Week 7. He did not record a carry but brought in all three of his targets for nine yards during Baltimore's 13-10 loss in Week 6. Derrick Henry accounted for 17 of the 18 rushing attempts out of the Ravens' backfield, a trend that should continue as long as he remains healthy. Hill should remain on fantasy benches against a Cincinnati defense that is tied for ninth in fantasy points allowed per game (19.0) to RBs
outlooksByWeek.8: Justice Hill and the Ravens are on the road for a Week 8 meeting with the Bills. He had three carries for seven yards and caught three of four targets for 26 yards during Baltimore's 35-13 loss in Week 7. Rasheen Ali registered 19 yards on four carries, but that can likely be attributed to the Ravens giving up all 35 points in the second half. Regardless, as long as Derrick Henry is healthy, Hill's involvement on offense will continue to be limited.
outlooksByWeek.9: Justice Hill and the Ravens return home for a meeting with the Jaguars on Thursday Night Football in Week 9. He rushed three times for 15 yards and caught four of eight targets for 20 yards during Baltimore's Week 8 loss. Hill led the team in receptions and targets while finishing second in yardage in a game where the Ravens managed just 167 total yards of offense. He could earn similar opportunities with Lamar Jackson (thumb) on IR and Joe Fagnano (knee) likely to start, but it's going to be difficult to trust any Baltimore player in fantasy going forward.

player.seasonOutlook: Hill heads into his seventh NFL season positioned for a larger role following the offseason departure of Keaton Mitchell. Derrick Henry remains the team's lead rusher, but he plays only about half of the snaps, leaving plenty of opportunity for Hill, particularly in passing situations. We've seen Hill in that role recently, including a 2024 campaign in which he posted a 42-383-3 receiving line on 55 targets (11th most among backs). Of course, Hill isn't trusted with much rushing work (his career high in carries is 84), which is why he has never had a top-35 fantasy campaign in his career. The 28-year-old has a limited ceiling and would be on the flex radar in PPR formats only if Henry were to miss time.

outlooksByWeek.2: AJ Barner is coming off a quiet season opener as Seattle heads to Arizona in Week 2. Barner logged just two catches on two targets for 13 yards against the Patriots last Wednesday, though those two receptions were tied for second-most on the squad. Drew Lock played most of that game at QB for Seattle, and he's expected to start in Week 2 with Sam Darnold dealing with a glute injury. The Cardinals gave up seven catches for 90  yards to Chargers tight ends in a win Sunday, so Barner could be a key target for Lock.
outlooksByWeek.3: AJ Barner should again lead Seattle's TE corps in a Week 3 tilt versus Washington. Barner logged a healthy 56 of the Seahawks' 70 offensive snaps Sunday versus the Cardinals, but he finished with just one catch (on one target) for eight yards. Barner did boost his fantasy line considerably with a rushing touchdown, though his three catches for 21 yards through two weeks isn't going to turn many heads. Nonetheless, he could be a sneaky option for Week 3 against a Commanders defense that has already given up four receiving TDs to tight ends, tied for most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: AJ Barner will look to build upon a big Week 3 performance when Seattle hosts the Chargers in Week 4. Against the Commanders this past Sunday, Barner registered season-high marks with five catches, nine targets and 69 yards. That production was particularly notable after the third-year tight end compiled just three catches on three targets for 21 yards over the first two weeks of the campaign. Barner could find additional success against the Chargers, who rank in the bottom half of the league in receiving yards allowed to tight ends so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: AJ Barner will look to amp up his production for Seattle in a Week 5 clash against the 49ers. Barner caught just one of three targets for 12 yards against the Chargers this past Sunday after posting a promising 5-69-0 receiving line the previous week. Barner logged nine targets in that Week 3 win over Washington, but he's drawn three or fewer targets in each of his other three contests. San Francisco has been tough against tight ends this season, giving up just 4.0 points per game to the position (fifth-best in the NFL).
outlooksByWeek.6: AJ Barner will look to get more involved as a pass catcher for Seattle in Week 6 against the Broncos. Barner caught three of five targets for 20 yards this past Sunday in a loss to San Francisco, with each of the catch, target and yardage totals representing his second-highest mark this season. Barner logged six receiving touchdowns across 17 regular-season games last year, but his only score this season has been on his lone rush attempt. Denver has struggled a bit against tight ends this season, giving up 9.9 fantasy points per game, ninth-most in the league.
outlooksByWeek.7: AJ Barner and the Seahawks return home for an interconference tilt against the Chiefs in Week 7. He caught three of four targets for 16 yards during Seattle's 17-14 overtime loss in Week 6. Outside of his five-catch, 69-yard performance (9 targets) in Week 3, Barner has a 10-69-0 receiving line on 15 targets in his other five games combined. With Jaxon Smith-Njigba commanding most of QB Sam Darnold's attention, it's hard to trust Barner as anything more than a backup TE. However, he could be a solid streaming option versus Kansas City's 30th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (20.0) to the position.
outlooksByWeek.8: AJ Barner should continue to lead Seattle's tight-end corps in Week 8 against the Bears. In Week 7 versus Kansas City, Barner recorded his second-most catches (four) and receiving yards (42) in a contest this season. Though he's yet to get into the end zone and isn't putting up prolific numbers, Barner has logged an offensive snap count of at least 80% in each of the Seahawks seven games. Chicago ranks 17th in the NFL by giving up 8.3fantasy points per game to tight ends.
outlooksByWeek.9: AJ Barner continues to put together a quiet campaign for Seattle heading into a Week 9 matchup against the Cardinals. Though Barner has consistently logged high offensive snap shares as the Seahawks' No. 1 tight end, he's exceeded three catches just twice through eight contests. Against Chicago in Week 8, he put up a modest 2-23-0 line but did draw five targets, tying his second-highest mark this season. Barner may be able to be more efficient against the Cardinals, who have allowed a 78.6% catch rate to tight ends, tied for fourth-highest in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Barner was a solid contributor for the Seattle offense last season. The 2024 fourth-round pick worked his way to the top of the depth chart, and although his overall volume was limited (20th among TEs in targets and yards), he found the end zone seven times and finished 14th in fantasy points (21st in PPG). The 24-year-old is a serviceable, short-range target for Sam Darnold, but even with some rushing worked in, his role in Seattle's low-volume passing offense won't allow much upside. In fact, it's possible he loses some targets to second-year TE Elijah Arroyo this season. Barner is a fringe TE2, at best.

outlooksByWeek.2: Wil Lutz's opportunities were minimal in the Broncos' season-opening loss to Kansas City, converting his only extra point and his sole field-goal attempt from 31 yards. The veteran kicker had been productive in his first three years with Denver, averaging just under 30 FGs and 38 extra points per season while going 12-for-18 on field-goal attempts of 50-plus yards. In Week 2, Lutz will take on a Jaguars team that ranked eighth in points per game allowed in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Wil Lutz has been perfect to begin the season for the Broncos, and in a Week 2 win over the Jaguars, he converted both his field-goal attempts and both his PATs. The veteran kicker has been consistent since following Sean Payton northwest from New Orleans, and kicking at altitude has allowed him to be reliable from long range, but the Denver offense doesn't provide him with enough opportunities to be among the elite at his position. Lutz will face a Rams team in Week 3 that just kept the Giants out of the end zone but which has allowed five FG attempts through two games.
outlooksByWeek.4: Wil Lutz missed his first kick of the season in the Broncos' Week 3 win over the Rams, hitting the left upright on a 43-yard field goal attempt but connecting on both his extra points. Game flow cost him opportunities, as Denver headed into halftime down 16-0 and attempted two-point conversions multiple times as part of their comeback. Lutz has converted three FGs and five extra points through three games, and his volume may not improve substantially until his offense develops some consistency. He'll take on a 49ers team in Week 4 that's allowed just 16.7 points a game, tied for third in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Wil Lutz continues to get little volume thanks to the struggles of the Broncos' offense. Through four games, the veteran kicker has attempted only five extra points, converting all, while going just 5-for-7 on FG attempts, with one of his misses coming from 58 yards out. Lutz is reliable, especially with most of his games coming either at altitude or indoors, but without more opportunities, he won't be able to make much of a contribution. He could get more chances in Week 5 against a Chargers team that has allowed 26.5 points per game, 24th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Wil Lutz has missed field goal attempts in the Broncos' last two games, but he's also benefited from increased volume, going 5-for-7 on FGs and 2-for-2 on PATs. The veteran kicker has had his production dragged down by the struggles of the offense, but with Sean Payton calling plays again, Lutz's outlook has brightened a little. He'll face a Seahawks team in Week 6 that's allowed 21.0 points per game this season, eighth in the league.
outlooksByWeek.7: Wil Lutz played hero for the Broncos in Week 6, with his only field goal coming in overtime during a win over the Seahawks. The veteran kicker's volume is inconsistent thanks to Denver's struggling offense, and through six games, he's gone 9-for-12 on FG attempts and a perfect 9-for-9 on extra points. Lutz could be busier than usual in Week 7 against a Cardinals team that's allowed 29.7 points per game, tied with the Saints for the worst mark in the league.
outlooksByWeek.8: Wil Lutz was busy and efficient in the Broncos' Week 7 win over the Cardinals, converting all three of his extra points and all three of his field-goal attempts for a season-best 12 points. The veteran kicker has booted multiple FGs in three of the last four games and multiple PATs in three straight, but the overall struggles of the Denver offense put a cap on Lutz's upside. He likely won't be able to squander any opportunities in Week 8 against a Kansas City team that ranks second in the NFL in points per game allowed.
outlooksByWeek.9: Wil Lutz hasn't missed a kick in three straight games, connecting on both his field goal attempts and both his PATs in the Broncos' Week 8 win over Kansas City. The veteran kicker is a perfect 14-for-14 on extra points this season, but his 82.4% showing on FG attempts (14-for-17, including two misses from inside 50 yards) would be his worst mark in four years since following Sean Payton to Denver from New Orleans. Lutz could see plenty of opportunities to improve that performance in Week 9 against a Panthers team that just fired its defensive coordinator after allowing 27.6 points a game, 28th in the league, through the first half of the season.

outlooksByWeek.2: Mack Hollins will look to capitalize on an elevated role in Week 2 when the Patriots face the Steelers. Hollins caught four of his five targets to open the year, finishing with 51 yards, and could slide into A.J. Brown's (ankle) vacated outside role. Hollins and DeMario Douglas have the trust of Drake Maye, something that can't currently be said for Romeo Doubs, suggesting Hollins will play against a secondary that's without top corner Joey Porter Jr. Hollins' size makes him a capable red zone target, which generates upside.
outlooksByWeek.3: Mack Hollins will seek a bounce back performance in Week 3 when the Patriots face the Jaguars. After a solid four catch, 51-yard opener with A.J. Brown leaving early, Hollins notched only two targets in Week 2. New England's passing game is struggling with Drake Maye completing just 14 passes in Week 2. Until he begins to bounce back, trusting any of his pass catchers appears a risky proposition even against a defense that is allowing a generous 10.3 yards per target.
outlooksByWeek.4: Mack Hollins will look to lead the Patriots' receiving corps in Week 4 against the Bills. Hollins gathered a season-high nine targets in Week 3, following just seven total in the team's first two games, as the Patriots continue to search for a top option without A.J. Brown (ankle) available. Drake Maye is struggling to move this offense, but Week 4 offers the potential to match the Bills' high-scoring offense. Buffalo is allowing the fifth-most fantasy points to opposing receivers and an enticing 9.2 yards per target.
outlooksByWeek.5: Mack Hollins' availability for Week 5 against the Raiders is in doubt due to a calf injury. Hollins has been a steady but unspectacular piece for the Patriots' receiving corps, going for 51 or more yards three times despite topping five targets just once with A.J. Brown sidelined by an ankle injury. Las Vegas can be vulnerable to opposing receivers, surrendering 70 or more yards four times. Efton Chism filled in after Hollins' early Week 4 exit and would likely do so again if Hollins does not suit up.

outlooksByWeek.2: Roman Wilson and the Steelers visit the Patriots in Week 2 as they look to improve to 2-0. He caught three of six targets for 26 yards during Pittsburgh's 20-13 Week 1 victory versus Atlanta. Wilson tied for second on the team in targets and was on the field for 37 of 67 offensive snaps. Despite the solid start, it's best he remains on benches or waiver wires until he can prove to be a consistent fantasy contributor.
outlooksByWeek.3: Roman Wilson and the Steelers welcome the division rival Bengals to town for a Week 3 matchup. With Michael Pittman (foot) on the sidelines last Sunday, Wilson stepped into the No. 2 receiver role behind DK Metcalf. He finished the 20-3 loss with a team-high five catches for 28 yards on six targets. Rookie Germie Bernard was one of Aaron Rodgers' favorite receivers, however, turning eight targets into four catches and a team-leading 35 yards. Pittman's status is cloudy at best for Week 3, but Wilson and the Steelers face a Cincinnati defense allowing 25.0 fantasy points per game (9th) to WRs, so he's best left on benches for now.
outlooksByWeek.4: Roman Wilson and the Steelers visit the Browns for an AFC North showdown in Week 4. He caught three of six targets for 60 yards and his first touchdown of the season during Pittsburgh's Week 3 victory. Wilson led the team in targets, tied for first in receptions, and finished second behind Darnell Washington in yardage. He has a favorable matchup versus Cleveland's 26th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (36.7) to WRs, but it's still difficult to trust him with so many mouths to feed in the Steelers' offense.
outlooksByWeek.5: Roman Wilson and the Steelers take on the Colts at home in Week 5. He caught three of six targets for 74 yards and one touchdown during Pittsburgh's Week 4 loss. Wilson tied for second on the team in receptions and targets while finishing second in yardage, and he now has a TD catch in two consecutive contests. He's been a reliable option for Aaron Rodgers, as he's generated six targets in all four outings this season en route to a 14-188-2 line. Wilson's next opportunity comes against the Colts' 20th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (35.0) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Roman Wilson and the Steelers travel to face the Buccaneers in Week 6. He failed to catch his only target prior to exiting Pittsburgh's 34-22 win in Week 5 with a finger injury. Wilson has already been ruled out for the trip to Tampa Bay, meaning Germie Bernard should see a boost in playing time and opportunities in his absence.

outlooksByWeek.2: Malachi Fields tied for third on the Giants in targets in Week 1. Fields caught two passes for 25 yards on four targets in his debut. Only Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely had more targets. The Giants are rather thin at wideout behind the aforementioned Nabers, and Fields is a huge target at 6-4, 225-lbs, so expect him to continue to be a decent contributor to the revamped offense. In Week 2, the G-Men will face a Rams defense that allowed 205 passing yards and three passing scores in a lackluster season-opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Malachi Fields finished third in receptions and second in targets for the Giants last game. Despite seeing increased involvement, Fields caught just two passes for just 30 yards in the dismal loss to the Rams. The bigger news may be that starting quarterback Jaxson Dart could be lost for the season due to a knee injury. With Jameis Winston under center, Fields will likely see his stock take a hit. However, in Week 3, the Giants will face a lackluster Titans defense allowing 233.5 passing yards per clash, which is 20th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Malachi Fields has two catches in each of his first three NFL games for the Giants.  Unfortunately, he has yet to find the end zone, and has not amassed more than 30 yards in any single contest.  Jameis Winston has been uninspiring to say the least at quarterback, which limits the upside for Fields as well. Winston should remain under center in Week 4 versus a vulnerable Cardinals defense. Arizona is allowing 234.3 passing yards per game, which is 22nd in the NFL. In addition, Arizona has allowed eight passing touchdowns already, which is 30th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Malachi Fields scored his first NFL touchdown last game for the Giants. The rookie flashed his big-play ability, snagging a 40-yarder from quarterback Jameis Winston along with the 12-yard score. He finished with two catches for a career-best 52 yards and the touchdown. In Week 5, Fields and company will face a Commanders defense that has struggled to defend the pass. Washington has allowed 11 passing scores, which is tied for last in the NFL. In addition, the Commanders are yielding 242.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 25th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Malachi Fields saw just two targets last game for the Giants. Meanwhile, star teammate Malik Nabers had a staggering 20 looks in the 27-27 tie with the Commanders. The production for the rookie Fields has been rather consistent through five contests, as he has two catches in every outing. In Week 6, the Giants host the Saints. New Orleans has been fairly stingy against the pass in 2026, allowing just 212.2 passing yards per tilt, which is 11th in the league. However, New Orleans has also given up eight passing scores already, which is tied for 20th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Malachi Fields finished third on the Giants in targets last game. Fields was targeted eight times, though managed two catches for just 18 yards in the 34-27 loss to the Saints. Fields has emerged as the No. 2 wideout behind Malik Nabers, though Isaiah Likely at tight end has also been extremely busy as a pass catcher. Fields has at least two catches in every game he's played, though has just 12 catches on the season. In Week 7, the Giants will face a porous Texans secondary allowing 246 passing yards per contest, which is 27th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.9: Malachi Fields is coming off a career-best performance for the Giants. Fields snagged four passes for 83 yards in the thrilling 27-21 OT win over the Texans. The rookie has caught at least two passes in every game in 2026. In Week 9, the Giants face divisional rival Philadelphia, which has struggled to defend the pass. Philadelphia's defense is allowing 235.4 passing yards per tilt, which is 24th in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Fields was selected by the Giants in the third round of April's draft. One of the biggest and strongest receivers in this rookie class, Fields figures to work as a perimeter, vertical target in the pros (career 13.3 aDOT during 49 collegiate games). Fields, who dropped just seven passes in college, handled a target share of, at least, 20% and air yard share of, at least, 30% during each of his final three collegiate seasons (two at Virginia, one at Notre Dame). Fields will battle Darnell Mooney and Darius Slayton for New York's No. 2 receiver gig behind Malik Nabers. The rookie is a fine late-round flier.

outlooksByWeek.9: Corey Kiner has had a minimal role in the Patriots' backfield entering a Week 9 matchup with the Packers. Kiner has rushed for 38 yards or more in three of the last four games, despite Rhamondre Stevenson leading the way in touches and TreVeyon Henderson factoring in when healthy. If Henderson were sidelined again in Week 9, Kiner may still not gather enough volume to be an option against a defense that's allowing 3.96 yards per carry.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tank Bigsby managed just one carry for the Eagles in Week 1. Bigsby rushed once for three yards in the 24-22 win over the Commanders. Meanwhile, fellow backup Will Shipley garnered three total touches for 12 yards. Both rushers remain firmly behind Saquon Barkley on the depth chart, though could see extra run in Week 2 if the game gets out of hand versus the Titans.  Tennessee allowed 367 yards from scrimmage to the Jets in their season opener. Tennessee was torched on the ground in particular, allowing 152 rushing yards and two touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tank Bigsby had 15 touches and a touchdown in Week 2 versus the Titans after Saquon Barkley suffered a stinger injury. Saquon missed portions of the game due to the ailment, leaving his status in question for Week 3 versus the Bears. Barkley is slated to undergo an MRI to determine if he will miss any time. Bigsby and Will Shipley would likely split touches if Barkley cannot go, with Bigsby getting the slight edge. The Eagles will face a Bears run defense in Week 3 allowing 122 yards per clash on the ground, which is 22nd in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tank Bigsby returned to his backup role last game for the Eagles. With Saquon Barkley recovered from his stinger, Bigsby did not receive a carry in the dismal loss to the Bears. Barring injury, Bigsby will get little run in Week 4 versus the Rams. Los Angeles is allowing 101.3 rushing yards per tilt, which is 11th in the NFL. In addition, the Rams have yielded just one rushing score through the first three games of the season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tank Bigsby replaced an injured Saquon Barkley last game for the Eagles, only to suffer an injury of his own late in the contest. Bigsby rushed 14 times for 55 yards to lead the Eagles before exiting with a lower-body issue. His status is up in the air for Week 5 versus the Jags. If neither Bigsby nor Barkley can play, Will Shipley would be in line for an expanded role. However, Jacksonville has played the run extremely well thus far in 2026. The Jags are allowing just 74.3 rushing yards per tote, which us second in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Bigsby was acquired by the Eagles early in the 2025 season and progressively worked his way up to primary backup duties, a role he's expected to play again in 2026. Granted, it's a small sample, but Bigsby has been extremely efficient over the last two seasons. Among 48 backs with 200-plus carries during the span, Bigsby ranks first in yards after contact per attempt (2.75) and eighth in yards per carry (4.86). In fact, Bigsby has led qualified RBs in YAC each of the last two seasons. On the other hand, he hasn't been used much as a receiver (20 career targets). With overworked Saquon Barkley entering his age-29 season, Bigsby certainly has some insurance appeal, even if he defers passing-down work to Will Shipley. Bigsby, 25, is worth consideration in the later rounds.

outlooksByWeek.2: Drew Lock is expected to serve as Seattle's starting quarterback in Week 2 versus Arizona due to Sam Darnold's glute injury. Lock took over in the first quarter of the Seahawks' season opener and guided the team to a win, completing 16 of 22 passes for 187 yards and one touchdown with no interceptions. Lock's TD was a 45-yard connection with Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who again figures to be his top target against the Cardinals. Arizona is coming off a surprising win against the Chargers, during which they limited Justin Herbert to 209 yards and an interception.
outlooksByWeek.3: Drew Lock could have another opportunity to lead Seattle's offense in Week 3 versus Washington. Lock started for the injured Sam Darnold (glute) on Sunday versus Arizona and threw for 235 yards with three touchdowns. Darnold is reportedly making good progress in his recovery, so it's not yet clear who will helm the team's offense in Week 3. Whichever QB gets the opportunity could be in for a big game against the Commanders, who have allowed a league-high seven passing touchdowns and have no interceptions through two weeks.

outlooksByWeek.2: Calvin Ridley wasn't targeted in Tennessee's season opener and is off the fantasy radar completely heading into a Week 2 home game against the elite Eagles secondary. The veteran WR may be as low as fifth in the Titans' WR pecking order behind Carnell Tate, Wan'Dale Robinson, Elic Ayomanor, and Chimere Dike. Second-year QB Cam Ward has struggled to keep any of his pass catchers consistently fantasy-relevant, let alone depth options.
outlooksByWeek.3: Calvin Ridley has drawn just two targets through two games in Tennessee's underwhelming passing game. The Titans don't have a player with more than 80 receiving yards heading into a Week 3 road game against the Giants, so Ridley's fantasy value is slim to none as a depth piece behind Carnell Tate and Wan'Dale Robinson. The Giants have struggled to defend WRs, but Ridley is unlikely to get enough passes thrown his way to capitalize on facing the banged-up Giants secondary.
outlooksByWeek.4: Calvin Ridley has just two catches through three games heading into the Titans' Week 4 trip to Baltimore. The Ravens have allowed the second-most catches to WRs this season, but Ridley remains a fantasy non-factor as a depth piece in a Titans offense that has generated the third-fewest passing yards in the NFL. Ridley is firmly behind Carnell Tate and Wan'Dale Robinson on the depth chart, and the 31-year-old WR has also been outplayed by Elic Ayomanor.
outlooksByWeek.5: Calvin Ridley has just three catches for 48 yards on five targets through four games. He's barely contributing as the No. 4 WR in a Titans offense that's averaging just 13.8 points per game, which is the second-fewest in the NFL. Even in a Week 5 matchup against a Texans defense that has struggled to defend wide receivers, Ridley remains a non-factor in fantasy.
outlooksByWeek.6: Calvin Ridley hasn't exceeded 35 yards in a game this season and has been blanked twice. The 31-year-old wide receiver appears to have lost a step after fracturing his fibula last season and has fallen to No. 4 on Tennessee's wide receiver depth chart behind Carnell Tate, Wan'Dale Robinson, and Elic Ayomanor. With QB Cam Ward averaging a meager 179 passing yards per game, Ridley is unlikely to post his first fantasy-relevant performance of the season in Week 6, even against the Colts' subpar secondary.
outlooksByWeek.7: Calvin Ridley finished without a catch in three of six games this season for the Titans and has just five receptions for 81 yards overall. The veteran WR has been relegated to a depth role at this stage of his career and can continue to be ignored in fantasy. After improving to 1-5 with a Week 6 win over the Colts, the Titans will host the 4-2 Browns in Week 7.
outlooksByWeek.8: Calvin Ridley (hip) sat out for the Titans in Week 7 against the Browns. Even if he returns for Week 8 against the Bengals, Ridley won't be a viable fantasy option. He has caught a pass in only three of six appearances this season, with season totals of five catches for 81 yards while operating in a depth role at WR.

player.seasonOutlook: Ridley's second season in Tennessee did not go as planned, as the veteran receiver missed 10 full games and was limited to a career-low 17 receptions. He remained a featured target when healthy (seven-plus targets in his four full games), but that led to only one double-digit fantasy performance. The lost season comes after Ridley delivered consecutive 1,000-yard seasons, finishing both as a top-30 fantasy receiver. Ridley is now 31 years old and has added target competition with Carnell Tate and Wan'Dale Robinson in the mix. A Year 2 leap from Cam Ward could get Ridley back into the flex discussion, but it's more likely that he's headed for a reduced role. Ridley is worth no more than a middle-round flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jake Elliott was perfect on all four of his kicks in Week 1 for the Eagles. Elliott connected on a 33-yard field goal as well as three extra points in the 24-22 win over the Commanders. In Week 2, Elliott will face a Titans squad that allowed a plethora of points last season. Tennessee gave up an average of 28.1 points per clash in 2025, which was 28th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jake Elliott nailed a 58-yard field goal in Philadelphia's last game. Elliott has not missed a kick through two games for the Eagles, connecting on two field goals and six PATs. In Week 3, the Eagles will face a Bears squad allowing 23 points per contest, which is in the middle of the pack thus far this NFL season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jake Elliott did not attempt a field goal last game for the Eagles, as the offense was stymied in the 27-7 loss to the Bears. Elliott did hit his lone extra point, though has now made just two field goals in three contests thus far this season. In Week 4, Philadelphia will face a Rams squad allowing 21 points per tilt, which is tied for 13th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jake Elliott still managed two field goals and two extra points last game for Philadelphia, despite massive struggles on offense for the Eagles. Elliott has just four field goals through four contests, as the Philadelphia offense has sputtered in part due to a bevy of injuries to skill players. With DeVonta Smith, Dallas Goedert and potentially Saquon Barkley sidelined for Week 5 versus the Jags, points may be at a premium. The Jags have also been extremely stingy in terms of points allowed this season. Jacksonville is giving up only 13.3 points per tilt, which is second in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jake Elliott connected on his lone field goal attempt last game for the Eagles. Elliott made a 48-yarder that initially looked like the game-winner, only for Philadelphia to somehow squander away the victory. Elliott has hit one field goal or fewer in all but one game in 2026, as the Eagles offense has struggled due to injury and inconsistency. However, in Week 6, the Eagles will face a Panthers squad allowing 27.3 points per contest, which is 27th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jake Elliott managed just two extra points last game for the Eagles, as the Philadelphia offense sputtered without Jalen Hurts. Tanner McKee lined up under center, and should continue to be the quarterback as Hurts will be sidelined for the season. Even with Hurts at the helm, the Eagles offense had failed to score more than 20 points in each of the previous three contests. Saquon Barkley continues to be sidelined as well. In sum, Elliott's prospects for a plethora of points does not look hopeful, even against a Dallas squad in Week 7 allowing 26.5 points per tilt, which is 25th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jake Elliott has not even attempted a field goal over the last two games for the Eagles. With Tanner McKee taking over the offense for Jalen Hurts, the offense has continued to sputter. The Eagles have scored 21 points or fewer in every contest during the current five-game losing streak.  In fact, Elliott has only attempted five field goals on the entire season. If the Eagles cannot put up points against an extremely suspect Washington defense in Week 8, Elliott's utility may have come to an end. The Commanders are allowing 28.7 points per game in 2026, which is second-to-last in the league.
outlooksByWeek.9: Jake Elliott has made just two field goals over his last four games for the Eagles. The Philadelphia offense has sputtered due to a bevy of injuries, scoring fewer than 20 points in three of those four contests. That has led to limited opportunities for Elliott, who also missed a three-pointer in the most recent loss to Washington. In Week 9, the Eagles will face division-leading New York. The Giants are allowing 23 points per tilt, which is 15th in the NFL.

outlooksByWeek.8: Eli Raridon could be a sneaky option when the Patriots face the Dolphins in Week 8. Since not playing in Week 3, Raridon has garnered 14 targets over the last four games, turning them into 10 catches and a touchdown. While the volume isn't elite and New England continues to spread passing work across a plethora of options, Miami has been very vulnerable to opposing tight ends, allowing six touchdowns in as many weeks and the second-highest yards per target at 9.3, suggesting Raridon could pop with minimal opportunities.

player.seasonOutlook: Raridon was selected by the Patriots in the third round of April's draft. Raridon is a tall, blocking tight end who was barely targeted (5% share) and totaled a 48-623-3 receiving line during four seasons at Notre Dame. Most of the receiving work came in 2025, so perhaps there's some hope in that area, but he's a long shot for fantasy value any time soon, especially with Hunter Henry ahead of him on the depth chart this season.

outlooksByWeek.2: Nick Folk will look to bounce back from a tough performance in the Falcons' Week 2 matchup against the Panthers. The 41-year-old went made just three of the five kicks he attempted in the Week 1 loss, missing field-goals from 54 and 45 yards. He could be in line to continue receiving scoring opportunities, with Atlanta's offense struggling to find the end zone last week. Additionally, Folk is in for a great matchup, with Carolina allowing 11 kicking points in a Week 1 loss to the Bears.
outlooksByWeek.3: Nick Folk's early-season struggled could continue in the Falcons' Week 3 matchup against the Packers, who have allowed just 6.0 kicking points per game this season. Through two games in 2026, Folk has made just three of six field-goal tries, which is the worst mark in the NFL. He could benefit from the return of quarterback Michael Penix, however, who is expected to drive improvement after Atlanta's offense averaged just 8.0 points per game prior to his return.
outlooksByWeek.4: Nick Folk could have plenty of scoring opportunities in the Falcons' Week 4 matchup against the Saints. Folk has struggled through three weeks this season, converting on just five of eight field-goal tries while making all four point-after attempts. He had his best game of the year in the Week 3 win over the Packers, making all five of his kicks (two field goals and three extra points). With Michael Penix back at the helm, Folk could see more scoring opportunities going forward. Additionally, Folk is in for a favorable Week 4 matchup against a Saints defense that's allowed 7.7 kicking points per game this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Nick Folk is expected to have plenty of scoring opportunities in the Falcons' Week 5 matchup against the Ravens. Since the return of Michael Penix in Week 3, Folk has converted all 12 of his kicks (three field goals and nine extra points), averaging 9.0 kicking points per game. With Atlanta's recent offensive success (40.0 points per game over the last two weeks) and Baltimore's defense having allowed 24.0 points and 7.5 kicking points per game, Folk is expected to have a favorable Week 5 matchup.
outlooksByWeek.6: Nick Folk will likely continue having scoring opportunities in the Falcons' Week 6 matchup against the Bears. Folk was perfect in the Week 5 overtime loss to the Ravens, making three field goals and two extra points. On the season, he's converted on nine of 12 field-goal tries but all 12 of his point-after attempts. He could have plenty of scoring chance in Week 6, as Chicago's defense just allowed 31 points while Packers' kicker Trey Smack attempted six kicks (three field goals and three extra points).
outlooksByWeek.7: Nick Folk could have plenty of scoring opportunities when the Falcons take on the 49ers in Week  7. Folk converted on his lone point-after attempt in the Week 6 loss to the Bears, with the Falcons converting on two two-point conversions in the second half. On the season, Folk has made nine of 12 field-goal tries and all 13 of his point-after attempts. The veteran kicker is in for a favorable Week 7 matchup as well, with San Francisco's defense giving up 8.6 kicking points per game through five contests this year.
outlooksByWeek.8: Nick Folk will likely have plenty of scoring opportunities in the Falcons' Week 8 matchup against the Buccaneers. Folk went five-for-six on kicks during the Week 7 win over the 49ers, making all three field goals but just two of three extra points. On the season, the veteran kicker has converted on 12 of 15 field-goal attempts and 15 of 16 point-after tries. He's in for a favorable Week 8 matchup against a Buccaneers defense that's allowed 8.7 kicking points per game this season.
outlooksByWeek.9: Nick Folk could have plenty of scoring opportunities in the Falcons' Week 9 matchup against the Bengals. Folk struggled in the pouring rain during the Week 8 loss to the Buccaneers, missing his only field goal try of the game. On the season, the veteran kicker has converted just 12 of 16 field goal attempts and 15 of 16 point-after tries. He could find success in Week 9, however, as Cincinnati's defense has allowed 8.0 kicking points per game this season.

outlooksByWeek.2: Greg Dulcich will look for increased target share in Week 2 when the Dolphins face the 49ers. Entering the season opener, Miami had minimal proven pass catchers, creating optimism around Dulcich, but despite a 74% snap rate, Dulcich was targeted just twice. San Francisco allowed just four catches and 31 yards to tight ends in their opener, so even if Miami is forced to throw from behind, it doesn't yet appear Dulcich has Malik Willis' eye, suggesting there are better fantasy options.
outlooksByWeek.3: Greg Dulcich's opportunities have been limited in Miami's passing game heading into a Week 3 matchup with the Chiefs. Dulcich has four total catches on five targets to open the year, tallying 35 yards. Kansas City has allowed volume to the position through two weeks, surrendering 12 catches and two touchdowns, but just 74 total yards and 4.6 yards per target. Better fantasy options are available.
outlooksByWeek.4: Greg Dulcich will look to build on Week 3's momentum in Week 4 when the Dolphins face the Vikings. After just five targets in his first two weeks, Dulcich recorded seven in Week 3, logging five receptions for 55 yards. Miami's receiving room is thin, and Malik Willis will be under constant pressure from Brian Flores' heavy-blitz scheme, allowing Dulcich to work underneath. Minnesota hasn't allowed a tight end to score, but three opposing tight ends have recorded at least 50 yards, giving Dulcich moderate Week 4 potential.
outlooksByWeek.5: Greg Dulcich hasn't played a meaningful role for the Dolphins as they enter a Week 5 matchup with the Bengals. After amassing seven targets in Week 3, Dulcich didn't get a look in Week 4 in a game where Miami completed only nine passes, giving him three or fewer targets in three of Miami's first four outings. While Cincinnati remains a defense that struggles against the position, allowing 67 or more yards to an opposing tight end in three straight weeks, Dulcich hasn't factored heavily enough to benefit.
outlooksByWeek.7: Greg Dulcich is facing an uphill battle for meaningful production when the Dolphins face the Jets in Week 7. Dulcich's usage has been sporadic, notching 12 targets in two games and five total in Miami's other three tilts, and he's topped 37 yards just once in five games. The Jets have been stingy against the position, allowing just one touchdown, though they have allowed 44 or more yards in three straight weeks. Miami's limited passing game further adds doubt to Dulcich's viability.
outlooksByWeek.8: Greg Dulcich has an uphill battle to maintain his ascending role in the Dolphins' passing game during a Week 8 matchup with the Patriots. He collected at least five targets in three of his last four games and is coming off a season-high 86 yards in Week 7, but New England has defended tight ends well, surrendering just 6.7 yards per target and two touchdowns. Game flow will likely favor Dulcich with the Patriots expected to jump out to a lead, though Dulcich lacking a touchdown reception tempers optimism.
outlooksByWeek.9: Greg Dulcich is an intriguing one-week option when the Dolphins face the Lions in Week 9. He has garnered at least five targets in three straight games, though he's topped 43 yards just once in that stretch. The matchup doesn't get much better, as Detroit has allowed 11 touchdown receptions to opposing tight ends through seven games and 8.6 yards per target.

player.seasonOutlook: Dulcich is back on the fantasy radar as the top tight end on the Miami depth chart. The 2022 third-round pick for the Denver Broncos made some noise as a rookie with a 33-411-2 receiving line in 10 games, but he went on to total 16 targets during the 2023 and 2024 seasons before landing in Miami last season. Dulcich didn't see his first target until Week 9 but went on to post a 26-335-1 receiving line the rest of the way. He wasn't a regular fantasy option (one top-15 week among TEs), but he certainly has a path to a substantial target share in 2026 with minimal competition at tight end and with Miami so short-handed at wide receiver. The 26-year-old is a long shot for consistent fantasy value in an offense expected to struggle, but there's some deep-league sleeper appeal.

outlooksByWeek.5: Tez Johnson is expected to remain a depth piece in Tampa Bay's wide-receiver room in the Week 5 matchup against the Cowboys. Johnson has had an underwhelming start to his 2026 campaign, catching four of nine targets for 74 yards through four games. Additionally, the Buccaneers will likely continue relying on the running game more, as it favors rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels while Baker Mayfield (thumb) remains out. Despite this, Johnson should be in for a favorable matchup against a Cowboys defense that's allowed 8.3 yards per pass attempt this year.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tez Johnson is expected to play a depth role in the Buccaneers' receiving corps in the Week 6 matchup against the Steelers. Although Johnson was targeted just once in the Week 5 win over the Cowboys, he made the most of his opportunity, totaling 64 receiving yards. He's appears firmly behind Emeka Egbuka, Chris Godwin and Cade Otton in Tampa Bay's passing attack, and likely won't be fantasy relevant without a touchdown going forward. Johnson is in for a tougher Week 6 matchup against a Pittsburgh secondary that's allowed 7.9 yards per target to opposing WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Tez Johnson is expected to remain a depth option in the Buccaneers' receiving corps in the Week 7 matchup against the Panthers. Johnson played just 34% of Tampa Bay's offensive snaps in the Week 6 overtime loss to the Steelers, catching two of three targets for seven yards. He could find more fantasy value if Baker Mayfield (thumb) were to return for the Week 7 contest, but Johnson will likely remain irrelevant for fantasy purposes without scoring a touchdown. Additionally, Johnson is in for a difficult matchup against a Panthers defense that's given up just two touchdowns to wideouts all season.
outlooksByWeek.8: Tez Johnson is expected to play a depth role in the Buccaneers' receiving corps in the Week 8 matchup against the Falcons. Johnson has operated as Tampa Bay's top deep threat over the last three weeks, catching five of six targets for 104 yards and a touchdown. Due to his lack of opportunities, he's unlikely to be fantasy relevant without scoring a touchdown. However, he could find the end zone against a Falcons defense that's allowed four receiving touchdowns to WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.9: Tez Johnson is expected to remain one of Tampa Bay's top pass-catchers in the Week 9 matchup against the Bears. His offensive role expanded with Emeka Egbuka (concussion/foot) sidelined over the last two weeks. However, Johnson has logged just two receptions for 33 yards and a touchdown during that span, largely because Tampa Bay attempted just 14 total passes. While the Buccaneers' offense remains extremely run-heavy, Johnson will likely be irrelevant for fantasy purposes without finding the end zone. He could struggle against a Bears secondary that's allowed just seven total touchdowns to wideouts this season.

outlooksByWeek.7: Christian Kirk and the 49ers hope to improve to 7-0 when they visit Atlanta in Week 7. The veteran receiver has been on the reserve/PUP list to begin 2026 due to a calf injury and has yet to suit up for San Francisco. The 49ers opened Kirk's practice window on Oct. 15 and there were reports of him possibly being activated for Week 6, but that was indeed not the case. With Mike Evans (Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring) expected to miss the road clash against the Falcons, San Francisco could really use Kirk's presence on the field.

player.seasonOutlook: Kirk signed with the 49ers after spending his first eight seasons with Arizona, Jacksonville and Houston. The 2018 second-round pick peaked with a 12th-place finish in fantasy points in 2022, but that marks his only career top-25 finish and he's been way off the fantasy radar the last two seasons, partially due to injury woes (13 missed games). Kirk doesn't have a clear path to consistent targets in San Francisco, with Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel and rookie De'Zhaun Stribling also in the mix (not to mention Christian McCaffrey and eventually George Kittle). The 29-year-old will begin the season on IR and is not on the fantasy radar.

Jeff Ulbrich's blitz-happy defense fueled 57 sacks, the league's second-best total, and a 13th best ranking in fantasy points. That approach could make this a streaming-worthy unit against weaker opposing quarterbacks, which could be the case with the Panthers (Weeks 2 and 18), Saints (4 and 17) and Browns (13). For those in deeper leagues, this could be an advantageous matchups-driven September D/ST if you wait until the end of the draft to fill the position.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jahan Dotson is in for a great Week 2 matchup when the Falcons take on the Panthers, whose defense just allowed 12.4 yards per completion last week. Dotson played 38 offensive snaps during Atlanta's Week 1 loss, out-snapping Olamide Zaccheaus and rookie Zachariah Branch, who each logged 18 snaps. Additionally, he trailed only Bijan Robinson and Drake London in targets, despite only receiving three. Regardless, Dotson should be in for a phenomenal Week 2 matchup after Carolina's defense gave up 59 points and eight total touchdowns in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jahan Dotson is expected to operate as Atlanta's No. 2 wideout in the Week 3 matchup against the Packers, whose defense has allowed just 8.3 yards per completion this season. Despite Dotson clearly operating as the Falcons' No. 2 wideout this season, he's had little fantasy value, in large part due to the problems at quarterback. With Michal Penix set to return in the Week 3 matchup, Dotson could be more relevant but will likely remain overshadowed by Drake London, Kyle Pitts and Bijan Robinson. Dotson could find the end zone, however, as the Packers' defense has already allowed three touchdowns to wideouts in two games, which is tied for the fourth-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jahan Dotson is expected to operate as the Falcons' No. 2 wideout in the Week 4 matchup against the Saints. Despite playing the second-most snaps amongst Atlanta wide receivers this season (137), Dotson has managed to catch just four of 11 targets for 41 yards. He's clearly behind Bijan Robinson and Drake London in the Falcons' offensive game plan and will likely struggle finding fantasy value without a touchdown. Additionally, Dotson is in for a difficult Week 4 matchup against a New Orleans defense that's allowed just 6.5 yards per target to opposing WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jahan Dotson is expected to remain one of the Falcons' top wideouts in the Week 5 matchup against the Ravens. Dotson had his best game of the 2026 campaign in the Week 4 win over the Saints, catching two of three targets for 54 yards and a touchdown. Despite this, Dotson has logged just 14 targets through four contests and will likely struggle remaining fantasy relevant without finding the end zone on a weekly basis. He is in for a favorable matchup, however, as Baltimore's defense has allowed 215.3 passing yards per game this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jahan Dotson will likely play a depth role on Atlanta's offense in the Week 6 matchup against the Bears. Dotson has been more involved in the Falcons' offensive game plan over the last two weeks, catching four of seven targets for 104 yards and a touchdown. However, he remains firmly behind Drake London, Kyle Pitts and Bijan Robinson as pass catchers, and he'll likely struggle finding fantasy value without a touchdown. Even so, Dotson could have plenty of scoring opportunities in Week 6, as Chicago's defense has already allowed five receiving touchdowns to WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jahan Dotson is expected to remain the Falcons' No. 2 wideout in the Week 7 matchup against the 49ers. Dotson had his most productive outing of the 2026 season in the Week 6 loss to the Bears, catching three of five targets for 87 yards and a touchdown. On the season, he's caught 11 of 23 targets for 236 yards and two touchdowns, benefitting from the return of quarterback Michael Penix. However, Dotson could struggle against the 49ers in Week 7, as they have allowed just 5.7 yards per pass attempt through five games this season.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jahan Dotson is expected to operate as one of Atlanta's top receiving options in the Week 8 matchup against the Buccaneers. Dotson had a quiet day in the Week 7 win over the 49ers, catching just one of three targets for six yards. However, he had already emerged as the Falcons' No. 2 wideout prior to Sunday's win, catching seven of 12 targets for 195 yards and two touchdowns from Weeks 4 through 6. Dotson will look to get back on track against a solid Buccaneers defense in Week 8 that's given up just 7.2 yards per target on the season.
outlooksByWeek.9: Jahan Dotson is expected to remain one of the Falcons' top wideouts in the Week 9 matchup against the Bengals. Dotson was one of the few bright spots in Atlanta's Week 8 loss to the Buccaneers, catching two of five targets for a game-high 95 yards. Dotson has been finding his groove as the Falcons' No. 2 WR as of late, recording more than 50 receiving yards in four of his last five games. He could find success against a Bengals secondary that's given up eight receiving touchdowns to WRs in just seven contests this season.

outlooksByWeek.2: Darnell Washington and the Steelers travel for a Week 2 showdown against the Patriots. He caught both of his targets for 18 yards during Pittsburgh's 20-13 win over the Falcons. Washington and Pat Freiermuth were co-starters at TE, but the latter tallied five catches for 46 yards and a TD. New England's defense is very stingy against the position, as they rank second in fantasy points allowed per game (3.3) to tight ends.
outlooksByWeek.5: Darnell Washington and the Steelers host the Colts in a matchup between 2-2 teams in Week 5. In Week 4, he played 70% of offensive snaps and caught three of five targets for 27 yards and a touchdown. Fellow tight end Pat Freiermuth (3-17-1) was also productive, playing 75% of the offensive snaps during Pittsburgh's 27-24 loss. They're both listed as starting tight ends for the Steelers, and it looks like they'll have a nearly even snap split as long as they're healthy. Indianapolis allows 13.7 fantasy points per game to TEs, which ranks 17th.
outlooksByWeek.6: Darnell Washington and the Steelers travel to square off against the 1-4 Buccaneers in Week 6. He played 34 snaps on offense (63%) en route to catching two of three targets for 12 yards during Pittsburgh's Week 5 victory. Fellow starting tight end Pat Freiermuth was on the field for 38 offensive snaps (70%) and was the more productive of the two, catching five of seven targets for 44 yards and two TDs. The playing time will continue to be relatively similar, making Washington a boom-or-bust fantasy option against Tampa Bay's 22nd-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (15.7) to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Darnell Washington and the Steelers are in Paris for an interconference tilt against the Saints in Week 7. He brought in four of six targets for 25 yards and a touchdown during Pittsburgh's thrilling comeback victory in overtime in Week 6. Washington and fellow tight end Pat Freiermuth each played 71% of the offensive snaps, lending more credibility to the "your turn, my turn" trend that's developing in 2026. He'll look to exploit New Orleans' 26th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (17.6) to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Darnell Washington and the Steelers host the Browns for a divisional clash in Week 8. He caught his only target for a four-yard touchdown in Week 7 during Pittsburgh's 16-10 victory in Paris. Washington has a TD in two straight contests and three of his last four, as he now has a 16-160-3 line on 23 targets across seven games. He remains a touchdown-or-bust play in fantasy, although his first score of the season came against Cleveland during their first matchup in Week 4.

player.seasonOutlook: Though he never quite made it onto the fantasy radar, Washington was one of the most fun, surprising "breakout" players of 2025. Essentially an extension of the offensive line at 6-foot-6, 264 pounds, Washington is known mainly for his blocking. Still, the 2023 third-round pick played well enough that he was stealing snaps and targets from both Jonnu Smith and Pat Freiermuth. Washington never cleared six targets or 10.7 fantasy points in any game, but he was effective with the ball in his hands and averaged 8.5 yards per target. Though Smith has been released, Pittsburgh's offense is no longer being led by TE superfan Arthur Smith, which is likely to lead to a lesser role for Washington. Expect him to operate as a rarely targeted blocking complement to Freiermuth.

The Titans finished 25th in fantasy scoring from the D/ST last season, and other than draftees Dl Keldrick Faulk and LB Anthony Hill, didn't do much to substantially upgrade during the offseason. This looks like a one-and-done streamer, as the Titans face the Jets at home, a plus matchup, but are then a no-go in fantasy for the month that follows (PHI, @NYG, @BAL, HOU, @IND).

The Raiders have a lengthy track record of defensive struggles, finishing in the upper half of the league in fantasy points from the D/ST in only one of the past 15 seasons. Still, the team added LBs Nakobe Dean and Quay Walker and CB Taron Johnson during the offseason, and it does still have DE Maxx Crosby on board. There could be some streaming potential here in favorable Weeks 1 (MIA) and 3 (@NO) matchups.

outlooksByWeek.2: Ted Hurst will look to build on his solid NFL debut in Tampa Bay's Week 2 matchup against the Browns. Hurst played 75 percent of the Buccaneers' offensive snaps and caught all three of his targets for 36 yards, taking advantage of increased opportunities with Jalen McMillan (knee) sidelined. Hurst could continue being a valuable asset to Tampa Bay's offense if McMillan continues to miss time, which he very well could in Week 2. The matchup against the Browns is also great, with that defense allowing a whopping 50.6 PPR fantasy points to wideouts in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Ted Hurst is expected to remain one of the Buccaneers' top receiving options in the Week 3 matchup against the Vikings. Despite the return of Jalen McMillan in the Week 2 loss to the Browns, Hurst played a career-high 45 offensive snaps -- 38 more than McMillan. Additionally, Hurst led the team with seven targets, though it led to just two receptions. Regardless, it appears as if Hurst will remain an important piece of the Buccaneers' offense as the season progresses. The rookie wideout will likely struggle but could find success against a Minnesota secondary that's allowed 12.6 yards per completion this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Ted Hurst is expected to play a depth role in the Buccaneers' receiving corps during the Week 4 matchup against the Packers. Hurst has proved to be a valuable part of Tampa Bay's offense just three games into his rookie campaign, catching six of 14 targets for 103 yards and a touchdown. With Jalen McMillan (knee) going down in the Week 3 loss to the Vikings, Hurst's role could continue to expand as the season progresses. He will likely see fewer opportunities in Week 4 with Baker Mayfield (thumb) sidelined, but the matchup remains favorable, as the Packers' defense allowed 14.2 yards per completion in a Week 3 loss to the Falcons.
outlooksByWeek.5: Ted Hurst is expected to remain one of Tampa Bay's top wideouts in the Week 5 matchup against the Cowboys. Hurst finished with the third-most receiving yards on the Buccaneers during the Week 4 loss to the Packers, catching two of three targets for 25 yards. He will likely get fewer scoring opportunities with Baker Mayfield (thumb) sidelined but should remain involved in the team's offensive game plan. Hurst could find success against a struggling Dallas secondary that's allowed 11.7 yards per reception on the season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Ted Hurts will look to bounce back from a poor performance in the Buccaneers' Week 6 matchup against the Steelers. Hurst went without a target for the first time in his NFL career during the Week 5 win over the Cowboys. On the season, the rookie wideout has caught eight of 16 targets for 128 yards and a touchdown, averaging 16.0 yards per reception. He could find success against a solid Steelers secondary in Week 6 that's allowed 10.8 yards per completion this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Ted Hurst will look to build on a solid Week 6 performance when the Buccaneers' travel to Carolina in Week 7. Hurst was Tampa Bay's second-leading receiver in the Week 6 overtime loss to the Steelers, catching three of six targets for 40 yards. While he remains firmly behind Emeka Egbuka and Chris Godwin in the Buccaneers' receiving corps, it appears as if he's established himself as the team's No. 3 wideout, at least while Jalen McMillan (knee) remains sidelined. Hurst could also benefit from the possible return of Baker Mayfield (thumb) at quarterback in Week  7, but he'll likely struggle against a Carolina secondary that's allowed just 9.7 yards per completion this year.
outlooksByWeek.8: Ted Hurst is expected to operate as one of the Buccaneers' top wideouts during the Week 8 matchup against the Falcons. Despite a larger offensive role without Emeka Egbuka (concussion/foot) in Week 7, Hurst was quiet, failing to catch his lone target. The rookie wideout has now been held without a reception in two of his last three games, suggesting Tez Johnson's return could limit Hurst's fantasy value going forward. Despite this, Hurst could find value against a Falcons defense that's given up 6.3 yards per pass attempt this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Hurst was selected by the Buccaneers in the third round of April's draft. Granted he played at a small school, but Hurst ranked third in this rookie class target share (26%) and first in air yard share (45%) during his FBS career. A tall, vertical receiver, Hurst posted solid collegiate efficiency despite inconsistent QB play (only 68% of his 235 FBS targets were catchable, which is easily lowest among qualified WRs in this class). His 135-inch broad jump was best among wide receivers at the combine. Hurst will get some run at 'X' receiver as a rookie, but he's a longshot for consistent rookie-season fantasy production with Emeka Egbuka, Chris Godwin and Jalen McMillan in the fold.

outlooksByWeek.3: Jameis Winston will take the reins of the Giants offense in Week 3 versus the Titans. Jaxson Dart suffered a serious knee injury and may not return this year. Winston's performance in relief of Dart last game left much to be desired, as he completed just 11-of-27 passes for 111 yards and an interception. Against Tennessee, at least Winston will have a week to prepare and face a lower-tier defense. The Titans are giving up 233.5 passing yards per game in 2026, which is 20th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jameis Winston led the Giants to an ugly victory last game against the Titans. Winston was underwhelming to say the least, though, as he passed for under 120 yards for the second-straight outing. On a positive note, he did not throw an interception, and the Giants won the contest. However, the G-Men just traded for JJ McCarthy from the Vikings, which could put some pressure on Winston to perform. Nevertheless, Winston should remain the starter for now, and the Giants have another very winnable game in Week 4 versus the Cardinals. Arizona is allowing 234.3 passing yards per game, which is 22nd in the NFL. In addition, Arizona has allowed eight passing touchdowns already, which is 30th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jameis Winston tossed three touchdowns last game for the Giants. It was the full Jameis Winston experience, though, as the veteran also threw two interceptions. However, he finished 18-of-29 for 250 yards in the 36-24 win over the Cardinals. Miraculously, the G-Men currently sit in first place in the NFC East. In Week 5, Jameis and company will face a Commanders defense that has struggled to defend the pass.  Washington has allowed 11 passing scores, which is tied for last in the NFL. In addition, the Commanders are yielding 242.5 passing yards per tilt, which is 25th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jameis Winston tossed three touchdowns for the second-consecutive week for the Giants. He also threw for over 300 yards for the first time this season in the 27-27 tie with the Commanders.  Winston did not throw a pick, though he did lose a fumble. While JJ McCarthy took a few snaps, the starting job will remain Winston's heading into a Week 6 clash with the Saints. New Orleans has been fairly stingy against the pass in 2026, allowing just 212.2 passing yards per tilt, which is 11th in the league. However, New Orleans has also given up eight passing scores already, which is tied for 20th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jameis Winston was benched in favor of J.J. McCarthy last game for the Giants. McCarthy led a furious comeback attempt, throwing for an astonishing 243 yards in the fourth quarter alone in relief of Winston. While the G-Men ultimately lost to the Saints by a score of 34-27, McCarthy's near-heroics have likely created a quarterback controversy heading into Week 7 versus the Texans. Whomever lines up under center may have a favorable matchup, as Houston is allowing 246 passing yards per tilt, which is 27th in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Winston is back with the Giants and with Russell Wilson out of the picture, he is expected to serve as the primary backup to Jaxson Dart in 2026. Winston hasn't been a full-time starter since 2019 and was limited to two starts last season. In typical Winston style, results varied, with 11.0 fantasy points against Green Bay in Week 11, followed by a 32.2-point showing against Detroit the very next week. The 32-year-old doesn't do much with his legs, but his boom/bust passing style makes him an occasional streaming option when the matchup is right. That's what he'll be, if called on for a spot start in place of Dart this season.

outlooksByWeek.2: Cam Ward threw for just 140 yards in Tennessee's 23-10 Week 1 loss to the Jets, bringing the 2025 first-overall pick's career average down to 184 passing yards per game. He's best avoided for fantasy purposes, even in multi-QB formats, for the Titans' Week 2 home game against the Eagles. Philadelphia's stingy pass defense limited Jayden Daniels to 164 passing yards and 4.8 yards per pass attempt in the Eagles' season-opening win over Washington.
outlooksByWeek.3: Cam Ward will be tough to trust outside of deeper multi-QB formats in Week 3, when the Titans face the Giants on the road. The 2025 first overall pick scored two short rushing TDs in Tennessee's surprisingly competitive Week 2 loss to the Eagles, matching his career total in that category heading into that game. Ward has just one touchdown pass this season and 16 touchdown passes through 19 NFL starts, of which he has won three. The Giants allowed two touchdown passes to Dak Prescott and four to reigning MVP Matthew Stafford, but those two veteran QBs are far more effective passers than Ward at this stage in their respective careers.
outlooksByWeek.4: Cam Ward has been arguably the worst starting QB in the NFL since entering the league as the Titans' first overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft. In the first three games of his sophomore season, Ward hasn't thrown for more than 183 yards or recorded multiple touchdown passes in a game. Dynasty managers can continue to stash him on the bench for the Titans' Week 4 trip to Baltimore in hopes of future improvements, but Ward's fantasy value in the present is negligible. The Ravens rank in the middle of the pack against the pass.
outlooksByWeek.5: Cam Ward hasn't thrown multiple touchdown passes in a game during the Titans' 0-4 start, and he's just 3-18 as a starter with 18 touchdown passes in 21 games. The 2025 first overall pick isn't an advisable fantasy option in Week 5 against the Texans, who have surprisingly surrendered the third-most passing yards in the league this season but still boast plenty of talent on defense and allowed the sixth-fewest passing yards in 2025. Dynasty managers looking for a silver lining with Ward can point to his season-high 222 passing yards in the Week 4 loss to Baltimore, 145 of which went to rookie fourth overall pick Carnell Tate.
outlooksByWeek.6: Cam Ward dropped to 3-19 as a starter for the Titans with a 26-3 loss to the Texans in Week 5, throwing an interception that dropped his season TD:INT to 3:3. He has declined in his second season after posting a 15:7 TD:INT as a rookie, while his passing yards per game have dropped from 186 in 2025 to 179 this year. Even against a Colts defense that's giving up the fifth-most passing yards per game, Ward can't be trusted in Week 6 fantasy lineups outside of deep superflex or multi-QB formats.
outlooksByWeek.7: Cam Ward and the Titans finally earned their first win of the season in Week 6 against the Colts, though the second-year QB certainly wasn't the primary driving force in the victory, as he threw for just 102 yards with a 1:1 TD:INT. Ward has mustered just four touchdown passes through six starts in his sophomore season while averaging 166 passing yards per game. He'll face a franchise that's all too familiar with subpar QB play in Week 7, taking on a Browns team that's off to a surprisingly strong 4-2 start this season while boasting one of the league's 10 stingiest defenses in terms of both passing yards and points allowed per game. Between Ward's own shortcomings and the tricky matchup, it's best to avoid him in fantasy for Week 7.
outlooksByWeek.8: Cam Ward has yet to throw multiple touchdown passes in a game heading into the Titans' Week 8 trip to Cincinnati. The second-year QB has an ugly 4:5 TD:INT while throwing for just 168 yards per game. Cincinnati's defense has limited QBs to a 6:4 TD:INT, but the Bengals allowed Baltimore's Tyler Huntley to throw for a career-high 298 yards in a Week 7 game that the Bengals won by 22 points. Until Ward shows signs of progress as a passer, he'll remain a fantasy non-factor, even in superflex formats.

player.seasonOutlook: Ward is eyeing a Year 2 leap following an underwhelming rookie campaign, albeit under tough circumstances. The 2025 No. 1 draft pick was plenty busy as a rookie (eighth in the league in dropbacks and pass attempts), but he struggled to 5.9 yards per attempt and took a league-high 55 sacks. Ward was rarely a factor with his legs (more than 12 yards three times) and produced one weekly fantasy finish better than 12th. The good news is that a tough rookie year isn't overly damning for a quarterback's career trajectory, and he'll be in a better spot in 2026 with new playcaller Brian Daboll and an improved supporting cast (Carnell Tate and Wan'Dale Robinson join a now-healthy Calvin Ridley). Ward will need to run more to become an elite fantasy option, but Year 2 is the breakout season for many quarterbacks, so he's well worth a late flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: George Holani looks set as Seattle's No. 2 RB heading into a Week 2 matchup versus the Cardinals. Holani somewhat surprisingly logged eight carries in a tight Week 1 win over the Patriots, recording only two fewer totes than rookie Jadarian Price. However, Price was much more efficient with 5.2 YPC to Holani's 3.6. Price could get a larger share of the workload against the Cardinals, who limited the Chargers to 81 rushing yards on 21 carries in a season-opening victory.
outlooksByWeek.3: George Holani may be asked to take on a bigger offensive role for Seattle in a Week 3 matchup against the Commanders. Jadarian Price suffered a shoulder injury late in a Week 2 win against Arizona, and if he isn't able to suit up versus Washington, Holani would figure to see more work, though Emanuel Wilson would presumably take over No. 1 RB duties. As it is, Holani has gotten involved on offense in each of Seattle's contests so far, combining to produce 42 yards on 12 carries and two yards on one reception. The Commanders have been decimated through the air this season, but they haven't surrendered a rushing touchdown so far.
outlooksByWeek.4: George Holani appears to be settled in as Seattle's No. 3 backfield option heading into a Week 4 matchup against the Chargers. Holani logged 10 yards on three carries against Washington in Week 3, but he had by far his best game of the season as a pass catcher, recording five receptions on five targets for 48 yards. Both Jadarian Price and Emanuel Wilson seem to be firmly ahead of Holani in the competition for carries, so work as a receiver will likely be the key to Holani being able to make an offensive impact. The Chargers haven't been hurt much by RBs as pass catchers, yielding just 4.37 yard per target to the position.
outlooksByWeek.5: George Holani looks to be locked in as Seattle's No. 2 RB heading into a Week 5 clash against the 49ers. That role didn't yield much fruit for Holani in Week 4, however, as he recorded just 18 yards on seven carries and two yards on one reception. Meanwhile, Emanuel Wilson recorded 120 total yards and two TDs on 24 touches, so he looks to be in full control of the backfield for the time being. San Francisco has given up just two touchdowns (one rushing, one receiving) to running backs this season, so they aren't a great draw for a player like Holani who probably needs to get into the end zone to put up meaningful fantasy points.
outlooksByWeek.6: George Holani will likely need to better protect the ball in Week 6 against the Broncos if he wants to continue getting opportunities in Seattle's ground game. Holani fumbled twice this past Sunday against the 49ers, and the fumble that was recovered by San Francisco was a game-changer, as it resulted in a touchdown just before halftime. With that said, Seattle is depleted at running back with Zach Charbonnet (knee - ACL) out at least another week and Jadrian Price (chest) on IR until at least early November, so Holani should get an opportunity to redeem himself against Denver. The Broncos are giving up 21.1 fantasy points per game to RBs, eighth-most in the league.
outlooksByWeek.7: George Holani and the Seahawks host the Chiefs on Sunday Night Football in Week 7. He rushed five times for 20 yards and a touchdown during Seattle's 17-14 loss in overtime in Week 6. Holani made the most of his touches by scoring his first rushing TD of the season, but he's expected to have his opportunities reduced with the likely return of Zach Charbonnet (knee) off the reserve/PUP list. It would be wise to steer clear of the Seahawks backfield against a Kansas City defense allowing 19.0 fantasy points allowed per game to RBs, which is tied for ninth.

player.seasonOutlook: Holani is on the 2026 fantasy radar with Kenneth Walker III no longer on the Seattle roster and Zach Charbonnet (ACL) in doubt for the early portion of the season. Holani will compete with rookie Jadrian Price and Emanuel Wilson for touches while Charbonnet is sidelined. The 2024 UDFA has 25 carries and three targets to his name through two NFL seasons. Price figures to get the first shot at lead back duties and, even if forced into a few starts in Seattle's run-friendly offense, Holani would be working in a committee and no more than a deep league flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: Andre Szmyt and the Browns are on the road to square off against the Buccaneers in Week 2. He finished Cleveland's 34-10 loss a perfect two-for-two on kicks, making a 26-yard field goal and connecting on his lone PAT. Tampa Bay gave up 33 points last week, but that was to an elite Bengals offense that isn't even in the same realm as the Browns. Szmyt should be left on waiver wires as long as Cleveland continues to struggle to create scoring opportunities.
outlooksByWeek.3: Andre Szmyt and the Browns host the Panthers in Week 3.
