He remained perfect through two games by connecting on all three of his field-goal attempts and both PATs to help Cleveland upset the Buccaneers 23-19 in Week 2. Szmyt drilled field goals of 34 yards (twice) and 50 yards, his first score from 50 or more in limited opportunities. He's proven to be reliable, but more is needed from the Browns' offense to say he's an every-week starter. After giving up a whopping 59 points in their season opener, Carolina's defense allowed just three points to the Falcons in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.4: Andre Szmyt and the Browns host the Steelers for a divisional tilt between 2-1 teams in Week 4. He connected on both of his field-goal attempts and made his only extra-point try during Cleveland's 21-18 victory in Week 3. Szmyt improved to 6-for-6 on FGAs and 4-for-4 on PATs across three contests in 2026. The Browns rank 24th in scoring at 18.0 points per game, but despite his perfect mark thus far, Szmyt should be considered a risky start in fantasy with other options available.
outlooksByWeek.5: Andre Szmyt and the Browns hope to improve to 4-1 on the season when they travel to take on the Jets in Week 5. He made both of his field-goal attempts, including a 56-yard game-winner with 10 seconds remaining, and connected on all three PATs during Cleveland's 27-24 win in Week 4. Szmyt set a new career high in distance and appears to be establishing himself as one of the best kickers in the league, as he's made 22 straight field goals dating back to last season. He'll face a tough Jets defense outdoors that allows 21.0 points per game, tied for 11th in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.6: Andre Szmyt and the Browns host Baltimore for an AFC North divisional clash in Week 6. He went 2-for-2 on field goals but missed his only extra-point try in Cleveland's 17-12 loss in Week 5. The PAT miss was Szmyt's first of the season, and he's now a perfect 10-for-10 on FGs and 7-for-8 on extra points. The Browns' offense took a step back after a three-game winning streak, but some of that can be attributed to the rainy conditions all afternoon. Either way, Szmyt will aim to contribute at home against a Ravens defense allowing 23.8 points per game.
outlooksByWeek.7: Andre Szmyt and the Browns visit the Titans for a Week 7 showdown. He made two of his three field-goal attempts, including the 48-yard game-winner, and his lone PAT during Cleveland's 13-10 win in Week 5. It was Szmyt's first field goal miss this season, as he's now 12-for-13 (92.3%) through six games. The Browns' offense has taken a step back in recent weeks, scoring a combined 22 points in their last two outings, leaving Szmyt a difficult kicker to rely on in fantasy.
outlooksByWeek.8: Andre Szmyt and the Browns travel to Pittsburgh for an AFC North showdown in Week 8. He went 2-for-3 on field goals and made all three of his PATs during Cleveland's 27-24 win in Week 7. Szmyt nailed the game-winning 32-yard field goal as time expired, making up for the 43-yarder he missed earlier in the fourth quarter. He's now made at least two FGs in six straight contests and drilled game-winners in consecutive games. Szmyt will try to keep up the momentum versus a Steelers defense allowing just 19.7 points per game, the fifth-lowest mark in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.9: Andre Szmyt and the Browns travel to take on the Saints in Week 9. He went 2-for-2 on field goal attempts but did not attempt an extra point during Cleveland's 27-6 loss in Week 8. Szmyt was the only source of scoring in another underwhelming performance by the Browns, and he's now 16-for-18 on FGs and 11-for-12 on PATs through eight contests. He's developing into a reliable kicker, but his fantasy appeal is almost nonexistent on a Browns offense that scores the fourth-fewest (17.4) points per game.

outlooksByWeek.2: Colby Parkinson will aim to be more productive when the Rams face the Giants in Week 2. Though Parkinson led Los Angeles tight ends with 47 offensive snaps in a season-opening loss to the 49ers, he caught just one pass for six yards. The Rams had three other tight ends log at least 12 offensive snaps in the contest, so the week-to-week individual production among that group could vary widely throughout the season. The Giants held Dallas' starting tight end, Jake Ferguson, to just two catches for six yards in Week 1, so Los Angeles' tight-end corps could have trouble as a whole.
outlooksByWeek.3: Colby Parkinson has had a quiet start to the season heading into the Rams' Week 3 matchup versus Denver. Parkinson logged just one catch Week 1 and followed that with a 2-15-0 receiving line on Monday Night Football. Meanwhile, fellow TE Terrance Ferguson put up a 6-54-1 line, proving that there's room for players at the position to thrive with QB Matthew Stafford -- though who that tight end is could vary on a week-to-week basis. Denver was burned by Travis Kelce for 71 yards in Week 1 but held Jaguars TEs to just 24 receiving yards in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.4: Colby Parkinson is uncertain to be able to play in the Rams' Week 4 clash against the Eagles due to a shoulder injury. Parkinson suffered the injury in Week 3 against Denver and finished the game with no catches on one target. Meanwhile, veteran Tyler Higbee put up a strong 8-62-1 line and could be poised for more opportunities even if Parkinson does end up playing. Philadelphia has been tough on tight ends this season, giving up just 3.0 fantasy points per game to the position, second-best in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Colby Parkinson didn't play in Week 4 and isn't certain to suit up in Week 5 for the Rams' matchup against Buffalo. Parkinson is dealing with a shoulder and a knee injury, and his practice participation level this week should help determine if he'll be able to suit up against the Bills. Tyler Higbee has had consecutive big games for Los Angeles and could work as the team's top TE even if Parkinson is able to play in Week 5. The Rams' offense often provides opportunities for multiple tight ends to thrive, though Buffalo has given up just 6.3 fantasy points per game to the position so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Colby Parkinson may have officially fallen behind Tyler Higbee in Los Angeles' tight-end pecking order heading into a matchup versus the Cardinals in Week 6. Parkinson logged just one catch on two targets for three yards Monday against Buffalo while Higbee went off again with a 5-83-0 receiving line on six targets. The good news for Parkinson is that he was able to suit up following a one-week absence, but he's yet to register more than two catches in a game so far this season. With that in mind, he could struggle to produce in Week 6 despite facing an Arizona defense that has given up the fourth-most fantasy points per game (13.3) to tight ends through five weeks.
outlooksByWeek.7: Colby Parkinson operates as the Rams' main blocking tight end, and while he's going to have a few catches here and there, he's behind Tyler Higbee in terms of the pecking order in the passing game. The matchup is favorable against the Raiders, who have allowed the sixth-most fantasy points per game to opposing TEs in 2026, but Parkinson's lack of involvement will limit his upside overall. He has just nine catches for 55 yards and a touchdown in five games this season.
outlooksByWeek.8: Colby Parkinson could play a key role for the Rams in Week 8 against the Chargers. With wideout Davante Adams sidelined by a hamstring injury this past Sunday, QB Matthew Stafford targeted tight ends 14 times. Parkinson logged six of those looks, turning them into a 5-48-0 line. Adams is expected to be out multiple more weeks, so Parkinson and the Rams' other tight ends should continue to be looked to often. The Chargers rank 10th in the league in fantasy points per game allowed to tight ends thanks largely to giving up only one touchdown to the position so far.

player.seasonOutlook: Parkinson is set to resume his role in the Rams' TE committee. The 2020 fourth-round pick was a part-time player early last season, but graduated to a much larger role in the second half. In fact, from Week 10 on (12 games, including the playoffs), Parkinson averaged 5.0 targets and 12.1 fantasy points per game, scoring nine touchdowns along the way. He finished the regular season with career-high marks across the board, which included his first top-35 fantasy campaign (17th). If Parkinson carries his increased role into 2026, he'll be a sneaky fantasy option, but the problem is that he needs to fend off Tyler Higbee and recent second-round picks Terrance Ferguson and Max Klare for work in an offense that also includes Puka Nacua and Davante Adams. Parkinson, 27, is a deep sleeper worth a look in leagues that start two tight ends.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jalen Nailor didn't make much of a splash in his Raiders debut, catching three of five targets for 27 yards in a season-opening win over the Dolphins. All three of the team's top wideouts, including Tre Tucker and Jack Bech, produced very similar numbers, with Bech catching the trio's only TD. The group figures to remain secondary pieces in the passing game as RB Ashton Jeanty and TE Brock Bowers, when healthy, figure to be the top weapons for Kirk Cousins and, eventually, Fernando Mendoza. Nailor isn't likely to break out in Week 2 against a Chargers' secondary that finished last season tied for eighth in points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jalen Nailor has had a quiet start to his Raiders' tenure, catching four of eight targets for 36 yards through two games without a touchdown. He hasn't been able to get on the same page as quarterback Kirk Cousins, even though the two were together in Minnesota for the first two years of Nailor's career, and the impending return of Brock Bowers will bump everyone else down a rung in the pecking order for looks. Nailor seems unlikely to break out in Week 3 against a Saints secondary that ranks in the middle of the pack in terms of volume allowed to wide receivers so far, but which has given up three TDs to the position in two games.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jalen Nailor has yet to earn much of a role as a pass catcher through his first three weeks as a Raider. While the fifth-year wide receiver does the kind of grunt work as a blocker that keeps him on the field, he's seen only 11 targets from Kirk Cousins and caught just five of them for 52 yards and zero touchdowns. With Brock Bowers making his season debut in Week 3 and immediately reclaiming his spot as the team's top target, Nailor's path to meaningful volume got even narrower. He faces a difficult task in Week 4 against a Kansas City secondary that ranks first in the league in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jalen Nailor's tough start to his Raiders tenure continued in Week 4, as he failed to get a target before leaving the game early due to a concussion. The former Viking has a meager 5-52-0 line on just 11 targets through four weeks, and while his spot in the lineup seems secure when he's healthy due to his blocking ability, he hasn't established much chemistry with Kirk Cousins despite the fact that the duo played together in Minnesota. If Nailor does clear the concussion protocol in time, he'll be little more than a dart throw in Week 5, even against a Patriots secondary that ranks 21st in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs and which could be without top cornerback Christian Gonzalez.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jalen Nailor sat out the Raiders' Week 5 loss to the Patriots with a concussion, but his absence may not last much longer. Whether he finds a bigger role in the game plan is another question. The former Viking has caught just five of 11 targets for 52 yards through four games, and his primary value in Klint Kubiak's offensive scheme seems to be as a blocker. Las Vegas doesn't have a true No. 1 wide receiver, with tight end Brock Bowers serving as Kirk Cousins' top option, so the door is still open for Nailor to work his way up in the pecking order. Assuming he's cleared to return, he'll get a great opportunity in Week 6 against a Bills secondary that ranks last in the league in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jalen Nailor returned in Week 6 from a one-game absence due to a concussion, but he was able to turn four targets into just one nine-yard catch. The former Viking remains an afterthought in the Raiders' passing game, and through five contests, he's managed just a 6-61-0 line on 15 targets. Nailor's prospects could improve if Fernando Mendoza replaces Kirk Cousins under center at some point, but he'd likely need injuries to the likes of Brock Bowers or Tre Tucker to be anything more than the No. 4 option for either QB. Nailor isn't likely to break out in Week 7 against a Rams secondary that ranks fourth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jalen Nailor cannot seem to get on the same page as Kirk Cousins. Despite a consistent snap share due to his blocking skills, Nailor has caught just three of nine targets for 23 yards in two games since returning from a concussion. Brock Bowers, Tre Tucker and Ashton Jeanty are the only players getting regular looks from Cousins, but Nailor isn't doing much with the small volume he does see, and he might be looking forward to the day when rookie Fernando Mendoza takes over the offense. Nailor will try to make a splash in Week 8 against a Jets secondary that is tied for 15th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Jalen Nailor finally began to show some chemistry with Kirk Cousins in the Raiders' Week 8 win over the Jets. Nailor set new season highs in receptions (four) and receiving yards (38) while hauling in his first touchdown of the year. The former Viking should continue seeing a big workload in terms of snaps due to his blocking ability and unselfish route running, but Nailor seems firmly behind Brock Bowers, Tre Tucker and Ashton Jeanty in the pecking order for targets. Nailor isn't likely to make a big impact in Week 9 against a 49ers secondary that ranks 11th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Nailor signed with the Raiders and will battle the likes of Tre Tucker and second-year receivers Jack Bech and Dont'e Thornton Jr. for a starting gig in Las Vegas' new-look offense. Nailor was a rarely used commodity during his first four NFL seasons, all with the Vikings. The 2022 sixth-round pick totaled a 69-1,066-11 receiving line and never reached 30 catches or 450 yards in a single season. In fact, he's yet to clear six targets in a game. The 27-year-old very well could lock down a starting job in Las Vegas, but he's a long shot to make the big leap to consistent fantasy output in his fifth professional season. He's no more than a late-round wild card in deep leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jason Sanders hopes to maintain his job when the Jets host the Packers in Week 2. Sanders secured the team's opportunities in Week 1 over Blake Grupe, finishing with eight points, more where distance matters as he made two field goals from beyond 50 yards. Assuming he's again active, a higher-scoring game could be on tap against a defense that allowed 39 points in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jason Sanders appears on track to serve as the Jets' kicker again in Week 3 at Detroit. Despite Blake Grupe being on the roster, Sanders has been the active option through two games, hitting four extra points and four of five field goals. Volume is questionable as the Jets' offense isn't highly efficient, and Detroit's defense has allowed just two field goal attempts while surrendering nine touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jason Sanders appears in line to handle kicking duties for the Jets again in Week 4 against the Bears. Sanders has routinely been activated from the practice squad in advance of game day and has made all five of his PATs and 5-of-6 field goals. Chicago has allowed just 17 points to opposing kickers through three weeks, and with the Jets not offering a high-powered offense, Sanders seems unlikely to provide a top-end fantasy return.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jason Sanders hasn't notched many scoring chances in the Jets' limited offense entering Week 5 against the Browns. Through four games, Sanders has eight field goal attempts and only five PATs, keeping his floor and ceiling low. Cleveland has allowed the second-most field goal attempts (12) through four games, so perhaps there's a chance at a productive Week 5 if the Jets continue to be held out of the end zone, but Sanders' overall body of work doesn't suggest fantasy relevance.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jason Sanders hasn't collected ample attempts to create a floor or ceiling ahead of the Jets' Week 6 matchup with the Patriots. Sanders has just seven PATs through five games, while only attempting multiple field goals in two of five outings. New England is the fourth-stingiest team to opposing kickers, allowing just six made field goals, likely again keeping Sanders out of the Week 6 fantasy mix.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jason Sanders could offer bye-week replacement production for the Jets in a Week 7 meeting with the Dolphins. Sanders drilled a season-high four field goals in Week 6, his third game in six appearances with multiple 3-point connections, and he's added multiple PATs at the same 50% clip. Miami's defense has allowed plenty of points to opposing kickers, surrendering three extra point attempts and two field goals per game, setting Sanders up for a potentially busy, high-scoring Week 7.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jason Sanders hasn't been a high-scoring option in the Jets' limited offense ahead of a Week 8 matchup with the Raiders. Through seven games, Sanders has only 10 PATs while making one or two field goals in five of those outings. The Raiders are allowing the 10th-fewest fantasy points to kickers, as opponents routinely convert drives into touchdowns (24 PATs, just 10 field goal attempts). There are likely safer kickers available for Week 8 fantasy production.
outlooksByWeek.9: Jason Sanders' opportunities have been uneven for the Jets ahead of a Week 9 game against the Chiefs. For the second time in three weeks and third time overall in Week 8, Sanders attempted four field goals. Unfortunately, he has four games with just one made 3-pointer, while three times collecting one or zero PATs. Kansas City has allowed 15 field goals through seven games but only 10 PATs, so while suggesting the Jets will have stalled drives is fair, field goals likely won't keep them competitive, making Sanders a risky Week 9 option.

outlooksByWeek.2: Will Shipley managed just three touches for the Eagles in Week 1.  Meanwhile, fellow backup Tank Bigsby had just one carry for three yards in the 24-22 win over Washington. Both rushers remain firmly behind Saquon Barkley on the depth chart, though could see extra run in Week 2 if the game gets out of hand versus the Titans. Tennessee allowed 367 yards from scrimmage to the Jets in their season opener. Tennessee was torched on the ground in particular, allowing 152 rushing yards and two touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.3: Will Shipley managed nine touches for 29 yards in Week 2 versus the Titans after Saquon Barkley suffered a stinger injury. Saquon missed portions of the game due to the ailment, leaving his status in question for Week 3 versus the Bears. Barkley is slated to undergo an MRI to determine if he will miss any time. Shipley and Tank Bigsby would likely split touches if Barkley cannot go, with Bigsby getting the slight edge, as the latter had 15 touches and a touchdown to outpace Shipley. In Week 3, the Eagles will face a Bears run defense allowing 122 yards per clash on the ground, which is 22nd in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Will Shipley may be the only healthy running back left for the Eagles. Tank Bigsby replaced an injured Saquon Barkley last game for the Eagles, only to suffer an injury of his own late in the contest. Bigsby rushed 14 times for 55 yards to lead the Eagles before exiting with a lower-body issue. His status is up in the air for Week 5 versus the Jags, as is Barkley's due to a hamstring ailment. If neither Bigsby nor Barkley can play, Shipley would be in line for an expanded role. Shipley did have six rushes for 23 yards following the injury to Bigsby. However, Jacksonville has played the run extremely well thus far in 2026. The Jags are allowing just 74.3 rushing yards per tote, which us second in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Will Shipley found the end zone last game for the Eagles but did not return to the contest due to a foot injury. His status for Week 6 versus Carolina is up in the air. The Eagles could be on their fourth-string running back in the form of Dameon Pierce, as Saquon Barkley is nursing a hamstring ailment and Tank Bigsby is on Injured Reserve. Whoever lines up in the backfield could have a tasty matchup versus a suspect Panthers run defense, though. Carolina is allowing 156.5 rushing yards per tilt, which is second-to-last in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Conner is entering his 10th NFL season without a clear path to touches. For starters, we haven't seen him in a while after he suffered a season-ending foot injury in Week 3 last season. Even prior to the injury, Conner was splitting work with Trey Benson, totaling 28 touches in two full games. Conner restructured his contract during the offseason, but his days as Arizona's lead back are over after Jeremiyah Love and Tyler Allgeier were added to the roster during the offseason. Conner, who delivered four straight top-15 fantasy (points per game) campaigns prior to 2025, will need to find a new home in order to have any shot at 2026 fantasy relevance. He'll begin the season on IR.

outlooksByWeek.2: Demarcus Robinson should again have a key role for San Francisco in Week 2 against the Dolphins. After rookie De'Zhaun Stribling hurt his ankle in a season-opening win over the Rams, Robinson stepped up as the team's No. 3 wideout and produced two catches for 50 yards and a touchdown. Stribling is expected to miss at least a month, so Robinson will likely continue to work as the 49ers third wideout behind Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel. Miami presents a good matchup after falling to the Raiders 27-13 and yielding three passing touchdowns Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Demarcus Robinson suffered an ankle injury in San Francisco's win over the Dolphins on Sunday, and his status is very much in doubt for a Week 3 matchup against Arizona. Before getting hurt, Robinson caught all three of his targets for 34 yards against Miami as the 49ers' No. 3 wideout. In the likely scenario that he can't play in Week 3, Jacob Cowing would stand to step into Robinson's place in the pecking order. Arizona has given up four receiving TDs to wide receivers through two weeks, tied for the most in the league.
outlooksByWeek.9: Demarcus Robinson (ankle) could return from injured reserve for San Francisco's Week 9 clash against the Raiders. Robinson suffered a high-ankle sprain against Miami in Week 2 and subsequently landed on IR. Fellow injured wideouts Mike Evans (Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring) also have a chance to return Week 9, so Robinson may be confined to a complementary role if he does play. With that said, there could be plenty of opportunities for SF's wideouts to succeed against a Raiders defense that has given up the sixth-most fantasy points per game (23.9) to the position .

Gardner Minshew will get his first opportunity as Arizona's starting quarterback in Week 9 against Seattle. Minshew took over for former starter Jacoby Brissett in the third quarter of this past Sunday's game against Dallas and threw for 188 yards and three touchdowns to lead his team to a rousing comeback win in overtime. That performance made the choice to start Minshew in Week 9 almost a no-brainer, but he'll likely need to perform well to hold onto the job for the remainder of the season. That won't be an easy task against the Seahawks, who have yielded the second-fewest fantasy points per game to quarterbacks this season.

outlooksByWeek.2: Carson Wentz could be in line to start again as the Vikings travel to Chicago in Week 2. Wentz came in for an injured Kyler Murray (concussion) against the Packers in Week 1, and he ended up delivering a come-from-behind win. The veteran completed 12 of 19 passes for 133 yards and three touchdowns, and he did not commit a turnover during the matchup. If Murray is unable to clear concussion protocol ahead of Sunday, Wentz will be in position to get his first start since 2025 against a Bears defense that gave up 361 passing yards, three touchdowns and one interception to Bryce Young in their opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Carson Wentz will return to Minnesota's backup role in Week 3 against the Buccaneers. Wentz performed well while leading the Vikings to a 2-0 record, completing 23 of 39 passes for 276 yards and three touchdowns in that stretch. The veteran quarterback will remain a solid backup behind Kyler Murray, although anything can happen as the season progresses.

outlooksByWeek.6: Pierre Strong could serve as Green Bay's secondary option at running back once again in Week 6 against the Cowboys. With Chris Brooks on IR with an ankle injury, Strong was brought up for Week 5 versus the Bears. The fourth-year ball carrier ended up serving as the Packers' No. 2 option instead of Kaleb Johnson, with MarShawn Lloyd leading the ground attack. Strong recorded five carries for seven yards and three catches for 11 yards off four targets. If the hierarchy stays the same, he could be in for another game of solid usage facing a Dallas defense that's ranked 25th in fantasy points allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Pierre Strong will look to make the most of his opportunities as the Packers play the Lions in Week 7. Strong led Green Bay's backfield in a Week 6 win over the Cowboys, rushing the ball 11 times for 28 yards and catching five of six targets for 39 yards. The fourth-year running back looks to be a more dynamic option than MarShawn Lloyd moving forward, but both players could see a diminished role with Josh Jacobs set to return from the Commissioner's Exempt list. Detroit has ranked eighth in fantasy points allowed to running backs this season.
outlooksByWeek.8: Pierre Strong will likely be a depth option again as the Packers play the Panthers in Week 8. The return of Josh Jacobs in Week 7 against the Lions knocked Strong down a peg, and he did not log a touch, with MarShawn Lloyd assuming the secondary running back role. Strong could remain a passing-down option with Chris Brooks out another week on IR, but his role moving forward still remains in jeopardy. Carolina has ranked 31st in fantasy points allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Pierre Strong is primed to be a depth option again as the Packers play the Patriots in Week 9. The continued presence of Josh Jacobs has knocked Strong down a peg, and he's logged just one carry for two yards in the last two weeks. With Chris Brooks now vying for a return off IR and MarShawn Lloyd remaining the complementary option to Jacobs, Strong's role could diminish fully in the coming weeks. New England's front has ranked sixth in fantasy points allowed to RBs.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kayshon Boutte was held to one catch in his Texans debut, so he doesn't profile as a viable fantasy option for Week 2 against the Bengals. Boutte may still be learning the playbook after being acquired in an Aug. 24 trade from New England, and facing a tough Buffalo secondary didn't help things in Week 1, but he will need to demonstrate greater involvement in the game plan to warrant lineup consideration outside the deepest of formats. Cincinnati's secondary played well in Week 1, as no Buccaneers WR exceeded 63 yards against them.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kayshon Boutte had three catches in his second game with the Texans in Week 2 after going without a catch in his team debut. He's probably the best downfield option in the absence of Nico Collins (hamstring), who looks likely to sit out again in Week 3 against the Colts after missing the Week 2 loss to Cincinnati. The Colts have talent in their secondary, led by CB Sauce Gardner, but they are vulnerable to big plays through the air since they often leave their cornerbacks in one-on-one coverage with receivers. Indianapolis has allowed the most points and yards in the NFL this season, so Boutte has starter-level upside in deep leagues for Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kayshon Boutte has 79 yards on nine targets through three games with the Texans heading into a Week 4 home game against the vulnerable Dallas secondary. Boutte's 8.8 yards per target (YPT) trails only Jaylin Noel's 11.2 YPT among Houston's wideouts, while Xavier Hutchinson (21 targets; 5.7 YPT) and Jared Wayne (12 targets; 5.4 YPT) haven't done much with their chances. The Texans traded for Boutte in late August, so it's possible he's being brought along slowly and could start to see his role increase, especially if Nico Collins (hamstring) misses a third consecutive game in Week 4. Until Boutte starts getting more opportunities, the former Patriots WR will be difficult to trust in any format.
outlooksByWeek.5: Kayshon Boutte is averaging 29 receiving yards per game and has yet to score this season for the Texans. The former Patriots wide receiver hasn't shown enough with his new team to warrant lineup consideration in most fantasy formats in Week 5 against a Titans defense that has allowed three TDs to WRs through four games. Three other Texans wideouts have more yards than Boutte this season, as does TE Dalton Schultz.
outlooksByWeek.6: Kayshon Boutte is averaging 31 receiving yards per game and has yet to score as a member of the Texans. Houston doesn't seem happy with the August trade acquisition from New England, considering the Texans dipped back into the trade market at wide receiver after their Week 5 win over the Titans and acquired Marvin Harrison from Arizona. Even if Harrison isn't ready to assume a prominent role in Week 6, Boutte hasn't shown enough to warrant fantasy consideration outside the deepest of formats, even in a favorable matchup against a Jacksonville defense that's allowing the most yards per game to wide receivers.

player.seasonOutlook: Boutte was traded to the Texans in August. Reportedly a cut/trade candidate throughout most of the 2025 offseason, Boutte went on to lead the AFC champion Patriots' wide receiver room in routes and touchdowns while playing 67% of the offensive snaps when active. Despite the generous usage in a good offense, Boutte wasn't a reliable fantasy option, averaging 8.9 fantasy PPG. After seeing a career-high nine targets in Week 1, Boutte didn't clear five in a game the rest of the regular season. The 2023 sixth-round pick has finished in the range of 500-600 yards each of the last two seasons and has yet to produce a top-50 fantasy campaign. Now with Houston, Boutte will compete with Xavier Hutchinson and Jaylin Noel for Houston's No. 2 receiver role behind Nico Collins. Even if he wins that job, he doesn't figure to see enough work to find his way into the weekly flex discussion.

outlooksByWeek.6: Fernando Mendoza saw his first NFL action late in the Raiders' Week 5 loss to the Patriots, completing six of eight passes for 48 yards. His lone drive stalled in the red zone after he came up just short on a fourth-and-4 scramble. Kirk Cousins has led the team to a 3-2 record and remains the starter, but after Las Vegas used the first overall pick in the 2026 draft on Mendoza, it's only a matter of time before he gets a proper look under center. Another loss or two, something that seems very possible given the Raiders' upcoming schedule, could prompt coach Klint Kubiak to make the switch. If Mendoza does see action again in Week 6, he could pop for some intriguing numbers against a Bills defense that ranks 29th in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Mendoza was selected by the Raiders with the No. 1 overall pick in April's draft. The reigning Heisman Trophy winner and national champion, Mendoza is a big, pocket quarterback with elite accuracy (his career 7.1% off-target rate is easily the best in this rookie class) and a solid arm. Mendoza's 2025 campaign at Indiana included class-best marks in passing TDs (41) and QBR (90.3). He posted a 65-440-7 rushing line in 16 games last season and figures to add some value with his legs in the pros. Mendoza will get some run as a rookie, but his supporting cast isn't overly impressive and he will not start in Week 1 (Kirk Cousins will get the call), so there's not much sense in drafting him in most formats. He'll be worth a speculative add only when he's named Las Vegas' starter.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jaylen Wright's role in the Dolphins' offense is limited entering a Week 2 matchup against the 49ers. Despite being their No. 2 back, Wright played just 6% of their offensive snaps to De'Von Achane's 88%. With Miami likely falling behind early and being forced to pass, Wright is far more insurance for Achane managers than a viable fantasy option.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jaylen Wright's role is limited in the Dolphins' backfield entering a Week 3 matchup with the Chiefs. He has logged just seven snaps through two games and is now dealing with a stinger issue that makes him uncertain to play. With no clear immediate path to touches, Wright is an insurance policy in a matchup against a defense allowing 4.0 yards per carry.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jaylen Wright will have an elevated role for the Dolphins in Week 4 against the Vikings if he's able to overcome a foot issue that kept him out last Sunday. Miami lost De'Von Achane for the season due to a knee injury, leaving just Wright and Ollie Gordon to handle carries. With the Dolphins falling behind often in most matchups, Wright has the chance to be the better pass-catching option of the two. Facing a Vikings defense that's allowing just 3.1 ypc and 11 catches to running backs to date however doesn't inspire confidence.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jaylen Wright hasn't emerged from the Dolphins' backfield ahead of a Week 5 tilt against the Bengals. After missing Week 3, Wright was thought to have an ascending role following De'Von Achane's season-ending knee injury but received only five carries in Week 4 while Ollie Gordon shined with 100 yards and a touchdown on nine carries. It doesn't appear Wright was limited by the foot issue that cost him a game, as he remained the team's primary kick returner. Facing a defense that's allowing 4.5 yards per carry should afford Wright additional running lanes, but the role uncertainty puts Wright in wait-and-see territory rather than as a viable flex option.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jaylen Wright hopes to come out of the Dolphins' bye with a larger role in Week 7 against the Jets. Wright has only amassed 11 carries over his last two outings, finishing with 18 yards while not being targeted in the passing game. Ollie Gordon has dominated backfield work since De'Von Achane (knee) went down for the season, leaving managers in a wait-and-see mode with regards to Wright against a defense that's allowing 4.2 yards per carry, ranking near the middle of the pack league-wide.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jaylen Wright has not played a meaningful role out of the Dolphins' backfield and is uncertain to play in Week 8 against the Patriots due to a quad issue. He had five or six carries in each of his last three games, failing to average better than 1.8 yards per carry, and has not caught a pass all season. Facing a middling New England run defense seems less important than considering Wright's continued lack of clean health and the potential that Miami falls behind early and abandons the run.
outlooksByWeek.9: Jaylen Wright continues to play a minor role in the Dolphins' rushing game ahead of a Week 9 matchup with the Lions. Wright has logged a 12% to 14% snap share over the last three weeks, not topping six offensive touches in any outing, with Ollie Gordon dominating carries. Detroit is allowing 4.0 yards per carry, which is in the middle of the pack, but they allow the third-fewest fantasy points to the position. Barring an injury to Gordon, Wright's usage is unlikely to change, keeping him off most fantasy radars.

player.seasonOutlook: Wright will once again compete with second-year Ollie Gordon II for backup reps behind feature back De'Von Achane. Wright has barely cleared 70 touches during each of his first two NFL seasons, but he has shined at times, including a 24-107-1 rushing line in Week 14 last season. The 2024 fourth-round pick has been effective as a rusher, but hasn't been involved in the passing game (15 targets in 25 games). The 23-year-old would be worth adding only in the event of an Achane injury and even then, it's possible he would split (or be on the short end of a committee) with Gordon in a rebuilding offense that may not score very often.

outlooksByWeek.2: Ray Davis remains largely uninvolved in the Bills' offense entering a Week 2 matchup with the Lions. He played more snaps on special teams (six) than on offense (five) in Week 1, and as long as James Cook remains healthy, Davis is an insurance policy more than a viable flex consideration. Davis' snaps would be further limited if RB Ty Johnson is able to suit up after missing Opening Week.
outlooksByWeek.3: Ray Davis has limited involvement in Buffalo's offense entering Week 3 against the Chargers. Through two weeks, Davis has logged one carry and no targets as James Cook's primary backup, making his only contribution on kick returns. Facing a defense that's allowing just 2.98 yards per carry and with no clear path to an uptick in opportunities, Davis is an insurance policy for Cook managers only.
outlooksByWeek.4: Ray Davis hasn't recorded a carry in consecutive weeks or a reception all season as the Bills get set to face the Patriots in Week 4. Davis logged a total of 16 offensive snaps all season, with Ty Johnson's return as a passing-down back further hindering Davis's hope for work. He remains solely an insurance policy for James Cook against a defense allowing 4.2 yards per carry.
outlooksByWeek.5: Ray Davis has not been a part of the Bills' game plan entering a Week 5 matchup with the Rams. He has only two carries through four weeks, adding one catch while factoring in on kickoff returns. Seemingly losing snaps to Ty Johnson on passing downs in what was already a limited role, Davis's only fantasy appeal would be to James Cook managers in the event of an injury.

player.seasonOutlook: Davis is back as the primary insurance option behind Bills' feature back James Cook III. The 2024 fourth-round pick is one of the most valuable backups in fantasy, but flies a bit under the radar due to a very small game-day role when Cook and passing-down specialist Ty Johnson are both healthy. That's been the scenario most of the last two seasons, but we've seen Davis play more than half of Buffalo's snaps in three games. During those outings, Davis averaged 21.0 touches, 130.3 yards and 19.4 fantasy points per game. The 26-year-old has no standalone value, but he'll leap into the RB2 mix should Cook miss time, which makes him worth stashing on the end of your bench.

So much is stacked against the Colts' defense at the onset of 2026. They were the second-worst scorer over the second half of 2025, in large part due to injuries to key performers, they lost CB Kenny Moore and LB Zaire Franklin during the offseason, and they have one of the most brutal opening schedules of any team (BAL, @KC, HOU the first three weeks). This is more of a wait-and-see D/ST than one to target on draft day.

outlooksByWeek.2: Cade Otton will likely operate as one of the Buccaneers' top receiving options in the Week 2 matchup against the Browns. Otton caught just three of five targets for 26 yards in the Week 1 loss, but he was on the field for 56 of 57 offensive snaps, solidifying his role as Tampa Bay's top tight end. Additionally, Otton received the third-most targets on the Buccaneers, suggesting there's more production on the way. He's in for a favorable Week 2 matchup against a Browns defense that allowed 34 total points and 12.2 PPR fantasy points to TEs in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Cade Otton is expected to remain Tampa Bay's top tight end in the Week 3 matchup against the Vikings. Through two weeks, Otton is tied for the most targets (11) and second-most receptions (eight) on the Buccaneers, which is a good sign for his outlook moving forward. He's currently on pace to finish with career highs in targets (93) and receptions (68), though is role could diminish once Jalen McMillan returns to full speed. Otton is in for a difficult matchup in Week 3, as Minnesota's defense has allowed just 9.9 PPR fantasy points per game to TEs this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Cade Otton is expected to remain a crucial part of Tampa Bay's offensive game plan in the Week 4 matchup against the Packers. Otton had his best performance of the season in the Week 3 loss to the Vikings, catching three of six targets for 56 yards. Through three weeks, Otton is the only Buccaneers tight end to record a reception, which is a positive sign for his outlook going forward. Otton could struggle in Week 4 with Baker Mayfield (thumb) set to miss time, but the matchup remains favorable, as Green Bay has allowed 11.5 PPR points per game to tight ends this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Cade Otton will operate as the Buccaneers' top tight end in the Week 5 matchup against the Cowboys. Otton led Tampa Bay in receiving yards during the Week 4 loss to the Packers, hauling in four of six targets for 37 yards. He appears to have a connection with rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels and could be a solid spot-start in Week 5, especially while facing a Dallas defense that's given up 15.3 fantasy points per game and three receiving touchdowns to opposing tight ends this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Cade Otton is expected to remain one of Tampa Bay's top receiving options in the Week 6 matchup against the Steelers. Otton had his worst performance of the season in the Week 5 win over the Cowboys, catching three of four targets for 25 yards. However, he ranks second on the Buccaneers in targets (27) and receiving yards (182) through five games, which is a positive sign for his outlook going forward. Otton is in for a relatively favorable matchup against a Pittsburgh defense that's given up 13.2 fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Cade Otton is expected to remain one of Tampa Bay's top pass catchers in the Week 7 matchup against the Panthers. Otton struggled during the Week 6 overtime loss to the Steelers, hauling in one of two targets for four yards. Despite this, he played 100% of the Buccaneers' offensive snaps, suggesting more fantasy production is coming in the near future. Otton is also in for a favorable matchup in Week 7, as Carolina's defense has given up 16.0 fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends this season.
outlooksByWeek.8: Cade Otton is expected to remain one of Baker Mayfield's top targets in the Buccaneers' Week 8 matchup against the Falcons. Otton went without a catch during Tampa Bay's Week 7 win over the Panthers. However, this was largely due to the Buccaneers' success on the ground, as quarterback Baker Mayfield threw for just 64 yards while the team accumulated 258 rushing yards. Otton will have a good bounce-back opportunity against a Falcons defense that's allowed 16.4 fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends this season.
outlooksByWeek.9: Cade Otton is expected to serve as one of the Buccaneers' top receiving options in the Week 9 matchup against the Bears. He has caught just one pass over Tampa Bay's last three games, making him hard to trust going forward. Since Baker Mayfield returned from injury in the Week 7 win over the Panthers, the Buccaneers have attempted just 14 passes, making it hard for their pass catchers to contribute to fantasy teams. Despite this, Otton is in for a relatively favorable Week 9 matchup against a Chicago defense that's allowed 13.1 fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends through seven contests this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Otton re-signed with Tampa Bay after spending his first four NFL seasons with the team. Since entering the league in 2022, Otton ranks first among all tight ends in snaps (3,530) and second in routes (1,838). That simply hasn't translated to much target volume (he is yet to clear 86 in a season) or goal-line work (11 TDs and 19 end zone targets in 63 games). In fact, Otton was the only player with 75-plus targets who didn't score multiple touchdowns last season. The 27-year-old has finished 25th or lower in fantasy PPG in three of four seasons and is a poor bet for his first top-10 finish in 2026. He's well off the fantasy radar.

outlooksByWeek.7: Tanner McKee started last game at quarterback for the Eagles, and he could potentially find himself under center for the foreseeable future. Starter Jalen Hurts will be sidelined for the remainder of the season due to blood clots, leaving McKee as next in line under center. He threw for 215 yards and a touchdown last game versus the Panthers. In Week 7, the Eagles will face a Dallas defense that has struggled to defend the pass in 2026. The Cowboys are allowing 232.7 passing yards per game, which is 23rd in the NFL. In addition, Dallas has surrendered 11 passing touchdowns, which is tied for 24th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.8: Tanner McKee was mediocre last game for the Eagles. McKee completed 23-of-35 passes for 211 yards, one touchdown and one interception in the 38-21 loss to Dallas. McKee has thrown for at least 210 yards and a touchdown in each of his starts for Philadelphia. In Week 8, he will face a Commanders defense that has been rather poor in defending the pass in 2026. Washington is allowing 254 passing yards per game, which is 28th in the NFL. In addition, the Commanders have surrendered 15 passing scores, which is tied for 28th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.9: Tanner McKee continues to struggle under center for the Eagles, though admittedly he is working with limited help. Though running back Saquon Barkley returned from injury in the loss to Washington, staring wideouts Devonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks remained sidelined, and the right side of the offensive line is still a work in progress. McKee had two turnovers while failing to throw a touchdown against the Commanders. In Week 9, McKee will face a much-improved Giants pass defense. The G-Men are allowing just 184.9 passing yards per tilt, which is third in the NFL. However, New York has yielded 14 passing scores in 2026, which is tied for 23rd in the league.

outlooksByWeek.2: Drew Stevens missed a field goal and an extra point in Week 1 for Washington. The Commanders lost by two points, making the misses all the more glaring. Stevens will have a chance to rebound in Week 2, though, as Washington faces a Dallas squad that allowed the most points in the NFL last season, and looked no better in their season opener versus the Giants. Dallas lost an ugly 28-20 affair to the G-Men.
outlooksByWeek.3: Drew Stevens missed his second field goal of the season last game for Washington. Stevens did make two other field goals as well as both of his PATs, but the Commanders offense is not a pretty option for a fairly shaky kicker heading into a brutal Week 3 matchup versus Seattle. The Seahawks are allowing just 8.5 points per contest thus far this season, which is second in the NFL. In addition, starting quarterback Jayden Daniels is unlikely to play for the Commanders after dislocating his elbow.
outlooksByWeek.4: Drew Stevens connected on an impressive 57-yard field goal in Washington's 33-31 win over the Seahawks last game. However, Stevens also missed an extra point, and has now missed four kicks through three outings. Stevens has a big leg but could be on thin ice with a few more misses. He should have ample opportunities in Week 4 versus the Colts, though. Indianapolis is allowing 30.3 points per tilt, which is 30th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Drew Stevens has made at least two field goals in three-straight games for the Commanders. Stevens connected on two field goals, as well as an extra point, in Washington's 30-13 loss to the Colts in London. In Week 5, Washington will face the first-place New York Giants. New York's defense has been much-improved in 2026, allowing just 19.8 points per tilt, which is eighth in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.6: Drew Stevens missed an extra point last game for Washington. With the contest resulting in a 27-27 tie, Stevens could have been viewed as the goat. However, late-game clock mismanagement by the offense failed to allow Stevens a chance at redemption, as the Commanders could not get off a game-winning field goal attempt as time expired in overtime. Stevens did hit two other field goals as well as another extra point in the contest. His job should still be safe heading into Week 6 versus the 49ers. However, his opportunities could be limited, as San Fran is yielding just 18.6 points per tilt, which is third in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.8: Drew Stevens has made at least two field goals in four of six games this season for Washington. However, he has made just 10 field goals the entire year overall, while missing three extra points. In Week 8, the Commanders face the Eagles. Philadelphia is allowing 22.8 points per contest, which is 17th in the league.

outlooksByWeek.5: Efton Chism's role could expand in Week 5 when the Patriots face the Raiders. He drew four targets in Week 4, turning them into two catches for 42 yards and a touchdown, getting additional snaps due to Mack Hollins' (calf) early exit. Seemingly ascending over Kyle Williams on the depth chart and with Hollins' availability uncertain, Chism could again produce against a vulnerable secondary that's allowed four opposing receivers to gain 70 or more yards in as many weeks.
outlooksByWeek.6: Efton Chism aims to continue ascending the Patriots receiver depth chart Week 6 against the Jets. Chism has 10 targets over the last two weeks with both Mack Hollins and A.J. Brown sidelined, compiling 97 yards and a touchdown. Drake Maye is spreading targets, making Chism a touch volatile, but facing a Jets defense that's allowed four opposing receivers to go for 63 yards or more in two weeks offers Chism the potential to keep it going.
outlooksByWeek.7: Efton Chism's role in the Patriots passing game is in doubt ahead of a Week 7 matchup with the Bears. With A.J. Brown returning from an ankle injury in Week 6, Chism only had one target after compiling 10 looks over the past two weeks. That low volume came with Romeo Doubs missing three quarters of action as well, so even if Doubs misses Week 7, Chism will still have limited opportunities to best a secondary that's allowing 9.8 yards per target, the third-highest mark in the league.
outlooksByWeek.8: Efton Chism will hope to be more than an afterthought in the Patriots' passing game in Week 8 against the Dolphins. After showing some potential with A.J. Brown sidelined, Chism has just two targets over the last two weeks, resulting in a 16-yard catch. New England heavily targeted tight ends in Week 7, and that appears to be an effective strategy against Miami as well, likely limiting opportunities for Chism to post high catch or yardage totals.
outlooksByWeek.9: Efton Chism hasn't provided chunk plays in the Patriots offense ahead of a Week 9 matchup with Green Bay. Chism drew five targets in Week 8 with A.J. Brown (knee) sidelined, an uptick from the two targets he collected over the previous two games with Brown on the field. His season-high has been 57 yards, not offering much potential. Even if Brown remains sidelined, Chism isn't likely to be a preferred option for Drake Maye or fantasy lineups against a secondary that's allowing 7.0 yards per target.

player.seasonOutlook: Sanders enters his second NFL season set to back up Deshaun Watson in Cleveland. Sanders made eight appearances during his rookie season and wasn't overly productive, scoring eight all-purpose touchdowns, throwing 10 interceptions and completing 57% of his passes. The fifth-round pick produced one weekly fantasy finish better than 18th, though it was an impressive 364-yard passing game with four total touchdowns (33.5 points). Sanders added some value with his legs, including 20-plus yards in five straight games to end the season. The 24-year-old remains a wild card and is likely to earn some starts this season, so that's enough to make him worthy off a stash in superflex/dynasty leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jauan Jennings will aim to make more of his opportunities as the Vikings take on the Bears in Week 2. Jennings garnered just one target against the Packers in Week 1, and he was unable to convert it into a reception. The veteran was still on the field for almost half of the offensive plays, which keeps him as the WR3 moving forward. He'll look to get his first catch of the season against a Chicago defense that allowed the fourth-most PPR points to Panthers wide receivers (46.3) in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jauan Jennings will hopefully return to action as the Vikings travel to Tampa Bay in Week 3. Jennings sat out in Week 2 due to personal reasons, so his practice availability this upcoming week should dictate whether he plays at the Bucs. The former 49ers wideout has yet to record a catch this season, but he played almost 50 percent of the offensive snaps in Week 1. He'll face a Bucs defense that's allowed 24.9 PPR points per game against wide receivers so far this season, a top-10 mark.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jauan Jennings will look to expand on his first catch of the year as the Vikings play the Dolphins in Week 4. Jennings brought in one of two targets for one yard against the Buccaneers in Week 3, which is promising given that he was out due to personal reasons the previous week. The veteran should continue to operate as Minnesota's No. 3 option at wide receiver moving forward, but Justin Jefferson's injury does have a bearing on Jennings' usage. Miami has allowed a top-five 24.2 fantasy points per game to WRs this year.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jauan Jennings remains a secondary option in the passing game ahead of Minnesota's Week 5 matchup at New Orleans. Jennings was projected to benefit from Justin Jefferson sitting out Week 4 with an ankle injury, but the veteran wideout logged just one catch for eight yards. He's now recorded two catches for nine yards in two weeks mostly without Jefferson, which especially doesn't bode well for his value when the star pass catcher returns to the field. He'll face a Saints defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy WRs so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jauan Jennings is a depth option ahead of Minnesota's Week 7 matchup against the Colts. Jennings has been unable to get things going so far this season, with just two catches for nine yards across his four appearances. The only positive outlook moving forward for the veteran is that he's been on the field for a favorable number of offensive snaps, but that hasn't translated into output. Indianapolis has ranked middle-of-the-pack against fantasy WRs this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jauan Jennings will seek to build on a season-best performance as the Vikings take on the Lions in Week 8. Jennings had a quiet start to the season heading into Minnesota's bye, logging just two catches for nine yards off five targets in four games. The veteran wide receiver turned it around in Week 7 against the Colts, though, hauling in two of three targets for 34 yards. Jennings should still be a secondary look moving forward, but he'll look to continue to carve out targets versus a Detroit defense that's ranked 26th in fantasy points allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Jauan Jennings will look to stay involved as the Vikings play the Bills in Week 9. Jennings brought in two catches for 11 yards in Minnesota's Week 8 loss to the Lions, which was his second straight game with two catches. The veteran pass catcher has now logged six receptions for 54 yards on 10 targets this season. He could see continued success against a Buffalo defense that's ranked 28th in fantasy points allowed to his position.

player.seasonOutlook: Jennings signed with the Vikings in May. The 2020 seventh-round pick was a situational player during his first three pro campaigns in San Francisco prior to breaking out with a 77-975-6 receiving line and 27th-place finish in fantasy PPG in 2024. He dipped quite a bit statistically in 2025 and failed to produce a single top-10 fantasy week, but did score nine touchdowns (sixth among WRs) in a good Niners offense. The 29-year-old will now file in third on the Minnesota depth chart behind Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison. He's headed for a big dip in targets and, especially with Kyler Murray under center, won't be a consistent fantasy option. He's barely worth late-round consideration.

outlooksByWeek.2: Chris Brooks will remain in the backfield mix for Green Bay against the Jets in Week 2. While Brooks took an ancillary role to Marshawn Lloyd in Week 1, Brooks still finished the game with seven rushes for 29 yards to Lloyd's 13 for 37. Brooks is also an excellent pass blocker, so he'll still get time on the field even if it doesn't convert to rushing attempts. New York dominated Tennessee in the trenches in Week 1, but they should be a lot less daunting than a staunch Minnesota front.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chris Brooks should continue to stay involved as the Packers play the Falcons in Week 3. Brooks was a non-factor on the ground against the Jets in Week 2 (four carries for 11 yards), but he did reel in his first catch of the season for 15 yards. The fourth-year running back should remain on the field for passing-situation plays moving forward, especially since he served that role last season even with Josh Jacobs on the field. He'll face an Atlanta defense that's been tough on RBs so far this season, allowing a top-10 16.3 PPR points per game.
outlooksByWeek.4: Chris Brooks will remain an option in Green Bay's crowded backfield against the Buccaneers in Week 4. Brooks failed to register a carry and caught his sole target for four yards in a Week 3 loss to Atlanta, but he did log his third straight game with a 40-plus percent snap share on offense. The fourth-year running back's consistent usage on late downs as a pass catcher and a blocker makes him a valuable asset to the Packers, but not to fantasy managers at this point in the year. Tampa Bay has allowed the second-fewest rushing yards (165) but the sixth-highest receiving yards (165) to RBs on the year.
outlooksByWeek.5: Chris Brooks will remain an option in Green Bay's crowded backfield if he's healthy in Week 5 against the Bears. Brooks rushed a solid four times for 30 yards and caught one ball for five yards in the first quarter of Week 4, but he then injured his ankle and did not record a stat after. The fourth-year running back will need to log some healthy practices this week if he hopes to play against the Packers' big rival. If he's able to suit up, Brooks will face a Bears defense that's allowed bottom-10 (4.73) yards per carry for RBs this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jordan Mason will remain sidelined for Week 6 as the Packers take on the Cowboys. Brooks is currently on IR due to an ankle injury, which will keep him out for at least the next three weeks. His absence from the field sets up MarShawn Lloyd, Kaleb Johnson and Pierre Strong as Green Bay's running back options in the near future.
outlooksByWeek.7: Chris Brooks will be out again in Week 7 when the Packers play the Lions. Brooks is currently on IR with an ankle injury, which will keep him out for at least the next two weeks. His absence from the field should continue to give Pierre Strong more opportunities in the run game.
outlooksByWeek.8: Chris Brooks will be out again in Week 8 as the Packers take on Carolina. Brooks is currently on IR with an ankle injury, which will keep him out for at least the next week. His absence from the field could continue to give Pierre Strong more opportunities, but the return of Josh Jacobs has shaken up the RB room. Brooks' next chance to see the field will be in Week 9 against the Patriots.
outlooksByWeek.9: Chris Brooks will aim to make a return as the Packers play the Patriots in Week 9. Brooks has been on IR for the last four weeks due to an ankle injury, but he could be on the field as soon as this week if his recovery allows it. The fourth-year running back remained a solid change-of-pace option in the first four weeks of the season, with excellent pass blocking that kept him involved. If he does play against New England, he's set to be an option in a backfield consisting of Josh Jacobs, MarShawn Lloyd and minimally Pierre Strong.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tre' Harris had a quiet performance in the Chargers' season-opening loss to the Cardinals, catching three of six targets for 20 yards. The second-year wideout struggled along with the rest of the passing game under new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel, with the exception of Ladd McConkey, and he was knocked out of the game in the third quarter with a rib injury. The injury doesn't appear to be serious, but if McConkey misses time, Harris could see additional volume. In Week 2, the second-year wideout will face a Raiders secondary that was tied for 21st in points allowed per game to WRs last season.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tre' Harris caught only one pass in the Chargers' Week 2 loss to the Raiders, but he made it count, connecting with a scrambling Justin Herbert for a 53-yard gain that set up a third-quarter touchdown. Harris has just a 4-73-0 line on nine targets through two games, but if he continues to show he can gain significant yards after the catch, he could prove to be a good fit for OC Mike McDaniel's scheme. The 2025 second-round pick will face a Bills secondary in Week 3 that's given up the fourth-most receiving yards to WRs so far this year.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tre' Harris is coming off his best performance of the season in the Chargers' Week 3 loss to the Bills. With Ladd McConkey limited by a rib injury, Harris handled a season-high seven targets and turned them into a 6-76-0 line that led the team. A second-round pick in 2025, Harris' ability to put together a breakout year will be hampered by the dysfunctional offense around him, but he appears to be close to moving past Quentin Johnston into the No. 2 spot on the depth chart. Harris faces a tough matchup in Week 4 against a Seahawks secondary that ranks fourth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tre' Harris is still looking for his first touchdown of the season, but he's been Justin Herbert's most reliable option, topping 50 receiving yards in each of the Chargers' last three games. Harris has put together a 13-209-0 line on 21 targets over four weeks, and he could make a push for the top spot on the WR depth chart with Ladd McConkey now dealing with both rib and foot injuries and Quentin Johnston failing to do much with his opportunities. Harris will aim for his first trip to the end zone in 2026 in Week 5 against a Broncos secondary that ranks eighth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs, but which could be missing its top two cornerbacks, including Patrick Surtain.
outlooksByWeek.6: Tre' Harris wasn't able to take advantage of the absences of Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston in the Chargers' Week 5 loss to the Broncos. He played 30 snaps, catching two of four targets for 16 yards before also getting hurt. Harris is viewed as week-to-week with a hamstring strain, but he was already struggling to make an impression in a Mike McDaniel scheme that is performing well below expectations in all areas. If Harris does get cleared to play in Week 6, he'll be facing a Kansas City secondary that ranks first in the NFL in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Tre' Harris missed the Chargers' last game before a bye due to a hamstring injury, but the time off could allow him to return to the lineup. The bigger issue for the second-year wideout is the state of the offense around him, as he's topped 60 receiving yards only once in five games and is still looking for his first touchdown of 2026. Ladd McConkey could also return from an injury in Week 8, which might leave Harris struggling to get significant volume against a stingy Rams secondary that ranks fifth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Tre' Harris missed the Chargers' last game before their Week 7 bye with a hamstring issue, but he returned to action in Week 8 against the Rams and caught all three of his targets for 31 yards. The second-year wide receiver remains a secondary part of a struggling offense as long as Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston are available, and through six games this season Harris has just an 18-256-0 line on 28 targets. He'll try to make a bigger impact in Week 9 against an underperforming Texans secondary that ranks a stunning 30th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Harris is a Year 2 breakout candidate after flashing in a limited role as a rookie. The 2025 second-round pick quietly played 49% of the Chargers' offensive snaps, but he spent a lot of that blocking and was limited to an 8% target share. Harris is likely to open the 2026 season behind Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston, but with Keenan Allen gone, his competition for No. 3 duties is 2025 fifth-round pick KeAndre Lambert-Smith and rookie Brenen Thompson. A potential starter in new playcaller Mike McDaniel's offense, the 24-year-old Harris is an intriguing late-round sleeper.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kendrick Bourne had a promising performance for Arizona in Week 1 and will look to be productive again versus the Seahawks in Week 2. Bourne led Cardinals wideouts with eight catches and 75 yards in a season-opening victory versus the Chargers, with only stud tight end Trey McBride outpacing his eight targets. The veteran Bourne looked to have great rapport with QB Jacoby Brissett, so it will be interesting to see how the target distribution shakes out in Week 2 and beyond. He won't have an easy matchup against Seattle, who limited New England to 178 yards through the air in a Week 1 win.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kendrick Bourne appears to have earned a key role in Arizona's passing game heading into a Week 3 matchup versus San Francisco. After joining the Cardinals in the offseason, Bourne has recorded 11 targets through two weeks, second-most among Arizona wide receivers. The veteran wideout has logged a 10-86-0 line on those opportunities, as he has established good chemistry with QB Jacoby Brissett. With that said, Week 3 could be another tough test for Arizona's air game: the 49ers have allowed just a 59.3 percent catch rate to WRs so far, ninth-best in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kendrick Bourne is coming off two quiet weeks heading into Arizona's Week 4 tilt versus the Giants. After posting an 8-75-0 receiving line in the season opener against the Chargers, the veteran wideout has managed a modest four catches on six targets for 33 yards combined over his subsequent two games. Bourne appears to be well behind WR Michael Wilson and TE Trey McBride, and at least marginally behind WR Marvin Harrison, in the passing-game pecking order at the moment. There could be an opportunity to make some noise against a Giants defense that ranks in the bottom half of the league in receiving yards allowed to wideouts so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Kendrick Bourne is looking to re-involve himself in Arizona's offense in Week 5 against the Lions. Bourne logged a healthy 42 of 66 offensive snaps against the Giants in Week 4, but he didn't draw a single target from QB Jacoby Brissett. In fact, Bourne has logged just six total targets across his past three games after posting an 8-75-0 line on eight targets in the Cardinals' season opener. Detroit could provide an opportunity for Bourne to get going, as the Lions have given up a league-high 61 total catches to wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Kendrick Bourne seems set for a major role in Arizona's offense ahead of a Week 6 matchup against the Rams. With Marvin Harrison now officially traded to the Texans, Bourne figures to slot in behind Michael Wilson as the Cardinals' No. 2 wideout. That positioning led to a nice game for Bourne this past Sunday against Detroit, as he outproduced Wilson with a 5-70-0 line on eight targets. The Rams could present a challenge, however, as they've yielded the fewest catches per game (8.0) to wideouts through five weeks.
outlooksByWeek.7: Kendrick Bourne has established himself as a regular contributor in Arizona's passing attack, catching 22 passes for 225 yards through six games, though he hasn't found the end zone. The veteran wideout is averaging a career-low 10.2 yards per catch in 2026, but that's also due to the struggles the Cardinals' passing attack has had with Jacoby Brissett under center. To make things even more complicated, he'll face the Broncos' secondary in Week 7, and Denver has allowed the seventh-fewest fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts in 2026. That makes Bourne a difficult player to trust outside deeper PPR leagues.
outlooksByWeek.8: Kendrick Bourne could be primed for a bounce-back performance when Arizona travels to Dallas in Week 8. Bourne was quiet against Denver this past Sunday, logging just three catches for nine yards. However, he tied for third on the team with six targets as he continues to get a decent amount of looks behind top wideout Michael Wilson and star tight end Trey McBride. Bourne has an appealing matchup against the Cowboys, who are giving up 163.1 receiving yards per game to wideouts to rank 25th in the league in that category.

Austin Ekeler managed just three touches for seven yards last game for Washington. Even with starting running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt on Injured Reserve with a groin injury, Ekeler was on the field for just seven of 67 offensive snaps. Rachaad White should get the start in Week 8 versus the Eagles, and Jeremy McNichols may see more work than Ekeler between the tackles. McNichols had five carries for 13 yards in his return from injury. Whomever gets touches does have a favorable matchup, as Philadelphia is giving up 119.3 yards per clash on the ground, which is 21st in the league.
outlooksByWeek.9: Austin Ekeler rushed eight times for 36 yards last game. Starter Rachaad White  rushed 11 times for 55 yards and a touchdown in the 27-10 win over the Eagles. Jeremy McNichols left this game with an injury, leaving Ekeler as the only other healthy backup option. In Week 9, Washington will face a Rams defense allowing 109.3 yards per tilt on the ground, which is 14th in the NFL. However, the Rams have surrendered just four rushing scores in 2026, which is tied for third in the league.

outlooksByWeek.4: Ty Johnson looks to remain a passing-down option in Week 4 when the Bills face the Patriots. In Week 3's season debut, Johnson caught all four targets for 50 yards against the Chargers-heavy volume for playing just 15 snaps. In 28 snaps last season against New England, Johnson failed to record a reception. The Patriots have allowed eight catches to opposing running backs, rendering Johnson an unappealing, low-ceiling, low-floor option.
outlooksByWeek.5: Ty Johnson continues to factor in the Bills' passing game out of the backfield ahead of a Week 5 matchup with the Rams. After missing Weeks 1 and 2, Johnson has amassed six catches in Weeks 3 and 4, adding one three-yard carry. The Rams have allowed only 19 catches and 103 yards to opposing backs as receivers, and James Cook will likely continue to dominate backfield touches, rendering Johnson's fantasy potential minimal.
outlooksByWeek.6: Ty Johnson will look to again create chunk plays in the passing game when the Bills face the Raiders in Week 6. Johnson has only one carry in three games, but for the second time this season, he snagged four passes, finishing with 72 yards in Week 5. Johnson's role appears clear, and he's unlikely to have the chance to exploit a Las Vegas defense that's allowing 5.2 yards per carry but has been stingy to running backs in the passing game, surrendering just 29 receiving yards per game.
outlooksByWeek.8: Ty Johnson continues to produce when asked, but his role remains limited as the Bills get set to face the Ravens in Week 8. Used almost exclusively in the passing game, Johnson has 12 catches over four games since returning to health, averaging a decent 12.9 yards per catch. The volume remains too small to trust, and the Ravens have allowed just 102 yards and 2.6 yards per target to opposing running backs in the passing game, further dampening Johnson's potential.
outlooksByWeek.9: Ty Johnson continues to log receiving opportunities out of the Bills backfield ahead of a Week 9 matchup with the Vikings. Johnson has 15 catches and 174 yards through five games but has amassed only six carries in a backfield dominated by James Cook. Minnesota has been stiff to backs in the passing game, allowing just 4.1 yards per target, and without a solid rushing floor, Johnson could be a high-risk option.

player.seasonOutlook: Johnson has settled in as a productive change-of-pace and receiving option in the Buffalo backfield behind James Cook. Johnson enters his eighth NFL season having yet to clear 63 carries or 34 catches in a season, but his role allows for him to hit for the occasional big game (15-plus fantasy points four times over the last two seasons). Of course, those games have come at random, making Johnson an unusable fantasy commodity. Even if Cook misses time this season, it's likely that Johnson would remain in his role, with Ray Davis instead stepping into lead back duties. Johnson plays a valuable role for Buffalo, but he's not a fantasy option.

outlooksByWeek.2: Najee Harris was a healthy scratch in Week 1 for the Giants, but that could change quickly. While Cam Skattebo and Devin Singletary look like the 1-2 duo out front, third-string running back Tyrone Tracy lost a fumble in the red zone that could have proven costly.  Tracy had a rough camp even before the gaffe, so his time on the Giants could be coming to an end. If Harris does suit up in Week 2, he will be facing a Rams defense that was surprisingly suspect against the run in their first game of the season.  The Rams allowed 174 yards on the ground, which currently ranks them 30th in the league. However, Aaron Donald will return to the fold out of retirement versus the G-Men.
outlooksByWeek.4: Najee Harris turned back the clock in the 12-7 win for the Giants over the Titans. Harris rushed nine times for 52 yards, and may have seized the backup running back job away from both Devin Singletary and Tyrone Tracy. With Jameis Winston under center, the Giants should continue to rely heavily on the running game in Week 4 versus Arizona, though Cam Skattebo remains atop the depth chart. The Cardinals have been suspect against the run in 2026, allowing 127.7 yards per clash on the ground, which is 26th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.5: Najee Harris has received nine carries in each of the last two games for the Giants. However, he is averaging just 4.0 yards per carry as teams dare the Giants to throw with backup quarterback Jameis Winston, and remains behind Cam Skattebo on the depth chart. In Week 5, the G-Men will face a rather stingy Washington run defense. The Commanders are allowing just 93.5 yards per tilt on the ground, which is sixth in the league. However, Washington did allow three rushing touchdowns last game versus the Colts.
outlooksByWeek.6: Najee Harris had five carries for just nine yards last game for the Giants. The running game as a whole was fairly contained, as starter Cam Skattebo rushed for just 58 yards in the 27-27 tie with Washington. Interestingly, Tyrone Tracy also had five touches in this contest, perhaps showing that the backup role remains up for grabs. In Week 6, the Giants will face a Saints defense that has been gutted on the ground thus far in 2026. New Orleans is allowing148.8 rushing yards per clash, which is 30th in the league. In addition, New Orleans has allowed the most rushing touchdowns in the league.

outlooksByWeek.2: Xavier Hutchinson remains off the fantasy radar in most formats heading into Houston's Week 2 home game against the Bengals. He was third on the Texans with six targets in the season opener but finished with just three catches for 32 receiving yards. Hutchinson has topped 42 yards just twice through 50 career regular-season appearances.
outlooksByWeek.3: Xavier Hutchinson drew nine targets in Nico Collins' (hamstring) absence in Week 2 but turned that into just three catches for 37 yards. Hutchinson figures to maintain a prominent role in Houston's passing game against the league-worst Colts defense in Week 3, especially if Collins remains sidelined. Whether Hutchinson can turn that significant usage into production is another matter, as he has usually failed to capitalize on such opportunities in the past, with only two career regular-season games of 42 or more receiving yards. Hutchinson is in the Week 3 deep-league flex conversation, but his lack of prior production is concerning.
outlooksByWeek.4: Xavier Hutchinson continues to do little with substantial volume, and that seems unlikely to change in Week 4, even with Houston hosting a weak Cowboys defense surrendering 27.3 points per game. Hutchinson has caught just nine of 21 targets this season and is averaging 40 receiving yards per game. Houston's lack of capable alternatives at WR figures to keep Hutchinson involved enough in Week 4 to earn deep-league flex consideration, especially if top wideout Nico Collins (hamstring) misses a third consecutive game.
outlooksByWeek.5: Xavier Hutchinson has exactly three catches in every game this season for the Texans and is averaging 42 receiving yards per game heading into a Week 5 road game against the Titans. He has drawn 11 targets in two games playing alongside Nico Collins and 15 targets during the two games Collins missed due to a hamstring injury. Collins should continue to work as C.J. Stroud's No. 1 option against Tennessee's beatable secondary, while the remainder of Houston's receiving corps is best left on the bench or waiver wire, Hutchinson included.
outlooksByWeek.6: Xavier Hutchinson set season highs with four catches and 65 yards in Houston's Week 5 win over the Titans, but he has yet to score this season and has just three touchdowns in 54 career regular-season games. He's likely to slide down a spot on the WR depth chart once trade acquisition Marvin Harrison is up to speed, but that may not happen in Week 6 against the Jaguars. Hutchinson should get enough opportunities against a Jaguars defense that has allowed the most yards in the NFL to wide receivers to warrant Week 6 flex consideration in deeper formats.
outlooksByWeek.7: Xavier Hutchinson had season-low totals across the board with two catches for 10 yards on three targets in Houston's Week 6 win over the Jaguars, and he won't be a recommended Week 7 fantasy play against the Giants, even in deeper formats. He was earning decent volume while Houston's WR room was banged up, but the return of Nico Collins from a hamstring injury, coupled with the trade for Marvin Harrison and emergence of Jaylin Noel, have relegated Hutchinson to a depth role. Hutchinson doesn't have the talent to find consistent success with limited usage, as he has just three TDs in 55 career regular-season games.
