On one hand, the 2023 fourth-overall pick has a ton of upside; he ranked no lower than sixth among QBs in carries, rushing yards and rush TDs in 2024 despite only playing 10 full games, while also pacing the position in average depth of throw and yards per completion. That led to four 20-plus fantasy point games. On the other hand, Richardson's poor passing may lead to many duds. He had fewer than 15 fantasy points in his other six outings, threw 12 INTs on the season (fourth most) and his 48% completion percentage ranked last. In total, he averaged 15.8 fantasy PPG in the 10 games, which would've ranked 15th over the full season. Richardson's elite rushing ability and aggressive passing style are the only reason to keep him stashed in deep dynasty leagues.

Simpson was selected by the Rams in the first round of April's draft. Simpson was a one-year starter at Alabama and wasn't overly impressive statistically, completing 64% of his passes and posting a pedestrian 76.6 QBR. He's fairly accurate with an average arm, but he's a bit undersized and doesn't figure to move the needle a ton with his legs (62-309-2 rushing in 2025). Simpson won't see the field consistently until Matthew Stafford retires, so he's well off the 2026 fantasy radar. Keep him stashed in dynasty, especially superflex formats.

outlooksByWeek.2: Skyy Moore should be a depth option in Green Bay's passing game at New York in Week 2. Skyy Moore was unable to catch his one target, but he also did play on offense more than was expected. The fifth-year wideout should remain a secondary choice, but he could start to garner more looks given the pass-heavy offense that Green Bay has operated with. He'll face a Jets secondary that allowed a middle-of-the-pack 26.4 PPR points to wide receivers in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Skyy Moore should remain a secondary option in Green Bay's passing game against the Falcons in Week 3. Moore was utilized more in Week 2 against the Jets after Jayden Reed went down with an injury, garnering three targets and bringing in two of them for six yards. The former Kansas City wideout is the top kick returner for the Packers, but his playmaking abilities make him an interesting target for Jordan Love if he gets more involved in the offense. He'll take on an Atlanta defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 30.3 PPR points per game to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Skyy Moore should continue to get opportunities as the Packers play the Buccaneers in Week 4. Moore recorded three catches for 31 yards on a career-high seven targets in Week 3 against the Falcons. While a pass-heavy game script definitely helped the fifth-year wideout's cause, he has seen more of an offensive role with Jayden Reed sidelined due to a neck injury. Moore will face a Tampa Bay defense that's allowed a top-ten 25.4 fantasy points per game to wide receivers in the first three games of the season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Skyy Moore will seek to stay involved as the Packers play the Bears in Week 5. Moore caught another pass in Week 5 against Tampa Bay, but it went for minus-two yards. The veteran remains an asset for Green Bay on special teams, but he'll need to do more in the coming weeks to hold any value fantasy-wise. He'll face a Chicago team that's ranked top five against fantasy wide receivers this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Skyy Moore holds a questionable tag ahead of Green Bay's Week 6 matchup against the Cowboys. Moore suffered an ankle injury in the second quarter of the Packers' Week 5 blowout win over the Bears, and he was unable to return. The utility player has seen more usage with Jayden Reed out for the season with a neck injury, but he'll need to stay healthy himself if he hopes to capitalize. Moore, who has a 7-35-0 receiving line, will face a Dallas defense that's ranked 21st in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers.
outlooksByWeek.7: Skyy Moore will remain out as the Packers play the Lions in Week 7. Moore was placed on IR ahead of Week 6 versus the Cowboys, so he'll have to sit out for at least the next three weeks. His absence should keep Coleman Owen and J. Michael Sturdivant busy on the return fronts.
outlooksByWeek.8: Skyy Moore will remain sidelined as the Packers play the Panthers in Week 8. Moore was placed on IR ahead of Week 6 versus the Cowboys, so he'll have to sit out for at least the next  two weeks. His absence should keep Coleman Owen, J. Michael Sturdivant and Bo Melton busy on the return fronts.
outlooksByWeek.9: Skyy Moore will remain inactive as the Packers play New England in Week 9. Moore was placed on IR ahead of Week 6 versus the Cowboys, so he'll have to sit out for at least the next week. His absence should keep Coleman Owen, J. Michael Sturdivant and Bo Melton busy as returners.

player.seasonOutlook: After failing to lock down a starting gig with the Bears, Steelers and Jets, Fields was traded to the Chiefs and will move forward as Patrick Mahomes' backup. That's obviously unlikely to lead to much playing time, barring a Mahomes injury. Should Fields start, he'll find his way into the QB1 discussion because of his elite rushing ability (45.1 rush rushing yards per game last season and four-plus rushing TDs in four straight seasons). In seven full games last season, Fields averaged 19.2 fantasy points, including 25 points in three of those games. He averaged 18.9 points with Pittsburgh in 2024 and 19.3 during his final two seasons in Chicago. Roster Fields in only deep superflex leagues.

outlooksByWeek.3: Brycen Tremayne is expected to play a reserve role in the Panthers' receiving corps in the Week 3 matchup against the Browns. Tremayne was thought to have a larger role in the Panthers' offensive game plan heading into Week 2, as the team cut ties with Jimmy Horn. However, Tremayne played just nine offensive snaps and didn't receive a target, as his role remains primarily on special teams. The third-year wideout is in for a favorable matchup, however, with the Browns' defense allowing four touchdowns to WRs through two contests.
outlooksByWeek.4: Brycen Tremayne is expected to remain a depth option in Carolina's receiving corps ahead of the Week 4 matchup against the Lions. Tremayne had the most productive game of his career in the Week 3 loss to the Browns, catching four of six targets for 83 yards while Jalen Coker (quadriceps) and Xavier Legette (knee) were sidelined. Tremayne could remain a larger part of the Panthers' offensive game plan if Coker or Legette were to remain sidelined for the Week 4 contest. Regardless, he's in for a tremendous matchup against a Lions secondary that's given up 568 receiving yards to wideouts through three games this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Brycen Tremayne is expected to remain a depth option in the Panthers' receiving corps during the Week 6 matchup against the Eagles. Tremayne played a career-high 92% of Carolina's offensive snaps in the Week 4 win over the Lions, catching two of three targets for 32 yards. However, this was without emerging star Jalen Coker (quadriceps), who's expected to return for the Week 6 contest. Regardless, Tremayne is in for a favorable matchup against an Eagles secondary that's given up 8.2 yards per target to opposing wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Brycen Tremayne is expected to play a depth role in the Panthers' receiving corps in the Week 7 matchup against the Buccaneers. Tremayne stepped up while Jalen Coker was sidelined catching six of nine targets for 135 yards in Weeks 3 and 4. However, Tremayne saw no targets in the Week 6 win over the Eagles, likely due to the return of Coker. Tremayne will likely remain irrelevant for fantasy purposes without scoring a touchdown, but he's in for a favorable Week 7 matchup against a Buccaneers defense that's allowed 7.6 yards per target this season.
outlooksByWeek.8: Brycen Tremayne is expected to remain a depth option in the Panthers' receiving corps during the Week 8 matchup against the Packers. Tremayne had a costly drop on fourth down during the Week 7 loss to the Buccaneers and has now went without a catch in four of his six appearances this season. He likely will remain irrelevant for fantasy purposes unless he finds the end zone going forward. However, Tremayne is in for a solid Week 8 matchup against a Packers defense that's given up 7.2 yards per target to opposing wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.9: Brycen Tremayne is expected to play a reserve role in the Panthers' receiving corps in the Week 9 matchup against the Broncos. Tremayne's role on Carolina's offense has shrank over the last three weeks, catching just one of two targets for 11 yards during that span. On the season, Tremayne has logged seven receptions for 125 yards and no touchdowns, with 83 of those yards coming in the Week 4 win over the Lions. Additionally, he's in for a tough matchup against a Denver secondary that's allowed just 10.2 yards per completion this season.

outlooksByWeek.4: AJ Dillon is expected to operate as the Panthers' No. 2 running back in the Week 4 matchup against the Lions. While backing up Chuba Hubbard in the Week 3 loss to the Browns, Dillon accumulated 14 yards on five total touches. He will likely struggle gaining fantasy relevance without finding the end zone, as Hubbard has a firm grasp on the Panthers' backfield. However, Dillon is in for a relatively favorable matchup against a Detroit defense allowing 4.5 yards per carry to opposing RBs through three weeks.
outlooksByWeek.6: AJ Dillon is expected to remain the Panthers' top backup running back in the Week 6 matchup against the Eagles. While operating as Carolina's No. 2 RB in Weeks 3 and 4, Dillon accumulated 21 yards on 11 touches. He likely won't be fantasy relevant without finding the end zone. Additionally, it could be very difficult against a strong Eagles defense that's allowed just three touchdowns to running backs all season.
outlooksByWeek.7: AJ Dillon (ankle) is expected to operate as Carolina's No. 2 running back if active for the Week 7 matchup against the Buccaneers. Dillon was sidelined in Week 6 due to an ankle injury but had been operating as the Panthers' top back up after Jonathon Brooks went down with a groin injury in Week 2. In Dillon's last two games, he's tallied 21 yards on 11 touches, playing behind Chuba Hubbard. If active for Week 7, Dillon will likely struggle against a Buccaneers defense that's given up just 3.6 yards per carry this season.

outlooksByWeek.3: Darius Slayton could make his Colts debut in Week 3 against the Texans. The veteran WR signed with Indianapolis after Alec Pierce aggravated a heel injury. Slayton is likely to fill Pierce's role as a field stretcher in one of the league's least impressive WR rooms. The 29-year-old wideout has a career average of 15.0 yards per catch and has exceeded 500 receiving yards in six of seven previous NFL seasons. Slayton could eventually produce the occasional big play, but he's best avoided in Week 3 since he still needs to learn the playbook and is facing a stout Texans secondary.
outlooksByWeek.4: Darius Slayton has a chance to make his Colts debut in Week 4 against the Commanders in London. The former Giants WR was inactive in Week 3 after signing with Indianapolis in the wake of Alec Pierce's heel injury, which landed Pierce on IR. Slayton brings similar field-stretching capabilities to Pierce, as Slayton has a career average of 15.0 yards per catch and has topped 500 receiving yards in six of seven previous NFL seasons. If Slayton gets the green light, he would be a viable deep-league flier given his big-play potential against a Commanders defense that has allowed the third-most yards to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Tonges enters his fourth NFL season with no standalone value, but as a potential fringe TE1 should George Kittle miss any time. Kittle missed seven full games last season, including the playoffs (Weeks 2-6, 17, 20). During those games, Tonges handled a 17.9% target share (6.6 per game) and posted a 34-328-3 receiving line. That works out to 11.8 fantasy PPG, which would've ranked eighth among all tight ends last season, ahead of the likes of Harold Fannin Jr., Travis Kelce, Tyler Warren and Jake Ferguson. Kittle (Achilles) is expected to be ready for Week 1, but if he's ruled out, Tonges will be a viable replacement.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kevin Coleman isn't a factor in the Dolphins' limited passing game ahead of a Week 2 matchup against the 49ers. He collected just two targets in the team's opener, failing to record a catch. While Miami will be forced to throw from behind often in Week 2 and beyond, it doesn't appear as though Coleman will garner enough looks to be a fantasy consideration.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kevin Coleman remains without a catch through two games as the Dolphins get set to host the Chiefs. Coleman logged a higher snap share than Chris Bell, and both roles could be elevated if Caleb Douglas (ankle) is unable to play. Miami has completed only 29 passes through two weeks, and the passing game seems unlikely to sustain even a second receiver in a matchup against a Kansas City secondary that's allowing a mere 6.2 yards per target.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kevin Coleman has a minimal role in Miami's lackluster passing game heading into a Week 4 matchup with the Dolphins. Coleman had a three-yard catch on four targets in Week 3 after being elevated to No. 3 on the WR depth chart due to Caleb Douglas' absence. This offense can't sustain a second receiver, let alone more, keeping Coleman far off fantasy radars ahead of a matchup with a Vikings secondary that's allowing a hearty 8.2 yards per target.
outlooksByWeek.5: Kevin Coleman continues to play a minimal role in the Dolphins' passing game ahead of a Week 5 matchup with the Bengals. He has drawn four targets in each of the last two games but has turned them into just two catches and six yards. Miami's passing is barely functioning at a high enough level to sustain one receiver, let alone multiple, topping 200 yards only once through four games. Coleman could further lose reps to Caleb Douglas (ankle), should he return from a two-game absence.
outlooksByWeek.7: Kevin Coleman has a modest role in the Dolphins' limited passing attack ahead of a Week 7 matchup with the Jets. Prior to last week's bye, Coleman saw a spike with seven targets but converted them into only three catches for 30 yards, both season highs, while also scoring his first touchdown of the season. He could slide further down the depth chart if Caleb Douglas is deemed healthy for the first time since Week 2, and Miami's passing game is struggling to provide even one meaningful receiver, let alone multiple. That doesn't figure to change against a defense that's allowing just 202 passing yards per game.
outlooksByWeek.8: Kevin Coleman was not a factor for the Dolphins with Caleb Douglas returning in Week 7, and in a low-volume passing scheme, he's not likely to produce against the Patriots in Week 8. Coleman collected 15 targets in three games without Douglas but garnered only one look in Week 7, failing to secure a catch. Miami should be forced to throw as the game progresses, but the likelihood of those looks going toward Coleman, or him capitalizing on them, appears slim.
outlooksByWeek.9: Kevin Coleman remains a factor in the Dolphins' passing game despite declining playing time ahead of a Week 9 matchup with the Lions. Coleman caught three passes for the second time in three weeks, scoring his first touchdown in Week 8. Since the team's Week 6 bye, Coleman has played just 26 total offensive snaps, however, after logging 27 snaps or more in three of the team's first five games. With Miami rarely throwing, Coleman belongs on the waiver wire.

player.seasonOutlook: Coleman Jr. was selected by the Dolphins in the fifth round of April's draft. Coleman is a small, slot receiver and punt returner who aligned inside on 83% of his 943 collegiate pass routes. Despite playing at three different FBS schools over the last three seasons, Coleman handled a solid 21% target share during the span and played well, catching 72% of his targets and dropping only four of 229 targets (1.7%). He posted a weak, 88 speed score at the combine, running a 4.49 40-yard dash at 179 pounds. Coleman will battle fellow rookies Chris Bell and Caleb Douglas, as well as a host of veterans for a role in a Miami offense likely to struggle to score points. He should only be drafted in dynasty.

Flacco re-signed with the Bengals and will back up Joe Burrow this season. The veteran quarterback made six starts for Cincinnati last season and showed well, totaling 14 touchdowns and four interceptions while averaging 19.9 fantasy PPG. The 41-year-old can still sling it, but he's a nonfactor with his legs and hasn't finished a season better than 20th in fantasy points since 2014. If Burrow is sidelined, Flacco will do enough through the air to land in the QB2 discussion, but that's his ceiling.

Jones returns for his second go as Brock Purdy's backup in San Francisco after showing well in relief duties in eight starts last season. In those eight appearances, Jones completed 70% of his passes and threw 13 touchdowns to six interceptions. The 2021 first-round pick was a nonfactor with his legs (28-64-0), however, which limited him to an underwhelming 16.3 fantasy PPG. Should Purdy miss time in 2026, Jones will be no more than a fringe QB2. The 28-year-old shouldn't be considered on draft day.

outlooksByWeek.4: Josh Cameron has two touchdown catches in his first three games for the Jaguars, but the rookie sixth-round pick has drawn only three targets heading into a Week 4 road game against the Bengals. His nose for the end zone could pique the interest of managers in dynasty or keeper leagues, but Cameron isn't a viable fantasy option as long as WRs Parker Washington, Jakobi Meyers, and Brian Thomas are healthy. Cameron has also been contributing on special teams, both as a kick returner and in kick coverage.
outlooksByWeek.5: Josh Cameron has made some splashy plays for the Jaguars, scoring two TDs in his first four games while catching five of six targets for 74 yards. Dynasty managers should take notice of the rookie sixth-round pick's promising start, but Cameron doesn't get enough volume in a Jaguars WR room that also includes Parker Washington, Jakobi Meyers, and Brian Thomas to warrant much attention in redraft leagues heading into the Jaguars' Week 5 matchup with the Eagles in London. The Eagles are allowing 162 yards per game to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Josh Cameron has topped 40 yards in each of Jacksonville's last two games and earned a career-high six targets in the Week 5 win over the Eagles as his role continues to grow. The rookie sixth-round pick drew just six targets over his first four games combined, so his floor remains too low to trust with a starting spot despite a favorable Week 6 matchup against a Texans secondary that has been among the worst in the league. However, Cameron's recent trends have been encouraging, so he's a player to monitor in dynasty formats and even deeper redraft leagues.
outlooksByWeek.8: Josh Cameron earned a season-high 50% snap share for the Jaguars in Week 6 against the Texans, though the rookie sixth-round pick finished that game without a target. Cameron's floor remains low due to his inconsistent usage in Jacksonville's deep WR room, but he has shown flashes of potential with either a TD or at least 42 receiving yards in four of his first six NFL appearances. Coming out of Jacksonville's Week 7 bye, Cameron is a viable forward-looking stash candidate but would be a risky lineup activation in Week 8 against the Colts, since Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers are still clearly ahead of him on the depth chart, and Brian Thomas and Travis Hunter both bring first-round pedigrees.

player.seasonOutlook: Cameron was selected by the Jaguars in the sixth round of April's draft. Cameron is a big, strong, perimeter receiver who aligned out wide on 84% of his collegiate routes across five seasons at Baylor. Cameron's overall efficiency is underwhelming (1.58 YPRR), but he was certainly busy the last two seasons, totaling 52-754-10 and 69-872-9 receiving lines. He'll begin his career no higher than fifth on the Jacksonville depth chart behind Brian Thomas Jr., Jakobi Meyers, Parker Washington and Travis Hunter.

Johnson was a solid find by the Giants in the fourth round of the 2024 draft, but he's headed for a reduced role this season following New York's signing of Isaiah Likely and Malik Nabers' return to health. The change comes after Johnson ranked top 12 among tight ends in both snaps and routes, but 23rd in catches and 19th in yards last season. Johnson was busy near the goal line (seven end zone targets), but struggled with drops (tight end-high nine), which led to a poor 63% catch rate. Johnson finished 23rd in fantasy PPG and now may be lucky to see a target or two per game. He's well off the fantasy radar.

Arroyo is eyeing a Year 2 breakout after an underwhelming rookie campaign in which he played a clear second fiddle to A.J. Barner. The 2025 second-round pick was limited to 39% of the offensive snaps during the 13 games he was active. He cleared three targets in a game only once (five in Week 7) and his lone touchdown came on one of just two targets in Week 9. Arroyo was effective as a vertical target at the collegiate level, so he remains an intriguing dynasty hold, but the 23-year-old has a tough path to short-term fantasy relevance while stuck behind Barner in Seattle's low-pass-volume offense.

outlooksByWeek.2: Barion Brown will likely have minimal offensive impact in the Saints' Week 2 matchup against the Ravens. Brown played just seven offensive snaps in his NFL debut, suggesting he's clearly behind fellow rookie Bryce Lance (62 snaps) in the Saints' receiving corps. With Tyler Shough attempting 56 passes in the Week 1 loss, it's tough to imagine a better scenario for Brown to make an impact as well. It'll be a tough Week 2 matchup against a Ravens defense that's given up just 25.0 PPR fantasy points to wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.3: Barion Brown is expected to play a depth role in the Saints' receiving corps in the Week 3 matchup against the Raiders. Brown has logged just nine offensive snaps through New Orleans' first two games, suggesting he's not a part of head coach Kellen Moore's offensive game plan. It appears as if the rookie's primary role is in the return game, as he's accumulated 34 punt-return yards and 128 kick-return yards already. Additionally, Brown is in for a difficult Week 3 matchup against a Raiders defense that's allowed just 6.8 yards per pass attempt thus far.
outlooksByWeek.4: Barion Brown (hamstring) is expected to play a depth role in the Saints' receiving corps if active for the Week 4 matchup against the Falcons. Brown was sidelined for the Week 3 loss but played a minimal offensive role prior to his absence, rushing once for three yards on nine offensive snaps. He's firmly behind Chris Olave, Devaughn Vele and Bryce Lance in New Orleans' WR room but will likely contribute on special teams when healthy. Despite this, Brown is in for a very favorable Week 4 matchup against a Falcons secondary that's given up 38.5 PPR fantasy points per game to wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Barion Brown is expected to remain largely uninvolved in the Saints' offensive game plan in the Week 6 matchup against the Giants. Brown has played just five offensive snaps over his last three games, suggesting he's assumed more of a special-teams role early in the season. The rookie wideout is expected to remain irrelevant for fantasy purposes unless finding the end zone in the near future. Additionally, he's in for a tougher matchup against a Giants defense that's given up 7.6 yards per target to opposing wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Barion Brown is expected to remain a depth option in the Saints' receiving corps in the Week 7 matchup against the Steelers. Brown played a season-high 25% of the Saints' offensive snaps in the Week 6 win over the Giants, catching his lone target for five yards. Despite this, he remains firmly behind Chris Olave, Devaughn Vele and Bryce Lance in the WR room and likely won't be fantasy relevant without scoring a touchdown. Additionally, Brown is in for a tough Week 7 matchup against a Steelers defense that's given up just 6.9 yards per target to opposing wideouts this year.
outlooksByWeek.9: Barion Brown is expected to play a reserve role in the Saints' receiving corps during the Week 9 matchup against the Browns. Brown caught a career-high three passes for 57 yards in the Week 7 loss to the Steelers, which could suggest his role is growing in New Orleans' offense. However, Brown remains firmly behind both Chirs Olave and Devaughn Vele in the team's WR room, so he'll likely remain irrelevant for fantasy purposes without scoring a touchdown. He could find the end zone in Week 9, however, as the Cleveland's defense has allowed seven touchdowns to opposing WRs this year.

player.seasonOutlook: Brown was selected by the Saints in the sixth round of April's draft. Brown is a thin, vertical receiver who handled a healthy 21% target share across 50 collegiate games at Kentucky and LSU. Brown struggled a bit with drops and efficiency, but made some noise as a rusher (32-228-2 across four seasons) and figures to make his biggest impact as a kick returner (65 kick returns for 1,910 yards and six TDs are all easily tops in this rookie class). With Chris Olave, Devaughn Vele and Jordyn Tyson (once healthy) cemented atop the depth chart, Brown is well off the fantasy radar.

outlooksByWeek.2: Riley Patterson's floor remains low in a limited Dolphins offense entering Week 2 against the 49ers. While he had three field goal opportunities to open the year (making two), he converted only one extra point. Field goals likely aren't going to cut it with the Dolphins defense allowing points early and often, keeping Patterson off fantasy rosters.
outlooksByWeek.3: Riley Patterson's floor remains capped by the Dolphins' limited offense entering Week 3 against the Chiefs. While Patterson has notched three field goal attempts in two straight weeks, he's attempted just one extra point in each outing. Kansas City is allowing 8.0 points to opposing kickers through two games, and that seems to be Patterson's ceiling.
outlooksByWeek.4: Riley Patterson brings limited potential in the Dolphins' low-scoring offense into a Week 4 matchup with the Vikings. Patterson has just three extra points in as many games this year while connecting on 5-of-7 field goal attempts. Minnesota's defense has allowed only three touchdowns with eight field goal attempts, and Patterson will have the benefit of kicking indoors, but it's difficult to envision a scenario where Patterson is busy in Week 4.
outlooksByWeek.5: Riley Patterson's chances have been sparse in the Dolphins' low-scoring offense as they enter a Week 5 matchup with the Bengals. Patterson has been limited to one field goal try in each of the last two games and hasn't had multiple PATs in any of Miami's first four games. Cincinnati has allowed 11 field goal tries and seven PATs through four weeks, allowing the sixth-most fantasy points to the position, but Patterson will likely again be hampered by the Dolphins' ineffective offense.
outlooksByWeek.7: Riley Patterson has struggled for meaningful reps given the Dolphins' limited offense entering Week 7 against the Jets. Patterson hasn't made multiple field goals since Week 2 and has just one game with multiple PATs, creating a low floor and an even lower ceiling, especially when paired with a lack of tries from 40-49 yards (three all season). The Jets have been middling against the position through six games, allowing 13 field goal attempts and 11 PATs, but with no signs Miami's offense will take a step forward after their bye week, Patterson will likely again fail to get enough opportunities to score.

player.seasonOutlook: Allar was selected by the Steelers in the third round of April's draft. Allar is one of the biggest quarterbacks in this rookie class and, while he has the arm to go with his frame, accuracy is a big concern. Allar was conservative during his time at Penn State (7.6 aDOT), but he still completed only 63% of his passes and averaged 7.4 yards per attempt. In 2025, he had the worst QBR in this rookie class prior to suffering a season-ending broken ankle. On the plus side, he could add value with his legs, as he posted a career 181-1,030-12 rushing line and his 8.3% scramble rate is second highest in this class. Allar will begin his career learning the ropes behind Aaron Rodgers and perhaps Mason Rudolph.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jordan Whittington will look to improve upon a quiet season opener when the Rams face the Giants in Week 2. Whittington had just one catch for eight yards in Week 1 versus San Francisco. Still, he was the only Rams WR outside of stars Puka Nacua and Davante Adams to log a reception. Nacua and Adams stand to command most of QB Matthew Stafford's attention, so Whittington figures to compete for scraps with Los Angeles' tight ends and other depth wideouts each week. The Giants held Dallas' passing game in check in Week 1, as QB Dak Prescott tallied just 175 yards through the air, though he did toss two TDs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jordan Whittington (quadriceps) sat out the Rams' Week 2 win over the Giants and isn't certain to return for a Week 3 matchup against Denver. It was a missed opportunity Monday for Whittington, as top wideout Puka Nacua (hip) was also sidelined, opening the door for other WRs to take on a bigger role. Whittington was quiet in Week 1 against San Francisco with just one catch on one target for eight yards, and when both Nacua and Davante Adams are healthy, he figures to be competing with a variety of other pass catchers for targets. Should Whittington return in Week 3, he'll draw a tough Broncos secondary that has allowed a 51.6 percent catch rate to wideouts -- second best in the league -- so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jordan Whittington will try to make more of an impact in the Rams' Week 5 battle against Buffalo. Whittington caught one of two targets for four yards in Week 4 against Philadelphia and has just two catches for 12 yards over three games this year. It may be hard for any wideout not named Puka Nacua or Davante Adams to log much production for Los Angeles when those star receivers are healthy given the amount of attention they draw from QB Matthew Stafford. However, there could be room for multiple Rams pass catchers to find success against a Buffalo defense that allowed four different Patriots players to log over 40 receiving yards in Week 4.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jordan Whittington continues to be a non-factor for the Rams heading into a Week 6 matchup against Arizona. Whittington didn't log a target this past Monday against Buffalo, marking the second time through four games that he's finished without a single ball thrown his way. There doesn't appear to be many targets for Los Angeles wideouts behind stars Puka Nacua and Davante Adams, and it doesn't help Whittington's outlook that QB Matthew Stafford has also frequently looked for his tight ends. With that said, Whittington isn't a desirable fantasy play in Week 6 despite the fact that the Cardinals have struggled to contain wideouts this season and have yielded the league's second-worst yards per target (10.17) to the position.
outlooksByWeek.7: Jordan Whittington is one of several players who should be in line for more targets and touches in the Rams' passing attack after it was confirmed that Davante Adams will miss six to 10 weeks with a hamstring injury. However, Whittington has recorded only two receptions for 12 yards through five games, making his projected increase in opportunities more speculative than established. The Raiders have been a below-average defense against pass-catchers in 2026 and have allowed the 10th-most fantasy points per game to WRs. However, it remains to be seen whether Whittington will handle the volume or even the opportunity to take advantage of that situation.
outlooksByWeek.8: Jordan Whittington has yet to make an impact this season heading into the Rams' Week 8 tilt against the Chargers. Some expected Whittington to take on a larger role in Week 7 with Davante Adams (hamstring) sidelined, but instead the wideout logged just 13 offensive snaps and didn't draw a target. In fact, aside from star wideout Puka Nacua, the Rams' WR corps combined for just one catch on two targets, as QB Matthew Stafford instead targeted his tight ends 14 times. Although Adams is expected to miss Week 8 and the Chargers are in the midst of a poor season, Whittington may simply not get enough playing time to be worth a roster spot in fantasy leagues.

outlooksByWeek.3: Tyler Badie was inactive for the Broncos' opener but worked into the backfield mix during Week 2's win over the Jaguars thanks to RJ Harvey's hamstring strain. Working as the No. 3 running back behind J.K. Dobbins and rookie Jonah Coleman, Badie gained just one yard on his only carry but caught two of three targets for 28 yards. Dobbins also picked up a hamstring injury in the win, and while the issue isn't expected to keep him sidelined, the veteran RB's history of injuries makes any appearance on the injury report a cause for some concern. If Badie does see a bigger role in Week 3, he'll be facing a Rams defense that just saw the return of Aaron Donald in Week 2 and has yet to allow a rushing TD this year.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tyler Badie worked as the No. 3 running back for the Broncos in a Week 3 win over the Rams, but he managed only two touches for 14 scrimmage yards. With rookie Jonah Coleman on IR, Badie doesn't have much competition for his spot, but he also doesn't pose much of a challenge to J.K. Dobbins as the primary early-down back or RJ Harvey as the main passing-down option. Badie will try to take advantage of his limited opportunities in Week 4 against a 49ers defense that ranks 22nd in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Tyler Badie notched a season-high four touches in the Broncos' Week 4 loss to the 49ers, taking two carries for seven yards and catching both his targets for 32 yards. The 2022 sixth-round pick remains No. 3 on the backfield depth chart behind J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey, but with Dobbins struggling in his early-down role, more work could begin filtering down to Badie. He could contribute on limited volume in Week 5 against a Chargers defense that ranks 22nd in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

Hunter Luepke continues to provide stellar blocking in the run game for the Cowboys. Luepke has not had a carry in either of the last two outings. He has just two rushes for eight yards on the season. In Week 5, Dallas will face a Tampa Bay defense that has been stellar against the run in 2026. The Bucs are allowing just 78.5 rushing yards per tilt, which is third in the NFL. In addition, Tampa Bay has yielded just one rushing touchdown through four games.
outlooksByWeek.6: Hunter Luepke received one carry for five yards out of the backfield last game for the Cowboys. Meanwhile, starter Javonte Williams had 14 touches and a touchdown and continues to be the workhorse for the offense on the ground. If Luepke somehow sees more touches in Week 6, he could find some room, though, as Green Bay's defense has been extremely suspect in defending the run. The Packers are allowing 127.6 rushing yards per contest, which is tied for 25th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.9: Hunter Luepke remains the blocking fullback for Dallas.  In Week 9, Dallas will face a Colts defense that has been subpar against the run. Indy is allowing 131.8 rushing yards per tote, which is 27th in the NFL.

outlooksByWeek.8: Davis Allen enters the Rams' Week 8 clash against the Chargers fresh off reeling in his first two touchdowns of the season. Those scores came in Week 7 against the Raiders, when Allen also logged season highs with four catches and five targets. Quarterback Matthew Stafford looked to his tight ends often with Davante Adams (hamstring) sidelined, and that could continue to be a trend over the next few weeks while Adams is on the shelf. However, Allen figures to complete for TE targets with Colby Parkinson and Tyler Higbee, and the Chargers have surrendered only one touchdown to tight ends so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.9: Davis Allen's role in Week 9 against Washington could partially depend on the health of another Rams tight end. With Colby Parkinson (ribs) inactive Week 8 against the Chargers, Allen logged a season-high 74% offensive snap share. However, Allen managed a modest two receptions for eight yards on two targets in the contest, and he remains largely touchdown-dependent for meaningful production. That could be relevant against the Commanders, who have given up eight touchdowns to tight ends this season, tied for second-most in the NFL.

outlooksByWeek.2: Bryce Lance is expected to play as the Saints' No. 3 wideout in the Week 2 matchup against the Ravens. Lance had a promising NFL debut, catching three of four targets for 42 yards. He was on the field for 62 of New Orleans' 90 offensive snaps, appearing to be the clear WR3 behind Chris Olave and Devaughn Vele, and Tyler Shough looked Lance's way on a failed two-point conversion attempt in OT that would have won the game. While Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) remains sidelined, Lance should continue to be a valuable part of this Saints offense, especially with Shough attempting 56 passes in Week 1. Lance is in for a tough matchup this week, however, with Baltimore's defense allowing just 7.8 yards per completion last week.
outlooksByWeek.3: Bryce Lance is expected to remain the Saints' No. 3 wideout in the Week 3 matchup against the Raiders. Despite playing 78 percent of New Orleans' offensive snaps in the Week 2 win over the Ravens, Lance drew just one target. He remains far behind Chris Olave and Devaugh Vele in the team's receiving corps, with his role likely diminishing further once Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) returns from IR. However, Lance, who ran a 4.34 40-yard dash, could find success against a Raiders secondary that's allowed 12.3 yards per completion this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Bryce Lance is expected to remain a depth option in the Saints' receiving corps in the Week 4 matchup against the Falcons. The rookie from North Dakota State has operated as New Orleans' WR3 this season while Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) has been sidelined. Despite this, Lance has struggled to produce, catching just four of eight targets for 50 yards. He's expected to remain a depth piece behind Chris Olave and Devaughn Vele and will likely struggle finding fantasy value without a TD. However, Lance is in for a favorable Week 4 matchup against a Falcons defense that's given up 10.5 yards per completion this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Bryce Lance is expected to remain the Saints' No. 3 wideout in the Week 5 matchup against the Vikings. Despite logging a career-high five targets in the Week 4 loss to the Falcons, Lance caught just one pass for seven yards. It appears as if his role in the Saints' offense is growing, as he played a career-best 86% of the team's offensive snaps as well. Even so, Lance will likely struggle against a tough Vikings secondary that's allowed just 43 total receptions to wide receivers through four contests this year.
outlooksByWeek.6: Bryce Lance is expected to remain the Saints' No. 3 wideout in the Week 6 matchup against the Giants. Despite receiving eight targets over his last two games, Lance has recorded just one catch for seven yards. He remains firmly behind Chris Olave and Devaughn Vele in the Saints' WR room and will likely struggle finding fantasy relevance without a touchdown. He could struggle against a solid Giants defense that's given up just 6.2 yards per reception this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: Bryce Lance is expected to remain a depth option in the Saints' receiver corps during the Week 7 matchup against the Steelers. Lance has been more involved in the Saints' offense over the last three weeks, catching three of 12 targets for 16 yards and a touchdown. He appears to have emerged as New Orleans' No. 3 wideout, at least until Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) returns from IR. Despite this, Lance will likely struggle against a strong Steelers secondary that's allowed just 9.9 yards per completion this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Lance was selected by the Saints in the fourth round of April's draft. Trey's little brother is the lone wide receiver in this rookie class who didn't play a single snap at the FBS level. However, he was productive as a perimeter receiver at North Dakota State, posting receiving lines of 75-1,053-17 and 51-1,079-8 over the last two seasons. He's a year or so older than most of his classmates, but he dominated at the combine with terrific showings in the 40-yard dash (4.34), vertical (41.5) and broad jump (133). He has the size and skillset to handle New Orleans' No. 3 gig behind Chris Olave and Devaughn Vele until first-round rookie Jordyn Tyson returns from injury. Lance's primary value is in dynasty leagues.

outlooksByWeek.6: Charlie Jones is technically listed as the fourth wideout for the Giants, but he has been mostly a return specialist since Braxton Berrios went down due to injury. Jones has yet to catch a ball on the season and will remain organizational depth on offense. In Week 6, the Giants host the Saints. New Orleans has been fairly stingy against the pass in 2026, allowing just 212.2 passing yards per tilt, which is 11th in the league. However, New Orleans has also given up eight passing scores already, which is tied for 20th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.7: Charlie Jones had a costly fumble for the Giants last game, though he did also post the best numbers of his career in terms of receiving. Jones snagged two passes for 66 yards in the 34-27 loss to the Saints. However, Jones fumbled a punt late in the first half which led to a New Orleans touchdown, completely shifting the momentum of the contest. Nevertheless, with Darnell Mooney managing a balky neck, Jones saw increased action on offense, a trend which could continue in Week 7 versus the Texans. Houston has also been suspect against the pass in 2026, allowing 246 passing yards per game, which is 27th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.9: Charlie Jones did not catch a pass last game for the Giants. In fact, Jones has just two catches for 66 yards on the entire season as the current No. 4 wideout on the depth chart. Malik Nabers and rookie Malachi Fields have drawn the majority of targets at wide receiver, with Darnell Mooney as a distant third. In Week 9, Jones will face a struggling Eagles pass defense. Philadelphia is allowing 235.4 passing yards per tilt, which is 24th in the NFL.

outlooksByWeek.7: Jawhar Jordan would be on the radar in deeper fantasy formats for Week 7 against the Giants if fellow Texans RB David Montgomery (groin) missed a second consecutive game. Jordan excelled in a change-of-pace role behind Woody Marks in the Week 6 win over Jacksonville, turning six carries and one target into 50 scrimmage yards, with half of that yardage coming on a 25-yard touchdown run in the third quarter. If Montgomery returns, Jordan would be hard-pressed to earn much playing time as the third-string RB option.

outlooksByWeek.3: Erick All Jr. and the Bengals travel to face the division-rival Steelers in Week 3. After not recording a target in the season opener, All tallied two catches on three targets for five yards in the Week 2 win over Houston. He was on the field for 24 offensive snaps compared to 21 for starter Mike Gesicki, but that trend will have to consistently continue for him to even be considered in fantasy formats. With Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins accounting for 19 of Joe Burrow's 31 Week 2 pass attempts, it's going to be hard to trust anyone outside of those two in the passing game, especially against Pittsburgh's second-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (5.5) to TEs.

outlooksByWeek.7: Will Mallory was targeted six times in the Colts' Week 6 loss to the Titans. He was the team's top pass-catching TE in the absence of Tyler Warren (groin), though Mallory corralled only two of those six looks from Daniel Jones for 20 yards. Mallory would be a viable deep-league dart throw in Week 7 against the Vikings if Warren remains sidelined, but Warren's return would push Mallory out of fantasy consideration in pretty much all formats.
outlooksByWeek.8: Will Mallory has drawn nine targets over the Colts' past two games while Tyler Warren has been shelved by a groin injury. Mallory caught just two for 20 yards. What little fantasy appeal Mallory carries would dissipate completely if Warren is cleared to return. Should Warren sit out a third consecutive game in Week 8, Mallory would be a viable deep-league dart throw as Indianapolis' top pass-catching TE against a Jaguars defense that has allowed four TDs in six games to the position.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jonnu Smith will look to stay involved in Green Bay's passing game at New York in Week 2. Smith was a solid option for Jordan Love in Week 1, converting two of his three targets for 50 yards. While the veteran remains an option behind Tucker Kraft, he should at least continue to be on the field and run routes. Smith will face a Jets defense that limited Titans tight ends to five catches for 35 yards in its opener.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jonnu Smith will seek to stay involved as the Packers travel to Tampa Bay in Week 4. Smith was a solid outlet for Jordan Love in Week 3 against the Falcons, hauling in two of three passes for 16 yards. The veteran tight end has only registered catches in games where Green Bay has thrown 40 or more times, but these games seem more likely than not in the coming weeks, especially given the struggles of the run game. He'll face a Bucs defense that's allowed a bottom-10 183 receiving yards to TEs this year.
outlooksByWeek.5: Jonnu Smith will aim to stay involved as the Packers take on the Bears in Week 5. Smith saw action again in Week 4 versus the Buccaneers, hauling in his sole target for 19 yards. The veteran tight end has now totaled 5 catches for 85 yards this season, logging at least one catch in three of four games. He'll face a Chicago defense that's ranked top five against fantasy TEs on the year.
outlooksByWeek.6: Jonnu Smith will seek to get more involved as the Packers play the Cowboys in Week 6. Smith was on the field for 36 percent of offensive snaps in Week 5 versus Chicago, but he was unable to register a target. The veteran tight end has now brought in five of seven targets for 85 yards so far this season. He'll face a Dallas defense that's ranked in the middle against fantasy TEs this year.

player.seasonOutlook: Sarratt was selected by the Ravens in the fourth round of April's draft. Surratt is a big, perimeter receiver who hauled in 31 touchdown receptions (most in this rookie WR class) in 40 collegiate games, which includes a FBS-high 15 in 2025. His efficiency was terrific across the board, including 10.7 yards per target, 2.69 YPRR and a 72% catch rate. Surratt is an intriguing prospect, but he may not see the field a ton as a rookie with Zay Flowers, Rashod Bateman and fellow rookie Ja'Kobi Lane also in the mix in Baltimore's low-volume pass attack. He's best as a dynasty stash.

Benson's pro career is off to a slow start due primarily to a variety of injuries. The 2024 third-round pick was essentially splitting the Arizona backfield with James Conner last season, but he was never able to return to the field after suffering a knee injury in Week 4. He was effective prior to the injury, averaging 5.5 yards per carry, and was busy as a receiver (four-plus targets in three straight games). The 24-year-old will open the 2026 season on injured reserve and, even when healthy, he's no longer assured of a role with a new coaching staff and after the team added Jeremiyah Love and Tyler Allgeier. Benson's best days are likely ahead of him, but his only shot at 2026 fantasy relevance is a new home or several injuries above him on the Arizona depth chart.

Sanders is back as a pass-catching tight end in Carolina, though he's unlikely to see a larger share of the target pie with veteran Darren Waller now in the mix. Sanders - a 2024 fourth-round pick - flashed as a rookie with a 33-342-1 receiving line while playing 55% of Carolina's offensive snaps and handling 9.1% of the targets across 16 games. He simply didn't progress in Year 2, posting a 29-190-1 line while playing 52% of the snaps and handling a 10% target share in 12 healthy games. Sanders has been an inefficient short-range target with little goal line activity thus far (four career end zone targets), placing the 23-year-old well off the fantasy radar.

outlooksByWeek.5: Sam Roush will look to keep his catch streak alive as the Bears play the Packers in Week 5. Roush stayed relevant in Chicago's passing game against the Jets in Week 4, taking his sole target for eight yards. The rookie tight end has now recorded a catch in three straight games, posting a 3-33-0 receiving line on the year. He'll face a Packers defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack against TEs so far.
outlooksByWeek.8: Sam Roush could be in line for an increased role as the Bears play the Seahawks in Week 8. With veteran Cole Kmet suffering a season-ending knee injury, Roush is currently Chicago's only healthy tight end behind Colston Loveland. Roush has recorded three catches for 33 yards through the first seven games of the season, but he could see his opportunities expand. He'll face a Seattle squad that's ranked fourth in fantasy points allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Sam Roush will aim to stay involved as the Bears play the Buccaneers in Week 9. Roush was utilized heavily in Chicago's run packages in a Week 8 win over the Seahawks, but he was unable to record a catch for the third straight matchup. The now TE2 should remain a solid contributor to the offense at some capacity in the weeks to come, but it's unknown whether that will include a receiving role. Tampa Bay has ranked 22nd in fantasy points allowed to tight ends this campaign.

player.seasonOutlook: Roush was selected by the Bears in the third round of April's draft. Roush is a huge, in-line blocking tight end. Though he did catch 40-plus passes each of his final two seasons at Stanford (including a healthy 22% target share in 2025), his overall receiving efficiency was underwhelming (6.6 YPT, 1.22 YPRR) and he totaled four TDs on 182 career targets. He's unlikely to see enough target volume in the pros to find his way to the fantasy radar and that's especially the case in Chicago, as he's buried behind Colston Loveland and Cole Kmet.

outlooksByWeek.8: Zane Gonzalez is poised for his second game as the Dolphins' kicker in Week 8 against the Patriots. He was added to the roster to replace Riley Patterson during the team's Week 6 bye and converted all four PATs in Week 7, though he did not attempt a field goal. Facing a better defense than the Jets' unit in his debut, and in a game where field goals likely won't keep the Dolphins competitive, Gonzalez lacks Week 8 fantasy appeal.
outlooksByWeek.9: Zane Gonzalez is expected to be the Dolphins' kicker in Week 9 against the Lions. Gonzalez didn't attempt a field goal in his Week 7 team debut but converted two of three in Week 8, including one from 50-plus yards. Miami's offense remains one of the lowest-scoring teams, and he'll face a Detroit defense that's allowing the fewest fantasy points to kickers, including just five made field goals in seven games, suggesting limited volume for Gonzalez.

outlooksByWeek.6: John Metchie is expected to play a depth role in Carolina's wide receiver room during the Week 6 matchup against the Eagles. Metchie had his best game as a Panther in the Week 4 win over the Lions, catching three of five targets for 37 yards. However, he played just 37% of Carolina's offensive snaps and will likely have a smaller role in Week 6, with Jalen Coker's (quadriceps) return imminent. Despite this, Metchie is in for a good matchup against an Eagles defense that's allowed 10.8 yards per completion this season.
outlooksByWeek.7: John Metchie is expected to remain a depth option in the Panthers' receiving corps during the Week 7 matchup against the Buccaneers. Metchie was targeted three times during the Week 6 win over the Eagles, recording two receptions for 24 yards. On the season, he's caught seven of 13 targets for 80 yards and a touchdown in four contests. Metchie likely won't be fantasy relevant without finding the end zone, but it's very possible against a Buccaneers secondary that's allowed four touchdowns to WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.8: John Metchie is expected to operate as one of the Panthers' top wideouts in the Week 8 matchup against the Packers. Metchie has established himself as Carolina's No. 3 wide receiver over the last four games, catching nine of 19 targets for 100 yards and a touchdown during that span. Despite this, he still remains firmly behind both Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker (shoulder) in the Panthers' receiving corps, likely carrying little fantasy value for the remainder of the season. He could find success in Week 8, however, against a Packers defense that's already allowed six receiving touchdowns to WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.9: John Metchie is expected to play a depth role in the Panthers' receiving corps in the Week 9 matchup against the Broncos. Metchie has established himself as Carolina's No. 3 receiver while Xavier Legette (knee) remains sidelined, catching 10 of 15 targets for 95 yards over the team's last four games. He's still clearly behind Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker in Carolina's WR room, so he likely won't be relevant for fantasy purposes without a touchdown. Finding the end zone will also be tough against a Broncos defense that's allowed just four touchdowns to WRs across eight games this season.

outlooksByWeek.7: Audric Estime and the Browns travel to face the Titans in Week 7. He rushed nine times for 19 yards, including a two-yard touchdown, during Cleveland's 13-10 victory in Week 6. With Quinshon Judkins (ankle) inactive for the contest, Estime and Jaleel McLaughlin each tallied nine carries to lead the backfield, but it was Estime who found the end zone in his debut for the Browns. However, he was out-snapped 39-19 by McLaughlin, so if Judkins does return versus Tennessee, Estime's role would be heavily reduced.

outlooksByWeek.3: Cody White is coming off the best game of his NFL career in the Raiders' Week 2 win over the Chargers. The journeyman wideout, who followed Klint Kubiak from Seattle to Las Vegas in the offseason, came off the practice squad and caught both his targets for 24 yards and two touchdowns, not bad for a player who had just one TD in his first 31 NFL games. White's main value comes on special teams however, and his path to an increased role in the offense will get even narrower once Brock Bowers is cleared to make his 2026 debut. White will remain a dart throw for fantasy purposes in Week 3 against a Saints secondary that ranks in the middle of the pack in terms of volume allowed to WRs so far, but which has given up three TDs to the position in two games.
outlooksByWeek.4: Cody White continues to surprise for the Raiders, catching his third touchdown in two games in a Week 3 win over the Saints. The former Seahawk, who followed head coach Klint Kubiak from Seattle to Las Vegas and knows the playbook well, has been bouncing between the practice squad and the game-day lineup, but with Jack Bech landing on IR, there's now an open spot for him to get added to the 53-man roster. White seems to have an edge on Malik Benson and Dareke Young for the vacant No. 3 spot on the wide receiver depth chart, and while he won't maintain that scoring pace, he seems to have earned the trust of Kirk Cousins as well. White will face a difficult task in Week 4 against a Kansas City secondary that ranks first in the league in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Cody White wasn't able to extend his touchdown streak in the Raiders' Week 4 loss to Kansas City, catching two of four targets for a season-high 36 yards. The former Seahawk stepped into a larger role with Jack Bech on IR, and White moved up another rung on the depth chart when Jalen Nailor left the game early with a concussion. If Nailor remains sidelined, White could have a hefty workload in Week 5 against a Patriots secondary that ranks 21st in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs and could be without top cornerback Christian Gonzalez.
outlooksByWeek.6: Cody White wasn't able to contribute significantly in the Raiders' Week 5 loss to the Patriots, catching two of four targets for a season-high 44 yards. The veteran depth wideout has already produced career-best numbers in his first year with Las Vegas, as three of his seven receptions have gone for touchdowns, but he has yet to show he can deliver consistent value, even as part of an unsettled Raiders depth chart. White will try to return to the end zone for the first time since Week 3 in a Week 6 matchup against a Bills secondary that ranks last in the league in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs
outlooksByWeek.7: Cody White's modest role in the Raiders' offense could be slipping away. Even in a high-scoring loss to the Bills in Week 6, the former Seahawk and Steeler logged only two targets and failed to catch either. Since scoring three touchdowns in two games in Weeks 2-3, White has a 4-80-0 line on 10 targets over the last three contests. He's unlikely to return to the end zone in Week 7 against a Rams secondary that ranks fourth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Cody White is in danger of falling out of the Raiders' game plan completely in the near future. Since surprisingly catching three TDs passes during the team's season-opening three-game win streak, White has managed just a 5-84-0 line on 13 targets during a four-game losing streak, and his snaps and routes have shrunk the last two weeks. With Dont'e Thornton and Jack Bech both back at practice and closing in on returns from IR, White is running out of time to cement his spot on the 53-man roster. He'll try to make something happen in Week 8 against a Jets secondary that is tied for 15th in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

outlooksByWeek.2: Devontez Walker and the Ravens face the Saints and their 21st-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (37.2) to WRs in Week 2. Walker, who has seven catches for 157 yards and four TDs across two seasons with Baltimore, sat out the Week 1 victory with a groin injury. Keep an eye on his status in practice leading up to their clash with New Orleans, as the Ravens are pretty banged up at receiver. Zay Flowers (hamstring) is considered day-to-day while rookie Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist) is doubtful, meaning Walker could have a chance to make some noise if he suits up in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.3: Devontez Walker and the Ravens travel to take on the Cowboys in Week 3. The third-year receiver hauled in one of two targets for 47 yards in Baltimore's Week 2 loss, good for third on the team in receiving yards. Rashod Bateman (7-88-1) filled in admirably for Zay Flowers, who sat out with a hamstring injury, but there's a high chance of the latter making his return to the field in Week 3. Walker's fantasy upside remains limited in a run-heavy offense, however, despite a potential shootout in Dallas.
outlooksByWeek.4: Devontez Walker and the Ravens host the Titans in Week 4 following their return from Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. He failed to catch his only target during Baltimore's thrilling 34-31 win in Week 3, and he now has a 1-47-0 line on three targets across two outings. Tennessee's defense ranks 18th in fantasy points allowed (32.9) to WRs, but Zay Flowers (hamstring) and Mark Andrews should continue earning the majority of looks from Lamar Jackson. Baltimore features one of the more run-heavy offenses with Jackson and Derrick Henry, ranking third in rush yards per game at 167.3.
outlooksByWeek.5: Devontez Walker and the Ravens are back on the road for the first time since the season opener to face the Falcons in Week 5. He caught one of two targets for 19 yards in Baltimore's Week 4 victory over Tennessee. Walker remains firmly behind Zay Flowers, Derrick Henry, Mark Andrews, and Rashod Bateman in the offensive pecking order. He should remain on waiver wires against a beatable Falcons secondary, allowing 38.4 fantasy points per game (T-27th) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Devontez Walker and the Ravens are on the road for an AFC North showdown versus the Browns. In Baltimore's 30-23 overtime win in Week 5, he caught both of his targets for nine yards, including a 7-yard touchdown that helped tie the game with 40 seconds remaining in the fourth quarter. The Ravens leaned on Derrick Henry, who rushed 24 times for 102 yards and had an 18-yard TD reception, but Tyler Huntley was also efficient with his 32 pass attempts, hitting seven different receivers. Walker should remain on fantasy waiver wires, planted firmly behind Henry, Lamar Jackson (ankle), Zay Flowers, Rashod Bateman, and Mark Andrews on the offensive food chain.
outlooksByWeek.7: Devontez Walker and the Ravens welcome the Bengals to town for an AFC North clash in Week 7. He was unable to catch either of his two targets during Baltimore's 13-10 loss in Week 6. With Rashod Bateman (shoulder) exiting in the first half, it was rookie Ja'Kobi Lane (4-40-0) who stepped up. Walker has compiled a 4-75-1 line on eight targets through five outings, thus leaving him off the fantasy radar against a Cincinnati defense allowing 29.3 points per game to WRs, which ranks ninth.
outlooksByWeek.8: Devontez Walker and the Ravens visit the Bills in Week 8. He failed to record a target in his 20 offensive snaps during Baltimore's blowout loss in Week 7. Walker is behind rookie Ja'Kobi Lane, who recorded a 3-25-0 line on five targets, on the depth chart and doesn't offer any fantasy potential despite a favorable matchup against a porous Buffalo secondary.
outlooksByWeek.9: Devontez Walker and the Ravens return home to take on the 5-2 Jaguars in Week 9. He was not targeted during Baltimore's 36-10 Week 8 loss to the Bills. Walker played 16% of the offensive snaps, his lowest mark on the season, and has failed to record a single target for two consecutive weeks. He should be left on fantasy waiver wires with the Ravens' offense in shambles due to multiple injuries.

outlooksByWeek.4: Elijah Higgins will look to build off a strong performance this past Sunday as Arizona heads to New York to face the Giants in Week 4. After not drawing a target over his first two games this season, Higgins caught all three of his targets for 20 yards in Week 3 against San Francisco. Not surprisingly, however, his production was dwarfed by No. 1 tight end Trey McBride, who has caught at least eight passes in all three of the Cardinals' contests so far this season. Higgins' opportunities will logically be limited by McBride's massive role in the passing game moving forward, but there could be room for some success against the Giants, who have surrendered 18 receptions to tight ends this season, tied for ninth-most in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.5: Elijah Higgins will be fresh off his first touchdown of the season when Arizona faces Detroit in Week 5. Against the Giants this past Sunday, Higgins found paydirt from two yards out for his first TD of 2026. The veteran tight end isn't going to challenge star Trey McBride for snaps or targets, but Higgins has at least carved out a small role on offense with a 5-39-1 receiving line over his past two games. Though he doesn't get enough looks to be a reliable fantasy asset, Higgins does have a prime Week 5 matchup, as the Lions have given up a league-high six receiving touchdowns to tight ends this season.
outlooksByWeek.6: Elijah Higgins is coming off a season-high yardage total as the Cardinals prepare to face the Rams in Week 6. Higgins caught all three of his targets for 57 yards against Detroit this past Sunday to finish as his team's third-leading pass catcher in terms of yardage. He's caught at least two passes in each of his past three contests, so Higgins has built a little momentum despite continuing to compete for scraps behind star TE Trey McBride on the depth chart. However, Higgins could be in for a challenging day against a Rams defense that has allowed a minuscule 41.2% catch rate to tight ends this seasons, by far the best mark in the league.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jahdae Walker will aim to stay involved as the Bears play the Vikings in Week 2. Walker made a mark in Chicago's season-opener win over the Panthers with his limited opportunities, reeling in his one catch for a one-yard touchdown. The second-year wide receiver could continue to see success this season, especially if the Bears continue to score at such a high rate. He'll face a Minnesota defense that allowed two touchdowns to Packers WRs in Week 1.

Bo Melton should remain a secondary option as the Packers take on the Jets in Week 2. Melton was a solid returner in Week 1 against the Vikings, but he also recorded a pivotal 10-yard first-down catch in the matchup. This makes it evident that while small, the fourth-year playmaker's role on offense is not gone. He'll aim to stay involved against a Jets defense that allowed a middle-of-the-pack 30.5 PPR points per game against wide receivers in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Bo Melton will aim to get involved as the Packers play the Falcons in Week 3. Melton was unable to reel in his sole target in Week 2 against the Jets, but he did get an uptick in usage after Jayden Reed went down with an injury. Melton could be in line for more looks, especially if Reed misses a lot of time. He'll face an Atlanta defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 30.3 PPR points per game to WRs so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Bo Melton could continue to see elevated usage as the Packers play the Buccaneers in Week 4. Melton was on the field with Green Bay's offense for a season-high 32 percent of the time in Week 3 against the Falcons, but he failed to bring in his sole target. Still, the fourth-year utility man should continue to be deployed to some degree, especially since there's no return timeline for wide receiver Jayden Reed. Melton will face a Tampa Bay defense that's allowed a top-six 25.4 fantasy points per game to wide receivers in the first three games of the season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Bo Melton will aim to do more as the Packers take on Chicago in Week 5. Melton garnered his fourth target of the season against the Buccaneers in Week 4, but he was unable to reel it in. He's now commanded a target in every game this campaign, but converted just one for 10 yards. The Bears have also ranked top five against fantasy wide receivers this season, which could make it hard for Melton to do much once again.
outlooksByWeek.6: Bo Melton will look to stay busy as the Packers play the Cowboys in Week 6. Melton logged his best performance of the year in a Week 5 blowout over the Bears, bringing in three of four targets for 20 yards. The utility player could also be in line for more opportunities, with Skyy Moore dealing with an ankle injury, but a Savion Williams (ankle) return from IR could balance this out. Melton will face a Dallas defense that's ranked 21st in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers.
outlooksByWeek.7: Bo Melton will look to get more involved in the passing game as the Packers travel to Detroit in Week 7. Melton failed to register a target in a Week 6 win over the Cowboys, which was a disappointment after a three-catch performance the prior week. The utility player has now recorded just four catches for 30 yards this season, and the return of Savion Williams could reduce his role even more. He'll face a Lions defense that's ranked 30th in fantasy points allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Bo Melton remains a depth option as the Packers play the Panthers in Week 8. Melton recorded his fifth catch of the season in a Week 7 loss to the Lions, taking it for just four yards. He's now garnered at least one target in all but one game this season, and the continued absence of Skyy Moore could keep some targets flowing. Melton will face a Carolina defense that's ranked fifth in fantasy points allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Bo Melton will seek to get more involved as the Packers play the Patriots in Week 9. Melton finished Week 8 against the Panthers with another goose egg, and he also registered zero targets. He's now logged a catch in just three of eight games, and it's looking like J. Michael Sturdivant could overtake his receiving role in the coming weeks. New England's defense has ranked 28th in fantasy points allowed to WRs in the last three weeks.

outlooksByWeek.2: Isaiah Bond and the Browns are in Tampa Bay to clash with the Buccaneers in Week 2. Although healthy and active for the season opener after clearing concussion protocol, Bond played just seven offensive snaps and didn't see any time on special teams. Cleveland's offense was not very good in its first appearance, and as long as questions remain at the quarterback position, there's no reason to trust any of their pass-catchers until proven otherwise.
outlooksByWeek.3: Isaiah Bond and the Browns welcome the Panthers to town for a Week 3 tilt. He caught his lone target for 10 yards during Cleveland's shocking victory over Tampa Bay in Week 2. It appears rookie receivers Denzel Boston (5-95-1) and KC Concepcion (6-28-0), along with tight end Harold Fannin Jr. (5-54-0), will be the focal point of the passing game, leaving Bond and Jerry Jeudy as the odd men out. Bond can be left on waiver wires in all formats versus a Panthers defense allowing 30.3 fantasy points (T-15th) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Isaiah Bond and the Browns host their division rival Steelers in Week 4. He was not targeted during Cleveland's 21-18 win in Week 3 after catching his only target for 10 yards in their Week 2 victory. Bond will continue to rotate with Jerry Jeudy behind rookies Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion, who combined for four catches and 50 yards on 13 targets. He should remain on waiver wires versus Pittsburgh's eighth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (28.0) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.5: Isaiah Bond and the Browns battle the Jets on the road in Week 5. He caught his lone target for two yards during Cleveland's surprising 27-24 victory in Week 4. Despite the improved look on offense, Bond remains a very limited fantasy option behind rookies Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion, along with tight end Harold Fannin Jr. Bond should remain on benches against the Jets' ninth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (28.5) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.6: Isaiah Bond and the Browns return home for a meeting with the division-rival Ravens in Week 6. He corralled three of seven targets for 74 yards during Cleveland's 17-12 loss in Week 5. Bond stepped up in the absence of KC Concepcion, who was ruled out with a concussion in the first quarter, as Bond tied for the team lead in receptions and targets while pacing the Browns in yardage. Denzel Boston and Jerry Jeudy each garnered seven looks as well, and if Concepcion is forced to miss the Week 6 matchup versus Baltimore, Bond could see a similar uptick in opportunities against a defense allowing 36.2 fantasy points per game to WRs (23rd).
outlooksByWeek.7: Isaiah Bond and the Browns are on the road to battle the Titans in Week 7. After leading Cleveland in receiving yards in a Week 5 loss, Bond was not targeted in their 13-10 victory in Week 6. He only played 15% of the offensive snaps, and with KC Concepcion (concussion) active, his opportunities and playing time reverted to the norm. As long as the Browns are healthy, it appears Bond is off the fantasy radar, even against a Tennessee defense allowing 35.9 fantasy points per game (24th) to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Isaiah Bond and the Browns travel to take on the division-rival Steelers in Week 8. He was not targeted in Cleveland's 27-24 comeback victory over the Titans in Week 7. Bond played just six offensive snaps (9%) despite Deshaun Watson throwing 36 times for a season-high 306 passing yards. Bond should remain on fantasy waiver wires for the matchup versus the Steelers' 14th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (30.5) to WRs.

outlooksByWeek.2: LaJohntay Wester and the Ravens host the Saints in Week 2. The second-year receiver played 19 of 68 offensive snaps in the season-opening victory, hauling in both of his targets for 15 yards. He also worked on special teams, but with Zay Flowers (hamstring), Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist), and Devontez Walker (groin) all either questionable or doubtful to play in Week 2, more opportunities open up. New Orleans surrendered 206 yards and two TDs through the air in its Week 1 loss to Detroit.

Brock Wright could continue to carve out a role for himself as the Lions travel to Buffalo in Week 2. There wasn't a lot of hype around Wright heading into the 2026 campaign, but the sixth-year tight end was on the field for nearly 50 percent of offensive snaps and reeled in his sole target for five yards. The veteran could be in store for more opportunities moving forward, and with the volatility of Sam LaPorta injury-wise, Wright is someone to keep on the radar. He'll face a Bills defense that ceded 14.4 PPR points to Texans tight ends this past Sunday.
outlooksByWeek.3: Brock Wright remains a depth option as the Lions play the Jets in Week 3. Wright remained on the field for a good number of snaps (26 percent) in Week 2, but the TE2 was unable to garner a target. The sixth-year tight end will need to run more routes before he can be trusted as anything more than a blocker. He'll also face a New York defense that ranks third in fantasy points per game allowed to tight ends so far this campaign.
outlooksByWeek.4: Brock Wright will aim to stay involved as the Lions travel to Carolina in Week 4. Wright was in the game for a season-high 59 percent of offensive snaps in Week 3 against the Jets, and he logged two catches for seven yards in the outing. The sixth-year tight end remains a secondary TE receiving option behind Sam LaPorta moving forward, but Wright has shown an ability to register looks from veteran Jared Goff so far. The Panthers have ranked middle-of-the-pack against tight ends this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Brock Wright will look to stay involved as the Lions play the Cardinals in Week 5. Wright stayed busy once again versus the Panthers in Week 4, reeling in one of two targets for eight yards. He's now recorded at least one catch in three of four games this season, staying involved even with Sam LaPorta getting most of the tight end targets. Wright will face an Arizona defense that's ranked 28th in fantasy points allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.7: Brock Wright remains a secondary option in Detroit's passing game heading into Week 7 against the Packers. Wright has stayed involved in each game so far this season, recording a catch in all but one outing. The veteran now has five catches for 31 yards across five games, with short-yardage situations being his forte. He'll face a Packers defense that's ranked fifth in fantasy points allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Brock Wright remains a depth option in Detroit's passing game heading into Week 8 against Minnesota. Wright has stayed involved so far this season, recording a catch in all but two games and being a go-to blocker. The veteran now has five catches for 31 yards across six games, with short-yardage situations being his forte. He'll face a Vikings defense that's ranked first in fantasy points allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Brock Wright will remain a depth option in Detroit's passing game against the Dolphins in Week 9. Wright has stayed involved so far this season, recording a catch in all but three games and being a go-to blocker. While he did not record a catch in Week 8 versus Minnesota, he was on the field for a season-high 78 percent of offensive snaps. The veteran now has five catches for 31 yards across seven games, and he'll face a Miami defense that's ranked 30th in fantasy points allowed to TEs.

outlooksByWeek.6: Charlie Kolar returned in Week 5 from a two-game absence due to a forearm injury, and the tight end wound up leading the Chargers with 37 receiving yards while catching three of four targets. His workload as a blocker figures to remain high as the team once again deals with injuries to its offensive line, but a depleted wide receiver room and coordinator Mike McDaniel's apparent unwillingness to deploy Oronde Gadsden could result in increased target volume for Kolar. He is an intriguing dart throw in Week 6 against a Kansas City defense that ranks 31st in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.8: Charlie Kolar has parlayed his blocking skills into a small but consistent role as a pass catcher in the Chargers' offense. He's caught exactly three passes in three straight games, putting together a 9-78-0 line on 13 targets in those contests. The veteran tight end received more targets than Oronde Gadsden in all three games, and the arrangement doesn't seem likely to change as long as Mike McDaniel is offensive coordinator. Kolar will look for his first TD of the season in Week 8 against a stingy Rams defense that's tied for third in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.9: Charlie Kolar remains at the top of the tight end depth chart for the Chargers due to his blocking skills, but he doesn't offer much as a receiver. In a Week 8 loss to the Rams, he caught one of four targets for 20 yards, while Oronde Gadsden caught all five of his targets for 52 yards. Kolar's role seems secure, especially given the injuries along the team's offensive line, but he's unlikely to make a splash as a pass catcher in Week 9 against a Texans defense that ranks fourth in fantasy points per game allowed to TEs.

player.seasonOutlook: Brazzell was selected by the Panthers in the third round of April's draft. He's expected to miss his rookie season due to a knee injury suffered in July. Brazzell is a tall, perimeter receiver with a big wingspan who will do most of his damage down field (career 14.2 aDOT at Tennessee) and doesn't offer much after the catch (3.6 RAC was worst in this rookie WR class). He has good speed (4.37 40-yard dash) and may settle in as a boom/bust low-volume, splash-play fantasy option. He'll battle for a starting role behind Tetairoa McMillan in 2027.

outlooksByWeek.2: Dyami Brown saw two targets in Week 1 for the Commanders. Unfortunately, he could not corral either target and went catchless in the opener. Meanwhile, rookie Antonio Williams looks to have cemented himself as the No. 3 wideout behind Scary Terry and Stefon Diggs with four catches for 64 yards and a touchdown to lead Washington. That being said, there could be plenty of ball to go around in Week 2 versus a Dallas defense that looked dreadful all of last season, as well as Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Dyami Brown tied for second on the Commanders last game with six targets. That led to four catches for 21 yards in the 37-20 loss to Dallas. Unfortunately, starting quarterback Jayden Daniels only played a half due to injury, so veteran backup Marcus Mariota will likely start in Week 3 versus a devastating Seattle defense.
